commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][torch.compile] Find the compiled module through `*args` in the bytecode hook
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fix `vllm serve` failing at engine startup with `KeyError: self` for Transformers modeling backend models (including Llama) on Transformers main. Split from #59224, which carries the same change; it unblocks the Transformers 5.24 bump and #66416.

## Claims

- `bytecode_hook` finds the compiled module when `forward` is wrapped by a `(*args, **kwargs)` decorator, such as Transformers' `deprecate_kwarg`.
- Behaviour is unchanged for ordinary `forward(self, ...)` methods: the first positional argument is still `self`.

## Validation

Repro (1x B200, Transformers main `166948d96c`, `VLLM_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE=1` so Dynamo runs):

```bash
vllm serve NousResearch/Hermes-3-Llama-3.1-8B --port 8217 --max-model-len 4096 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.6
curl -s localhost:8217/v1/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model": "NousResearch/Hermes-3-Llama-3.1-8B", "prompt": "The capital of France is", "max_tokens": 16, "temperature": 0}'
```

`main` (e805e2546e):

```text
(EngineCore pid=...) INFO [utils.py:418] Backends selected for TransformersForCausalLM (NousResearch/Hermes-3-Llama-3.1-8B):
(EngineCore pid=...) ERROR [core.py:1771]   File ".../vllm/compilation/wrapper.py", line 253, in bytecode_hook
(EngineCore pid=...) ERROR [core.py:1771]     if frame.f_locals["self"] is not self:
(EngineCore pid=...) ERROR [core.py:1771] torch._dynamo.exc.InternalTorchDynamoError: KeyError: self
RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed. See root cause above. Failed core proc(s): {}
```

This PR (effde8ff74):

```text
(EngineCore pid=...) INFO [utils.py:418] Backends selected for TransformersForCausalLM (NousResearch/Hermes-3-Llama-3.1-8B):
INFO:     Application startup complete.
"text":" a city of romance, art, and history. It’s a city that has"
```

New test, at effde8ff74:

```text
$ pytest tests/compile/test_wrapper.py -v --durations=0
tests/compile/test_wrapper.py::test_bytecode_hook_with_args_only_decorated_forward PASSED
0.02s call     tests/compile/test_wrapper.py::test_bytecode_hook_with_args_only_decorated_forward
6 passed, 15 warnings in 1.40s
```

With `vllm/compilation/wrapper.py` from `main`:

```text
E       torch._dynamo.exc.InternalTorchDynamoError: KeyError: self
1 failed, 5 deselected, 14 warnings in 0.64s
```

The test runs in CI through `.buildkite/test_areas/distributed.yaml` (and `test-amd.yaml`).

## Details

- **Root cause:** huggingface/transformers#50585 renamed `past_key_values` to `cache` and wraps model forwards in `@deprecate_kwarg`, whose wrapper is `wrapped_func(*args, **kwargs)`. `LlamaModel.forward.__code__` is now that wrapper's code, so Dynamo compiles a frame whose locals are `args` and `kwargs`. `bytecode_hook` indexed `f_locals["self"]` to check the frame belongs to this module, and raised.
- **Fix:** read the frame's first argument from its code object: the first positional parameter, or `args[0]` when the function only takes `*args`.
- **Shared code object:** every `deprecate_kwarg`-wrapped function shares one `wrapped_func` code object, so the code identity check alone can match other modules' frames. The instance check is what filters those out, which is why it has to find the instance rather than be skipped.
- **Offline `LLM(...)`:** in my runs the offline path did not call `bytecode_hook` for this model and worked on `main`. `vllm serve` reproduces reliably.
- **Duplicate check:** the only open PR with this change is my own draft #59224 (Mamba2 support), which it was split from; that PR will drop the hunk once this lands. No issue tracks the crash.

commits.pr_title: [Feature][Frontend] Add metadata value to mm_payload on render requests
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Adds `mm_payload: "metadata"` to render requests: `kwargs_data` is null and `mm_metadata` stays. Prefill can then load embeddings through the EC connector without render serializing the processed tensors. Closes #64997, part of #46722.

## Claims

- A `metadata` render returns the same token IDs, hashes, placeholders and `mm_metadata` as a `tensors` render, without the tensors.
- Prefill from a `metadata` render matches single-instance output end to end.
- `none` and the `tensors` default are unchanged, except for the fix below.
- Fixes a 400 on `tensors` when one modality in a request has no metadata, such as image + video on LLaVA-OneVision and Gemma 4.
- A `metadata` render returns 400 when any modality has no metadata, instead of a response with both fields null that generate would read as fully cached.

## Validation

```bash
pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_mm_serde.py  # 29 passed
pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/render/test_render.py                # 56 passed
MODEL=<model> bash tests/entrypoints/scale_out/ec_integration/run_scale_out_ec_e2e_test.sh
```

Before the fix: 11 of the new or changed test cases fail. `RenderedGenerateRequest` does not exist on main, so alias it to let the file collect:

```bash
git checkout origin/main -- vllm
T=tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_mm_serde.py
sed -i '/^    RenderedGenerateRequest,$/d' $T
echo 'RenderedGenerateRequest = GenerateRequest' >> $T
pytest $T tests/entrypoints/scale_out/render/test_render.py -k 'metadata or mm_kwargs_is_alias'
```

```text
Input should be 'tensors' or 'none' [type=literal_error, input_value='metadata', ...]
Value error, mm_metadata must use the same modalities as mm_hashes
assert {200, 400} == {<HTTPStatus.OK: 200>}
11 failed, 14 passed
```

I extended the EC e2e test so prefill features come from a `metadata` render, after asserting they match the `tensors` render. Single image, two images and text all match the baseline:

| Model | GPU | Metadata source |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-VL-2B | 2 L4 | declared `embedding_fields` |
| LLaVA-OneVision | 1 A100 (both instances), `MAX_MODEL_LEN=16384` | `keep_on_cpu` only |

Response bytes from `vllm launch render` on CPU:

| Model, request | `tensors` | `metadata` | `none` | `mm_metadata` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen2-VL-2B, image | 1,878,981 | 3,411 | 3,285 | present |
| Qwen2-VL-2B, image + video | 3,122,734 | 5,055 | 4,800 | present |
| LLaVA-OneVision, image | 3,554,748 | 15,598 | 15,488 | present |
| LLaVA-OneVision, image + video | 22,451,203 (400 on main) | 400 | 37,564 | null |
| Gemma-4-31B, video | 20,869,285 | 9,679 | 9,205 | present |
| Gemma-4-31B, image + video | 26,085,713 (400 on main) | 400 (same path, not re-run) | 11,182 | null |

The GPU results above are from `8530a778f7` and were not repeated. The review fix only changes `metadata` responses whose metadata is incomplete, and the render tests cover that. On the current head (CPU): `test_render.py` 57 passed, `test_mm_serde.py` 29 passed. The two new rejection tests fail on the previous head (200 instead of 400; no `ValueError`).

## Details

- **New value, not a changed `none`.** #62152 and #64685 rely on `none` being layout only.
- **`RenderedGenerateRequest`.** Render returns `GenerateRequest`, whose EC check rejects metadata-only items, and render output has no EC params until encode runs. Without this subclass every `metadata` render with metadata returns 400, and keeping metadata under `none` would too. The subclass turns the check off with a `ClassVar` flag (`_metadata_only_requires_ec`), not by overriding the validator. `/inference/v1/generate` still validates its input as `GenerateRequest`, so metadata-only items without `ec_transfer_params` are still rejected.
- **Incomplete metadata.** The encoder used to drop a modality without metadata, and `MultiModalFeatures` then rejected the mismatch. `mm_metadata` is now null if any modality has none, which keeps it complete when present (see #56069). For `tensors` and `none` that is a 200 with null `mm_metadata`: `tensors` still carries every field in `kwargs_data`. For `metadata` the response would have both fields null, and generate with `ec_transfer_params` would treat every item as cached and run prefill without fields such as LLaVA-OneVision's `keep_on_cpu` image fields. So render returns 400 and tells the caller to use `tensors`.
- **Limits.** Prefill was not run on Gemma 4 or on real audio. Image + audio is covered by unit tests only. In the EC e2e test, encode takes `kwargs_data` from a `tensors` render. I did not run encode from `content_parts` on a GPU. On CPU, that path gives the same hashes as render (Qwen2-VL-2B and LLaVA-OneVision, 3 requests each), but it expands rendered `token_ids` again (87 to 150 tokens for one image on Qwen2-VL-2B). That is existing behavior and this PR doesn't change it. I did not measure serving latency: #64997 reports the prefill cost of the current fallback.
- **Overlaps.** #60526 moves `MMPayload`, so whichever lands second needs a small rebase. The Rust render (#64685) doesn't accept `metadata` yet and doesn't model `mm_metadata`: #68273.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Support batched prompts on /v1/completions
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

The Rust frontend rejects a batch of prompts on `/v1/completions` with a 400, while Python and OpenAI accept a list of texts or a list of token-ID lists (#62460). This PR supports batched prompts by reusing the `n > 1` fan-out (#65625) per prompt.

Fixes #62460. Supersedes #62495 by @MuonChaser, credited as co-author: same feature, rebuilt on the `n > 1` fan-out, which landed after it was opened.

## Claims

- `prompt` accepts a list of texts or a list of token-ID lists, and each prompt gets `n` choices. Choice indices are prompt-major (`prompt_index * n + i`). In the usage, each prompt's tokens count once and completion tokens add up; a stream sends one final usage chunk. A single prompt behaves as before.
- Like Python, each prompt of a batch is its own engine request, with `-{index}` appended to the request ID.
- `/v1/completions/render` returns one generate request per prompt, with the same request IDs as Python (`cmpl-x` for one prompt, `cmpl-x-0`, `cmpl-x-1`, ... for a batch).
- A batch mixing texts and token-ID lists, or holding a prompt that fails to lower or submit, returns a 400 before any choice streams. Prompts already submitted are aborted.
- CI runs the Python tests that were deselected only because of batched prompts: `test_prompt_logprobs_completion`, `test_multiple_lora_adapters`, and `test_loading_invalid_adapters_does_not_break_others`.

## Validation

- `cargo nextest run -p vllm-server`: 715 passed after merging main; `cargo clippy -p vllm-server --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean. The first commit passes the existing 704 tests on its own.
- New tests:
  - `completions_batched_prompts_return_n_choices_per_prompt`: two text prompts with `n = 2`, `echo`, and a seed. Checks the engine requests (`{id}-0` and `{id}-1`, each with seeds 7 and 8), prompt-major choices that each echo their own prompt, and the usage.
  - `completions_stream_batched_prompts_index_chunks_and_send_one_usage_chunk`: the same for a streamed token-ID batch, with exactly one usage chunk at the end.
  - `completions_batched_prompts_abort_earlier_prompts_when_a_later_prompt_fails`: the engine receives an abort for the first prompt when the second fails to submit.
  - `render_completion_returns_one_generate_request_per_prompt` and `prompt_accepts_one_prompt_or_a_batch_of_one_kind` (wire shapes, including the rejected mixed batch).
  - The usage tests fail when each prompt is counted like another choice of one prompt (`add_choice` instead of `add_prompt`); the abort test fails when the earlier prompts' streams are leaked instead of dropped.
- GPU (one GB200, `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1`, the CI commands from `rust_frontend.yaml` with the new deselects): `entrypoints/openai/completion/test_completion.py -k "not test_batch_completions"` 24 passed, 1 deselected (all four `test_prompt_logprobs_completion` cases now run); `entrypoints/serve/lora/test_lora_adapters.py -k "not test_beam_search_with_lora_adapters"` 12 passed, 1 deselected.
- Live run: `vllm-rs serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` against `vllm-mock-engine` (random tokens). The engine log shows `cmpl-batch1-0-<suffix>` and `cmpl-batch1-1-<suffix>` for the first request.

  <details><summary>Requests and responses (summarized with jq)</summary>

  ```
  $ curl -s $B/v1/completions -d '{"model":"Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B","prompt":["Hello","The capital of France is"],"n":2,"max_tokens":3,"echo":true}' | jq -c ...
  {"id":"cmpl-batch1","choices":[{"index":0,"text":"Hello/newQual Wisconsin"},{"index":1,"text":"Hello__)\n }))\nHead"},{"index":2,"text":"The capital of France is>(\" Gr"},{"index":3,"text":"The capital of France is summe"}],"usage":{"prompt_tokens":6,"total_tokens":18,"completion_tokens":12,"completion_tokens_details":null}}

  $ curl -sN $B/v1/completions -d '{"model":"Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B","prompt":[[9707],[785,6722,315]],"n":2,"max_tokens":2,"stream":true,"stream_options":{"include_usage":true}}'
  {"choices":[{"index":0,"finish_reason":null}],"usage":null}
  {"choices":[{"index":1,"finish_reason":null}],"usage":null}
  {"choices":[{"index":2,"finish_reason":null}],"usage":null}
  {"choices":[{"index":3,"finish_reason":null}],"usage":null}
  {"choices":[{"index":0,"finish_reason":null}],"usage":null}
  {"choices":[{"index":1,"finish_reason":null}],"usage":null}
  {"choices":[{"index":2,"finish_reason":null}],"usage":null}
  {"choices":[{"index":3,"finish_reason":null}],"usage":null}
  {"choices":[{"index":0,"finish_reason":"length"}],"usage":null}
  {"choices":[{"index":1,"finish_reason":"length"}],"usage":null}
  {"choices":[{"index":2,"finish_reason":"length"}],"usage":null}
  {"choices":[{"index":3,"finish_reason":"length"}],"usage":null}
  {"choices":[],"usage":{"prompt_tokens":4,"total_tokens":12,"completion_tokens":8,"completion_tokens_details":null}}
  [DONE]

  $ curl -s $B/v1/completions -d '{"model":"Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B","prompt":"Hello","max_tokens":3}' | jq -c ...
  {"choices":[{"index":0}],"usage":{"prompt_tokens":1,"total_tokens":4,"completion_tokens":3,"completion_tokens_details":null}}

  $ curl -s $B/v1/completions -d '{"model":"Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B","prompt":["Hello",[9707]],"max_tokens":3}'
  {"error":{"message":"Failed to deserialize the JSON body into the target type: prompt: data did not match any variant of untagged enum CompletionPrompt at line 1 column 52", ...} HTTP 400
  ```

  </details>

## Details

- **Layering.** Lowering builds the request-level fields once and expands them into one text request per prompt. The handler submits each with the existing `generate_n`. The shared choice merges gain batch variants, `merge_batch_choice_chunk_streams` and `merge_batch_choice_responses`, which take the choices grouped by prompt; `merge_choice_chunk_streams` and `merge_choice_responses` are the single-prompt case, so chat completions and generate do not change.
- **First commit.** Completions, chat completions, and generate each kept a copy of the non-streaming `merge_choice_responses`. It moves next to `merge_choice_chunk_streams` as one function over a `ChoiceResponse` trait, the counterpart of `ChoiceChunk`, so the batch variant extends one shared merge.
- **Divergences from Python.**
  - A prompt that fails to submit fails the whole request with an HTTP error before streaming, as a single invalid prompt already does in the Rust frontend. Python validates lazily, so a streamed request can report it as an error event after a 200.
  - `prompt: []` is a single empty token-ID prompt and returns the existing empty-prompt 400; Python reports "You must pass at least one prompt". Both are 400s.
  - `cached_tokens` adds up over the prompts. Python reports one prompt's value (the first prompt's when streaming, the last one's otherwise).
- Not covered here: `test_batch_completions` stays deselected because it also sends beam search, which the Rust frontend rejects.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Serve /generative_scoring
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

The Rust frontend answers `POST /generative_scoring` with a 501. This PR serves it with the Python route's semantics: each item becomes one `max_tokens=1` request that reads the label tokens' logprobs. Part of #44280.

Supersedes #46427 by @jesco-absolut, credited as co-author: same route, rebuilt on the current `vllm-text` request preparation, without that PR's speculative-decoding guard and item cap (see Details).

## Claims

- `/generative_scoring` accepts a text or token-ID `query` and `items`, `label_token_ids`, `apply_softmax`, `item_first`, `add_special_tokens`, `cache_salt`, `priority`, and `request_id`, and returns Python's response shape. Usage sums prompt and completion tokens over the items, without prompt-token details, like Python.
- Prompts are built like Python: the query is tokenized with `add_special_tokens`, items without, the two are concatenated as token IDs, and the result keeps its first `max_model_len - 1` tokens. Item `i` is engine request `generative-scoring-{id}-{i}`.
- Label reads use vLLM's neutral sampling defaults rather than the model's generation config, like Python. Under `--logprobs-mode processed_logprobs`, the scores would otherwise depend on the model's temperature and top-k/top-p. The second commit adds `SamplingParams::neutral` to `vllm-text` for this, so the route does not repeat the values.
- Every item is validated (`max_logprobs`, vocabulary range, `cache_salt`) before any is submitted. An engine error on any item fails the request.
- The route counts toward `/load` and runs on the offloaded request runtime, like the other generation routes.
- CI runs `tests/entrypoints/generate/generative_scoring/test_generative_scoring_e2e.py` against the Rust frontend.

## Validation

- `cargo nextest run -p vllm-text -p vllm-server` on `bd62a627b8`: 849 passed, 1 skipped. `cargo clippy -p vllm-text -p vllm-server --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.
- New and changed tests (all pass on `bd62a627b8`):
  - `generative_scoring_reads_label_logprobs_with_plain_sampling_params`: the backend has generation defaults; the engine requests still carry temperature 1, top-k 0, no penalties, `max_tokens = 1`, and the label token IDs, and the scores and usage match the mocked logprobs. It fails when the label reads inherit the generation config.
  - `generative_scoring_joins_and_truncates_item_prompts`: query-first and `item_first` joins, `add_special_tokens`, truncation to `max_model_len - 1`, and token-ID items without a tokenizer.
  - `generative_scoring_rejects_invalid_requests_before_submission`: unknown model, empty labels, empty items, too many labels, and an unsafe `cache_salt` each return their 4xx.
  - `neutral_sampling_params_ignore_generation_defaults`: `SamplingParams::neutral` lowers the same with every generation default set as `SamplingParams::default` with none. It fails when a neutral field is dropped.
  - `/generative_scoring` cases in `engine_request_errors_map_to_http_status` and `skip_tokenizer_init_serves_token_id_completions_only`.
- GPU, one GB200, `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, the route commit `d2cd7cbaa0` (the later commits leave the engine requests unchanged, see the snapshot above): the same 16 requests sent to the Python and Rust frontends.
  - All 9 successful cases return identical scores (max |Δ| = 0), usage, model, and response keys, also with ngram speculative decoding. The cases cover softmax and true-probability scores, `item_first` without special tokens, token-ID inputs, duplicate labels, `cache_salt` with `priority`, a 700-word query truncated to 511 prompt tokens, 40 items over `--max-num-seqs 32`, and a body `request_id`.
  - The 6 error cases return the same status codes; the wording differs (see Details). A batch mixing text and token-ID items returns 200 on Rust and 400 on Python.
  - `pytest -q tests/entrypoints/generate/generative_scoring/test_generative_scoring_e2e.py`: `6 passed, 2 warnings in 51.73s` with `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1`, `6 passed, 2 warnings in 53.15s` without.

  <details><summary>Server commands</summary>

  ```bash
  VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND={0,1} vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --dtype bfloat16 \
    --max-model-len 512 --enforce-eager --max-num-seqs 32
  # Speculative decoding run:
  #   --speculative-config '{"method":"ngram","num_speculative_tokens":3,"prompt_lookup_max":4,"prompt_lookup_min":2}'
  ```

  </details>

## Details

- **Layering.** The route lives in `vllm-server` and lowers each item into an ordinary `TextRequest`, so validation and submission go through the existing `TextRequestProcessor::prepare` and `generate_prepared_n`. `vllm-text` gains only `SamplingParams::neutral`.
- **Speculative decoding.** #46427 rejected scoring under speculative decoding because of #42592. Python has no such guard, and on current main the paired ngram run above returned identical scores with no engine errors, so this PR adds none. Only ngram on the GPU model runner was exercised.
- **Divergences from Python.**
  - A batch may mix text and token-ID items. Python's `items` annotation rejects the mix, but its item loop handles each item on its own, and a text query with token-ID items is already valid, so the restriction is not carried over.
  - Token-ID inputs work without a tokenizer (`--skip-tokenizer-init`); Python rejects every request then. Text inputs without a tokenizer return a 400.
  - Like the other Rust generation routes, the priority, session, and data-parallel-rank headers apply.
  - No admission check: Python calls `check_admission(len(items))`, and the Rust frontend has no admission control on any route yet. There is no separate item cap either.
  - Error wording: the `max_logprobs`, vocabulary, and `cache_salt` messages come from the shared `vllm-text` checks; the 404 message has no "Valid aliases" list; empty labels and empty items set `param`. Status codes match.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Decode the Mooncake store's lookup_lease stats
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

With selective leases (#63420), `MooncakeStoreConnector` records a `lookup_lease` operation that the Rust frontend's `MooncakeOperation` does not know. An interval that contains one stops decoding as Mooncake store stats; inside a `MultiConnector`, the whole payload falls back to `KvConnectorStats::Other`, so that interval's Mooncake store metrics and its sibling connectors' metrics (e.g. NIXL) are dropped. This keeps Mooncake store operation and status names as strings, as Python does, so `lookup_lease` and any later operation are exported without a Rust change; the UMBP store's operation names get the same treatment.

## Claims

- On the Rust frontend, `vllm:mooncake_store_operation_*` include `operation="lookup_lease"`, as on the Python frontend.
- A Mooncake store operation or status, or a UMBP store operation, that Rust code does not name no longer drops the interval's KV connector metrics; it is exported under its own label, as on the Python frontend.

## Validation

On 7f4720ef49 (main 9438027e3b + this change):

```
$ cargo nextest run -p vllm-engine-core-client -p vllm-metrics   # 191 passed
$ cargo clippy -p vllm-engine-core-client -p vllm-metrics --all-targets    # no warnings
$ cargo fmt --check -p vllm-engine-core-client -p vllm-metrics             # clean
```

- New `mooncake_stats_keep_unknown_operations_and_statuses` decodes an operation and a status no Rust code names, alone and as the `MooncakeStoreConnector` child of a `MultiConnector` with a NIXL sibling; on the previous head the unknown status alone made the payload fail as Mooncake.
- `kv_connector_stats_ignore_unknown_fields` now includes an unknown UMBP operation; with the enum key it decoded as `Multi`, dropping the UMBP metrics.
- `python_compat.py` now encodes a `lookup_lease` record with msgspec, and `python_msgpack_fixtures_match_rust_encoding_and_record_nixl_metrics` asserts it decodes. With only that fixture change on unmodified main the test fails: even the payload's `load_get` is lost.

  ```
  assertion failed: matches!(mooncake_stats, KvConnectorStats::Mooncake(stats) if
      stats.0.contains_key(&MooncakeOperation::LoadGet))
  ```

- Found on a 2P1D GLM-5.3 deployment (Rust frontend, `MultiConnector` of NIXL and `MooncakeStoreConnector`, `VLLM_MOONCAKE_STORE_SELECTIVE_LEASE=1`), where the store's operation metrics went missing.

## Details

- Root cause: `MooncakeStats` is a map keyed by `MooncakeOperation`, so one unknown key fails the map. `KvConnectorStats` is untagged: `Mooncake` fails, and `Multi` fails on its `MooncakeStoreConnector` field, leaving `Other`.
- Python records any operation name and status string (`record_operation(operation: str, ..., status: str)`) and exports them as labels, and the Rust labels were already strings; the closed enums were only converted back with `as_str()`. They are removed, along with `UmbpOperation`, so `MooncakeStats` and `UmbpStats` are keyed by `String`.
- The variants stay distinct by value shape, not by key names: Mooncake values must be lists of operation records and UMBP values maps of operation counters, so other connectors' payloads (NIXL fields are number lists; SimpleCPUOffload and `MultiConnector` values are other maps) still fail them and keep their own; `kv_connector_stats_ignore_unknown_fields` covers that ordering and still passes.
- #65917 adds `save_remove` to the old enum; with this change it needs no Rust change.
- The Python `metrics.py` docstring that lists the operations gains `lookup_lease`.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][CI] Dump child process stacks before the Model Executor test timeout
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`(MI300) Model Executor` occasionally hangs with an EngineCore still alive until `--timeout=900` kills the test:

- https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/103769#01a1ed5c-a880-496e-8b5b-abbb6c123a04
- https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/103769#01a1ed79-29a6-4aec-812b-9d05b596bb2b
- https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/103780#01a1ed78-adad-4ff8-afd7-48e182e0875f

#67605 prints the stacks of child processes when a test outlives `faulthandler_timeout`, but `run-amd-test.sh` sets that to 1500 s, so for this step the test is killed at 900 s before the dump fires. This sets `faulthandler_timeout=600` on the `pytest -v -s model_executor` command of the step, where the hangs happen, so the next hang shows where the EngineCore is stuck.

## Claims

- A Model Executor test that runs past 600 s prints the Python stacks of the test process, then the native and Python stacks and kernel wait channels of every child, before `--timeout=900` kills it.
- Test results are unchanged. The dump only prints.

## Validation

I could not reproduce the hang locally: replaying the CI shard from 103769 with its image, test list and environment on MI300X ran 240 times without a hang.

To check the option combination, I ran a test whose child sleeps for 60 s with the CI `PYTEST_ADDOPTS` (`-o faulthandler_timeout=1500 -p amd_ci_fast_exit`) and the step's options, scaled down to `--timeout=15 -o faulthandler_timeout=5`, as root in the ROCm CI image:

```text
test_hang.py::test_hangs_in_child Timeout (0:00:05)!
...
[amd-ci] test timed out: stacks of 1 child processes
[amd-ci] ---- pid 68300 ppid 68296 (sleeping): /usr/bin/python3 -c import time; time.sleep(60)
[amd-ci] kernel wait channels: hrtimer_nanosleep x1
Process 68300: /usr/bin/python3 -c import time; time.sleep(60)
Python v3.12.15 (/usr/bin/python3.12)

Thread 68300 (idle)
    clock_nanosleep (libc.so.6)
    <module> (<string>:1)
    0x7f26cc47ad90 (libc.so.6)
[amd-ci] end of child process stacks
+++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++ Timeout ++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
```

The step's `-o faulthandler_timeout` overrides the value from `PYTEST_ADDOPTS`, the dump fires at 6 s and pytest-timeout still kills the test at 15 s.

## Details

The change is applied to the step in both `test_areas/model_executor.yaml` and `test-amd.yaml`. 600 s leaves 300 s for the dump before the test is killed, and `amd_ci_fast_exit` gives each child at most 60 s. A test that legitimately runs longer than 600 s only gets the extra output.

Not a duplicate: no open PR changes the timeouts of this step.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Kernel] fused_qk_norm_rope: fix int32 offset overflow and NeoX partial-rotary corruption
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes three bugs in `csrc/fused_qknorm_rope_kernel.cu`, one commit each, plus a one-line warp barrier (kernel +37/-21, tests +45/-1):

1. The 32-bit QKV offset overflows for large `num_tokens`.
2. Partial NeoX RoPE is corrupted in the multi-head-per-warp kernel (fixes #51049).
3. The NeoX partner lane is wrong when `rotary_dim / 2` is not a power-of-two number of lanes.
4. The multi-head-per-warp kernel now syncs the warp after the cp.async wait, so the cos/sin copied by other lanes is visible on the GPT-J path too. It was not observed to fail; the NeoX path already gets this ordering from the barrier in fix 2.

This supersedes the stale #43166 (bug 1). It overlaps #50903 (bug 2); see Details.

## Claims

- GLM-5.3-Flash at DP4 + EP on H200 starts with its vision encoder enabled. Main hits an illegal memory access in encoder profiling, which runs the ViT on 960,000 patches.
- `token_heads_per_warp` 2/4/8 and auto are bit-identical to the one-head kernel with partial rotary. Main differs on 33-70% of elements and returns NaN at 8.
- NeoX with a non-power-of-two pair offset (e.g. rotary_dim 48 of 128) matches the reference.
- No slowdown with full rotary.

## Validation

All runs were on H200. The tests ran against main's precompiled op (f538463a2e, whose kernel file is unchanged on current main) and against each commit's kernel, built standalone and swapped in for `torch.ops._C.fused_qk_norm_rope`:

```
pytest tests/kernels/core/test_fused_qk_norm_rope.py
```

| kernel | large_num_tokens (2) | matches_reference (64) |
|---|---|---|
| main | 2 failed (IMA) | 16 failed: F=4 NeoX with ratios 0.5, 0.25, 0.375, and F=1 NeoX with ratio 0.375 |
| commit 1 | pass | 16 failed |
| commit 2 | pass | 8 failed (ratio 0.375) |
| commit 3 | pass | pass |

On main the large-N test fails with:

```
E       torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered
E       Sticky error detected
```

**Server.** The command was:

```
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --tokenizer-mode glm5_next --enable-expert-parallel --data-parallel-size 4 --max-num-seqs 128 --kv-cache-memory=14000000000 --reasoning-parser glm47
```

- On main it dies in encoder profiling with `RuntimeError: Worker failed with error 'CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered'`.
- With the fix it is up after 126 s.
- Ten 1120x1120 synthetic images (printed words and numbers, counts of coloured shapes) plus one GSM8K-style prompt: 11/11 answers correct. They are identical to main with the op run in 512k-token chunks as a workaround.

**Kernel, bf16, 3 runs.** 16/16/16 heads × 64, rot 32, F=2/4/8 vs F=1:

| N | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 4,096 | 4.2M / 6.3M / 7.3M of 12.6M elements differ, NaN | 0 |
| 699,100 | IMA | 0 |
| 969,000 | IMA | 0 |

The Ling shape from #51049 (16q / 4kv × 128, rot 64), at N = 4,096 and 65,536, is also bit-identical to F=1. Full rotary and GPT-J outputs are bit-identical to main.

The server run and this table used an earlier revision of these changes. Its output is bit-identical to this branch at the GLM ViT (rot 64 and 32) and Ling shapes, F=1/2/4/8, N = 4,096 and 700,000.

**Timing** (16/16/16 × 64, median of 50, CUDA events):

| N, F | rot 64 main | rot 64 PR | rot 32 main | rot 32 PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8,192, auto | 53.3 µs | 50.2 µs | 91.1 µs (wrong values) | 50.5 µs |
| 8,192, 1 | 67.9 µs | 66.0 µs | 76.0 µs | 66.0 µs |
| 600,000, auto | 3039 µs | 2853 µs | 5372 µs (wrong values) | 2890 µs |
| 600,000, 1 | 4431 µs | 4169 µs | 5050 µs | 4172 µs |

## Details

**1. Offset overflow.** Both kernels computed `tokenIdx * num_heads * head_dim` in `int`. With 48 heads × 64 dims, the row of token 699,051 starts past INT_MAX. GLM-5.3-Flash's ViT hits this when profiling its maximum dummy video. The fix moves `qkv` to the token's row once, in 64-bit math. The per-head offsets stay row-relative `int`; promoting every offset to `int64_t` (#43166's approach) cost 4-6%. Host-side warp counts would overflow only beyond 2^31 (token, head) pairs, which is at least 256 GiB of QKV, so they are unchanged.

**2. Partial NeoX.** Only lanes `< rotary_lanes` entered the NeoX block, but it called `__syncwarp` and `__shfl_xor_sync` with the full mask. On sm_70+, `shfl.sync` waits until the other lanes in the mask execute any `shfl.sync` with the same qualifiers and mask (PTX ISA 9.7.10.6). The lanes that skipped the block met it with the next head's `warpReduceSum` shuffle, which mixed RMS sums across heads.

Now every lane enters the NeoX block, and only the rotary lanes store the result. The non-rotary lanes' cos/sin index stays below `rotary_dim / 2`, so their reads are in bounds. The existing `__syncwarp` now runs on all lanes. It also orders the cos/sin that other lanes copied with cp.async before they are read: a cp.async write is visible only to its own thread after the wait (PTX ISA 9.7.10.28.3.3).

#50903 instead moves the shuffle out of the guard and drops that `__syncwarp`, which leaves those reads unordered.

**3. Partner lane.** `laneId ^ pairOffset` equals `laneId ± pairOffset` only for power-of-two `pairOffset`. Rot 48 of 128 gives 6. The fix shuffles from the explicit lane. It keeps width 32, because the file is also built for ROCm, where the source lane must stay inside the 32-lane group on wave64.

**4. Barrier after the cp.async wait.** The GPT-J path in the multi-head kernel read cos/sin copied by other lanes with no warp barrier after `cp_async_wait_group<0>()`. A `__syncwarp()` is added there. With it, tests pass (66/66) and output is bit-identical to the previous commit at F=1/2/4/8 for GLM ViT rot 64/32 and Ling shapes, NeoX and GPT-J, N = 4,096 and 700,000.

**Tests.** The existing reference test now also runs `token_heads_per_warp=4` and rotary ratio 0.375. A compact large-N test (about 4.5 GiB; skips below 12 GiB free) covers bug 1. Both run in the H200 MIG 35GB Core Operation Kernels job. ROCm was not tested here.

commits.pr_title: [Hisparse] Support HiSparse for QSA
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

Add HiSparse support for NVIDIA QSA. Main K/V can be offloaded to host; indexer keys, raw-key rings and GDN state stay on GPU.

## Design

QSA reuses the existing HiSparse planner and index-group runtime shared with DSA. Sparse-role fields (cache_role, topk_buffer_width, and is_index_group_leader) now live on AttentionSpec, extending sparse-role metadata from MLA to full K/V attention independently of whether HiSparse is enabled (QSA falls back to its normal backend when HiSparse is off).

The device cache uses a BLNHC layout so each token's K/V across local heads forms one contiguous transfer row. Each TP rank manages a private host pool; host_pool_gib budgets unique KV heads per replica, while padding and replicated heads still consume physical memory.

Fused QSA prepare writes to the resident cache. During decode, the shared resolver maps logical selections to resident/hot physical KV rows (refilling hot-cache misses from host) before BF16/FP8 split-K attention:

QSA logical selections -> HiSparse resolver -> physical KV rows -> BF16/FP8 QSA split-K attention

- **Prefill & split-K:** Prefill reads resident KV directly or via shared staging; split-K honors the backing cache's actual block stride (including padding).
- **MTP & prefix caching:** Target and draft layers reuse logical selections while keeping separate physical-index buffers for CUDA graph replay. Prefix reuse is limited to whole scheduler pages.
- **Warmup:** Covers physical-index decode; BF16 split-K no longer recompiles when the cache-pool block count changes.

NIXL P/D support is split into #68281 (either PR can merge first; QSA P-OFF/D-ON requires both). QSA does not yet support DCP.

## Concurrency and throughput

> Note: GB300 measurements below predate the latest review changes and reflect the highest loads tested (not capacity limits).

**Single engine (single-run).** At 256 clients, HiSparse increased peak running requests from 64 to 179 with 5.3% lower throughput (3,542 vs. 3,354 tok/s). Preemption-free throughput peaked at 32 clients with HiSparse off (2,926 tok/s) vs. 128 clients with it on (3,414 tok/s, also overall ON peak).

![Single-engine output throughput, mean ITL and peak running requests at four client loads.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/31c26b59-362b-4ccb-9b7d-7eebb772692a)

**Disaggregated P/D (3P1D).** Three TP2 prefill replicas fed one TP2 decoder (only D toggled HiSparse; reproducing requires #68281). Across 3-start medians, throughput improved 38.1% at 16 open roots and 42.8% at 64 roots, reaching 899 / 1,680 tok/s (off / on) at 128 roots (1 preemption each; each root can issue multiple requests).

| Open roots | D KV GiB/rank | Starts/mode | Output tok/s, off / on | Mean ITL (ms), off / on | Mean TTFT (s), off / on | D batch mean (peak), off / on |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 8 | 32 | 1, shared host | 907 / 1,158 | 7.67 / 6.84 | 4.16 / 3.90 | 7.8 (17) / 6.4 (20) |
| 16, fixed replay | 64 | 3 | 782 / 1,080 | 12.97 / 6.51 | 6.42 / 4.23 | 6.0 (16) / 5.1 (14) |
| 32 | 64 | 3 | 837 / 1,324 | 36.66 / 23.90 | 7.59 / 7.79 | 40.2 (52) / 31.8 (47) |
| 64 | 64 | 3 | 1,012 / 1,445 | 57.56 / 43.04 | 19.66 / 10.42 | 64.0 (75) / 67.7 (85) |
| 128 | 32 | 1 | 899 / 1,680 | 29.97 / 20.79 | 110.27 / 66.00 | 33.4 (41) / 36.3 (44) |

Three-start entries are medians. Batch counts requests in nonempty decode-only steps. The 8- and 128-root pairs are preliminary. All reported requests completed at the requested length with zero HTTP errors.

![3P1D output throughput, matched-request ITL and peak decoder batch at five root-session limits.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9e7ddd5e-a9f6-4978-8301-91ebf591f697)

**Host landing (128 roots).** When D's GPU cache first hit 99.75% (31.85 / 31.93 GiB), per-rank host main-KV usage was 21.10 / 127.97 GiB (peaking later at 26.47 GiB). NIXL lands main KV directly on host, while decode retains GPU blocks for hot buffers, resident pages, indexer keys, and GDN state. [Upstream landing policy](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65888)

## Low-concurrency overhead

| Workload | Starts/mode | Output tok/s, off / on | Mean client ITL (ms), off / on |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Single engine, one request at a time, 32k input / 512 output | 1 | 105.66 / 97.40 (−7.8%) | 4.06 / 4.54 |
| Single engine, eight requests, 60k input / 10k output | 1 | 1,143.21 / 868.84 (−24.0%) | 6.42 / 8.48 |
| 3P1D, fixed 128-request replay at 16 open roots | 3 | 781.89 / 1,079.63 (+38.1%) | 12.97 / 6.51 |

Single-engine runs are preliminary (the 1-request row averages 3 sequential runs on an earlier build; both ON runs had zero hot misses and H2D bytes). In 3P1D, mean ITL improved in all 3 replays, though one run's P95 rose from 43.37 to 53.62 ms.

![Low-load client ITL for the one-request and eight-request single-engine runs and the fixed 3P1D replay.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/38ee4e10-692f-4016-9e14-f6820b922af6)

**Trace note.** On a BF16 MTP-off single-request trace (126 matched steps), graph-to-graph intervals averaged 7.52 ms off vs. 10.11–10.14 ms on; the resolver took 0.084 ms/rank/step and CPU prep overlapped GPU work, leaving the 0.48 ms client ITL gap open for follow-up.  An experimental FP8 single-pass kernel cut attention to 40 vs. 78 µs at 256 padded rows, with +0.86% / −3.40% end-to-end throughput at 32 roots; this PR keeps split-K. [Single-pass kernel](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/66512)

<details>
<summary>Benchmark configuration and timing</summary>

- **Single engine.** AIPerf 0.13.0, TP2, BF16 main/indexer KV, MTP and prefix caching off, async scheduling on, FULL_DECODE_ONLY. The capacity sweep used 32k input / 8k output, 32 GiB of GPU KV per rank and one start per mode. ON used 4,096 hot rows/request and 256 GiB of logical host KV/replica (128 GiB for the eight-request control). Throughput excludes a full-length warmup and includes 600 s of issuance plus drain.
- **3P1D.** Same eight GB300 GPUs and routes per pair. BLNHC, 3,328-token pages, FP8 E4M3 main KV, BF16 indexer, FP32 GDN, MTP3. P used eager execution, prefix caching on and synchronous scheduling. D used FULL_DECODE_ONLY, prefix caching off and async scheduling on. Max context 1,048,576, max sequences 512, P/D batched-token limits 6,656/2,048. ON used 9,984 hot rows/request and 256 GiB of host KV/TP2 replica. The measured difference includes D's automatic all-reduce choice (MNNVL off, TRTLLM on).
- **AgentX 1.0.12.** Streaming, seed 42, fixed P affinity. The fixed replay used four workers, 32 trajectories, and the same 128 requests (6,454,502 input / 100,825 output tokens) after four separate warmups. Timed replays used eight workers and 393 trajectories with trace delays skipped. Throughput excludes 180 s of warmup and divides output tokens from 600 s of issuance by wall time through the last completion. Drain at 128 roots took 156 s off and 195 s on. ITL and TTFT use matched turns, prompt hashes, lengths and endpoints.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Request counts, cache occupancy and transfers</summary>

**128-root host landing.** All 13 main-KV regions targeted host in NIXL path validation. HiSparse restores the tail after import and can promote older pages into spare GPU blocks. During the 128-root run, each rank enqueued at least 1,514 host-to-resident pages, including tails. The two peaks below pair the GPU and host gauges from the same scrape.

At the first GPU peak, 25 blocks were free. A fresh import needs 39 blocks for hot buffers alone (13 groups × 3). With MTP3, a request fitting one GDN state page also budgets 144 GDN blocks (36 groups × 4). Per-group occupancy and individual admission failures were uninstrumented.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf] W4A16: fix the gfx1151 bf16 tile cliff at decode-sized M (up to +44% decode throughput)
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

On gfx1151, bf16 W4A16 Triton layers have a tile cliff at decode-sized M. The existing prefill-tuned tiles are especially slow at M=33..64 for wide-N layers and at M=65..128 for g32 tall-K layers.

This PR adds gfx1151 bf16 decode-sized-M tile selection for M=9..128. It keeps the existing ladder when a swept tile is not consistently better. The fp16 selector and packed-dequant path are unchanged.

## Results

- Qwen3.8-27B output throughput in the original run: +43.8% at C=64, +41.9% with MTP at C=12, and +33.6% with MTP at C=16.
- Independent rerun: +36.9% at C=64, +37.8% with MTP at C=12, and +33.2% with MTP at C=16. The three PR runs varied by at most 1.3%.
- Kernel benchmark: 1.38x geometric mean over 35 rotated-weight cases, including unchanged M=32 cases. Worst case is 0.90x.
- Maximum relative error against the float32 reference is 0.0031.

## Kernel benchmark

Measurements use gfx1151, five interleaved rounds, the production weight layout, rotated weights totaling at least 128 MB, and a 256 MB flush before each timed replay. This prevents the 32 MB MALL from serving the same weight tensor repeatedly. The GPU used the default power profile; kernel-run sclk had a median of 2864 MHz.

| shape (K → N), weights | M=16 | M=32 | M=48 | M=64 | M=96 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3.8 gate_up 5120 → 34816, 88 MB | 760 → 638 (-16%) | 784 → 782 (-0%) | 2950 → 1006 (-66%) | 2935 → 1058 (-64%) | 1818 → 1818 (-0%) |
| Qwen3.8 gdn in_proj 5120 → 16384, 41 MB | 400 → 361 (-10%) | 423 → 418 (-1%) | 1406 → 539 (-62%) | 1413 → 556 (-61%) | 962 → 968 (+1%) |
| Qwen3.8 attn qkv 5120 → 14336, 36 MB | 346 → 324 (-6%) | 359 → 357 (-1%) | 1207 → 468 (-61%) | 1213 → 478 (-61%) | 804 → 801 (-0%) |
| Qwen3.8 down 17408 → 5120, 44 MB | 416 → 391 (-6%) | 446 → 442 (-1%) | 781 → 595 (-24%) | 814 → 622 (-24%) | 1265 → 850 (-33%) |
| Qwen3-8B qkv 4096 → 6144, 12 MB | 379 → 302 (-20%) | 387 → 347 (-10%) | 405 → 422 (+4%) | 424 → 469 (+11%) | 445 → 443 (-0%) |
| Llama-3-8B gate_up 4096 → 28672, 58 MB | 598 → 627 (+5%) | 655 → 661 (+1%) | 3421 → 963 (-72%) | 3232 → 1030 (-68%) | 1743 → 1742 (-0%) |
| g32 down 17408 → 5120, 48 MB | 731 → 734 (+0%) | 776 → 835 (+8%) | 857 → 829 (-3%) | 912 → 885 (-3%) | 4994 → 1123 (-78%) |

## Implementation

- bf16 M=9..64 bypasses the prefill overrides and uses the decode selector.
- The selector distinguishes g32/g64/g128 and tall-K/wide-N shapes.
- M=8, M=32, and g32 fallback behavior are covered by selection tests.
- fp16 selection is unchanged. A no-plot spot check on four Qwen3-4B shapes at M=16, 32, 48, 64 and 96 stayed within 4.2% of main; this is not a full fp16 sweep.

## Validation and limitations

- New selection tests: 8 passed in the ROCm gfx1151 container.
- Correctness validation covers fp16 and bf16, symmetric and asymmetric weights, and the new M ranges.
- End-to-end validation used Qwen3.8-27B-Quark-AWQ-INT4-W4A16 and GSM8K.
- The change is gfx1151-specific and has one model end-to-end validation.
- The M=33..64 range remains bandwidth-bound; a dedicated bandwidth-bound kernel is future work.

commits.pr_title: [XPU] Add VLLM_XPU_SUPPORT_FP8_QUERY to control FP8 query in flash attention
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

On XPU, `flash_attn_supports_quant_query_input()` always returns False, so the FA backend never quantizes the query to FP8 even with an FP8 KV cache. Xe3p kernels in vllm-xpu-kernels (>= 0.1.17) can run full-FP8 attention (FP8 Q/K/V, `q_scale` fused in the kernel), while Xe2 kernels cannot.

This PR adds `VLLM_XPU_SUPPORT_FP8_QUERY` (`bool | None`, default unset) to control it:

| `VLLM_XPU_SUPPORT_FP8_QUERY` | Device | FP8 query |
|---|---|---|
| `1` | any XPU | on |
| `0` | any XPU | off |
| unset | Xe3p (`torch.ops._xpu_C.is_xe3p_arch()`) | on |
| unset | other XPU (e.g. BMG), or op missing | off (unchanged) |

Implementation: `XPUPlatform.support_fp8_query()` resolves the value, and `flash_attn_supports_quant_query_input()` calls it on XPU. Other platforms are unchanged (still True).

Limitation: the Xe3p full-FP8 kernels currently only support head_size 128 (and Q/K/V of the same FP8 type), so models with another head size fail on Xe3p when the FP8 KV cache is on; set `VLLM_XPU_SUPPORT_FP8_QUERY=0` for those until the kernels are extended.

## Test Plan

On an Xe3p GPU, serve a model with FP8 KV cache (`--kv-cache-dtype fp8`) and check the query is quantized; compare with `VLLM_XPU_SUPPORT_FP8_QUERY=0`. On a non-Xe3p XPU the default stays off. Not yet run on hardware.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][ROCm][MoRIIO] Fix heterogeneous-TP WRITE of NVFP4 KV pages and replicated indexer caches
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

MoRIIO's heterogeneous-TP WRITE (prefill TP != decode TP) cannot serve MiniMax-M3 today, for two independent reasons. This PR fixes both:

1. **NVFP4 KV pages** (`--kv-cache-dtype nvfp4` on ROCm): the WRITE cuts the page into per-head slots as if each KV head's bytes were contiguous, but the ROCm page stores all heads' FP4 data before all heads' block scales on each K/V side. A decode instance with a smaller TP than prefill (e.g. TP4 -> TP1) receives scrambled KV and generates garbage. This PR slices those pages by their real layout, and refuses any other packed NVFP4 page instead of mis-slicing it.
2. **Replicated indexer key cache**: MiniMax-M3's lightning-indexer keys live in an MLA-type cache (one vector per token, identical on every TP rank) inside a GQA model. The per-layer WRITE mapping sizes it by the model's KV heads, so with prefill TP > decode TP (and fewer prefill ranks than KV heads, e.g. TP4 -> TP2) it tries to slice it by head and every request fails with `MoRIIOError: Heterogeneous-TP WRITE of layer ...indexer... needs a KV head layout on both sides`. This PR maps such a layer like an MLA latent: copied whole, by one prefill rank per decode rank on fan-in and to every decode rank on fan-out.

## Claims

- Prefill TP != decode TP over MoRIIO WRITE with an NVFP4 KV cache on ROCm (MiniMax-M3) now lands every KV byte where the decode kernels read it; before, the decoder output was garbage.
- A packed NVFP4 page MoRIIO cannot slice (e.g. laid out by KV head, `kv_head_major_slots=True`) now fails with a clear `ValueError` instead of silently writing the wrong head slots.
- Prefill TP > decode TP over MoRIIO WRITE with an MLA-type cache in a non-MLA model (MiniMax-M3's indexer keys) now copies that cache whole; before, it raised `MoRIIOError: ... needs a KV head layout on both sides`. Topologies where it already worked (prefill TP < decode TP, or more prefill ranks than KV heads, e.g. TP8 -> TP4 with 4 KV heads) did so only because the head counts happened to collapse to one head per rank; they now take the whole-block path explicitly.
- No change for any other KV cache, for MLA models, or when prefill and decode hold the same KV heads.

## Validation

**Unit tests** (CPU): `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/moriio/test_moriio_hetero_tp_write.py` gets an NVFP4 layer and a replicated indexer layer.

*NVFP4.* The NVFP4 layer's spec comes from the real `MiniMaxM3SparseRocmNvfp4Backend.customize_spec`; every producer rank fills its pages in the ROCm layout (per side: held heads' data, then held heads' scales), and the existing harness runs the real MoRIIO writer and connector offset code, copies the planned bytes into the decode ranks' caches and compares every decode page byte for byte with the expected one.

- `test_nvfp4_write_lands_every_shard_byte_exact[P-D]` for (prefill TP, decode TP) in (4, 1), (2, 1), (4, 2), (1, 2), (1, 4), (2, 2), with 4 KV heads.
- `test_nvfp4_page_laid_out_by_kv_head_is_not_sliced`: the same page laid out by KV head (as the NVIDIA MSA backend publishes it) must be refused under TP2 -> TP1.

```
# base (origin/main 9929e84fd), tests from this PR
$ pytest -q tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/moriio/test_moriio_hetero_tp_write.py -k nvfp4
E               AssertionError: 1005 of 3456 bytes of attn0 wrong on decode rank 0
E               AssertionError: 863 of 3456 bytes of attn0 wrong on decode rank 0
E               AssertionError: 431 of 1728 bytes of attn0 wrong on decode rank 0
E               AssertionError: 320 of 1728 bytes of attn0 wrong on decode rank 0
E               AssertionError: 160 of 864 bytes of attn0 wrong on decode rank 0
E               AssertionError: 863 of 3456 bytes of attn0 wrong on decode rank 0
FAILED ...::test_nvfp4_write_lands_every_shard_byte_exact[4-1]
FAILED ...::test_nvfp4_write_lands_every_shard_byte_exact[2-1]
FAILED ...::test_nvfp4_write_lands_every_shard_byte_exact[4-2]
FAILED ...::test_nvfp4_write_lands_every_shard_byte_exact[1-2]
FAILED ...::test_nvfp4_write_lands_every_shard_byte_exact[1-4]
FAILED ...::test_nvfp4_page_laid_out_by_kv_head_is_not_sliced
6 failed, 1 passed, 325 deselected

# this PR
7 passed, 325 deselected
```

(The one passing case on base is TP2 -> TP2, which copies whole blocks.) `test_moriio_read_tp.py` imports the same model table, so the READ path is also exercised with the indexer layer (unchanged code, passes before and after).

*Replicated indexer cache.* A new `gqa_indexer` model (4 KV heads: a GQA attention layer plus an MLA-type `indexer0` layer, as in MiniMax-M3) joins the end-to-end harness for every (prefill TP, decode TP) in (1, 2), (2, 4), (2, 1), (4, 2), (2, 2), (1, 4), (4, 8), (8, 4), with and without HMA and with token-major / head-major / mixed layouts; every decode rank must hold the full indexer block. `test_replicated_indexer_cache_is_copied_whole[P-D]` checks the mapping directly for (4, 2), (8, 4), (2, 4): on fan-in only the first prefill rank of each decode rank's group writes it, as a whole-block copy; on fan-out every decode rank gets the whole block.

```
# before this fix (23284ad37, NVFP4 fix only), new tests
$ pytest -q tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/moriio/test_moriio_hetero_tp_write.py -k indexer
E   MoRIIOError: Heterogeneous-TP WRITE of layer indexer0 needs a KV head layout on both sides; ...
FAILED ...::test_replicated_indexer_cache_is_copied_whole[4-2]
FAILED ...::test_write_lands_every_shard_byte_exact[gqa_indexer-2-1-{True,False}-{token-major,head-major,mixed}]  (6)
FAILED ...::test_write_lands_every_shard_byte_exact[gqa_indexer-4-2-{True,False}-{token-major,head-major,mixed}]  (6)
13 failed, 38 passed, 332 deselected

# this PR
51 passed, 332 deselected
```

The whole `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/moriio/` directory with this PR (`examples/` on the path for the proxy tests): `1226 passed`; the NVFP4 commit alone: `1157 passed`. In both runs the same 25 tests in `test_moriio_connector.py` fail on our GPU-less test host because they build a `VllmConfig` for a real model (`Model architectures ['OPTForCausalLM'] failed to be inspected`); they are unrelated to this PR.

**End to end** (with equivalent fixes for both issues, on an older vLLM; see the note below):

- 9n, 2 nodes x 8 MI355X, `MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Quark-MXFP4`, MoRIIO WRITE P/D: prefill PP2 x TP4 (one node) -> decode DP8 x TP1 + EP8 (MoRI EPv2, the other node), `--kv-cache-dtype nvfp4`, indexer KV dtype nvfp4, `--block-size 128`, `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=LBHNC`. Every prefill TP rank writes 1/4 of the KV heads into each decode page. gsm8k (1319 questions, through the router): **strict 0.9409 / flex 0.9401**, 0 errors.
- Crusoe, 1 node x 8 MI355X, same model and KV settings, 1P1D prefill TP4 (GPUs 0-3) -> decode DP4 x TP1 + EP4 (GPUs 4-7) over MoRIIO WRITE (xGMI): without the fix every decode output is garbage (`licliclic...`); with it gsm8k (1319) strict 0.9583 / flex 0.9575.

Note: both runs used older vLLM builds (vLLM `a2bcb5657a` on Crusoe, the image's upstream `65de218` on 9n) with an overlay holding an equivalent fix that hardcoded the head_size 128 sizes (64 B data, 8 B scales, 72 B slots). This PR derives the sizes from the spec. The overlay copied the indexer cache whole with a special case in the writer (first producer of each decode group on fan-in, every target on fan-out); this PR expresses the same thing through the per-layer WRITE mapping that main now has, so the writer and the offset code need no special case.

CI: the changed files are covered by the existing `:amd: (MI355 DPX) MoRIIO Connector Unit Tests` step (`pytest -v -s -rs v1/kv_connector/unit/moriio`).

## Details

**Flow** (MoRIIO WRITE, prefill TP4 -> decode TP1, 4 KV heads):

1. Decode allocates blocks and sends their ids to every prefill rank.
2. Each prefill rank `p` holds KV head `p`. After each layer's forward it computes byte offsets that move its head from its page into head `p` of the decode page, and posts RDMA writes.
3. The decode kernels read the page assuming the ROCm NVFP4 layout.

Step 2 is where the bytes went to the wrong place.

**NVFP4: root cause.** `MiniMaxM3SparseRocmNvfp4Backend.customize_spec` publishes the page as `2 * num_kv_heads` head slots of `nvfp4_kv_cache_full_dim(head_size)` bytes (72 B per token for head_size 128) and does not set `kv_head_major_slots`. The kernels do not store a slot per head, though. Each block is `[K side | V side]`, and each side holds every KV head's FP4 data (`BLK x head_size / 2` bytes per head) followed by every KV head's E4M3 block scales (`BLK x head_size / 16` bytes per head):

- writer, `vllm/models/minimax_m3/amd/ops/norm_rope_nvfp4_insert/kernel.py`: `SIDE = nkv * BLK * 72`; K data at `h * (BLK * 64)`, K scales at `nkv * BLK * 64 + h * (BLK * 8)`; V the same from `SIDE`.
- reader, `vllm/models/minimax_m3/amd/ops/nvfp4_prefill/kernel.py` `kv_lane_loader`: `side_b = hkv * (DATA_B + SCALE_B)`, `k_scl = hkv * DATA_B + kvh * SCALE_B`, `v_data = side_b + kvh * DATA_B`, `v_scl = side_b + hkv * DATA_B + kvh * SCALE_B`.

MoRIIO's `get_layer_head_layout` reads this `[B, 2H, N, C]` view as `2H` heads of `N x C` bytes, and `compute_head_slice_offsets` copies slot `h` for KV head `h`, which mixes data and scales of different heads and sides. NIXL already refuses this case ("NVFP4 pages store all heads' data before all heads' scales"); MoRIIO had no NVFP4 handling.

**NVFP4: fix.**

- `get_nvfp4_page_split(spec)` recognizes the split page from the spec (`kv_quant_mode.is_nvfp4`, `state_content_bytes` set, not `kv_head_major_slots`, `2 * num_kv_heads` slots) and returns the data and scale bytes per token of one head (`head_size // 2`, `head_size // 16`). Any other packed NVFP4 page raises `ValueError`.
- `compute_head_slice_offsets(..., nvfp4_split=...)` counts KV heads instead of slots and, per block, copies one data run and one scale run per side for the written heads. The page must be head-major, which the ROCm backend requires anyway (`LBHNC` / `BLHNC`).
- Only the heterogeneous-TP WRITE path passes the split. Whole-block copies and the READ path, which moves every slot of the page, are unchanged.

**Replicated indexer cache: root cause.** Since the per-layer WRITE mapping (`MoRIIOConnectorWorker._write_tp_mapping(remote_tp_size, layer_name)`), each attention layer is mapped with its own KV-head count, and `is_mla` / one head is used only when the whole model is MLA (`self.use_mla`). MiniMax-M3 is a GQA model whose indexer keys use an `MLAAttentionSpec` (`num_kv_heads=1`). `_layer_total_num_kv_heads` treats that one head as a replicated GQA head and returns `min(total_num_kv_heads, tp_size)`, so with prefill TP4 -> decode TP2 the indexer is mapped as 4 heads, each decode rank "holds" 2 of them, the producer's target is a 1-head slice of a 2-head block, and `_compute_head_slice_transfer_offsets` raises because the layer has no KV head layout. When both sides end up with one "head" per rank (prefill TP < decode TP, or prefill TP >= KV heads) the target happens to be a whole-block copy, which is why only some topologies failed.

**Replicated indexer cache: fix.** `_write_tp_mapping` treats a layer as MLA when the model is MLA *or* the layer's spec is an `MLAAttentionSpec` (`_is_mla_cache_layer`, which the block-offset path already uses for its TP validation). `compute_write_tp_mapping` then maps the layer with one head and `is_mla=True`: on fan-in the first prefill rank of each group gets a whole-block target and the others get none (`num_heads == 0`, skipped by the writer); on fan-out every target is a whole-block copy. Request-level targets and `write_done` counting still use the model-wide mapping and are unchanged.

Limitations: an NVFP4 page laid out by KV head (`kv_head_major_slots=True`, the NVIDIA MSA backend) is refused under heterogeneous TP rather than supported; MoRIIO runs on ROCm, where no backend uses that layout today.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Avoid torch 2.13 Inductor gather bug in Nemotron diffusion sampler
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`test_nemotron_dllm.py::test_greedy_generation` and `::test_stochastic_rollouts` fail on `(MI355 DPX) Language Models (Extended Generation) Shard 4/5` with `NameError('tmp27 is not defined')` while Inductor compiles `_compiled_masked_step` ([build 104240](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/104240/list?jid=01a1f311-c30d-42da-b4d6-9b5f5e6fec2f&tab=output)). This is a torch 2.13 Inductor bug ([pytorch#194490](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/194490)), fixed in torch 2.14 ([pytorch#194786](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/194786)). The ROCm image still uses torch 2.13, while CUDA already uses 2.14.

On torch < 2.14 this PR computes the chosen token logit with a masked max instead of `gather`. The result is the same. On torch >= 2.14 the code is unchanged.

## Claims

Fixes the two Nemotron diffusion tests on AMD (MI355). No change for CUDA.

## Validation

MI355X, `rocm/vllm-ci:test-deps-rocm-732c5b866ce79bb3` (torch 2.13.0+rocm10.0.0), base e2c96445a5, Inductor caches disabled. The DPX partitions in CI have 128 CUs, and the bug only shows with that CU count, so Inductor's CU count was set to 128 locally.

`pytest tests/models/language/generation/test_nemotron_dllm.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_nemotron_dllm_sampler.py`: 27 passed with 128 CUs and with 256 CUs. Without the fix, `test_greedy_generation` fails with the same `NameError` as CI.

The old and new `_compiled_masked_step` give bit-identical outputs for 1, 4 and 16 requests, with and without logprobs.

## Details

Inductor fuses `argmax`, `gather`, the rank count and `logsumexp` into one Triton kernel with several reduction loops. The `gather` load is emitted inside a loop but cached as if it were outside, so the epilogue after the loop reuses a variable that does not exist there. A masked max is a normal reduction, so no indirect load is cached. `chosen_lp` reuses the result instead of a second `gather`.

The torch < 2.14 branch can be removed once ROCm moves to torch 2.14.

AI assistance was used for this PR.

---

commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fixes #67946. With `deduplicate_contexts="all"` and speculative decoding, a context whose earlier occurrence starts in the prompt and ends in the output is not detected as repeated, so the token is watermarked where non-speculative decoding skips the watermark. This fixes the repeated-context mask for verification rows and draft steps. Found while reviewing #65961, whose token-identity claim depends on this mask.

## Claims

- The repeated-context mask of speculative rows equals the non-speculative mask in all three modes (`none`, `single_turn`, `all`).
- `single_turn` and `none` are unchanged: same masks, same generated code.
- With greedy drafts from #65961, speculative and non-speculative output are token-identical in mode `all`.

## Validation

One H200, main at 9986df412, precompiled wheel.

- **New test** `test_speculative_contexts_compare_prompt_tokens` (CPU, and CUDA when available): width 3 with a repeat that crosses the prompt boundary by two tokens; the `all` cases fail on main with `assert ([True, True, False, False, False], [False, False, True, True]) == ([True, True, False, True, False], [False, False, True, False])` and pass here. The `single_turn` cases pass on both.
- **Existing tests:** `tests/watermarking`, `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_rejection_sampler_utils.py`, `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_rejection_sampler_chunking.py`: 323 passed on main, 327 here (the 4 new cases), same 10 skips.
- **Mask equivalence, real Triton kernel:** over random token sequences, each speculative row compared with the non-speculative mask after its drafts are committed. Wrong skip decisions go from 34 of 112,521 verification rows and 45 of 145,813 draft steps on main to 0. The only rows whose mask changes are those rows.
- **End to end** on #65961 merged onto main: 523 of 528 requests token-identical on main, 528 of 528 with this PR (mode `all`); `single_turn` 528 of 528 on both.
- **Cost** of `repeated_context_mask`: `single_turn` 0.998 to 1.005x, `all` 1.017 to 1.033x (under 1 µs per call, independent of history length). End-to-end throughput not measured.

<details>
<summary>Commands and setup</summary>

Mask equivalence grid: mode x `max_history` {None, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8192} x `context_width` {1, 2, 4} x K {1, 3, 7}, 20,000 random trials. Wrong rows on main are all mode `all`, `context_width` 2 or 4, with fewer generated tokens than `context_width` before the step.

End to end: Qwen/Qwen3-8B, EAGLE-3 drafter, 528 requests with fixed seeds, each compared between a speculative and a non-speculative server:

```
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B \
  --watermark-config '{"key":42,"context_width":4,"algorithm":"dual_key_gumbel","alpha":0.1,"deduplicate_contexts":"all"}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"eagle3","model":"RedHatAI/Qwen3-8B-speculator.eagle3","num_speculative_tokens":3,"draft_sample_method":"greedy"}'
```

All 5 differing requests on main differ first at output position 4. Non-speculative output is the same with and without this PR.

Cost: 64 requests x 8 rows, width 4, K 7, `max_history` 8192, main and this PR alternating in one process, 3 processes of 3,000 calls per arm.

</details>

## Details

Root cause: `_get_contexts` writes -1 at context positions inside the prompt. For speculative rows the kernel compares n-grams ending at the last committed token or at a draft through the contexts of earlier rows of the same block (`prior_contexts` on the draft side). In mode `all` the non-speculative path compares real prompt tokens at those positions, but the stored contexts hold -1, which never matches.

Fix: under `INCLUDE_PROMPT`, the block comparison reads the prompt token from `all_token_ids` where the earlier context lies inside the prompt. That is `K * context_width` masked scalar loads per row and no extra history scan. No signature change; `_get_contexts`, the partial-context rule from #61194 and the contents of `prior_contexts` are untouched. The CPU reference gets the same change.

#65909 edits the same kernel; whichever lands second gets a small textual conflict.

---

commits.pr_title: [KV Connector] Honor per-request Mooncake offload limits
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Honor `kv_transfer_params.max_offload_tokens` in `MooncakeStoreConnector`. A limit of `0` disables writes; positive limits cap the prefix written to the store while preserving lookups and loads.

## Claims

- Regular saves round down to complete blocks within the cap: with 16-token blocks, `100` permits a 96-token regular prefix.
- Boundary-state handoffs, finish-time checkpoints, and partial-tail attention proofs stay within the cap.
- The cap uses existing request tracking and store metadata. Mooncake and the native OffloadingConnector share parsing, preserving integer zero and the existing warning-and-ignore behavior for invalid values.

## Validation

Tests use real requests, scheduler configuration, metadata, cache groups, and block pools; only the external lookup service is stubbed. They cover zero, positive caps, block rounding, exact checkpoint/proof boundaries, preserved loads, decode, finish-time saves, and request-ID reuse.

Validation was run on `9571bbfeec4f3e23a5b39ab67ac9aae631207412` with a UV-managed Python environment. The existing CPU Buildkite step already selects the changed test file.

```bash
PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_scheduler.py -q --tb=short
```

`103 passed, 1 warning in 11.56s`

```bash
PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -m cpu_test \
  -k 'zero_offload_policy or request_offload_limit or shared_prefix_junction_handoff' \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_scheduler.py
```

`18 passed, 85 deselected, 1 warning in 2.36s`

Pre-commit checks, including formatting, lint, mypy, and test selection, pass. GPU/OpenAI-server validation and model evaluations were not run on this macOS host; this remains a draft pending integration validation.

<details>
<summary>Before-fix reproduction</summary>

With the new tests but unchanged upstream store code at `2aa3f0ec1e`, run:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_scheduler.py \
  -k 'zero_offload_policy or request_offload_limit_bounds' -q --tb=short
```

`7 failed, 4 passed, 91 deselected, 1 warning in 1.34s`

The zero request still emits a store job. A cap of `100` emits a 128-token regular prefix; a cap of `131` accepts a checkpoint at 132; a cap of `132` writes decode tokens through 160.

</details>

## Details

Merged current upstream main to resolve test-import and appended-test conflicts. Both the request-cap regressions and upstream failed-transfer completion test are preserved.

Parse the limit when the existing request tracker is created. Clamp its regular save length without changing the computed or loaded token count, and carry the cap into store metadata for partial-tail proofs. Reject out-of-range handoffs before acquiring block references.

No overlapping Mooncake cap fix was found in open upstream PRs. [#52397](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52397) and [#62012](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62012) address the native OffloadingConnector's partial-tail assertion, rather than Mooncake request-cap support.

---

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Preserve assistant refusal history in the HF renderer
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Preserve assistant history carried in a top-level `refusal` when `content` is empty during shared Python chat normalization. This restores the refusal text in prompts produced by the HF renderer.

## Claims

- Missing `content`, `content: null`, `""`, and `[]` with a non-empty string `refusal` produce the same normalized conversation as an explicit refusal content block; the HF `/tokenize` path produces the same token IDs too.
- Non-empty content keeps precedence, including content supplied as a one-shot iterator.

## Validation

Compared Python source at `a4910b41280ae228bcc74ebc9d21144e09ef63ef` with and without this change, using the same test file for the before/after comparison. Validation ran on macOS arm64 CPU with official `HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM2-135M-Instruct` weights, revision `12fd25f77366fa6b3b4b768ec3050bf629380bac`.

- Base source plus the new tests: `20 failed, 9 passed`. Sixteen normalization cases and four real HTTP cases lose the refusal text; the six non-empty controls and three original tests pass.
- With the fix: `29 passed` in the full assistant suite, including four real `RemoteOpenAIServer` `/tokenize` cases; `9 passed` in the existing tokenization suite.
- All applicable pre-commit hooks passed on the three changed files, including markdownlint, mypy and test tethering. No hooks were manually excluded.
- Final fixture validation with `--kv-cache-memory-bytes 268435456` and both `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND` and `VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE` unset: `29 passed, 2 warnings in 22.34s`. The server reported a 0.25 GiB KV cache with capacity for 5,760 tokens. All applicable pre-commit hooks passed again.

The SDK replay fixture builds a `ChatCompletionMessage(content=None, refusal=...)` and serializes it with `model_dump(exclude_none=True)` before placing it between two user messages. The full conversation is checked after both `ChatCompletionRequest` and `TokenizeChatRequest` validation in string/openai formats, and through the real `/tokenize` endpoint against explicit assistant text. All earlier empty-content cases remain.

The added unit tests construct real `ModelConfig` and `MultiModalItemTracker` objects. A module-scoped fixture reuses the model configuration; each parse creates its own tracker. The original `_parse_one` helper and all three existing reasoning tests are unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Final fixture validation command and output</summary>

The launcher removed both environment variables before starting pytest. Equivalent command from the repository root in the configured CPU environment (`$PYTHON` is the selected virtual environment's interpreter):

```bash
env -u VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND -u VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE \
  "$PYTHON" -m pytest -p pytest_asyncio.plugin -p pytest_timeout -v -s --tb=short --timeout=150 \
  tests/renderers/chat_utils/test_assistant.py
```

The fixture started this server (the port is allocated dynamically):

```text
vllm serve HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM2-135M-Instruct --dtype float32 --max-model-len 256 --enforce-eager --kv-cache-memory-bytes 268435456 --port 57284 --seed 0
```

Relevant output:

```text
Explicitly set (0.25/24.0) GiB for KV cache on node 0.
CPU KV cache size: 5,760 tokens, Maximum concurrency for 256 tokens per request: 22.50x
======================= 29 passed, 2 warnings in 22.34s ========================
```

This final fixture run was on CPU. The tokenization suite's `9 passed` result below is from the earlier validation; that unchanged test file was not rerun for this fixture-only update. GPU execution has not been validated for this update.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Before/after regression evidence (earlier fixture)</summary>

The following recorded before/after runs used the earlier fixture with a 1 GiB CPU cache limit. They establish the refusal regression; the final fixture's fresh run is shown above. The local launcher provided a hash-verified offline model cache, a short IPC temporary directory, the checkout on `PYTHONPATH`, and these settings:

```bash
export VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=0 VLLM_ENABLE_COHERE_API=0
export VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE=1 VLLM_CPU_OMP_THREADS_BIND=nobind
export VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=2 MKL_NUM_THREADS=2 NUMBA_NUM_THREADS=2
export HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1 TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM=false
export VLLM_NO_USAGE_STATS=1 DO_NOT_TRACK=1 PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1
export NO_PROXY=localhost,127.0.0.1,::1 no_proxy=localhost,127.0.0.1,::1

"$PYTHON" -m pytest -p pytest_asyncio.plugin -p pytest_timeout -v -s --tb=short --timeout=150 \
  tests/renderers/chat_utils/test_assistant.py
"$PYTHON" -m pytest -p pytest_asyncio.plugin -p pytest_timeout -v -s --tb=short --timeout=150 \
  tests/entrypoints/serve/tokenize/test_tokenization.py
"$PYTHON" -m pre_commit run --files \
  vllm/renderers/chat_utils/chat_message.py \
  tests/renderers/chat_utils/test_assistant.py \
  docs/serving/online_serving/openai_compatible_server.md
```

The first command was identical before and after the fix. The test fixture started these servers (ports are allocated dynamically):

```text
Base assistant suite:
vllm serve HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM2-135M-Instruct --dtype float32 --max-model-len 256 --enforce-eager --port 52376 --seed 0
Fixed assistant suite:
vllm serve HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM2-135M-Instruct --dtype float32 --max-model-len 256 --enforce-eager --port 52463 --seed 0
Existing tokenization suite on the fix:
vllm serve HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM2-135M-Instruct --dtype bfloat16 --max-model-len 8192 --enforce-eager --max-num-seqs 128 --enable-tokenizer-info-endpoint --port 52538 --seed 0
```

Raw base-source failure excerpts:

```text
___ test_assistant_refusal_replays_sdk_history[string-ChatCompletionRequest] ___
tests/renderers/chat_utils/test_assistant.py:124: in test_assistant_refusal_replays_sdk_history
    assert conversation == expected
E   AssertionError: assert [{'role': 'us...ou suggest?'}] == [{'role': 'us...ou suggest?'}]
E     
E     At index 1 diff: {'role': 'assistant', 'content': ''} != {'role': 'assistant', 'content': 'I cannot provide private details, but can suggest public sources.'}

____________________ test_tokenize_chat_replays_sdk_refusal ____________________
tests/renderers/chat_utils/test_assistant.py:239: in test_tokenize_chat_replays_sdk_refusal
    assert results[0] == results[1]
E   AssertionError: assert {'count': 53,...n_strs': None} == {'count': 65,...n_strs': None}
E     
E     Omitting 2 identical items, use -vv to show
E     Differing items:
E     {'tokens': [1, 9690, 198, 2683, 359, 253, ...]} != {'tokens': [1, 9690, 198, 2683, 359, 253, ...]}
E     {'count': 53} != {'count': 65}

================== 20 failed, 9 passed, 2 warnings in 21.50s ===================
```

Raw summaries after applying the fix, first the assistant suite and then the existing tokenization suite:

```text
======================= 29 passed, 2 warnings in 20.67s ========================
======================== 9 passed, 2 warnings in 18.79s ========================
```

Runtime: PyTorch `2.14.0`, Transformers `5.23.0`, Pydantic `2.12.0`, OpenAI SDK `2.44.0`, pytest `9.1.0`. The two pytest warnings are SWIG deprecations. CPU shutdown also emitted multiprocessing resource-tracker warnings; the fixture reported server termination and the launcher removed its temporary IPC directory.

</details>

The `cpu-reasoning-renderers` CI step selects this test file and uses the CPU test image. CI suitability was checked from repository configuration and through local CPU execution; the upstream Buildkite job has not yet run for this change. The HTTP fixture sets an explicit 256 MiB KV-cache budget with `--kv-cache-memory-bytes` and does not override environment variables.

The local runtime reused native CPU extensions from official build `615c9d6474a7793a024786e67fbb99791e809d98`; they were not rebuilt at the Python base commit. These checks establish prompt preservation, not generated-answer quality.

## Details

The replay test uses `exclude_none=True` because the default OpenAI SDK 2.44.0 dump includes `tool_calls: null`, which both request schemas reject at this revision. Removing just `tool_calls` allows the other null fields through validation. This schema limitation is separate from the refusal fallback and is not changed here.

The parser reads `content` but does not use a top-level `refusal` as a fallback. Request validation can also represent an empty content list as a truthy `ValidatorIterator`. When a non-empty refusal is present, materialize non-string content once, then use the existing refusal content-part parser if it is empty. This adds a shallow list allocation only on that refusal path; downstream parsing already traverses the content.

The production change is confined to `parse_chat_message_content()`. The Chat API documentation now describes the empty-content fallback and non-empty-content precedence, scoped to the Python frontend's HF renderer.

The end-to-end evidence covers the HF renderer. Native Mistral and Inkling construct prompts from the original messages rather than the normalized conversation, so this change does not establish refusal preservation in those prompts. Other renderer backends have not been validated end-to-end; Rust and Harmony paths are outside this change.

A duplicate search on 2026-11-16 found no overlapping open PR in the searched results. The closest changes, [#55479](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55479), [#49130](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49130), and [#64961](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64961), address Harmony or Responses conversion rather than this fallback.

AI assistance: Codex was used to prepare and validate this change.

I reviewed all changed lines and ran the tests above.

---
