commits.pr_title: [Quantization] Lower peak memory of online requantization, support block-FP8 to MXFP4
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Disclosure

AI assistance was used. The changes were reviewed and tested manually.

## Overview

Online requantization (a serialized checkpoint, e.g. NVFP4 / MXFP8 / block-FP8, converted to another format at load through `--quantization-config`) **allocated the serialized weights of the whole model on the device before converting them**, so the peak load memory was the serialized model plus the quantized model.

This PR now creates requantization source on the meta device and materializes them the layerwise loader one layer at a time, **a layer is requantization as soon as it is loaded.** This is the same mechanism bf16 online quantization already uses.

`Mistral-Large-4-1T-A52B` (FP8 block checkpoint, experts requantized to MXFP4, TP4):

| Configuration | Peak VRAM per GPU during load (1 Hz) | Model memory after loading |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Base commit fa6c77f5954ef22e705cd82456cc731ba67d0ae9, `VLLM_FP8_MOE_REQUANT=mxfp4`, `VLLM_FP8_MOE_REQUANT_ACT=a4w4` | 144.2 GiB | 135.73 GiB |
| Base commit fa6c77f5954ef22e705cd82456cc731ba67d0ae9 + `dequantize_weight` only (without the meta device changes in `requantization.py`), `--quantization-config.moe mxfp4` | 287.9 GiB (device capacity, no OOM) | 136.98 GiB |
| This PR, `--quantization-config.moe mxfp4` | 147.9 GiB | 135.75 GiB |

This PR also adds `dequantize_weight` to the FP8 MoE methods (block, per-tensor and per-channel scales):

- `Fp8MoEMethod`,
- `CompressedTensorsW8A8Fp8MoEMethod`,
- `QuarkW8A8Fp8MoEMethod`,

built on a shared `dequantize_fp8_moe_weights` helper, driven by the method's weight `QuantKey` (chunked to bound the fp32 staging memory).

Split from #67529.

Related: #67136 (CPU offloading with online quantization, reviewers asked for progressive quantization during loading) and #67290 (quantize MoE experts one at a time during loading for every online scheme). This PR bounds the peak of requantization sources to one layer; per-expert granularity is left to #67290.

## Claims

- Requantization sources stay on the meta device until their layer is fully loaded, so the load peak holds one serialized layer, not the whole serialized model. `test_online_quant_peak_mem[requantization]` fails on the base commit.
- Block-FP8 experts requantized to MXFP4 (AITER, a4w4) are byte-identical to online-quantizing the same dequantized bf16 experts. FP8 MoE `dequantize_weight` (block, per-tensor, per-channel) is bit-exact against a reference.
- A layer is now requantized as soon as its loaded element count reaches its size, so a loader that counts elements twice silently drops the layer's last tensors. Quark NVFP4 `w13_input_scale_2` did this and is now loaded per shard, like ModelOpt. For the same reason, FP8 checkpoints with static activation scales raise `NotImplementedError`.

**Behavior changes vs base:**
- A requantization source layer missing a checkpoint tensor raises a `ValueError` at the end of loading, instead of being requantized from zeros.
- Quark NVFP4 MoE: an expert's w13 input scale is `max(w1, w3)` instead of the w3 scale, also without requantization. Checkpoints with equal w1 / w3 scales are unaffected.
- `--quantization-config.moe mxfp4` is accepted for FP8 checkpoints with dynamic activation scales; only block scales are validated end to end.

Left to other PRs:
- [ ] Remove the `VLLM_FP8_MOE_REQUANT*` environment variables and `Fp8BlockExpertsAsMxfp4FusedMoE`, which this PR makes redundant (#67529).
- [ ] Support MXFP4 weights with MXFP8 or bf16 activations (a8w4 / a16w4) on `AITER_MXFP4_BF16`. This PR only covers MXFP4 activations (a4w4).
- [ ] Quantize requantized experts chunk by chunk for the FP8, INT8, NVFP4 and LUT targets as well. They still assemble the dequantized chunks into a full bf16 layer before quantizing it (#67290).
- [ ] Use FP32 as intermediary for online requantization. The FP8 and NVFP4 sources still dequantize to bf16, because some target kernels only accept 16-bit input (AITER MXFP4 falls back to emulation otherwise) and FP32 would double the full-layer staging of the targets above.

## Validation

### Unit tests

New / modified tests:

```bash
pytest -s -vvvvv tests/quantization/test_online.py \
  -k "dequantize_weight or configures_prequantized_moe or requantizes_block_fp8 or test_online_quant_peak_mem or online_prequantized or weight_loading_requantization or requantized_moe or test_online_quantization or removes_source_scales or requantization_source"
```

```text
142 passed, 6 skipped, 134 deselected, 16 warnings in 167.98s (0:02:47)
```

Related tests (the full `test_online.py` and other existing test files touching online quantization, MoE and requantization):

```bash
pytest -s -vvvvv \
  tests/quantization/test_online.py \
  tests/quantization/test_online_mxfp4.py \
  tests/quantization/test_online_shared_expert_fusion.py \
  tests/quantization/test_keep_param_objects.py \
  tests/quantization/test_gfx950_moe.py
```

```text
318 passed, 75 skipped, 16 warnings in 405.35s (0:06:45)
```

Without the `vllm/` changes, the new peak memory test fails:

```text
E       AssertionError: peak_memory_gib=1.09 higher than 1.0639999999999998
1 failed, 260 deselected, 16 warnings in 33.80s
```

Ran on MI355X (gfx950), ROCm (torch 2.13.0+rocm10.0.0), vLLM commit 7450cb3ac8 (the head of the PR) for the new / modified tests, 7e6b0e34ad for the related tests, b7e0405118 for the end-to-end runs (base fa6c77f5954ef22e705cd82456cc731ba67d0ae9).

### End-to-end tests

Mistral-Large-4-1T-A52B (FP8 block checkpoint), routed experts requantized to MXFP4 at load, TP4:

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 \
vllm serve mistralai/Mistral-Large-4-1T-A52B \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --tokenizer-mode mistral --config-format mistral --load-format mistral \
  --max-model-len 262144 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 128 \
  --quantization-config.moe mxfp4 \
  --reasoning-parser mistral
```

```text
(Worker_TP0) INFO [base_loader.py:164] Quantizing 71 layers of types: mlp.experts: 71 (from moe: mxfp4)
(Worker_TP0) INFO [base_loader.py:177] Online quantization as part of model loading took 1.98 seconds
(Worker_TP0) INFO [model_runner.py:449] Model loading took 135.75 GiB memory and 397.34 seconds
```

| Configuration | Peak VRAM per GPU during load (1 Hz) | Model memory after loading |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Base commit fa6c77f5954ef22e705cd82456cc731ba67d0ae9, `VLLM_FP8_MOE_REQUANT=mxfp4`, `VLLM_FP8_MOE_REQUANT_ACT=a4w4` | 144.2 GiB | 135.73 GiB |
| Base commit fa6c77f5954ef22e705cd82456cc731ba67d0ae9 + `dequantize_weight` only (without the meta device changes in `requantization.py`), `--quantization-config.moe mxfp4` | 287.9 GiB (device capacity, no OOM) | 136.98 GiB |
| This PR, `--quantization-config.moe mxfp4` | 147.9 GiB | 135.75 GiB |

The load time is dominated by a cold page cache (396 s weight read).

Without the `requantization.py` changes, the whole FP8 model is loaded on the device before requantization: the sampled VRAM sits at ~253 GiB for the load, then reaches the device capacity (~288 GiB) while experts are requantized (8 s, instead of 2 s), and loading only just succeeds. This is the memory overhead this PR removes.

**GSM8K is not an accuracy claim, only a check that nothing is obviously broken**: full GSM8K Platinum against each server (single repeat), with `lm-evaluation-harness` at https://github.com/fxmarty-amd/lm-evaluation-harness/tree/503ad16e088dc9dea08e29f6df76dbb26129941b. commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Accept NumPy images in vLLM's own HF processors
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

vLLM accepts NumPy arrays as images (`HfImageItem` in `vllm/multimodal/inputs.py` includes `np.ndarray`), and models that use an HF-hosted processor, like Qwen2-VL, handle them fine. The processors vLLM ships itself in `vllm/transformers_utils/processors/` assume a PIL image instead. They call `image.size`, `image.mode` or `image.width`, so the same image passed as a NumPy array fails the request:

```python
llm = LLM("OpenGVLab/InternVL3-1B", trust_remote_code=True, max_model_len=4096)
llm.generate({"prompt": prompt, "multi_modal_data": {"image": np.asarray(pil_image)}})
# ValueError: Failed to apply InternVLChatProcessor on data={'images': [array(...)]}
#   caused by TypeError: cannot unpack non-iterable int object
```

This PR converts the image with `transformers.image_transforms.to_pil_image` at the point where each of these processors first uses it. PIL images go through unchanged.

How I found it: I was checking how the multimodal processors handle the image types vLLM's parser accepts. I processed the same image as PIL and as `np.asarray` of it on several small VLMs. The models with HF-hosted processors (Qwen2-VL, SmolVLM, InternVL3-hf, Phi-3.5-vision, Aria, LLaVA-OneVision) handled the NumPy image fine, but most of the processors in `vllm/transformers_utils/processors/` failed on it. OpenVLA's was the one that worked. I then reproduced it end to end with `LLM.generate` on InternVL3-1B (table below).

Not a duplicate: I found no issue or open PR for this. #68367 also deals with NumPy images, but it's a different problem. It normalizes negative-stride arrays in the shared parser (`vllm/multimodal/parse.py`) and doesn't touch these processors.

## Claims

- InternVL, H2OVL, Llama Nemotron Nano VL, Nemotron Nano VL v2, Ovis2, Ovis2.5, DeepSeek-VL2, DeepSeek-OCR and Isaac now accept NumPy images, and they give the same prompt token ids and processed tensors as for the same image in PIL form.
- PIL inputs are unchanged. The per-model processing tests and the common processing correctness tests for these models still pass.

## Validation

The first revision added a test, `test_numpy_image_matches_pil`. It was dropped at review because it mostly exercises `to_pil_image`, which vLLM doesn't maintain. The processor changes are the same in the current head. The results below are from that first revision.

Commit `2a5a7db0e54a5679648e74eeb5f754129b9fac6c`, on top of main `a87e3a655`. RTX 4070 Laptop, WSL2 Ubuntu, Python 3.12, transformers 5.22.0. For the "main" runs I put main's versions of the changed processor files back on top of the same commit.

The test processed one random image as PIL and as `np.asarray` of it, and checked that both gave the same output:

```
pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_common.py -k test_numpy_image_matches_pil -v
```

<details>
<summary>main: 9 failed</summary>

```
test_numpy_image_matches_pil[AIDC-AI/Ovis2-1B] FAILED [ 11%]
test_numpy_image_matches_pil[AIDC-AI/Ovis2.5-2B] FAILED [ 22%]
test_numpy_image_matches_pil[OpenGVLab/InternVL3-1B] FAILED [ 33%]
test_numpy_image_matches_pil[PerceptronAI/Isaac-0.1] FAILED [ 44%]
test_numpy_image_matches_pil[deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-OCR] FAILED [ 55%]
test_numpy_image_matches_pil[deepseek-ai/deepseek-vl2-tiny] FAILED [ 66%]
test_numpy_image_matches_pil[h2oai/h2ovl-mississippi-800m] FAILED [ 77%]
test_numpy_image_matches_pil[nvidia/Llama-3.1-Nemotron-Nano-VL-8B-V1] FAILED [ 88%]
test_numpy_image_matches_pil[nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-Nano-12B-v2-VL-BF16] FAILED [100%]
```

The underlying errors:

```

E       TypeError: cannot unpack non-iterable int object                   # InternVL, H2OVL, DeepSeek-VL2, both Nemotron
E       AttributeError: 'numpy.ndarray' object has no attribute 'width'    # Isaac
E       TypeError: 'int' object is not subscriptable                       # DeepSeek-OCR
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>this PR: 9 passed</summary>

```
test_numpy_image_matches_pil[AIDC-AI/Ovis2-1B] PASSED [ 11%]
test_numpy_image_matches_pil[AIDC-AI/Ovis2.5-2B] PASSED [ 22%]

test_numpy_image_matches_pil[PerceptronAI/Isaac-0.1] PASSED [ 44%]

================ 9 passed, 551 deselected, 6 warnings in 27.82s ================
```

</details>

End to end with `LLM.generate` on `OpenGVLab/InternVL3-1B` (`max_model_len=4096`, `gpu_memory_utilization=0.6`, `enforce_eager=True`, `temperature=0`, `max_tokens=12`). The image is 448x448 with the left half red, and the prompt asks "What color is the left half of the image?". Both runs are on the commit above, the "main" one with main's `internvl.py`:

| image passed as | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| PIL | `'The left half of the image is red.'` | `'The left half of the image is red.'` |
| `np.ndarray` (same pixels) | `ValueError: Failed to apply InternVLChatProcessor ...`, caused by `TypeError: cannot unpack non-iterable int object` | `'The left half of the image is red.'` |

<details>
<summary>Reproducer script</summary>

```python
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image

from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams


def main() -> None:
    llm = LLM(model="OpenGVLab/InternVL3-1B", trust_remote_code=True,
              max_model_len=4096, gpu_memory_utilization=0.6,
              limit_mm_per_prompt={"image": 1}, enforce_eager=True)
    arr = np.zeros((448, 448, 3), dtype=np.uint8)
    arr[:, :224] = (255, 0, 0)
    prompt = ("<|im_start|>user\n<image>\nWhat color is the left half of the image?"
              "<|im_end|>\n<|im_start|>assistant\n")
    params = SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=12)
    for name, img in [("PIL", Image.fromarray(arr)), ("numpy", arr)]:
        out = llm.generate({"prompt": prompt, "multi_modal_data": {"image": img}}, params)
        print(name, out[0].outputs[0].text)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

</details>

Existing tests, on the same processor code:

- `pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_internvl.py tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_h2ovl.py tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_nemotron_vl.py tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_deepseek_vl2.py tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_deepseek_ocr.py`: `513 passed, 101 warnings in 283.45s (0:04:43)`
- `pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_common.py -k "test_processing_correctness and (InternVL3-1B or h2ovl or Ovis2 or deepseek or Isaac or Nemotron-Nano)"`: `51 passed, 3 skipped, 506 deselected, 15 warnings in 113.98s (0:01:53)`
- `pre-commit run --files` on the changed files: all hooks pass.

## Details

The parser passes images to the HF processor as it gets them, so a NumPy image from the user reaches the processor as a NumPy array. These processors were ported from model repos whose code only ever got PIL images. The common processing test builds its images with `random_image`, which returns PIL, so CI never sent them an array.

Why not just tell users to pass PIL: the image type, the parser and earlier fixes all treat NumPy images as supported. #45057 fixed `ImageProcessorItems.get_image_size` for HWC NumPy images, noting that InternVL and H2OVL size their placeholders with it. And `OvisProcessor`'s own docstring lists `np.ndarray` as an accepted image type. Models with HF-hosted processors already accept arrays, so today whether a NumPy image works depends on where the model's processor happens to live.

I convert inside each of these processors instead of turning every image into PIL in the parser, so HF-hosted processors keep getting the arrays they already handle. `to_pil_image` is the existing transformers helper. It deals with HWC and CHW layouts and returns PIL images as they are. In `internvl.py` the change is in `InternVLChatImageProcessor.__call__`, which the H2OVL and Llama Nemotron Nano VL processors inherit.

3-D `torch.Tensor` images are out of scope, since the parser treats those as image embeddings.

I found this with Claude Code. It wrote the comparison script, the fix and the test, and ran the tests above on my machine. I reproduced the `LLM.generate` failure on InternVL3-1B myself, and I went through every changed line.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Kimi-K3: don't bake the fused decode MLA path into PIECEWISE graphs
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

On ROCm, Kimi-K3 bakes the decode-only fused MLA path into PIECEWISE CUDA graphs at capture time, so every later replay runs decode kernels on prefill/mixed tokens; with `max_cudagraph_capture_size=1024` the first request crashes or hangs. This PR skips the fused path inside PIECEWISE graphs and warms the skinny-GEMM workspace in `allocate_kv_cache` for every KV cache allocation path, which the unfused path then needs before capture.

No existing PR covers this (searched open PRs for "kimi k3 piecewise", "fused decode cudagraph", "aiter_mla piecewise", "wvSplitKrc", "kimi k3 cudagraph" on 2026-11-09).

## Claims

- Kimi-K3 (AITER MLA, TP8, MI355X/MI350X) at `max_cudagraph_capture_size=1024`: main crashes or hangs on its first request; this PR serves correctly.

## Validation

Kimi-K3, TP8 on 8x MI350X (gfx950), same image for every leg of sections 1 and 2: `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-be47189f37f6162991366ff6b91539f6e9d1f432`. This PR applied over the nightly image by bind-mounting the two changed files (`vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/mla.py`, `vllm/v1/worker/utils.py`) into the container; main is the same image with those two files left stock.

### 1. Main vs. this PR, same image, same flags

Server command (identical on both sides; only whether the two fix files are bind-mounted differ):

<details>
<summary>serve command + env</summary>

```
docker run --rm \
  --device /dev/kfd --device /dev/dri --group-add video --ipc host --network host \
  --security-opt seccomp=unconfined --shm-size 128g \
  -v /mnt/data/hf/hub:/root/.cache/huggingface/hub \
  -e HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 \
  -e VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 -e VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 -e VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MLA=1 \
  -e VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_SITUV2=1 -e SAFETENSORS_FAST_GPU=1 \
  -e VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 \
  vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-be47189f37f6162991366ff6b91539f6e9d1f432 \
  vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 --served-model-name moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 8 --trust-remote-code --max-model-len 131072 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 \
    --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 --no-enable-prefix-caching --async-scheduling \
    --max-cudagraph-capture-size 1024 --port 8000 \
    --compilation-config '{"mode":3,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE","custom_ops":["+fused_rms_norm_gated"]}' \
    --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 1}' --mm-processor-cache-gb 0 --reasoning-parser kimi_k3 --tool-call-parser kimi_k3
```

main uses the same command and env, with the stock `mla.py`/`utils.py` from the image (no bind mounts).
</details>

Canary request (sent once the server reports ready):

```
curl -sf localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"moonshotai/Kimi-K3","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say hi."}],"max_tokens":8}'
```

| Build | Canary request at capture size 1024 (1 start each) |
|---|---|
| main, same image | fails: engine crashes handling the canary request (see tail below), HTTP 500 |
| this PR (75a5a2581a), same image | succeeds; full `vllm bench serve` sweep below completes |

Tail of the main error:

```
(EngineCore pid=962) ERROR 11-12 09:41:07 [core.py:1781] EngineCore encountered a fatal error.
(EngineCore pid=962) ERROR 11-12 09:41:07 [core.py:1781] Traceback (most recent call last):
...
(EngineCore pid=962) ERROR 11-12 09:41:07 [core.py:1781]   File ".../vllm/distributed/device_communicators/shm_broadcast.py", line 874, in _wait_until_readable
(EngineCore pid=962) ERROR 11-12 09:41:07 [core.py:1781]     raise RuntimeError("cancelled")
(EngineCore pid=962) ERROR 11-12 09:41:07 [core.py:1781] RuntimeError: cancelled
(APIServer pid=28) ERROR 11-12 09:41:07 [async_llm.py:962] vllm.v1.engine.exceptions.EngineDeadError: EngineCore encountered an issue. See stack trace (above) for the root cause.
INFO:     127.0.0.1:57500 - "POST /v1/chat/completions HTTP/1.1" 500 Internal Server Error
```

(This IPC teardown masks the worker-side failure, a GPU memory fault at the first request after capture completed. The wvSplitKrc workspace failure during capture is what happens with only the mla.py change applied; see the isolated trace in section 2.)

Log line showing PIECEWISE graphs were captured on this PR (one line per TP rank):
```
(Worker_TP6 pid=1240) INFO 11-12 11:00:19 [model_runner.py:1231] Graph capturing finished in 67 secs, took 16.27 GiB
```

(All 8 ranks report the same, 67 secs and 16.27 GiB each; capture reaches `Capturing CUDA graphs (PIECEWISE): 100%|██████████| 83/83` before this.)

### 2. The reproduction needs the warmup move

This reproduction takes the extensible KV cache path: `enable_extensible_kv_cache` defaults to on whenever the platform supports it and no KV connector forces it off (`vllm/config/vllm.py`'s `_resolve_extensible_kv_cache`), and our server command passes no `--kv-transfer-config`, so on ROCm it's on by default here. That's the path whose `allocate` callable bypasses `_allocate_kv_cache_buffer` and, pre-PR, skipped the warmup entirely. On main (and on the `mla.py`-change-only variant below) the KV cache itself still initializes (log below), but on the extensible path the warmup in _allocate_kv_cache_buffer never runs, because the path passes its own allocate:

```
[utils.py:426] Using LBNHC KV cache layout.
[gpu_worker.py:810] Available KV cache memory: 76.87 GiB
```

With only the `mla.py` hunk applied (`not in_piecewise_cudagraph()` added to the fused-decode condition, **no** `utils.py` change — same image, same flags, `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1`), PIECEWISE capture proceeds past KV-cache init and fails partway through capture itself, exactly in `wvSplitKrc`:

```
Capturing CUDA graphs (PIECEWISE):  92%|█████████▏| 76/83 [00:28<00:02,  2.69it/s]
...
(Worker_TP0 pid=1233) ERROR 11-12 12:06:48 [multiproc_executor.py:1223]   File ".../vllm/model_executor/layers/utils.py", line 514, in rocm_unquantized_gemm_impl
(Worker_TP0 pid=1233) ERROR 11-12 12:06:48 [multiproc_executor.py:1223]     return ops.wvSplitKrc(x_view, weight, cu_count, bias)
(Worker_TP0 pid=1233) ERROR 11-12 12:06:48 [multiproc_executor.py:1223] RuntimeError: wvSplitKrc: the split-K workspace pool cannot be allocated during graph capture. Call warmup_rocm_skinny_gemm_workspaces() (vllm/model_executor/layers/utils.py) eagerly first.
```

The server never reaches readiness (crash happens inside engine-core init, before the API server can accept the canary request). This confirms the `mla.py` change alone is not sufficient: once the fused decode path is skipped inside PIECEWISE graphs, the unfused `q_b_proj` GEMM becomes the first `wvSplitKrc` caller during capture, and its split-K workspace pool cannot be created mid-capture — it must be warmed up eagerly beforehand, which is exactly what moving the warmup into `allocate_kv_cache` (the `utils.py` change) does. With both files applied (this PR), the same code path captures all 83 PIECEWISE graphs cleanly (see section 1 above).


### 3. GSM8K accuracy

Image: `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-be47189f37f6162991366ff6b91539f6e9d1f432`, the same for every row below. This PR, applied by bind-mounting the two changed files over the image; main is the stock image. Server flags as in section 1, plus the recipe's `--max-num-seqs 128` and `--cudagraph-metrics`.

GSM8K with `lm_eval` 0.4.13 (`local-completions`), all 1319 problems, `--num_fewshot 20`, `num_concurrent=256`, one run per row.

| Build | `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH`, `cudagraph_mode` | strict-match | flexible-extract |
|---|---|---|---|
| main (recipe setting) | `0`, `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` | 0.9613 ± 0.0053 | 0.9613 ± 0.0053 |
| this PR | `1`, `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` | 0.9613 ± 0.0053 | 0.9613 ± 0.0053 |
| this PR | `0`, `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` | 0.9659 ± 0.0050 | 0.9659 ± 0.0050 |

<details>
<summary>lm_eval command</summary>

```
lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 20 \
  --model_args model=moonshotai/Kimi-K3,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=256,max_retries=3,timeout=1200,tokenized_requests=False,trust_remote_code=True
```
</details>

With `--max-num-seqs 128` and 256 concurrent requests, prefill and decode tokens mix in the same batches. The `--cudagraph-metrics` stats of the `=1` run show such batches replaying PIECEWISE graphs (e.g. 844 tokens padded to 848, 358 to 368, 91 to 96), while FULL graphs served only decode batches of at most 128 tokens; the `=0` runs show no PIECEWISE batches. Generated text differs for about two thirds of the problems between any two runs (865/1319 for main `=0` vs this PR `=1`, 876/1319 for main `=0` vs this PR `=0`, which use the same graph mode), so this is run-to-run nondeterminism, not an effect of the PR's path. Between main `=0` and this PR `=1`, 25 problems are right only on main and 25 only on the PR; all score differences are within one standard error. This is also the baseline for the recipe follow-up.

---

### Throughput comparison

Same image as sections 1 and 2: `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-be47189f37f6162991366ff6b91539f6e9d1f432`. Comparison with the Kimi-K3 recipe's ROCm setting (`VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0`, `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`, no PIECEWISE graphs) on main, against this PR with `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1` and `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`. Both sides use the recipe's `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 --max-num-batched-tokens 4096` and `--max-cudagraph-capture-size 1024`; 2 server starts each, interleaved (mean). `vllm bench serve --backend vllm --dataset-name random --random-output-len 256 --ignore-eos --request-rate inf --num-warmups 4 --seed 7`, with `--num-prompts` 32, 128, 256 and 96 for the four rows. Throughput is total tokens per second.

| Input len, concurrency | Throughput (tok/s), recipe `=0` on main / this PR `=1` | Mean TTFT (ms) | Mean TPOT (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1024, 4 | 1130 / 1165 | 385 / 285 | 16.3 / 16.1 |
| 1024, 16 | 3292 / 3295 | 640 / 642 | 21.9 / 21.8 |
| 1024, 64 | 7447 / 7528 | 1159 / 1143 | 38.4 / 38.0 |
| 4096, 16 | 7789 / 7916 | 1166 / 1147 | 30.4 / 29.9 |

0 failed requests on either side. The PR legs ran mla.py and utils.py as of f8867da8b1. The PR's own changes to both files are unchanged in the current head; the merge of main since then only changed unrelated parts of utils.py.

### Unittests

<details>
<summary>Unit tests on GPU (1x MI350X, nightly be47189f): all pass with this PR; the stock image fails the fix-specific cases</summary>

Run at commit `75a5a2581a` (PR head `60692599d4` + the test commit), image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-be47189f37f6162991366ff6b91539f6e9d1f432` (vllm `0.34.0rc1.dev302+gbe47189f3`, torch `2.13.0+rocm10.0.0`), 1 GPU (AMD Instinct MI350X, gfx950). The repo's `tests/` tree and `tests/conftest.py` were mounted into the image, `tblib` (needed by that conftest) was pip-installed. Pytest warnings are omitted.

**With this PR** (the two changed files `vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/mla.py` and `vllm/v1/worker/utils.py` bind-mounted over the image):

```
$ pytest tests/v1/worker/test_extensible_kv_cache.py::test_allocate_kv_cache_warms_up_wvsplitkrc_before_backing
collected 4 items

tests/v1/worker/test_extensible_kv_cache.py::test_allocate_kv_cache_warms_up_wvsplitkrc_before_backing[default-rocm] PASSED [ 25%]
```

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Quantization] Remove the Qwen3.5 MTP draft quantization workaround
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

The Qwen3.5 MTP drafter nulled `vllm_config.quant_config` while building its decoder layers whenever the checkpoint's `dynamic` had a `-:` rule mentioning `mtp` (#48816). #49539 is the centralized fix: AutoGPTQ reads those rules where it picks a layer's method, and `moe_wna16` does too after #67413. The block is dead code and is removed from both copies of the drafter.

## Claims

- build the draft from the checkpoint's own quantization rules instead of blanking the shared config, which was only restored on the success path.

## Validation

```
HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4 \
  --served-model-name qwen35 --port 8031 --max-model-len 8192 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.55 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":2}'
```

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| target / draft load | `7.33 s` / `0.52 s` | `7.24 s` / `0.39 s` |
| 16 greedy completions | sha256 `94c0ff955fcb9151` | identical |
| `mtp.*` WNA16 fallback warnings | 0 | 0 |
| `SpecDecoding metrics` | 83-94% per window | 82-100% per window |
| forced `--quantization moe_wna16` | loads (the block covers it) | loads with #67413; without it `AttributeError: ... no parameter 'w2_weight'` |

```
pytest tests/quantization/test_auto_gptq.py -k "not test_auto_gptq_quantization_method"   # 12 passed, 1 deselected
```

The added test passes on main too: the draft is unquantized either way, so the removal is not observable at that seam. It pins the linear `-:` contract the removal relies on, which had no coverage. CI: `tests/quantization/test_auto_gptq.py` is not selected by an active step - the directory-wide `pytest -v -s quantization/` run is commented out since #63608 and the remaining quantization steps name specific files - so it was run locally on a GPU host.

## Details

The block was the model-level fix for "a GPTQ checkpoint that stores its MTP head in BF16", a class of bug that belongs in the quantization config. #49539 moved it there: the `RoutedExperts` branch of `AutoGPTQConfig.get_quant_method()` now reads the negative `dynamic` rules and `modules_in_block_to_quantize`, ahead of the Marlin/WNA16 split, so every module the block covered resolves per module, and linears already did through `get_linear_quant_method`.

Depends on #67413 (the forced `--quantization moe_wna16` path keeps working because of it).

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Scope block reuse fences to the source pool
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Prevent a HiSparse host-pool block ID from being mistaken for reuse of a pending device-pool block by the KV offloading scheduler.

## Claims

- Allocations from a separate pool no longer add an unrelated pending offload store to `jobs_to_flush`.
- Reuse in any group sharing the offloaded source pool still flushes the pending store before reuse.
- Regression coverage exercises the real core scheduler and CPU offloading manager with synchronous and asynchronous scheduling.

## Validation

- Negative control on the current `main` scheduler code: the new regression fails because `jobs_to_flush` contains the pending store (`{0}`) after a host-pool block with the same numeric ID is allocated.
- Focused regression: `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 "$VENV/bin/python" -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py -k hisparse_host_block_id_does_not_flush_gpu_store -xq` — 2 passed with the fix.
- Full scheduler suite: `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 "$VENV/bin/python" -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py -xq` — 541 passed, 16 warnings.
- `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `git diff --check`, and commit hooks passed.
- No model evaluation applies because this changes scheduler bookkeeping, not model computation or outputs.

## Details

Block IDs are local to a pool. HiSparse keeps its source KV in a dedicated host pool, while the generic offloading path stores the indexer group from the shared device pool. In a `MultiConnector` setup, allocation callbacks can reach OffloadingConnector even when another connector handles the request. A host-pool block can therefore have the same integer ID as a device block with a pending store; the scheduler previously treated that numeric match as physical block reuse and added the unrelated store to `jobs_to_flush`.

The scheduler now derives fence candidates from the pool used by OffloadingConnector's configured source groups. It tracks every group sharing that pool, while excluding allocations from separate pools. This preserves genuine device-pool reuse fences without checking HiSparse connector or manager classes. No public API or configuration changes.

This is separate from [PR #47046](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47046) and its related open draft [PR #46960](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46960), which address recording allocations from zero-token MultiConnector callbacks. This change handles false matches across pools after those allocations are recorded. It is also separate from [PR #67084](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/67084), which bounds synthetic block IDs used during GPU warmup rather than runtime offloading fences.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Normalize negative-stride image inputs
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Make valid NumPy image views with negative strides work in vLLM's multimodal input path. The parser normalizes only negative-stride arrays before passing them to Hugging Face image processors.

## Claims

- Fixes failures for valid image views such as flipped images, which PyTorch cannot convert to tensors while they have negative strides.
- Preserves pixel values and passes positive-stride arrays through without copying.
- This is a focused compatibility fix; it does not claim to improve model accuracy.

## Validation

- `python -m pytest tests/multimodal/test_parse.py -q -k 'negative_strides or positive_stride'` — 4 passed, using the current worktree on `PYTHONPATH` with an existing vLLM development environment.
- Applicable pre-commit hooks passed, including Ruff, test tethering, and docstring checks; `git diff --check` passed.
- The full parser test file was attempted, but the reused local PyTorch environment segfaulted during test cleanup in `torch.accelerator.memory.empty_host_cache`. The full-file result is unavailable in this environment.

## Details

NumPy operations such as `np.flip` can produce image views with negative strides. The parser previously passed these arrays directly to Hugging Face image processors, where conversion to a PyTorch tensor failed. The parser now makes only negative-stride arrays contiguous, preserving their values while avoiding copies for positive-stride inputs. The redundant Qwen2-VL model-level test was removed following review because the parser tests cover this behavior.

No existing open PR addressing negative-stride multimodal image inputs was found during the duplicate-work check.

AI assistance was used, and I reviewed all the changes and tests.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf][DSv4.1] Pack the decode sparse-MLA ragged top-k in one launch from the MXFP4 indexer's row bounds
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

On gfx950 with the MXFP4 sparse indexer and no `--monokernel`, every DeepSeek-V4.1 index layer converts its decode top-k into the ragged form sparse MLA reads: global slot ids, indptr and lengths. Main builds it in 4 launches per index layer: a count kernel, a zero fill, a cumsum and a pack. This PR builds it in 1. Each row's length is `min(topk, row_len)`, where `row_len` is the bound the indexer's top-k already ran over, so the count and the scan are not needed.

Over the 8 index layers this removes 24 of the 32 launches per decode step, with identical output. It runs on the layouts that decode without `--monokernel`: DEP8 (C128 and up), 2x TP4+EP4 (C64), and TP2 steps of more than 48 rows (C32).

Since #66047, a TP>1 decode step of 64 or more rows narrows the indexer's `decode_row_lens` to the rank's own shard. The PR therefore keeps the whole step's bounds in `decode_step_row_lens`, set before the narrowing. Every rank's top-k rows are all-gathered before the pack runs, so the bounds of the whole step are the right ones.

Part of a series that trims the DSv4.1 sparse-indexer launch overhead on MI355X, after #63888: #67363, #67364, #67366, #67367 and #67368. This PR is independent of the others.

## Performance vs main

Setup:
- Base: stock `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-60bd6dd2`, AITER 0.1.29. Every file this PR touches, and the indexer ops it reads, is identical to main 2c1fc9b3d3 (this PR's base). The md5s inside the containers matched.
- This PR: the same image with the PR's two Python files mounted over it.
- Hardware and model: MI355X, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DSpark k=6.

| Measure | main | this PR | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ragged top-k launches per decode step (torch profiler, TP4+EP4 and DEP8 serving) | 32 | 8 | **-24** |
| Ragged top-k time per decode step, isolated in a HIP graph (7-1024 rows) | 64.0-79.3 us | 16.8-32.5 us | **-47 to -52 us (-59% to -74%)** |
| Decode step, 2x TP4+EP4, 32 requests per replica (median ITL, 6 paired rounds) | 15.799 ms | 15.760 ms | **-0.039 ms (-0.25%)**, 95% CI ±0.058 ms |
| Output throughput, same runs | 4,072 tok/s | 4,076 tok/s | +0.10%, 95% CI ±0.40% |

The microbenchmark predicts about -49 us at 224 rows, which is -0.31% of a 15.8 ms step. The end-to-end delta is consistent with that, but 6 rounds do not resolve it from zero.

**Per decode step, isolated** (8 builds: 3 at compress ratio 2 and 5 at ratio 1).
- Method: graphs of 10 steps, median of 2000 replays, ABBA over 5 rounds, mean of 2 independent processes.
- Rows are DSpark requests of 7 rows plus invalid padding rows, with contexts of 4K-128K and top-k 512.
- Both paths produced identical lengths, indptr and slot ids in every case.

| decode rows | main (us) | this PR (us) | change (us) | launches |

**End to end.** Client: `vllm bench serve`, random 8192 in / 1024 out, `--ignore-eos`, 3 reps after a warmup. DSpark k=6 with synthetic acceptance 3.8 and adaptive verification (measured AL 3.41 at TP4 and 3.75 at DEP8, the same in both arms). Server flags are the production C64 and C128 recipes on the stock image, without their local patches. 0 failed requests and 0 server errors.

| 2x (TP4+EP4), 32 requests per replica, 224 decode rows per step | 6 rounds, the two arms side by side on the two GPU halves, halves swapped every round | 15.799 ms | 15.760 ms | -0.039 ms (-0.25%), 95% CI ±0.058 ms (±0.045 placement-balanced) |
| DEP8 (DP8 x TP1, EP8), 128 requests, 112 rows per rank | ABBA, 2+2 servers | 23.861 ms | 23.709 ms | -0.152 ms (-0.64%), server-level 95% CI ±1.03 ms |

The PR traces contain only the new kernel: 1280 launches at TP4 and 2560 at DEP8, and none of main's 4. So no step fell back, including the TP4 steps of more than 64 rows that #66047 shards.

## Long-context accuracy

The output is identical by construction. These runs show that on long contexts, where the sparse top-k decides what each query attends to, accuracy matches main.

Setup:

- Serving: DSpark k=6 with real block acceptance and adaptive verification, the production setting.
- Calibration: greedy outputs are not run-to-run deterministic on this stack. The same server repeats only 50-54% of its outputs verbatim. So each comparison has a main-vs-main (A/A) row for the expected churn.

| Layout | Comparison | main | this PR | main-only / PR-only correct | McNemar p |

| 2x TP4+EP4, 16 requests per server | main vs PR | 0.652 | 0.667 | 26 / 33 | 0.44 |

By length (accuracy over the 160 prompts of each length):

|---|---|---|---|

- Acceptance length, eval requests only: TP4 4.077 (main) vs 4.017 (PR) vs 4.032 (main A/A); DEP8 3.981 vs 3.987.
- The 64K TP-shard-path dip (16 / 8 discordant, p 0.15) is within that regime's A/A at 64K (17 / 13).

## Claims

- **24 fewer launches per decode step** (32 -> 8) on every decode step of up to 1024 rows that runs without `--monokernel`, including TP>1 steps that #66047 shards. Measured in serving profiles at TP4+EP4 and DEP8.
- **-47 to -52 us per decode step** for the ragged top-k (measured, 7-1024 rows). End to end that is about -0.3% of the decode step. The measured TP4+EP4 delta is -0.25%, with a 95% CI of ±0.37%.
- **Identical output.** Lengths, indptr and slot ids equal main's 4-launch path for every row class production produces. Long-context accuracy and acceptance length match main within run-to-run churn.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Kernel] Pass packed rows to the sm90 FlashInfer FP8 block-scale GEMM
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes wrong results from the SM90 FlashInfer FP8 block-scale GEMM (`flashinfer.gemm.fp8_blockscale_gemm_sm90`) when the activation is not row-contiguous. The kernel binding takes only a data pointer and assumes rows of exactly K elements, but the dynamic FP8 block-scaled linear kernel forwards every M < 32 batch as-is, so a strided input (e.g. a column slice) is read from the wrong memory for every row after the first. The fix passes packed (contiguous) rows in both wrappers and adds a regression test.

## Claims

- **Bugfix:** the sm90 FlashInfer FP8 block-scale GEMM no longer misreads strided activations. Previously, rows 1..M-1 of a non-contiguous input were computed from the wrong memory; they now match the packed-row result bit-exactly.
- **Scope:** only the small-batch (M < 32) FlashInfer path is affected; M >= 32 already goes through DeepGEMM, which honours strides. Already-contiguous inputs are untouched (`Tensor.contiguous()` is a no-op), so there is no overhead in the common case and no host synchronization is added.

## Validation

- New regression test `test_flashinfer_fp8_blockscale_gemm_strided_input` in `tests/kernels/quantization/test_block_fp8.py` (parametrized over M in {2, 31}): feeds the wrapper a column slice whose row stride is larger than K and asserts the result is bit-exact against the packed copy. It executes on SM90 + FlashInfer and skips elsewhere.
- `pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_block_fp8.py -k "strided_input or flashinfer"`: validated on an H200 by the original author — 42 passed, 5 skipped. This PR's environment has no CUDA device, so the module skips here; the new test needs an SM90 machine (or the relevant CI job) to execute.
- Wrapper semantics additionally smoke-tested on CPU with a stubbed kernel binding: a strided input reaches the kernel packed with identical values, and a contiguous input passes through without a copy.
- `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, and the full pre-commit hook set (including mypy and the test-tethering check) pass on the changed files.

## Details

**Root cause.** `flashinfer_fp8_blockscale_gemm` wraps `flashinfer.gemm.fp8_blockscale_gemm_sm90`, whose SM90 kernel takes only a data pointer and assumes packed rows of K elements. `_flashinfer_fp8_blockscale_gemm_impl` and the swapAB branch of `_dynamic_flashinfer_deepgemm_blockscale_gemm_impl` forwarded the activation unchanged, so a non-contiguous input (row stride > K) was misread from row 1 onward. Any Hopper caller that hands this path a non-contiguous FP8 block-scaled activation with M < 32 is affected — e.g. a row-parallel input projection that passes column slices of an `[M, hidden]` tensor, as some speculative-decoding drafters do.

**Fix.** Call `input.contiguous()` before the kernel in both wrappers. The copy happens only when the input is actually strided; packed inputs pass through unchanged.

**Trade-offs / limitations.** The copy is at most M x K bf16 elements on the M < 32 path (a few hundred KB at most), one small D2D copy per call, only for strided inputs. No model-level evaluation was run for this PR (no GPU in this environment); this is a correctness fix on a narrow kernel path, covered by the bit-exact unit test. End-to-end validation on Hopper with an affected configuration is welcome as a follow-up.

**Not a duplicate.** Searched open PRs for `fp8_blockscale_gemm`, strided/packed-row fixes, and related kernel bugfixes — none cover this.

**Credits.** The fix was originally authored by Cyprien Courtot (co-author on the commit).

**AI assistance** was used during the creation of this PR (porting the change and drafting this description).

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] LFM2-VL: honor do_image_splitting and use_thumbnail
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

LFM2-VL computes its image placeholders without looking at the `do_image_splitting` and `use_thumbnail` processor kwargs, while the HF processor that produces the image features does. Passing either one (`mm_processor_kwargs` at init or per request) gives a placeholder count that does not match the features, and the engine core dies. This makes vLLM's placeholder layout follow the same kwargs as the HF processor.

## Claims

- With `do_image_splitting=False` or `use_thumbnail=False`, LFM2-VL requests now run instead of killing the engine, and the prompt token ids are identical to the HF processor's `input_ids`.
- Default kwargs and the kwargs that already worked (`min_tiles`/`max_tiles`, etc.) produce the same placeholders as before.

## Validation

End to end with `LiquidAI/LFM2-VL-450M` on one RTX 5090 (`LLM.chat(..., mm_processor_kwargs=kw)`, one 1024x768 image, `temperature=0`, `max_tokens=24`, a fresh process per kwargs set), compared with HF `AutoModelForImageTextToText` + `AutoProcessor(**kw)` (transformers 5.22.2):

| `mm_processor_kwargs` | HF prompt len | main | this PR: prompt len | this PR: text vs HF |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `{}` | 1793 | 1793 | 1793 | identical |
| `{"do_image_splitting": false}` | 250 | `EngineDeadError` | 250 | same up to the last few tokens (`The pattern is` vs `The pattern consists`) |
| `{"use_thumbnail": false}` | 1558 | `EngineDeadError` | 1558 | identical |
| `{"min_tiles": 2, "max_tiles": 4}` | 1279 | 1279 | 1279 | identical |

Root error on main for `do_image_splitting=False`:

```
ValueError: Attempted to assign 234 = 234 multimodal tokens to 1770 placeholders
```

New processing test, which compares vLLM's prompt token ids with the HF processor's `input_ids` and checks the image token count (kwargs at init and per request, 1 and 2 images):

```
$ pytest -q tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_lfm2_vl.py

# main (vllm/model_executor/models/lfm2_vl.py from 865cf8c1f)
FAILED ...test_processor_override[True-1-mm_processor_kwargs1-234-LiquidAI/LFM2-VL-450M]
FAILED ...test_processor_override[True-1-mm_processor_kwargs2-1536-LiquidAI/LFM2-VL-450M]
... (the same two kwargs sets, for 2 images and kwargs per request)
E       assert [1, 6, 6423, ...498, 397, ...] == [1, 6, 6423, ...498, 396, ...]
E       IndexError: index -1 is out of bounds for dimension 0 with size 0
8 failed, 8 passed

# this PR
16 passed
```

`pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_common.py -k LFM2-VL`: 3 passed. The ruff (check/format), mypy, typos, SPDX and test-tethering hooks pass on the changed files.

CI: the new test is under `tests/models/multimodal/processing`, which the CPU `Multimodal Processing` step in `.buildkite/test_areas/models_multimodal.yaml` runs.

## Details

Root cause: `Lfm2VLProcessingInfo._get_image_feature_grid_size` decides whether to tile only from `min_tiles`/`max_tiles`, and always adds a thumbnail patch when the image is tiled; `get_image_repl` appends the thumbnail placeholder whenever `num_thumbnail_tokens > 0`. The HF `Lfm2VlImageProcessor` sets `min_tiles = max_tiles = 1` when `do_image_splitting=False` and only adds the thumbnail when `use_thumbnail=True`, so with either kwarg vLLM asked for 1770 placeholders (tiles + thumbnail) for features of a single 234-token image, or for a thumbnail that was never produced.

Fix, in `vllm/model_executor/models/lfm2_vl.py` only (+6/−3): read both kwargs from the merged mm kwargs with the image processor's defaults, turn tiling off the same way HF does, count the thumbnail only when `use_thumbnail` is set, and let `get_image_repl` append the thumbnail placeholder only when `_get_image_feature_grid_size` counted one. `get_num_patches` (used for `num_patches` when splitting `pixel_values` per image) goes through the same function, so it stays consistent with the placeholders.

Test: `tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_lfm2_vl.py`, following `test_smolvlm.py` / `test_idefics3.py`, which cover the same kind of kwargs for those models. The engine crash comes from the placeholder count, which this test checks against the HF processor directly on CPU; the end-to-end run above was done outside CI.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][Parser] Skip per-tick conversion of non-JSON DeepSeek DSML argument values
commits.pr_body:
## Overview DeepSeek V3.2, V4, and V4.1 reconvert a whole `string="false"` or attribute-less tool argument on every `">` chunk when the value is markup rather than JSON. That is quadratic, and non-streaming `parse()` runs it on the API server event loop. This holds the open value until its closing tag instead, including when the markup is the first or only parameter. Fixes the markup case of #67988. ## Claims - A 50k-character HTML `content` argument drops from about 18 s to 0.16 s in non-streaming `parse()`, for both `string="false"` and a missing `string` attribute (`path` first). - The same argument as the only parameter drops from 1,901 conversions and 3.6 s to 5 conversions and about 0.1 s at 31k characters. - Parsed arguments are unchanged, including streaming. Values that can start JSON (`{`, `[`, `"`, a number, `true`, `false`, `null`) still go through the full converter. ## Validation CPU only, Python 3.12, no model weights. Base is `9929e84fd5`. Tests run on the branch at `7ce9ee15d7`. New tests on the commit before the engine hook (`ff5b6cfe20`), where the content-only tests were added: ```text $ .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v4.py -k NonStringArgValue -q FAILED ...::test_markup_only_parameter_non_streaming[false] FAILED ...::test_markup_only_parameter_non_streaming[absent] FAILED ...::test_markup_only_parameter_streaming[false] FAILED ...::test_markup_only_parameter_streaming[absent] 4 failed, 4 passed ``` On `7ce9ee15d7`, all 8 `NonStringArgValue` tests pass. `test_deepseek_v4.py`, `test_deepseek_v41.py`, and `test_deepseek_v32.py` pass (169). Parser timing, `DeepSeekV4Parser.parse()`, `write_file` with `content` as the only parameter and the value `
title
` repeated: | case | chars | base | `ff5b6cfe20` | `7ce9ee15d7` | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | `string="false"`, content only | 31,000 | 3.600 s (1,901 conversions) | 3.571 s (1,901 conversions) | 0.097 s (5 conversions) | | `string="false"`, `path` first | 50,000 | 18.019 s | 0.161 s | 0.166 s | | omitted attribute, `path` first | 50,000 | 18.043 s | 0.162 s | 0.163 s | Differential checks: - 720 cases (path first): V4 and V4.1, three tool schema settings, 20 values, three attribute forms, repeated parameter; `parse()` and streaming at chunk sizes 1, 5, 13, and whole text. Identical to base after normalizing random `chatcmpl-tool-` IDs, on `7ce9ee15d7`. - 360 cases (content only): same matrix without `path`. Identical between base, `ff5b6cfe20`, and `7ce9ee15d7`. - Qwen3: streaming vs `parse()` for six values, both parameter orders, chunk sizes 1, 7, and whole text. 0 mismatches with and without the engine hook. - GLM-4.7: same comparison, 42 cases, 0 mismatches with and without the engine hook. - Gemma4: streaming vs `extract_tool_calls()` for six values (prose, HTML, code, a number, an object, a long string), alone / first of two / second of two, chunk sizes 1, 3, 7, 16, and whole text (90 runs). The mismatch set is identical with and without the hook: 9 mismatches, all at chunk size 16, which splits Gemma4 special tokens across text-only deltas. They are pre-existing and not caused by this PR. - For Qwen3 (156 calls), GLM-4.7 (56), and Gemma4 (142), `_hold_open_value` was reached but installed 0 extenders, because the extender returns `None` at that point. The hook is inert for these parsers on the inputs above. Review independently found the same for Qwen3, MiMo, MiniMax-M2, and GLM-4.7 in [this comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/68070#issuecomment-6965869546). `pytest tests/parser` on `7ce9ee15d7`: 7797 passed and 16 failed. Fifteen failures are in `tests/parser/mistral/test_tool_calls.py`, and one is `tests/parser/test_abstract_parser.py::TestToolChoice_Plus_ResponseFormat::test_auto_with_lark_grammar`. All 16 fail the same way on base. Review on macOS arm64 got the same 15 Mistral failures and no head-only failures. `pre-commit run --files` on the changed files passes, including mypy. End to end through the GPU-less render server, using the real `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` tokenizer and chat template (no weights): ```text vllm launch render deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --enable-auto-tool-choice \ --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 ``` The client renders a `write_file` chat request with `/v1/chat/completions/render`. It tokenizes a V4.1 tool-call completion (reasoning, then `<｜DSML｜ calls>` with `path` and `content`, or `content` only) and sends the token IDs plus EOS to `/v1/chat/completions/derender`. Non-streaming runs 3 times per case (median shown). Streaming derender uses a 2,000-char value in 16-token chunks. | case | value chars | output tokens | base | `7ce9ee15d7` | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | `string="false"`, `path` first | 8,000 | 2,999 | 1.068 s | 0.089 s | | `string="false"`, `path` first | 31,000 | 11,449 | 14.369 s | 0.404 s | | `string="false"`, content only | 8,000 | 2,982 | 0.577 s | 0.090 s | | `string="false"`, content only | 31,000 | 11,432 | 7.506 s | 0.402 s | | omitted attribute, `path` first | 8,000 | 2,995 | 1.032 s | 0.091 s | | omitted attribute, `path` first | 31,000 | 11,445 | 14.263 s | 0.401 s | | omitted attribute, content only | 8,000 | 2,978 | 0.557 s | 0.086 s | | omitted attribute, content only | 31,000 | 11,428 | 7.353 s | 0.401 s | | streaming, 4 cases | 2,000 | 49–50 chunks | 0.86–1.23 s | 0.50–0.54 s | In all 12 cases the arguments decode to the exact input. The non-streaming responses (after normalizing IDs and `created`) and the streamed delta sequences are identical between base and this PR. The render server runs `parse()` in its renderer executor, so `/health` stayed under 30 ms on both base and this PR. This setup does not reproduce the event-loop stall from the issue, which comes from `vllm serve` calling `parse()` on the event loop. It shows the request latency and the unchanged output through a real entry point. No `vllm bench serve` or accuracy eval: the change is in the CPU parser, and it produces the same output as base in every comparison above. ## Details `_compute_arg_delta` calls the DSML converter, `_fix_arg_types`, and `_safe_arg_prefix` for every argument chunk that contains `>`. The lexer treats `">` (`INVOKE_NAME_END`) as a terminal in every state, so an HTML or XML value is split at every attribute quote. For `string="false"` and a missing `string` attribute, the partial converter drops an open value that `json.loads` rejects, so each of those calls only rediscovers that the streamed prefix did not grow. `_dsml_arg_value_extender` already holds these values (and handles `string="true"`) once the converter has produced a JSON prefix. When the markup is the first or only parameter, the converter returns `{}`, `_safe_arg_prefix` returns an empty string, and `_compute_arg_delta` returns before the extender is installed. That is the gap found in review. The engine change (`vllm/parser/engine/parser_engine.py`) installs the extender on those two early returns when nothing has streamed yet. It is a shared path, so per AGENTS.md this change is called out here: - The hook is opt-in. Only configs that set `arg_value_extender` are affected: DeepSeek V3.2/V4/V4.1, GLM-4.7, Qwen3 and its subclasses, Gemma4, MiniMax-M2, and MiMo. - The DeepSeek path is covered by the tests and differentials above. It is the only path where the hook installs an extender in any check so far. - Qwen3, GLM-4.7, and Gemma4 were checked by hand, and MiniMax-M2 and MiMo were checked in review. The hook installed no extender for any of them. - If another parser's extender does install there, the hook sets `open_value_streams = False`, so nothing is emitted until the extender returns `None` and the full converter runs. The worst case is delayed streaming of that value, not different arguments. Review measured long first-parameter strings still streaming incrementally (242 non-empty argument deltas on both base and head) for Qwen3, MiMo, MiniMax-M2, GLM-4.7, and DeepSeek V4. Limitations: - The hook only covers the case where the open value is the first thing in the arguments. A markup value after a streamed parameter already took the extender path before this change. - A repeated parameter name still takes the full converter. Suggested by xiaoke12345678 in review, which found the first-parameter gap and wrote the engine patch sketch. #64196 (draft) also adds a DSML `arg_value_extender`, for long `string="true"` values, and edits the same function. The two changes cover different values and will conflict. ---

commits.pr_title: [Build] Cap nvidia-cudnn-frontend below 1.33
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`nvidia-cudnn-frontend` 1.33.0 (released 2026-11-18) breaks FlashInfer 0.7.4's cuDNN linear-attention path, and `requirements/cuda.txt` allows it (`>=1.31.0`). This caps it at `<1.33` until vLLM moves to a FlashInfer release that supports 1.33 (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#9672 is moving FlashInfer to require it).

## Claims

- Fresh installs and image builds resolve `nvidia-cudnn-frontend` to 1.32.3 instead of 1.33.0.
- `tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda.py::test_kda_prefill_near_collinear_keys_remain_finite[flashinfer]` passes again on images built after 1.33.0's release.

## Validation

- Failure seen on a PR image that resolved requirements after the release (Buildkite build 104115, Kimi K3 unit tests): `ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 3)` at `flashinfer/cudnn/linear_attention.py:380`, `O, fs, _checkpoints = getattr(graph, family)(**ports, **attrs)`. That image had `nvidia-cudnn-frontend==1.33.0`.
- Main's CI image still has 1.32.3 from a cached layer built before the release, and the same job passes on recent main builds. Main gets 1.33.0 the next time that layer rebuilds, i.e. the next change to `requirements/common.txt` or `requirements/cuda.txt`.
- `uv pip compile` of the new specifier resolves to `nvidia-cudnn-frontend==1.32.3`. Pre-commit (including the pip-compile lock hooks) passes; no lock file changes.
- Not yet run: the CI image built from this branch. This PR changes `requirements/cuda.txt`, so its `/ci run` rebuilds that layer and runs the Kimi K3 tests on 1.32.3.

## Details

- Upper bound only; the `>=1.31.0` floor and its reason stay.
- Capping here rather than waiting for FlashInfer, because `requirements/cuda.txt` also feeds the wheel's install requirements, so user installs of vLLM get 1.33.0 today too.
- Lift the cap together with the FlashInfer bump that supports 1.33.

commits.pr_title: [KV Connector] Validate Mooncake results and complete failed transfers
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Validate Mooncake SDK batch replies and report failed transfers so requests can recover instead of treating malformed replies as successful cache operations.

## Claims

- Empty or mismatched SDK reply lengths become full-batch failures for existence checks, PUTs, GETs, and prefix lookups.
- Failed prefix lookups return an IPC error instead of a successful cache miss.
- Load preparation errors and unread split-load suffixes report failed completion. With `kv_load_failure_policy="recompute"`, requests recompute after every worker finishes.
- SDK calls and queues are isolated in a worker-local service; transfer threads retain buffer ownership and scheduler reference accounting stays unchanged.

## Validation

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_hma_e2e.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_worker.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_lookup.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_connector.py -q
```

On `e8b0df2b3060294135485c2e6687c1beb6c25eb2` with the CPU CI pin `mistral-common==1.13.0`: `512 passed, 5 skipped, 1 warning in 75.00s`. Repository hooks passed, including mypy and test tethering. The warning is the source checkout missing generated `vllm._version` metadata.

A focused reproducer uses the existing sending-thread fixture with two keys and an empty SDK PUT reply. On base `a4910b4128`, it fails because the saved offset advances to 32 tokens; with this change, the offset remains zero and the reproducer passes.

No live GPU/RDMA or model-output evaluation was run.

## Details

Updated on November 18 by merging upstream `main` at `1282680cd6ebed079a7e9a2d8b539888c41a6a9a`. Mergify could not synchronize the branch because GitHub rejected its workflow-file update without `workflows` permission. The manual merge completes that update; the connector diff is unchanged.

SDK callers previously relied on reply lengths matching the requested keys. An empty reply could therefore advance SAVE state without a successful write. Validation now feeds malformed replies into the existing per-key failure handling. GET completion runs even when preparation raises, while failed request state survives cross-rank aggregation until all transfers finish.

Related #63464 addresses unread split-load suffixes. This change also validates the SDK boundary and handles prefix-lookup and preparation failures. #65702 optimizes lookup construction and parsing; it does not validate SDK reply cardinality.

Safe buffer release still depends on the synchronous SDK draining native accesses before returning.

commits.pr_title: [CI][Test] Skip HYV4 and Inkling in PP equivalence below Hopper
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`(L4) [Nightly] PP Equivalence Shard 2/3` fails on `HYV4ForCausalLM` and `InklingForCausalLM` in every recent Full CI build ([103594](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/103594), [103780](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/103780), [104023](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/104023)) because neither model can run on SM89. This skips them below Hopper, like the other sparse MLA architectures.

## Claims

- `HYV4ForCausalLM` joins `SPARSE_MLA_ARCHS`, so it is skipped below compute capability 9.0.
- `InklingForCausalLM` is skipped on CUDA below compute capability 9.0 (ROCm keeps running it on its own attention path).
- Test-only change.

## Validation

Errors on L4 (build 104023):

```
HYV4:    RuntimeError: HYV4 sparse attention was requested, but no valid sparse MLA backend is available for current runtime/config. Refusing to fall back to dense attention.
Inkling: ValueError: SM80 forward does not support paged KV   (vllm/models/inkling/nvidia/ops/fa4_rel_attention.py -> flash_attn cute validate_fwd_config)
```

Skip conditions checked by patching `current_platform.get_device_capability` in a pytest plugin:

| Faked capability | HYV4 | Inkling | DeepseekV32 (reference) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8.9 | skipped: "Sparse MLA needs compute capability 9.0 or newer" | skipped: "Inkling's FA4 attention (SM8x support: #55078) needs compute capability 9.0 or newer" | skipped |
| 9.0 | runs | runs | runs |

`pre-commit` passes. The nightly step is optional and runs only on L4, so this PR's CI will not exercise it; the next Full CI will.

## Details

- NVIDIA Inkling has only the FA4 attention path, which needs SM90+. #55078 adds an SM8x Triton path; once it lands, the `CUDA_SM90_ARCHS` entry can go.
- I did not get a clean PP=4 run of either model on SM100+ to confirm they pass there (local runs hit an outdated DeepGEMM build and a concurrent GPU job). Their behavior on Hopper+ is unchanged by this PR either way.
- Other failures in the same shard are tracked elsewhere: `Cohere2ForCausalLM` in #68396, `NemotronLabsDiffusionModel` (GPU sync) fixed by #68376.
- No duplicate: no open PR touches these entries. #67354 edits the sparse MLA skip condition; this keeps the Inkling skip separate to stay out of its way.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf][Qwen4Exp] Export PLE short-conv prefill checkpoints on ROCm
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Let the AMD Qwen4Exp PLE short-conv layer export align-mode prefill checkpoints, as the NVIDIA layer does since #61601. Qwen4Exp's GDN layers export checkpoints on ROCm since #68310, but the scheduler stops splitting a prompt at its last Mamba block boundary only when every Mamba layer can export one, so on ROCm Qwen4Exp still split.

No open PR covers the AMD PLE layer.

## Claims

- The AMD `Qwen4ExpPLELayer` declares the same checkpoint alignment as the NVIDIA layer and exports the conv window after its prefill short conv, through the shared `MambaPrefillCheckpointExporter`. The code is the NVIDIA layer's, copied into the AMD package as the rest of this layer is.
- When another Mamba layer cannot export checkpoints (for example GDN on a backend without them), the PLE layer reserves no checkpoint block, as on NVIDIA.
- Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 TP4 on MI355X: TTFT −26% / −36% / −26% at concurrency 1 / 4 / 8; gsm8k unchanged.

## Validation

`test_prefill_exports_conv_window_at_checkpoint` (from #61601) now also runs the AMD layer's dispatch: each checkpoint must equal the conv state of the same prefill stopped at its offset, and nothing else in the cache may change.

GB300, this branch at `1992229271` (the AMD layer's dispatch is plain Triton/PyTorch, so the AMD cases also run on CUDA):

```bash
pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_ple.py
# 131 passed, 2 skipped in 57.31s
```

With the AMD export call disabled, the 4 new `amd` cases of `test_prefill_exports_conv_window_at_checkpoint` fail and the 4 `nvidia` cases still pass.

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8, 4x MI355X, TP4, default (FlyDSL) GDN prefill backend, `--enable-prefix-caching` (align mode), `--block-size 64`, ISL 8000 / OSL 64, 16 fresh prompts per point. All timed requests succeeded.

| concurrency | TTFT ms, base → PR | output tok/s, base → PR | TPOT ms, base → PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 332.3 → 246.1 (−25.9%) | 75.3 → 84.5 (+12.2%) | 8.22 → 8.11 |
| 4 | 1091.3 → 695.3 (−36.3%) | 125.1 → 148.4 (+18.7%) | 15.13 → 16.28 |
| 8 | 1208.0 → 894.2 (−26.0%) | 199.4 → 204.6 (+2.6%) | 21.32 → 25.24 |

TPOT rises 7.6% at concurrency 4 and 18.4% at 8: the unsplit 8000-token prefill shares steps with the other requests' decodes, and with OSL 64 most decode steps overlap a prefill. It does not come from the FlyDSL → Triton handoff of #68310: with both arms forced to `--gdn-prefill-backend triton` the TPOT gap is about the same. Pure decode is unchanged (no prefix caching, ISL 128 / OSL 512, 32 requests): TPOT 10.186 → 10.179 ms at concurrency 4, 11.000 → 11.111 ms at 8.

gsm8k on MI355X, same server setup, all 1319 questions: base and PR both 0.974981 (1286 / 1319), no invalid or empty responses.

On MI355X, the 4 new `amd` cases of `test_prefill_exports_conv_window_at_checkpoint` pass.

## Details

- The window is taken from the layer inputs only: checkpoint offsets are multiples of the prefix-cache grid, which is at least the conv window length (asserted).
- AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the implementation.

commits.pr_title: [CPU] Add AArch64 top-k and top-p sampling kernels
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

This PR brings the CPU top-k/top-p sampling implementation from #43452 and #55874 to the current vLLM main branch while preserving the original authorship:

- Tianmu Li implemented the base C++ kernels and integration for top-k, top-p, and combined top-k/top-p sampling.
- Fadi Arafeh added the AArch64 implementation.

The cleanup commit:

- removes the AVX512 and AVX2 sampling paths;
- removes the added AVX2 fast-exp macro and `-mfma` build flag;
- retains the AArch64 and scalar implementations;
- applies repository formatting; and
- adds `TestCpuTopkTopp` to the Arm CPU hardware CI kernel shard.

## Performance

Benchmarks were run on an AWS Neoverse-V2 system with 96 physical CPU cores and no SMT. Operator benchmarks used either 1 or 16 threads. For the end-to-end benchmark, the server was pinned to cores `0-15`, and the client was pinned to cores `16-31`.

### Operator Benchmark

The AArch64 C++ kernels were compared with the PyTorch CPU implementation using:

- FP32 Zipf-like logits (`rank^-1.1`);
- vocabulary size: `131,072`;
- batch sizes: `1`, `8`, and `64`;
- top-k: `k=50`;
- top-p: `p=0.9`;
- combined top-k/top-p: `k=100`, `p=0.9`;
- `5` warm-up iterations and `20` measured iterations;
- `3` repeated A/B runs with alternating execution order.

Input cloning was excluded from the measured region. All 18 configurations produced output masks identical to the PyTorch baseline.

| Threads | Batch | Mode          | PyTorch baseline (ms) | AArch64 C++ PR (ms) | Speedup |
| ------- | ----- | ------------- | --------------------- | -------------------- | ------- |
| 1       | 1     | Top-k         | 0.466                 | 0.315                | 1.48x   |
| 1       | 1     | Top-p         | 10.537                | 0.995                | 10.59x  |
| 1       | 1     | Top-k + top-p | 10.665                | 0.742                | 14.38x  |
| 1       | 8     | Top-k         | 2.865                 | 2.359                | 1.21x   |
| 1       | 8     | Top-p         | 83.848                | 7.862                | 10.66x  |
| 1       | 8     | Top-k + top-p | 85.467                | 6.068                | 14.09x  |
| 1       | 64    | Top-k         | 21.919                | 19.117               | 1.15x   |
| 1       | 64    | Top-p         | 672.106               | 62.797               | 10.70x  |
| 1       | 64    | Top-k + top-p | 681.255               | 45.613               | 14.94x  |
| 16      | 1     | Top-k         | 0.379                 | 0.331                | 1.14x   |
| 16      | 1     | Top-p         | 10.400                | 1.009                | 10.31x  |
| 16      | 1     | Top-k + top-p | 10.449                | 0.764                | 13.67x  |
| 16      | 8     | Top-k         | 0.436                 | 0.342                | 1.28x   |
| 16      | 8     | Top-p         | 10.738                | 1.018                | 10.55x  |
| 16      | 8     | Top-k + top-p | 10.816                | 0.803                | 13.48x  |
| 16      | 64    | Top-k         | 2.163                 | 1.323                | 1.64x   |
| 16      | 64    | Top-p         | 43.061                | 4.062                | 10.60x  |
| 16      | 64    | Top-k + top-p | 43.917                | 3.206                | 13.70x  |

### End-to-End Benchmark

The end-to-end benchmark used:

- model: `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`;
- dtype: BF16;
- exact input/output lengths: `128/128` tokens;
- `32` requests per concurrency level and `5` warm-up requests;
- `temperature=0.6`, `top_k=50`, `top_p=0.9`, and `min_p=0`;
- prefix caching disabled;
- EOS ignored;
- unlimited request rate.

The baseline and optimized runs used the same PR source and compiled binary. The only difference was whether top-k/top-p filtering used the PyTorch implementation or the AArch64 C++ kernels.

| 16              | 100.63          | 115.35              | 14.62%          | 149.07             | 128.84                 | 13.57%         | 12.76%        |

All requests completed successfully.

## Test Plan

Validated using a clean CPU source build on an AArch64 Neoverse-V2 system:

```text

Applicable vLLM pre-commit hooks: passed
```

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Make Unlimited-OCR-2 DASH routing batch invariant
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Use fixed-order FP32 prefix sums in DASH `entmax15` with `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`. Fixes #68555. No competing open PR found.

## Claims

Fixed-order scans make the replayed routing bias identical across batch sizes on MI350X.

## Validation

MI350X, PyTorch 2.13.0, ROCm 10.0.0, `ROCM_AITER_FA`, BF16.

| Reproducer | Baseline | Fixed-order scans |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Captured routing scores, one row versus batch sizes 2–256 | Max bias difference `2.3841858e-7` | Max difference `0` |
| Fixed visual features, 80 KV blocks, 2 requests, 192 forced `<PAGE>` tokens per request | `0.9375` at index `123` in 5/5 runs on `b067b6f6fa`, above the `0.5` tolerance | All 384 raw logits matched in 5/5 runs, with one preemption per batch |

- Fixed-feature model revision `04647c7a6098d8d58915f003536a741c82eafb40`. [Prior routing and CK replay](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/66031#issuecomment-6716784892).
- Live vision model revision `cb16b920ec2249c4b280f3aa67942e00b5099122`. `test_unlimited_ocr.py`: **8 passed in 200.48 s**. The existing ROCm preemption case also passed independently in 41.30 s.
- `test_unlimited_ocr2.py`: **36 passed, 1 skipped** across two runs. Ruff lint and format checks passed.
- MI355 DPX validation in the original Buildkite environment is pending.

## Details

PyTorch's FP32 `cumsum` can change addition order with batch shape. The fixed order removes that source of routing bias drift before BF16 decoding.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Add packed_modules_mapping to DeepSeek-V4 DSpark models
commits.pr_body:
### Summary

Fixes #65618.

`DSparkDeepseekV4ForCausalLM` across AMD, NVIDIA, and XPU platforms fuses `gate_up_proj` (from shards `w1`, `w3`) and `fused_wqa_wkv` (from shards `wq_a`, `wkv`) via `stacked_params_mapping`.

However, unlike the target model `DeepseekV4ForCausalLM`, `DSparkDeepseekV4ForCausalLM` omitted `packed_modules_mapping`. Consequently, when quantizers inspect whether layers are skipped via `is_layer_skipped(prefix, ignored_layers, fused_mapping=quant_config.packed_modules_mapping)`, the draft's fused layer prefixes could not be expanded to their constituent shard names.

When a checkpoint leaves these draft linear layers in unquantized BF16 via `quantization_config.ignored_layers`, the draft's fused layers still received `Fp8LinearMethod` with uninitialized weight scales (`weight_scale_inv`), leading to 0% draft token acceptance and invalid output.

### Changes
1. Added `packed_modules_mapping` to `DSparkDeepseekV4ForCausalLM` in:
   - `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/amd/dspark.py`
   - `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/dspark.py`
   - `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/xpu/dspark.py`
   - `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/dspark.py`
   - `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/dspark.py`
2. Added unit tests in `tests/models/test_deepseek_dspark_packed_mapping.py` verifying that all DSpark draft model entry points define `packed_modules_mapping` and that `is_layer_skipped()` correctly resolves unfused shard names to skip fused draft layers.

### Testing
- `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu python -m pytest --noconftest -q tests/models/test_deepseek_dspark_packed_mapping.py` passed all 7 CPU-selected tests with PyTorch 2.14.0 on macOS arm64. These cover the NVIDIA v4 and v4.1 mappings, the XPU mapping, and the NVIDIA `context_wkv_proj` ignored-layer cases. The run verified that the test did not load the ROCm platform or replace `torch.cuda.get_device_properties`.
- The two AMD mapping cases run under ROCm in the existing MI355 Basic Models (Other) job. The updated Buildkite run will verify them on that backend.
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean.


The NVIDIA context projection now checks that the quantization configuration exists and supports the ignored-layer matching mode before accessing it. This resolves the 10 mypy errors in the prior pre-commit run. The repository mypy hook passed across the Python tree with mypy 1.20.2, Python target 3.11 and Linux platform settings. All-file Ruff lint and format hooks passed.

The prior [CPU Buildkite job](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/101629#01a1c839-d9a5-4fea-a212-eb701a3cc489) aborted at collection because importing ROCm from the CPU runner registered the `_C` native extension twice. The test now imports AMD models only on ROCm and no longer patches CUDA device discovery globally.

AI assistance was used for the CI type-checking, test collection and formatting fixes, and local validation.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Turn off the extensible KV cache for Unlimited-OCR-2
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

On CUDA, Unlimited-OCR-2 does not start with the default KV cache settings:

```
ValueError: Unlimited-OCR-2 requires <PAGE><image> for every page
```

#64016 turned off JIT warmup for this model because "generic JIT warmup submits text-only requests, which DASH cannot use". The extensible KV cache (#56492) is on by default on CUDA, and it runs the same `warmup_kernels` to measure its peak. That warmup sends the text-only requests DASH rejects. This PR extends the existing opt-out to the extensible KV cache. If it is requested explicitly, it is turned off with a warning.

## Claims

- Unlimited-OCR-2 starts with the default KV cache and warmup settings, and reads 1- and 2-page documents correctly.
- `--enable-extensible-kv-cache` with Unlimited-OCR-2 logs `Unlimited-OCR-2 does not support the extensible KV cache; turning it off.` and resolves to the same engine config as the default, instead of failing later in the engine core.
- No other model is affected. The change is in `UnlimitedOCRForCausalLMConfig._configure_v2`, which runs only for Unlimited-OCR-2.

## Validation

One L4, wheel of main. Only `vllm/model_executor/models/config.py` differs between the two arms (sha256 checked). That file is unchanged on current main.

New test `test_unlimited_ocr2_starts_with_default_kv_cache`. It sets no `kv_cache_memory_bytes`, so the extensible KV cache is on by default on main, and it reads one rendered page.

```
(EngineCore) ERROR [core.py:1764]   File ".../vllm/model_executor/layers/dash_attention.py", line 70, in page_coordinates
(EngineCore) ERROR [core.py:1764] ValueError: Unlimited-OCR-2 requires <PAGE><image> for every page
```
