```
RUN fix:kvbytes {"code": 0}
SERVE fix {"startup_s": 60.0, "text_only_completion": {"status": 400, "body": "{\"error\":{\"message\":\"Unlimited-OCR-2 requires <PAGE><image> for every page and at least one image. (parameter=prompt)\",\"type\":\"BadRequestError\",\"param\":\"prompt\",\"code\":400}}"}, "health_after": 200, "server_log_errors": ["(APIServer pid=20977) WARNING 11-17 21:19:36 [base.py:407] Traceback (most recent call last):"]}
EXIT 0 at 2026-11-17T21:19:38Z
```
Run 2: the final committed test, with `gpu_memory_utilization=0.5`.
```
START 2026-11-17T21:31:10Z GPU NVIDIA L4, 580.82.07, 23034 MiB
INSTALL exit=0 vllm 0.34.0rc1.dev735+g61dc78bc9
ENV {"blobs_ok": true}
PYTEST base test_unlimited_ocr2_starts_with_default_kv_cache 1 ["(EngineCore pid=19610) ERROR 11-17 21:35:09 [core.py:1764] EngineCore failed to start.", "1 failed, 4 warnings in 176.54s (0:02:56)"]
PYTEST fix test_unlimited_ocr2_starts_with_default_kv_cache 0 ["1 passed, 4 warnings in 37.54s"]
EXIT 0 at 2026-11-17T21:36:12Z
```
The server `Traceback` line is the frontend's "Chat template warmup failed" warning (`base.py:407`). CI shows the same warning on main.
</details>

Config resolution on CPU (`EngineArgs(...).create_engine_config()`): Unlimited-OCR-2 resolves to off when the setting is unset, False or True. With True it logs the warning, and the resulting cache, kernel, compilation and scheduler configs are identical to the default ones. Unlimited-OCR is unchanged.

## Details

- **Root cause.** `gpu_worker._compile_or_warm_up_model` runs `warmup_kernels` when `enable_jit_warmup or enable_extensible_kv_cache`. Model Runner V2's warmup (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/warmup.py`) builds text-only requests: `prompt_token_ids = range(prompt_len)` with no `mm_features`. For M-RoPE models, `add_request` calls `get_mrope_input_positions`, which for Unlimited-OCR-2 is `prompt_page_positions`. `page_coordinates` there raises when a prompt has no `<PAGE><image>`. The opt-out from #64016 covers only the first condition.
- **Why CI did not catch it.** The existing Unlimited-OCR-2 tests set `kv_cache_memory_bytes`, which turns the extensible KV cache off. `vllm_runner` also defaults to `enable_jit_warmup=False`.
- **Cost.** With the extensible KV cache off, the model sizes its KV cache from the profiling estimate, the path its CI tests already use. I can't give a capacity comparison against the extensible KV cache, because with it on the model never starts.
- **Alternatives.**
  - Return page-0 positions for prompts without an image, so DASH accepts the warmup requests. It also worked on the L4. But it relaxes a shared DASH helper against the model's stated design: the renderer rejects text-only prompts, and the opt-out exists for that reason. I can switch to it if you'd rather keep the extensible KV cache for this model.
  - Have the warmup skip models that cannot take text-only requests. That needs a new model-runner hook in core code for one model.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Attention] AITER FA: dedicated split-KV kernels for decode and speculative-decode verify (GQA 8, head 64, FP8 KV)
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Purpose

With k draft tokens, each decode request verifies k + 1 query tokens. On `ROCM_AITER_FA` these batches go through AITER `unified_attention`, which dominates the decode step at long context; plain decode (`paged_attention_v1`) also waits for the longest request. This PR adds a FlyDSL split-KV kernel for layers with head size 64 and 8 query heads per KV head, on gfx950 with an FP8 KV cache, for plain decode and 1-7 draft tokens:

- full-attention layers: a length-balanced grid, so time tracks total KV rather than the longest request while there are well under two requests per CU (each request takes at least one workgroup); the metadata builder maps the work once per step;
- sliding-window layers: the window mask with equal splits per request.

The kernel is adapted from sgl-project/sglang#47371. Any other batch, layer or model keeps the existing path.

## Results

MI355X, Muse Spark TEP4, FP8 KV, default block size.

**One layer** vs `unified_attention`, both on 32-token kernel blocks, graph replay, µs. Full attention excludes the work map, one launch per step shared by all full-attention layers (~5 µs in a server profile):

| batch | full attention, q_len 8 | full attention, q_len 4 | sliding window, q_len 8 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 24 x 100k | 780 -> 261 | 762 -> 224 | 73 -> 23 |
| 40 x 100k | 1479 -> 412 | 1198 -> 360 | 84 -> 27 |
| 40, mixed 200k..3k | 1945 -> 212 | 1434 -> 181 | 84 -> 27 |

**Decode step p50**, k=7, D requests at 100k context (+: two of them at 500k), ms:

| D | 4 | 8 | 16 | 24 | 32 | 8+ | 24+ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | 25.8 | 33.5 | 45.4 | 53.4 | 68.9 | 48.0 | 96.1 |
| this PR | 21.1 | 25.8 | 33.4 | 41.5 | 46.2 | 27.5 | 42.7 |

**Plain decode** (no speculative decoding). One layer vs `paged_attention_v1`: 1.1-1.5x at 1-128 x 100k and 1.7-3.2x with mixed lengths (full attention), 1.2-1.4x on sliding-window layers. Decode step p50, D requests at 100k context (+: two of them at 500k), ms, median over 6 context seeds (3 for 24+) and 3 server starts per arm; both arms ran at once on the two halves of one node:

| D | 1 | 8 | 24 | 40 | 64 | 24+ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | 10.6 | 17.2 | 26.1 | 33.8 | 43.2 | 29.4 |
| this PR | 10.3 | 16.1 | 23.0 | 28.9 | 35.3 | 24.3 |

**Serving.** Muse Spark Open, TEP4 on 4x MI355X, FP8 KV, DSpark k=7 (synthetic acceptance 4.05), `--max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --prefill-schedule-interval 48`; one run per arm on the same GPUs:

```bash
vllm bench serve --dataset-name prefix_repetition \
  --prefix-repetition-prefix-len 60000 --prefix-repetition-suffix-len 4000 \
  --prefix-repetition-num-prefixes 16 --prefix-repetition-output-len 1024 \
  --num-prompts 96 --max-concurrency 16 --ignore-eos
```

| | output tok/s | TTFT p50 / p90, ms | ITL p50 / p90, ms |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | 532.0 | 6194 / 25424 | 40.84 / 41.67 |
| this PR | 572.7 (+7.6%) | 5850 / 25291 | 32.60 / 33.55 |

**AgentX** ([agentic trace](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX), 3600 s). Same server setup without `--max-num-batched-tokens`, `--max-num-seqs` = 2x concurrency. Mean of two runs per arm; both arms ran at once on the two halves of one node, swapping halves between runs. tok/s/GPU @ ITL p50 / p90 ms, TTFT p50:

| concurrency | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 10 | 13,123 @ 7.44 / 11.37, 1.50 s | 14,796 @ 5.04 / 6.46, 1.19 s (+13%) |
| 24 | 20,522 @ 20.95 / 32.43, 3.42 s | 31,637 @ 7.41 / 11.83, 2.04 s (+54%) |
| 40 | 20,442 @ 41.48 / 55.60, 5.61 s | 40,685 @ 11.28 / 21.45, 3.08 s (+99%) |

**Accuracy.** Relative L2 vs float32 is 2.3-2.4e-3 at every q_len 1-8 (QK and PV stay in BF16; `paged_attention_v1` with an FP8 cache runs them as FP8 MFMAs, 2.7-3.2e-2). Greedy MATH-500: 0.976 (one pass; previous revision over 20 passes: 0.9718 main vs 0.9758, paired p = 0.12), real acceptance length 4.35 (previous revision 4.27). Without speculative decoding, over 6 paired passes: 0.9697 main vs 0.9703, p = 0.93. Needle (48 prompts, ~80k tokens): 48/48, also without speculative decoding.

## Test plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_gqa_verify.py   # gfx950: 725 passed, 1 skipped (FlyDSL-missing case), 5-7 min on one MI355X
pytest tests/models/test_muse_spark_rocm_loading.py -k test_aiter_kv_workspace_only_for_cache_readers   # 3 passed
python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_rocm_gqa_verify.py --query-len 8 4 --page 32 [--window 2048]
```

`test_aiter_kv_workspace_only_for_cache_readers` builds the layer without `__init__`; it now also sets `impl._fast_verify` (and the `(-1, -1)` window that `__init__` sets for no window), which the builder reads.

The tests check the kernel against a float32 reference for q_len 1-8, 16- and 32-token pages and 1-16 KV heads per rank (window edges, zero-length padding, stale NaN bytes outside the window or past a request, pools past 2^31 bytes, graph replay), run plain-decode (no speculative config) and verify batches through the backend (gate, builder map, forward hook) against the float32 reference, and check that batches the kernel doesn't cover fall back without touching the output.

## Notes

- **Gate.** Head size 64, GQA 8, at most 16 KV heads per rank, no sinks / soft cap / ALiBi, FP8 e4m3 KV (default layout), gfx950, the same q_len (1-8) for every decode request (host metadata), and for full attention fewer than two requests per CU. Sliding-window layers on the kernel need no window-trimmed block tables, so the builder skips them. Among common checkpoints this matches Muse Spark (and TinyLlama-1.1B); gpt-oss has the shape but uses sinks.
- **Draft model.** Draft layers with the same shape take the kernel too. Muse Spark's five DSpark layers are sliding-window layers with 7 query tokens per request, so they run the sliding-window kernel; with no full-attention layer the drafter builds no work map.
- **Block size.** The kernel reads 16- or 32-token kernel blocks, so it works with the default block size and changes nothing about the KV cache.
- **Dependency.** FlyDSL, through its public API and vLLM's FlyDSL helpers; without it the existing path is used, with a warning. Tested with flydsl 0.4.2 and aiter 0.1.28.post1; aiter v0.1.29, which vLLM's ROCm image pins, requires the same flydsl 0.4.2.
- **Compilation.** One FlyDSL compile per q_len, page size and grid: two full-attention grids (one or two workgroups per CU, switching at 24 requests, or at 3 with two or fewer KV heads per rank) and one sliding-window grid. The Triton map and reduce kernels specialize on the request count's power-of-two bucket and the split count. CUDA-graph capture compiles the variants of the captured sizes; any other, such as an eager batch above the largest captured size, compiles once while serving and is cached on disk.
- **Follow-ups.** Other ROCm backends.
- **Related.** The drafts #66741 / #66743 (@sawsa307) also target verify; they are stacked on #66741, which needs an AITER change not yet released. On identical inputs (TEP4 shapes, 1-128 requests at 100k), this PR's full-attention verify took 1.2-1.5x less time than #66743's at q_len 8 (1.3-1.6x at q_len 4). Their ideas this PR doesn't cover (e.g. ragged q_len batches) are complementary and can follow on top once a suitable AITER is integrated into vLLM.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to prepare this PR. I have carefully reviewed the changes, tests, and results.

commits.pr_title: [Do Not Merge][Build] Point vllm-flash-attn at vllm-project/flash-attention#222 for CI
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Companion to [vllm-project/flash-attention#222](https://github.com/vllm-project/flash-attention/pull/222) ("the upstream PR" below), which disables the append-KV kernels in FA2, following [vllm-project/flash-attention#107](https://github.com/vllm-project/flash-attention/pull/107). This PR points `vllm-flash-attn` at the upstream PR's head commit so that vLLM CI can run against it.

## Claims

- `_vllm_fa2_C.abi3.so`: 70.69 MiB → 39.96 MiB (43.5% smaller).
- `_vllm_fa2_C` build wall time: 407.5 s → 220.2 s (median of 5 paired rounds; the median per-round reduction is 44.6%).
- vLLM's in-tree FA2 call sites are unaffected. Direct calls to `torch.ops._vllm_fa2_C.fwd_kvcache` that append new K/V now raise an error.

## Validation

**How the numbers were measured** (all in the upstream PR, on flash-attention `af5422c5`, the pin at that time):
- I built only the `_vllm_fa2_C` target with vLLM `18480131`'s CMake. `VLLM_FLASH_ATTN_SRC_DIR` pointed at flash-attention with and without the upstream patch. Settings: CUDA 13.0, `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST='7.5 8.0 8.6 8.9 9.0 10.0 11.0 12.0'`, Release, `-j64`.
- I did not build a full vLLM wheel. Swapping each `.so` into the nightly wheel `0ef2a95c` gives 229.32 MiB → 201.20 MiB.
- `af5422c5` → `8dd9eaea` (the current pin) only changes `flash_attn/cute/flash_fwd_sm90.py` and the supported Python versions in `CMakeLists.txt`. FA2 sources are the same, so I expect the same FA2 result on top of `8dd9eaea`; this PR's CI build is the check.

**Kernels** (static comparison of the two builds):
- The removed kernel entries are exactly the 864 `Append_KV = true` instantiations of `flash_fwd_splitkv_kernel`.
- Every remaining kernel has the same SASS (`.text`) and relocations as in the baseline build.

**GPU** (RTX 4080, which runs the shipped sm_80 cubin):
- 192 cases: head dims 32/64/96/128/192/256 × fp16/bf16, through `varlen_fwd` (non-paged, paged prefill, paged decode with `num_splits=0` and `num_splits=1`) and `fwd_kvcache` with and without new K/V.
- All 180 cases that remain supported produce bitwise-identical `out` and `softmax_lse`. The other 12 are `fwd_kvcache` with new K/V, and each raises the new error as intended.
- `fwd_sparse` and `varlen_fwd_sparse` were not run. vLLM has wrappers for them but no callers, and their kernels are among those with unchanged SASS.

**This PR:**
- It changes only the two lines that set the repository and commit.
- A CMake project with the same `FetchContent_Declare` fetches `08a4a4105e70b6da5a501d98209e7217714fd728` with its submodules (`csrc/cutlass` `62750a2b`, `csrc/composable_kernel` `c56c6750`, `third_party/aiter` `f0966b0a`).
- `08a4a41` is one commit on top of `8dd9eaea`. It changes only the four FA2 files of the upstream PR.

**Call sites** in vLLM `df763962`:
- `torch.ops._vllm_fa2_C` is used only by the `varlen_fwd`, `fwd_sparse` and `varlen_fwd_sparse` wrappers in `vllm/vllm_flash_attn/flash_attn_interface.py`.
- Nothing references `fwd_kvcache`.
- The `flash_attn_with_kvcache` in `rocm_aiter_fa.py` is imported from aiter.

## Details

- Why the append-KV path can go: vLLM has always written the KV cache with its own `reshape_and_cache_flash` (slot mapping, FP8 cache dtype) and never passed new K/V to FA. Since #6052 it only uses `varlen_fwd`, and #28429 removed the `flash_attn_with_kvcache` wrapper.
- The repository temporarily points to my fork because the upstream PR is not merged yet, so a plain clone of `vllm-project/flash-attention` cannot check out `08a4a41`. #67280 did the same.
- Once the upstream PR lands, this should point back to `vllm-project/flash-attention` at the merge commit. I can push that, or maintainers can edit the branch directly.

commits.pr_title: [LoRA][Model] Add LoRA support for GLM-5.3-Flash
commits.pr_body:
## Overview Enable LoRA adapters on GLM-5.3-Flash (`Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration`, added in #53906), including the absorbed MLA and sparse-indexer paths that bypassed the LoRA wrappers. The MLA prefill follow-up is #56718; the matching DeepSeek-V4 compressor fix is #64880. ## Claims - `packed_modules_mapping` maps each fused runtime projection to its adapter-visible submodules: `gate_up_proj` -> gate/up, the 6-way KDA `in_proj_qkvbfg_a` -> q/k/v/b/f_a/g_a, `fused_qkv_a_proj` -> q_a/kv_a_proj_with_mqa, `wk_weights_proj` -> wk/weights_proj, and the vision `qkv`. - `MergedColumnParallelLinearWithLoRA` respects `replicated_shard_ids`, so the TP-replicated `f_a_proj`/`g_a_proj` keep their full LoRA-B on every rank. - Absorbed MLA decode adds the `kv_b_proj` adapter after the cached `W_UK`/`W_UV` BMMs, in a dedicated `MLAKVBProjWithLoRA` (and fully sharded variant) that claims the `kv_b_proj` `MLAAttention` marks. - The indexer's FP32 head gate keeps its adapter: `Glm5NextIndexerWkWeightsLinear` owns the fused `wk`/`weights_proj` GEMM and FP32 gate, and `Glm5NextIndexerWkWeightsWithLoRA` adds the delta to `k` and the gate. - `lm_head` adapters apply (`embedding_modules`, `get_mm_mapping`). - Weight sync with LoRA enabled: checkpoint shards and the FP8 indexer/attention dequant targets resolve through the wrapper's `base_layer` (the FP8 targets also by unique suffix), and `FusedMoEModularMethod.process_weights_after_loading` ignores the call it receives through `FusedMoEWithLoRA`, so routed experts are post-processed once. - GLM-5.2 (`glm_moe_dsa`) gets the missing `wk_weights_proj` packed mapping. ## Validation 2026-11-16 rebase on `a4910b4128`: local pre-commit (including mypy), syntax checks, and `git diff --check` passed. CUDA tests and model evaluations were not rerun on this macOS host. The earlier H20 results below predate this rebase; FP8 coverage now uses real LoRA-wrapped projections in `test_fp8_dequant.py`. Unit tests (CUDA): ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/lora/test_layers.py -v -k "mla_absorbed or column_parallel or indexer_gate or moe_lora_reload or base_layer_with_lora or merged_lora_b_replicated or variable_slice" .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/lora/test_lora_manager.py -v -k "not from_lora_tensors" .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/quantization/test_quark.py -v -k glm5next .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/quantization/test_fp8_dequant.py -v -k "glm5next or indexer" .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/glm5next/test_kda_conv_weight_refit.py -v ``` Earlier CUDA validation on one H20: 48 passed / 24 skipped, 40 passed, 6 passed, 4 passed. `test_moe_lora_reload_processes_routed_experts_once` and `test_model_refits_lora_wrapped_conv` fail without their fixes. A tiny random-weight DeepSeek-V2 run (`load_format="dummy"`, FLASH_ATTN_MLA) with a `kv_b_proj`-only adapter wraps every `kv_b_proj` in `MLAKVBProjWithLoRA`, runs the absorbed hook during decode, and changes the greedy output. E2E LoRA training with verl (https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/7483): with the MLA and indexer fixes, the training/inference mismatch is back to normal. Independent checks from other users: [per-token logprobs match HF + PEFT](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56327#issuecomment-6003627647) for q/k/v, q_a/kv_a and g_a at TP=4 (f_a_proj also needs #60131), and [stable SkyRL training](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56327#issuecomment-5801665331). ## Details - Absorbed MLA folds `kv_b_proj` into the cached `W_UK_T`/`W_UV`, so the wrapper's forward never runs. The delta is added after each BMM as `(q_nope · B_nope) · A` and `(x · Aᵀ) · B_vᵀ`, per token's adapter slot, gathering LoRA-B across DCP ranks when queries are replicated. `kv_b_proj` is a plain `ColumnParallelLinear` in every MLA model, so `MLAAttention` marks the one it receives (as it already does for `_cpu_skip_gemm_dispatch`) and the dedicated LoRA class claims it; no model changes how it builds `kv_b_proj`. Punica's kernels don't fit this path: their metadata covers the whole mapped batch while MQA sees only the decode tokens, and expand needs contiguous per-slice LoRA-B, which per-head `kv_b_proj` blocks aren't. - The indexer gate is computed in FP32 from a cached copy of its weight rows, which also bypassed the wrapper. ---

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][LoRA] Allow non-divisible BLIP-2 encoder budgets
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

BLIP-2 can fail during tower/connector LoRA initialization when the encoder budget is not a multiple of the query tokens per image. This change sizes the wrappers for the number of complete images that fit.

Fixes #67264. Tracked by #61608.

## Claims

- A budget of 5000 with 32 query tokens per image sizes the wrappers for 156 images. The unused 8 tokens do not trigger an assertion.
- The per-image path still checks that the token count represents complete images.

## Validation

- Local regression testing before removing the standalone test file: `uv run --active --no-project .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_blip2.py -q` reproduced the assertion at a budget of 5000 (1 failed, 3 passed). All four cases passed with the fix (non-divisible, divisible and zero budgets, and one image). The test file was removed from the PR after review.
- Ruff 0.17.2 lint and format checks passed for the final BLIP-2 source file. `git diff --check` passed.
- RTX 3090 end-to-end smoke test with PyTorch `2.13.0+cu129`, vLLM `0.32.0rc1.dev100+g77154ca61.cu129`, and the `Salesforce/blip2-opt-2.7b` configuration with dummy weights. The wheel's `blip2.py` matches upstream `f0787a9ab8` byte for byte. The test used `VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn`, `TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM=false`, and `OMP_NUM_THREADS=4`.
  - Baseline at `max_num_batched_tokens=5000` failed during LoRA initialization with the expected divisibility assertion.
  - The baseline at 4992 and patched model at 5000 both initialized and returned the same four token IDs for an image request.
  - The patched model also completed an image request at 5000 with a synthetic rank-8 LoRA adapter targeting a vision projection.
- The CUDA runs use dummy weights to validate startup and request execution. Pretrained checkpoint accuracy was outside the scope of this sizing change.

## Details

The startup call uses `mm_kwargs=None` and supplies the overall encoder budget. For a budget `B` and `Q` query tokens per image, at most `B // Q` images fit. The hook uses that image count to size both wrappers. The divisibility check applies when processing actual image input.

No overlapping BLIP-2 sizing PR was found in searches for open PRs referencing #61608 or matching BLIP-2 LoRA and sizing. The related PRs cover other models or BLIP-2 encoder CUDA Graphs. AI assistance was used for implementation, tests and draft preparation.

commits.pr_title: [Core] Configurable async scheduling depth for Model Runner V2
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Add `--async-scheduling-depth` (`SchedulerConfig.async_scheduling_depth`, default 2): how many steps Model Runner V2 keeps in flight with async scheduling. The default keeps today's count (`pp_size + 1`).

## Claims

- New option, default unchanged. With depth N the scheduler runs up to N − 1 steps ahead of the step on the GPU (plus one per extra pipeline stage, as before).
- It helps when the host round trip per step (output processing, scheduling, the broadcast to the workers, input preparation) is longer than a GPU step: low-batch decode with speculative decoding, across nodes.
- On DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP8 over two GB300 trays with DSpark (7 draft tokens), one request: **885 tok/s at depth 2, 1,212 at 3, 1,263 at 4, 1,359 at 6** (plateau). That is with #61869 and the TP8 specialized decode (#64146).

## Validation

- `tests/test_config.py`: new tests for `max_concurrent_batches` (PP 1 at depths 2 and 6, PP 2 at depths 2 and 4) and for rejecting depth < 2. They pass on GB300, along with the existing async-scheduling tests.
- End to end on vLLM main (nightly `5d35ce39`), TP8 as above but without #61869: 899 → 942 tok/s (depth 2 → 6, 8 runs each). The gain is smaller here because main runs the DSpark draft on the stock path, so the GPU step is longer than the host round trip.
- The UVA staging pools, the engine core's batch queue and the aux-output store already size themselves from `max_concurrent_batches`, so nothing else changes.

## Details

- Only `VllmConfig.max_concurrent_batches` reads the new field.
- Model Runner V1 ignores it: async scheduling there stays at 2 concurrent batches.
- A deeper queue holds more steps' inputs and outputs in flight. The cost is a little pinned host memory.
- The scheduler already handles several steps in flight (PP > 1, and async scheduling at depth 2). Depth only raises the count. Our DeepSeek-V4.1 deployment runs depth 6 with DSpark and up to 8 sequences.
- Not run: `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` (no new code on the step path).

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf][DSv4.1] Insert the compressed KV cache inside the compression launch
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

**TL;DR (MI355X, DeepSeek-V4.1 decode):** the compression launch now writes the compressed-cache record itself.
- At the 4 kv-source layers, the compress + insert chain drops from 8 launches to 4, and from 21.78 to 14.26 us per C1 decode step (**-34.5%**; -23% to -25% for 14-336-row graphs).
- Cache bytes equal main's.
- NVIDIA is unaffected: nothing on CUDA takes the fused path, unit tests pass on GB300, and the kernels compile to the same instructions.
- GSM8K and RULER at 32K / 64K / 128K are unchanged on both changed paths (every McNemar p >= 0.1).
- End to end, the saving is about 0.17% of a 4.30 ms C1 step. That is below the noise between serving runs, so serving ITL shows no measurable change.

**Today.** On ROCm, every DeepSeek-V4.1 decode step compresses the KV at the 4 kv-source layers (L2, L8 and L14 at compress ratio 2, L20 at ratio 1). A second Triton launch, `_rope_quant_insert_kernel`, then reads the BF16 latent back and writes its 584-B fp8_ds_mla record into the paged compressed cache.

**With this PR.** `fused_save_compress_norm` writes that record from the row it has just produced. Two ROCm decode call sites switch to the fused form:
- the TP `--monokernel` decode (`amd/mono_decode._select`);
- the CSA aux-stream chain of FULL-graph decode (`amd/rocm.py` `_forward_csa2_full`).

These keep the separate insert: NVIDIA, ROCm prefill and mixed steps, PCP, and the plain-row caches.

**Series.** This PR is part of a series that trims the DeepSeek-V4.1 sparse-indexer launch floor on MI355X, after #63888 (merged). The others are #67363, #67365, #67366 and #67367, and each of them applies to main on its own. #67368 is stacked on this PR.

## Performance vs. baseline

- **Baseline:** the stock `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-60bd6dd2edd175a1c55fd3488f871e4c3d2ef27d` (2026-11-16). Its copies of the 4 source files this PR changes equal main's, except for gfx942-only code in `mono_decode.py`.
- **This PR:** the same image with this PR's diff applied to those 4 files, mounted over the image and sha-checked inside every container.

| Measured on MI355X | Baseline | This PR | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Microbenchmark: compression + cache insert at the 4 kv-source layers, C1 decode step (1 request x 7 rows, DSpark k=6), 32K context | 21.78 us | 14.26 us | **-7.52 us (-34.5%)** |
| Same, 128K context | 21.69 us | 14.11 us | **-7.58 us (-35.0%)** |
| Same, decode graphs of 14 to 336 rows | 23.26 to 24.64 us | 17.61 to 18.81 us | **-5.5 to -5.9 us (-23% to -25%)** |
| Kernel launches in that chain per decode step (microbenchmark; the same in TP4 server profiles, with and without `--monokernel`) | 8 | 4 | **-4** |
| C1 serving, 1x TP8 `--monokernel`, ITL p50, 32K / 128K context (synthetic AL 3.87) | 4.302 / 4.330 ms | 4.304 / 4.330 ms | +2 +- 8 / +1 +- 17 us (mean +- SE, 3 ABBA pairs; expected -7.5 us): not resolvable |

- **Microbenchmark.** It runs the real `fused_save_compress_norm`, plus main's separate `rope_quant_insert` on the baseline, at production shapes.
  - Each arm's 50 decode steps are captured in one HIP graph; ABBA over 7 rounds, reporting medians.
  - The 14 timings per arm spread by at most 0.08 us on the C1 rows, and by under 0.03 us for the 14-336-row graphs.
- **What it is worth end to end.**
  - -7.5 us of a 4.30 ms C1 TP8 step is about -0.17%.
  - The per-pair ITL deltas range from -7 to +19 us at 32K and from -17 to +34 us at 128K, so three ABBA server pairs cannot resolve it; the kernel rows are the measurement.
  - Output throughput (baseline 716.1, this PR 715.9 tok/s at 32K) is unchanged, and no request failed.
  - These perf servers use synthetic acceptance (AL fixed at 3.87), so acceptance is compared only under Accuracy.
  - TP4 `--monokernel` at concurrency 1, 2 and 4 (one baseline and one PR server at once, GPU halves swapped between 2 rounds) gives the same picture: ITL p50 changes by +3 +- 37, -5 +- 56 and +18 +- 59 us. A ~40 us bias between the GPU halves, the same for both arms, dominates the difference.
- **Where the saving lands.**
  - `--monokernel` decode (steps up to 48 rows) runs the chain serially, so the full saving counts.
  - FULL-graph decode without mono (for example C64 2x TP4+EP4, or DEP8) runs the chain on aux stream 0, next to the q/kv chain. There it counts only when that stream is the longer path.
- **The whole series** (all six PRs on nightly f5d93296c8, agentic sweep below) measured median per-request decode time 1.0-2.0% lower at C1, C4 and C64-C256. Only C64 is statistically significant (p 0.029); with 2+2 servers, p cannot go below 0.33. This PR's expected share is about -0.17% of the C1 step, and less off the mono path.

<details>
<summary>Server profiles (TP4, torch profiler, 32K context)</summary>

| Per decode step | Baseline | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `_rope_quant_insert_kernel`, `--monokernel` / FULL graph without mono | 4 launches, 18.0 / 18.4 us | 0 / 0 |
| `_fused_save_compress_norm_kernel`, `--monokernel` / FULL graph without mono | 4 launches, 27.1 / 30.8 us | 4 launches, 27.9 / 28.4 us |
| All kernels, `--monokernel` / FULL graph without mono | 318 / 1665 launches | 314 / 1661 launches |

- **These confirm the launch count only, not the cost.** The torch profiler shows short graph kernels at about 2-2.5x their microbenchmark cost.
- **Whole-step kernel times are not comparable.** They are dominated by long kernels (mono K2, collectives), and each arm ran on a different GPU half, so they do not measure this PR.

</details>

## Accuracy

**No change, on both changed paths.**
- **Setup:** 1x TP8 at concurrency 1 with real (block) DSpark k=6 acceptance, one server per arm (baseline, then this PR).
  - `--monokernel` (the CI C1 recipe) sends every decode step through the fused insert in `_select`; this is the main table.
  - The FULL-graph decode without mono (`_forward_csa2_full`, the recipe's no-mono branch with expert parallelism) is the second table.
- **Same inputs:** both arms saw the same prompts. All 900 RULER doc hashes are shared, and GSM8K runs the same 1319 questions in the same order.
- **What it exercises:** prompt KV is written by prefill, which this PR does not change. Every compressed row that a generated token completes (one row per two tokens at ratio 2) is written by the fused insert. Later decode steps read that row back when the indexer's top-512 selects it.

| Benchmark | Baseline | This PR | Prompts right in only one arm (baseline / PR) | McNemar p |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GSM8K-1319, 8-shot, greedy | 91.81% | 91.43% | 34 / 29 | 0.62 |
| RULER NIAH, 8 tasks, **32K** (50 each, 400 prompts) | 99.81% | 99.81% | 3 / 3 | 1.00 |
| RULER NIAH, 8 tasks, **64K** (25 each, 200 prompts) | 99.75% | 99.75% | 1 / 1 | 1.00 |
| RULER NIAH, 8 tasks, **128K** (25 each, 200 prompts) | 99.50% | 99.25% | 2 / 1 | 1.00 |
| RULER vt + cwe, **32K** (25 each) | 99.20% | 99.80% | 1 / 3 | 0.62 |
| RULER vt + cwe, **128K** (25 each) | 84.60% | 89.60% | 0 / 3 | 0.25 |
| DSpark acceptance length: GSM8K / NIAH 32K / 64K / 128K / vt+cwe 32K / 128K | 3.580 / 5.004 / 5.054 / 5.100 / 4.220 / 4.052 | 3.583 / 5.032 / 5.026 / 5.124 / 4.153 / 3.837 | | |

- **Scoring.** RULER scores are lm-eval 0.4.13's mean score; a prompt counts as right when it scores 1.0.
- **The differences are run-to-run noise.** The write is byte-exact.
  - multivalue at 128K: 4 vs 5 of 25 prompts score below 1.0.
  - cwe at 128K: 0.692 vs 0.792, from 3 prompts (p 0.25).
  - vt+cwe 128K acceptance: 5% lower on this PR, from one server each (about 760 verify steps).
- **Nondeterminism.** The stack is not bit-reproducible from run to run even with identical kernels: 325 of 1319 GSM8K outputs match here. In an earlier A/B on another image (TP4 `--monokernel`), two cold servers of the same build matched 333 of 1319. The bit-exactness evidence is the kernel test under Validation.

**FULL-graph decode without mono** (`_forward_csa2_full`; 1x TP8 with expert parallelism, concurrency 1, real acceptance):

| Benchmark | Baseline | This PR | Prompts right in only one arm (baseline / PR) | McNemar p |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GSM8K-1319, 8-shot, greedy | 91.05% | 92.19% | 30 / 45 | 0.11 |
| RULER NIAH, 8 tasks, **32K** (25 each, 200 prompts) | 99.75% | 99.88% | 0 / 1 | 1.00 |
| RULER NIAH, 8 tasks, **128K** (25 each, 200 prompts) | 99.38% | 98.75% | 2 / 0 | 0.50 |
| DSpark acceptance length: GSM8K / NIAH 32K / 128K | 3.595 / 4.991 / 5.141 | 3.586 / 5.019 / 5.204 | | |

<details>
<summary>RULER per task</summary>

| Context | Arm | multikey_1 | multikey_2 | multikey_3 | multiquery | multivalue | single_1 | single_2 | single_3 | mean |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 32K | baseline | 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.985 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.9981 |
| 32K | this PR | 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.985 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.9981 |
| 64K | baseline | 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.980 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.9975 |
| 64K | this PR | 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.980 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.9975 |
| 128K | baseline | 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.960 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.9950 |
| 128K | this PR | 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.940 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.9925 |

| Context | Arm | cwe | vt |
|---|---|---|---|
| 32K | baseline | 0.984 | 1.000 |
| 32K | this PR | 0.996 | 1.000 |

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf][DSv4.1] Build the MXFP4 indexer decode metadata in one launch
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

On ROCm, `RocmMxfp4IndexerMetadataBuilder` (the DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 MXFP4 sparse indexer on gfx950) builds its decode metadata every step with a chain of small eager torch ops before the graph replay. This PR builds it with one Triton launch per indexer KV group, `RocmMxfp4DecodeRowsKernel`, in the ROCm-only ops module. The shared `DeepseekV32IndexerMetadataBuilder` gets a documented `_build_decode_rows()` hook (+29/-2) that returns None by default. `build()` calls it on decode steps that use neither varlen decode nor DCP, and keeps its current path when it returns None, so CUDA and the other builders are unchanged. Varlen decode and DCP skip the hook and always take the default path. Readers get the same integers as on main. Only never-read padding rows differ: they are zeroed.

## At a glance (main -> this PR)

| Metric | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Eager indexer-builder launches per decode step, C1 (both KV groups) | 17 | 4 |
| Builder GPU time per step, C1 / adaptive verification 56 rows (microbenchmark) | 38.6 / 99.3 us | 16.2 / 22.9 us |
| TP8 1K/1K serving, C1 decode step (ITL p50, 2 servers per arm) | 4.219 ms | 4.195 ms (-23 us, -0.55%) |
| TP8 1K/1K serving, C2-C64 ITL p50 | | -1.8% to +0.1%: no slowdown, gain not resolved by the A/A gap |
| TP8 C1 32K decode step, ITL p50 (identical-output pairs) | 4.25 ms | -25.8 us (-0.61%) |
| GPQA-diamond, 2 runs x 198 per arm | 86.11% | 86.11% |
| RULER 32K-128K, 4 tasks, 2640 items | 99.66% | 99.70% |
| GSM8K-1319 at C64, TP decode-row shard engaged | 91.74% | 91.58% |

## Performance vs main

All runs: MI355X, image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-60bd6dd2edd175a1c55fd3488f871e4c3d2ef27d`. The image's copies of the 3 `vllm/` files this PR touches are byte-identical to main (df763962fc); in the serving runs the PR arm mounts this PR's copies over them. The 1K/1K sweep and GPQA ran at e1cda700ff, whose `vllm/` files are identical to this PR's head (9fee1098b0). The microbenchmark, the 32K run, the profile, RULER and GSM8K ran on an earlier revision that switched the path with a class flag instead of the hook; its Triton kernel file is byte-identical to e1cda700ff.

**Builder microbenchmark** (1 GPU, 2 runs). One step is `build()` of both V4.1 indexer KV groups (ratios 2 and 1), with the real aiter cache layout and schedule. Main is the same builder in the same process with the fused path switched off. GPU time is the median of 60 steps queued behind a spin kernel.

| Step shape | Launches/step | GPU us/step, run 1 / run 2 | GPU change, mean | Host us/step, mean |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| C1: 1 req x 7 rows, 32K ctx | 17 -> 4 | 39.2 -> 16.0 / 38.0 -> 16.3 | -22.5 (-58%) | 228 -> 152 |
| Adaptive verification, 20 reqs, 56 rows in a 64-row graph | 49 -> 6 | 97.3 -> 22.9 / 101.2 -> 22.8 | -76.4 (-77%) | 465 -> 181 |
| Adaptive verification, 48 x 7 = 336 rows | 47 -> 6 | 119.1 -> 30.8 / 116.2 -> 30.9 | -86.8 (-74%) | 452 -> 182 |

**Serving sweep, 1K in / 1K out** (e1cda700ff). DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP8 `--monokernel`, DSpark k=6 with real acceptance, adaptive verification off. `vllm bench serve` random 1024 in / 1024 out, `--ignore-eos`, greedy; 16 prompts at C1-C4 and 4 x C above that, the same prompts on every server, one excluded warm-up per C, 0 failed requests. Four fresh servers in ABBA order (main, PR, PR, main); each cell is the mean of an arm's 2 servers. The A/A gap is the larger of the two same-arm differences (main vs main, PR vs PR), in %. AL is tokens per decode step.

| C | ITL p50 ms, main / PR | ITL change % (A/A gap) | TPOT p50 ms, main / PR | TPOT change % (A/A gap) | Output tok/s, main / PR | tok/s change % (A/A gap) | AL, main / PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 4.219 / 4.195 | **-0.55** (0.02) | 0.663 / 0.665 | +0.30 (8.10) | 1321 / 1291 | -2.29 (3.21) | 5.80 / 5.63 |
| 2 | 4.944 / 4.940 | -0.10 (0.56) | 0.793 / 0.847 | +6.78 (6.41) | 1973 / 1702 | -13.71 (16.30) | 5.58 / 4.72 |
| 4 | 6.645 / 6.655 | +0.14 (1.70) | 1.169 / 1.190 | +1.84 (11.93) | 2477 / 2203 | -11.07 (19.13) | 4.92 / 4.48 |
| 8 | 10.152 / 9.966 | -1.83 (2.48) | 1.732 / 1.668 | -3.65 (1.39) | 3414 / 3437 | +0.70 (7.31) | 5.28 / 5.35 |
| 16 | 12.145 / 12.089 | -0.46 (2.63) | 2.208 / 2.218 | +0.46 (1.78) | 5606 / 5436 | -3.03 (8.29) | 5.56 / 5.30 |
| 32 | 16.017 / 15.921 | -0.60 (1.42) | 3.060 / 3.035 | -0.81 (3.02) | 7613 / 7818 | +2.70 (7.83) | 5.06 / 5.13 |
| 64 | 23.942 / 23.819 | -0.51 (0.45) | 4.408 / 4.375 | -0.74 (1.12) | 10802 / 10783 | -0.18 (9.85) | 5.28 / 5.29 |

- ITL p50 is the per-step time: each streamed chunk is one engine step of about AL tokens. Only C1 clears the A/A gap in both ABBA halves: -23 us per step, -0.55% in each half against a 0.02% gap, in line with the microbenchmark's -22.5 us. Paired by prompt it is -23.8 us [95% CI -36.4, -11.2], with the PR faster on 14 of 16 prompts.
- C2-C64 show no slowdown, but the gain is not resolved there: the expected saving, tens of microseconds on 4.9-24 ms steps, is below the 0.45-2.6% A/A gap. C64's -0.51% clears its gap on the mean, but one ABBA half (-0.24%) does not, so it is not counted as a gain.
- TPOT and output tok/s follow AL, which differed by up to 19% between two servers of the same arm: greedy DSpark outputs on random-token prompts are not reproducible across servers. The two TPOT changes past the gap track it. At C2 one PR server had AL 4.30 against 5.1-5.6 on the other three; at C8 the PR's AL was 1.2% higher and its ITL 1.8% lower.
- TTFT p50 (not in the table) is within its gap except at C1 (+0.3%, +86 us) and C64 (+6.0%). C1 TTFT has two modes about 4 ms apart, and the p50 moves with how many requests land in each. Paired by prompt over the 12 prompts in the slow mode on all 4 servers, the difference is +121 us [95% CI -71, +313]. At C64 the mean TTFT is 2.8% lower on the PR.
- On both PR servers, per-rank counters show every decode-step build went through the kernel (20.3k-20.8k per rank in the sweep); main, which has no hook, ran none. The TP decode-row shard engaged in both arms on about 23% of the sweep's decode builds (only C16-C64 reach 64 rows).

**End to end, 32K** (earlier revision): DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP8 `--monokernel`, DSpark k=6 with real acceptance, C1, 32K in / 1024 out, greedy. Each arm ran 3 reps x 6 prompts, the same prompts in both. Step time is each request's median inter-token gap.

| ITL p50 per request | main | PR | PR - main [95% CI] |
|---|---|---|---|
| All 18 pairs | 4.2512 ms | 4.2197 ms | -31.5 us (-0.74%) [-43.4, -20.6] |
| 8 pairs with identical output | | | **-25.8 us (-0.61%)** [-27.1, -24.5] |

AL was 6.14 on main and 6.59 on the PR. The gap comes from 3 main requests whose output diverged into low-acceptance text, and the identical-output pairs exclude them. That run had one server per arm, main first, and no A/A; the ABBA sweep above repeats the C1 result with two servers per arm.

**Serving profile** (same 32K servers, torch profiler, 8 ranks): 17 -> 4 builder launches on every profiled decode step (30 main / 29 PR steps on each rank). Builder GPU time was 72.2 -> 18.7 us/step (all-rank median; profiler-inflated).

## Accuracy

**GPQA-diamond** (e1cda700ff, on the 4 sweep servers after the sweep, so 2 runs per arm): 198 questions, OpenAI simple-evals prompt, choice order and answer regex; greedy; the model's default thinking mode (effort high); `max_tokens` 65536; concurrency 64.

| | main | PR |
|---|---|---|
| Correct, 2 runs | 341 / 396 (86.11%) | 341 / 396 (86.11%) |
| Per run | 84.85%, 87.37% | 87.37%, 84.85% |
| Replies that hit `max_tokens` (no answer, scored wrong) | 29 | 35 |
| The 164 questions that finished in all 4 runs | 95.12% | 95.73% |

PR - main, paired by question: +0.00 pts [95% CI -2.73, +2.73]; exact McNemar on the two ABBA-adjacent cross-arm run pairs 15 / 15, p = 1.0. Two runs from different arms disagree on 8.1% of questions on average (6.6-9.1% per pair), two runs from the same arm on 8.6% (6.6% main, 10.6% PR). Most of that churn is replies that hit the token cap, most of whose tails are repetition loops: 26 of the 30 questions whose result changed hit the cap in at least one run. Which questions hit it changes between servers of the same arm too (34 in at least one run, 2 in all four; 29 vs 35 replies by arm, Fisher p = 0.52). The TP decode-row shard engaged on 79-84% of GPQA's decode builds in both arms. The 86% is this harness's greedy score, not a published-style number.

**RULER** (32K servers, earlier revision) at concurrency 1, greedy, 220 items per cell, paired by id. Full-correct rate in %:

| Task | 32K main / PR | 64K main / PR | 128K main / PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| niah_multikey_3, vt | 100 / 100 | 100 / 100 | 100 / 100 |
| niah_multivalue | 100 / 100 | 100 / 99.55 | 100 / 99.55 |
| cwe | 100 / 100 | 98.64 / 99.09 | 97.27 / 98.18 |
| **4 tasks, n = 880** | **100 / 100** | **99.66 / 99.66** | **99.32 / 99.43** |
| PR - main, pts [95% CI] | 0.00 [-0.43, +0.43] | 0.00 [-0.62, +0.62] | +0.11 [-0.60, +0.86] |

Across all 2640 items: +0.04 pts [-0.24, +0.33], McNemar p = 1.0. No cell has Holm p <= 0.05. Both PR-only niah_multivalue misses were truncated at the 128-token cap.

**GSM8K-1319** (32K servers, 8-shot, concurrency 64; engages #66047's TP decode-row shard): 91.74% on main vs 91.58% on the PR, -0.15 pts [-1.45, +1.15], McNemar 38/36, p = 0.908. Sharded builds ran on all 8 ranks (main 230 per rank, PR 222). On the PR, ranks 1-7 read their block ends at `shard.start`.

commits.pr_title: [Frontend] generate: keep sample logprobs as engine rows and render them without objects
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Part of RFC #57479 (cheap frontend after an RL `pause(mode="abort")`).

A non-streaming `output_mode="tokens"` `/inference/v1/generate` request with top-k logprobs costs Python objects proportional to tokens × candidates:
- a `Logprob` per (position, candidate) in the output processor;
- a pydantic `GenerateLogProbs` entry per candidate when the response is built;
- one `model_dump` and one `JSONResponse` over all of it.

After an abort, every in-flight request is rendered at once on the API server's event loop. At this PR's GPU benchmark load (32 requests × about 12.5k tokens × top-128), `/pause?mode=abort` itself takes 82–86 s to return on current main. The full RL shape (245,760 tokens × top-128) exhausted node memory on main in the RFC #57479 runs.

## Changes

**1. `FlatLogprobs` is stored as numpy columns** (`vllm/logprobs.py`).
- Entries live in append-only numpy columns, each one buffer that doubles when full: int32 token ids and float32 logprobs (the engine's dtypes), per-position first-entry ranks, and per-position end offsets only once positions have different widths. That is about 8.5 bytes per entry instead of about 90.
- A column switches to int64 / float64 when a value would not round-trip, so values read back exactly.
- Per-entry ranks and decoded tokens are kept only when needed: a non-engine rank layout, or a non-None decoded token.
- The list-like API is unchanged: `len`, `flat[i]` returning `dict[int, Logprob]`, iteration, slicing, `append`, `append_fast`, `extend`.
- New: `append_rows()` for engine rows in bulk, `rows()` for the `[N, S]` arrays, `num_entries`, `first_token_ids()`.
- This replaces the separate `ArrayLogprobs` container from the earlier revision of this PR, per review, so there is one flat logprobs container.

**2. `LogprobsProcessor` appends engine rows in bulk** when no decoded tokens are needed, for both sample and prompt logprobs. With a tokenizer it still detokenizes per position, as before.

**3. The generate endpoint renders tokens-mode logprobs from the arrays.**
- For non-streaming `output_mode="tokens"` requests with `logprobs >= 0` and no `prompt_logprobs`, it sets `flat_logprobs=True` and a private `SamplingParams._detokenize_logprobs=False`. Tokens mode never reads decoded tokens, and clients can't set the private flag.
- It then writes `GenerateLogProbs` JSON straight from `rows()`, with no Python object per entry.
- The bytes are the same as the per-entry pydantic path (`_create_tokens_logprobs` + `model_dump` + `JSONResponse`), including clamping and `rank` 0 → `null`.
- The render runs on the event loop in blocks of 8k logprob entries, with `await asyncio.sleep(0)` between blocks, like the output handler. No thread pool.
- Renders longer than one block hold a per-`ServingTokens` `asyncio.Lock`, so one API server renders one large response at a time. They share the loop's one core, so interleaving them adds no throughput; it only keeps every in-flight render's partial output alive at once. Single-block renders don't take the lock, so small requests never wait behind a large one.
- Rows that don't map directly to the per-entry shape fall back to the per-entry path for that choice. That covers irregular widths, repeated top-k ids, a sampled id not in slot 0, and values JSON can't represent.
- Unchanged: streaming, `output_mode="text"`, `logprobs=-1`, and requests with prompt logprobs. The response returns prompt logprobs as lists, so those requests keep list storage.

There is no HTTP API or output change.

**Behavior notes for direct Python users of `FlatLogprobs`.** Nothing inside vLLM depends on these, but code outside vLLM could:
- `token_ids`, `logprobs`, `ranks`, `start_indices`, `end_indices` and `decoded_tokens` are now read-only views over the columns rather than lists. Indexing, slicing, iteration, `len` and `==` against a list work as before, at O(1) per element read; they can't be mutated, and `json.dumps` needs `list(...)` first.
- `FlatLogprobs` is no longer a `@dataclass`: `dataclasses.asdict` / `replace` don't apply, and `repr` is a summary.
- Objects pickled by the old version don't unpickle with the new one.
- Stepped slices (`flat[::2]`) now return the right positions; the old code mixed in entries in between.

**Based on:** aoshen02/vllm#109 and aoshen02/vllm#111 (by @aoshen02), the Python "container hook" and "default fast render" PRs from the RFC #57479 work, ported to current main. The render targets the integer-id `GenerateLogProbs` shape of #58181 and respects `output_mode` (#58588).

**Not a duplicate.** No open PR changes how generate logprobs are stored or rendered:
- `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "57479 in:body"` returns only #58278 and #58314 (the `/v1/completions` serializer).
- #57442 (`return_token_logprobs`, the k=0 sampled-only path) is complementary: it handles k=0, this PR handles k>0. #57442 reads `FlatLogprobs.logprobs` and `start_indices`, which still return the same values here. #60915 (packed top-k) is stacked on this PR and no longer includes #57442.

Co-authored-by: @aoshen02

## Test Plan

> **Latest update:** merged current main (`fc9b7e6546`), including #59518's removal of the top-k cut and the `derender` output mode. The response build no longer uses a thread pool; see "Why no thread pool" below. Every number below was re-measured on this head unless marked otherwise.

```bash
pytest -q tests/test_logprobs.py tests/v1/engine/test_logprobs_processor.py tests/test_outputs.py \
  tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/
pre-commit run --files <changed files>   # incl. mypy 3.10 and 3.12 (manual stage)
```

- `tests/test_logprobs.py`:
  - the existing `FlatLogprobs` tests pass unchanged;
  - a new randomized test checks that mixes of every append path read back like `list[dict]` across buffer growth, mixed widths, `None` positions and ranks, and int32 / float32 overflow. I checked that it catches planted bugs in offsets, widening, stepped slices and ranks.
- `test_logprobs_processor.py`:
  - bulk-stored rows read like the list path, including `logprobs=-1` and irregular widths;
  - `_detokenize_logprobs=False` keeps no decoded tokens even with a tokenizer.
- `test_logprobs_render.py` (new) covers:
  - byte identity of the rendered body against `JSONResponse(model_dump)` for k ∈ {0, 1, 3, 8}, up to 1,500 rows, and n > 1;
  - rank 0, NaN, ±inf, −0.0 and large ids;
  - each fallback case;
  - the sampled id repeated in the top-k;
  - which requests use the flat storage;
  - that a multi-block render yields to the event loop with unchanged bytes, and that two large renders don't overlap while a small one doesn't wait.

Real-GPU end to end (GB200, Qwen3-0.6B, `--data-parallel-size 2`, default API servers), using a driver script that is not part of this PR:
- **Parity:** sequential greedy requests with `ignore_eos` and k ∈ {0, 1, 8, 128}, compared against main with the `created` timestamp blanked.
- **Abort stress:** 32 concurrent non-streaming requests at top-128, with `POST /pause?mode=abort` 45 s after submission. The client only receives bytes while the clock runs and parses afterwards. Server RSS is sampled from the process tree.

## Test Result

- **pytest:** `tests/test_logprobs.py`, `test_logprobs_processor.py`, `test_outputs.py` and all of `tests/entrypoints/scale_out/`: 532 passed, 7 skipped, 1 xfailed on GB200 at `341b5e40a7`, including the live-server and multimodal tests. The two later commits (a `FlatLogprobs.__eq__` rank fix with a test, and freezing `created` in the render tests, which flaked when a second boundary fell between two compared builds) were checked with the CPU tests: 96 passed, three runs in a row.
  - `tests/v1/engine/test_output_processor.py` needs the gated Llama tokenizer, which my host can't download (unchanged from the previous revision: with Qwen3-0.6B substituted, the same tokenizer-specific `test_stop_token` failures as the parent commit).
- **pre-commit:** clean, including manual-stage mypy.

**Parity:** the default response bytes are identical to main for all 16 requests (4 prompts × k ∈ {0, 1, 8, 128}, 256 tokens each). This was run on the head before the render lock; the lock doesn't change bytes, which the new unit test checks.

**Abort stress:** all 32 requests passed in every run. Each run left about 400k aborted positions, about 3.0 GB of response bodies. Two runs each.

| | main (`fc9b7e6546`) | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `/pause?mode=abort` returns | 82.1 / 86.1 s | 0.37 / 0.29 s |
| abort → all bodies received and parsed | 88.5 / 86.3 s | 7.4 / 6.7 s |
| peak RSS, largest server process | 7.8 GiB | 4.1 GiB |
| peak RSS, whole server process tree | 29.9 / 29.8 GiB | 17.5 / 18.2 GiB |

The `/pause` row is the event loop being freed. On main the pause request queues behind the per-entry builds of every aborted response.

The previous revision also compared main with `/generate` switched to the existing list-backed `FlatLogprobs` (160–177 s, slower than main), so turning on the existing class alone doesn't help.

**Why no thread pool.** The previous revision built large bodies in a two-thread pool. Profiling with py-spy showed the renderer holds the GIL about 78% of the time, so the pool overlapped only the remaining ~22% (numpy and large `bytes.join`):
- At DP2 (2 API servers, ~16 aborted bodies each) the pool was about 10–15% faster than rendering on the loop: 5.4–6.2 s vs 7.0–7.9 s abort → parsed.
- At the DP8 RL shape below, nearly all of the earlier gap came from block size, not threads. The pool version rendered 1,024-row blocks (~132k entries at k=128). Under 32 concurrent renders the renderer is memory-bandwidth bound, and big blocks slow each render 3.5× vs 2.2× for 8k-entry blocks. With small blocks, the pool version (10–12 s) and this PR (11–14 s) are close there.
- Without the render lock, rendering on the loop interleaved all of a server's large bodies and used about 3.5 GiB more RSS at DP2 (21.1–21.5 GiB). The lock removes that, with latency unchanged.

So this PR keeps the existing pattern (chunked work on the loop) and adds no thread pool or tunable.

**CPU microbenchmarks** (one request, one engine row per step, through `LogprobsProcessor` and `serve_tokens_full_generator`; best of several runs, pinned to one core; re-run on current main, matching the previous revision's numbers).

At 12.5k tokens × top-128:

| | list (main) | old `FlatLogprobs` | `ArrayLogprobs` | numpy `FlatLogprobs` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ingest per engine row | 157 µs | 14.6 µs | 3.7 µs | 4.0 µs |
| stored bytes per entry | 181 | 90 | 10.5 | 10.6 |
| response build | 5.4 s | 7.5 s | 0.41 s | 0.44 s |
| build peak memory | 1225 MiB | 1225 MiB | 181 MiB | 182 MiB |

The `ArrayLogprobs` column is from the previous revision. At the full RL shape (245,760 tokens × top-128), this PR builds the 1.79 GB body in 8.5 s with a 3.5 GiB peak. The body bytes are identical across all columns.

**RL shape at DP8, end to end (frontend only, mock engines).** RFC #57479's harness, adapted to current main: 8 CPU mock engine ranks behind the real `DPCoordinatorProc`, and 32 Python API servers on 112 cores of one GB200 node. 32 non-streaming requests, each with a 16k-token prompt and 245,760 output tokens at top-128, are held at the cap, then `POST /pause?mode=abort`. Two runs each.

| | main (`fc9b7e6546`) | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| abort → all bodies received | out of memory (harness stopped it at 456 GiB) | 12.5 / 13.6 s |
| `/pause?mode=abort` returns | — | 0.06 s |
| peak RSS, whole server process tree | 456 GiB when stopped | 123 / 132 GiB |
| peak RSS, largest server process | 14.5 GiB when stopped | 5.3 / 5.8 GiB |

Each body is 1.82 GB. The previous revision's 14.9 s doesn't reproduce on current main: as pushed it measures 19–22 s, because of the 1,024-row blocks described above. The mock emits 1,024 tokens per step and doesn't model the real DP pause consensus. The driver is not part of this PR.

Other `FlatLogprobs` paths, old → new, µs per position:

| | k=5 | k=128 |
|---|---|---|
| prompt logprobs via `LogprobsProcessor` (no tokenizer) | 1.7 → 0.09 | 18 → 0.16 |
| `extend` (DELTA aggregation) | 3.5 → 1.3 | 57 → 1.4 |
| sample logprobs with a tokenizer | 58 → 67 | 333 → 335 |
| DELTA streaming (ingest + `[-1:]` slice per step) | 9.4 → 20.8 | 64 → 62 |
| `flat[i]` | 2.6 → 5.3 | 47 → 48 |
| direct `append_logprobs_for_next_position` | 1.7 → 9.2 | 18 → 35 |

The small-k per-position paths are slower; the slice costs a few numpy calls. No server endpoint enables `flat_logprobs` for streaming.

commits.pr_title: [CI/Build] Make Python 3.14 the default for images and CI
commits.pr_body:
> **NOTE** this is https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65313 re-opened so that we can build the rocm image cache

## Overview

Make Python 3.14 the default: every Docker image and the CI that runs in them move from 3.12 to 3.14, the test lock files are resolved for 3.14, and the nightly smoke test that covered 3.14 now covers 3.12. It also includes the code and test fixes that 3.14 needs (see **Python 3.14 fixes**). Follows #34770 (3.14 support) and #60456 (nightly 3.14 smoke test); requested in #41264 (CVE fixes in newer Python).

## Claims

- All images build on Python 3.14: CUDA, CPU, Zen, XPU, ROCm and gfx1250 bases, s390x and ppc64le.
- CI tests run on 3.14 (they run in these images); the Ray compatibility check and the macOS smoke test target 3.14; the nightly `python_only_compile.sh` smoke test now installs into a 3.12 venv.
- Every package in the CUDA, ROCm, XPU and CPU runtime requirements, KV connectors included, has 3.14 wheels (except TPU's `nixl` pin, see risks).
- Code that broke on 3.14 is fixed: depyf debug dumps, the LMCache connector against LMCache 0.5.7, and three tests.

## Validation

The images build and CI runs on this branch. The fixes under **Python 3.14 fixes** came out of those runs. Before that, I checked:

- **Wheel availability for 3.14** (wheels only, `uv pip compile --no-build`, each requirement separately, x86_64 and aarch64 at glibc 2.35): all of `requirements/common.txt`, `cuda.txt`, `rocm.txt`, `xpu.txt`, `cpu.txt` resolve, including `torch==2.14.0`, `triton`, `flashinfer-python`, `numba`, `xgrammar`, `tilelang`, `nvidia-cutlass-dsl`. Platform indexes: AMD's TheRock index has cp314 for the pinned torch/torchvision/torchaudio/triton; `vllm_xpu_kernels` is `cp38-abi3` and the XPU torch/`auto_round_lib` have cp314; IBM's ppc64le index has cp314 for torch, torchvision, numpy, pyarrow, xgrammar; UBI 9 AppStream ships `python3.14-devel`/`-pip` for s390x and ppc64le.
- **Test lock files** regenerated through the pinned pre-commit `pip-compile` hooks (uv 0.13.6). Changes are only what 3.14 needs: pydantic 2.14 / pydantic-core 2.50; numpy 2.4.6, scipy, pandas, matplotlib, cramjam and other compiled packages moved to versions with cp314 wheels (the old pins only had sdists for 3.14); `datasets` >= 5 (below); stdlib backports `audioop-lts` and `standard-*` (XPU), and dropped `greenlet` / `torch-c-dlpack-ext` that only older Pythons pull in. XPU's resolution also moves pandas 3.0.5 -> 2.3.3.
- `pre-commit` passes, including `validate-docker-versions` (`docker/versions.json` regenerated).
- `therock_wheels.py`: `external-links` now takes `cp314` from `Dockerfile.rocm_base` and keeps `py3` wheels (checked directly).

## Details

**Changes.**

- Dockerfiles: `PYTHON_VERSION` default 3.12 -> 3.14 (`docker/versions.json` regenerated). How each gets Python: CUDA build stage from the manylinux image's `/opt/python/cp314-cp314`, runtime from deadsnakes; CPU and XPU via `uv venv --python`; ROCm bases via deadsnakes; s390x/ppc64le from UBI 9 packages.
- ROCm bases: install `python3.X-lib2to3` only below 3.13 (lib2to3 was removed in 3.13).
- s390x: drop the `python3.X-wheel` RPM, which UBI 9 doesn't have for 3.14; `pip install -U pip wheel uv` already installs it in the venv.
- `docker/build_vllm_ppc64le.sh`: takes `PYTHON_VERSION` (default 3.14) instead of hard-coded 3.12.
- `tools/vllm-rocm/therock_wheels.py`: link TheRock wheels for `Dockerfile.rocm_base`'s `PYTHON_VERSION` rather than `cp312`.
- CI: the nightly smoke step becomes `Python 3.12 Smoke` (`python-312-smoke-nightly`); the Mooncake disaggregation test's venv uses the image's `python3` instead of hard-coded 3.12; `check-ray-compatibility.sh` resolves for 3.14; macOS smoke test on 3.14.
- `.pre-commit-config.yaml`: CUDA, ROCm, XPU and CPU test locks compile for 3.14. The docs lock stays on 3.12, matching `.readthedocs.yaml`.
- `requirements/test/xpu.in`: `librosa >= 0.10`. Without it the 3.14 resolve backtracks into librosa 0.6.2, an sdist that imports the removed `imp` module and fails to build; it resolves to librosa 1.0.0 as before.
- Docs: quickstart, ROCm and XPU install pages and `AGENTS.md` recommend 3.14. ROCm's nightly (`rocm100`) wheels become 3.14-only, as they are built in the ROCm image. The XPU page's "Python 3.12 is a MUST" no longer applies: `vllm_xpu_kernels` is abi3.

- `docker/Dockerfile` (arm64 build stage): skip `PyNvVideoCodec` in the build venv. Its cp314 aarch64 wheels are manylinux_2_34 only, which the glibc 2.28 manylinux builder can't install. The build doesn't need it; the wheel and runtime image still get it.

**Python 3.14 fixes.**

- **depyf** (`vllm/compilation/depyf_compat.py`): depyf reads the next compiled-function id with `next(copy(itertools.count))`, and 3.14 can't copy itertools objects, so every compilation under depyf debug dumps failed. Read it from the counter's `repr` instead (test in `tests/compile/test_depyf_compat.py`).
- **LMCache 0.5.7** (the first release with 3.14 wheels): `lmcache >= 0.5.7.post1` (cu12: `0.5.7`). 0.5.7 takes token IDs as packed big-endian uint32 bytes (`token_bytes` / `packed_token_ids`), so `lmcache_mp_connector.py` now packs them from the request's `TokenBuffer` with numpy, and keeps passing lists to older LMCache. A test checks the bytes against LMCache's codec. ROCm: build LMCache v0.5.7.post1 from source (v0.5.3 predates 3.14) and check its renamed `lmcache.cuda_ops` extension.
- **Mooncake**: `mooncake-transfer-engine-rocm >= 0.3.14` in `requirements/rocm.txt` (CUDA's `>= 0.3.14` came from main).
- **`datasets` >= 5** in the CUDA and ROCm test requirements (was `<= 3.6`): older `datasets` caps `dill` < 0.3.9 and `multiprocess` < 0.70.17, which break on 3.14. The torchcodec reason for the cap no longer applies. Because datasets 4 changed streaming shuffle, `tests/evals/mrcr/mrcr_eval.py` reimplements the 3.x shuffle so the same seed still selects the samples its thresholds were calibrated on (checked against datasets 3.3.0).
- **Tests**: the xgrammar tests' `classmethod`-wrapped fixture never ran (3.14 no longer chains `classmethod` through other descriptors), so it's now a plain fixture; `test_argparse_utils.py` turns off the help colors 3.14's argparse adds under `FORCE_COLOR`.

**Blockers (resolved).** The CUDA images install `requirements/kv_connectors.txt`; LMCache (0.5.7.post1) and Mooncake (0.3.14, CUDA and ROCm) now have cp314 wheels on PyPI.

**Other risks to watch in CI.**

- ROCm base builds Triton, FlashAttention, AITER and MORI from source; untested on 3.14. Open: #51312 (torchao fix for 3.14 on ROCm). The AITER nightly wheel selection (`select_aiter_nightly_wheel.py`) follows the running Python, so needs cp314 AITER nightlies.
- TPU: `requirements/tpu.txt` pins `nixl==0.3.0`, which has no cp314 wheel (`nixl` 1.5.2 is `py3`).
- Source-only test dependencies (`arctic-inference`, `pytrec-eval-terrier` on aarch64) build from sdist as today; not yet built on 3.14.
- Interpreter performance and `torch.compile` behavior on 3.14 vs 3.12 still need an end-to-end serving comparison.

**Not changed:** tooling that only needs some Python (pre-commit workflow, CI helper workflows, wheel upload/nightly-index scripts, Rust frontend script runner, macOS wheel build), the 33 model recipes with `uv venv --python 3.12` (any supported version works), and example tracebacks in docs.

---

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Model Loader] Preserve CPU-offloaded Engram storage during layerwise reload
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Keep CPU-offloaded DeepSeek-V4.1 Engram tables in their existing host storage during layerwise weight reload. Their original weight loaders consume checkpoint tensors directly, while other layers retain the existing layerwise lifecycle.

Duplicate-work checks found no open PR implementing this Engram opt-out. #62063 addresses the analogous Qwen4Exp PLE issue by restoring on CPU and filtering non-local shards; this change preserves the original Engram allocations and loaders throughout the update. #65713 optimizes checkpoint copies and does not change layerwise initialization. Open PR searches covered `Engram layerwise`, `CPU offload reload`, and `"skip_layerwise_reload"`; the related reload RFC #59502 and its comments were also inspected.

## Claims

- Only `cpu_offload and peer_rows == 0` opts out: no meta restoration, online loader wrapping, temporary GPU table, or copy-back for this Engram storage path.
- Empty captured metadata excludes the offloaded table from `max_layer_reload_bytes()` without changing generic memory accounting.
- The normal `finish_reload()` -> `finalize_layerwise_reload()` -> `finalize_model_weights()` path remains intact, including module post-load hooks. Direct reload, GPU-resident Engram, and peer-HBM behavior are unchanged.

## Validation

Current head merges upstream `main` at `a7b75c977da92789278e6bcf818c888643459881`. The last implementation edit only reformatted the three reload guards using the repository-pinned Ruff 0.17.2; the previous formatting failure is fixed. Functional verification of the latest merged head remains pending.

```text
All checks passed!

5 files already formatted
git diff --check
# exit 0
```

The local pre-commit launcher could not initialize because Windows Git's shell failed with `NtCreateDirectoryObject ... 0xC0000022`; the pinned Ruff checks above were run directly. The [full GitHub pre-commit workflow](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/actions/runs/44216214086) **passed** on `8182b1d7261a7728a43796046d79914da0841992`, including the all-files manual hooks and the workflow's remaining steps.

The original implementation at `4807e0f771` has a separate [contributor-reported H20 validation report](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/68048#issuecomment-6951822959), including repeated weight/scale/lookup checks and GPU peak-memory measurements. That report predates the simplified tests and latest upstream merges; it is not a functional test result for the current head. No additional GPU tests were run for the latest upstream merges.

Two focused tests (four parameterized cases; not executed):

- A CPU-offloaded table beside a normal Linear, in layerwise and direct modes: memory accounting excludes the table; A -> B -> A updates of weight and scale retain storage and original loaders, load each input once, update CPU values immediately, preserve normal Linear reloading, and run post-load hooks on the new values.

Layerwise initialization previously saved the CPU table as kernel tensors, restored checkpoint-shaped parameters on meta, and wrapped its original loaders. commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Reject non-finite Newton steps in the acceptance estimator refit
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Reject non-finite Newton steps in the online acceptance estimator's refit (`_refit_kernel`), which drives adaptive verification. The NaN-only guards let `+inf` through, and one infinite step leaves the estimator non-finite for the life of the server.

## Claims

- An infinite slope or intercept step is now discarded and that coefficient keeps its previous value; NaN steps are discarded as before. Other coefficients still update.
- Finite steps are unaffected: the new predicate accepts exactly the finite values the old one did, and the non-negative-slope check is unchanged.
- No new buffers, parameters, or host syncs: the change is the predicate of two existing `tl.where` guards.

## Validation

New tests in `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_acceptance_estimator.py`, both driven through `OnlineAcceptanceEstimator.step()`:

- `test_refit_rejects_a_non_finite_slope_step`: nonnegative statistics `a_k = b_k = c_k = 2**16` (every feature equal to 1) for which fp32 rounds away the `L2` ridge, so the Schur complement is exactly 0 and the slope step is `4 / 0 = +inf`. Asserts the slope is unchanged and the intercepts get their exact update conditional on a zero slope step.
- `test_refit_rejects_only_non_finite_intercept_steps[inf, -inf, nan]`: a non-finite gradient is injected at one position to exercise the intercept guard directly (the accumulator can't produce one while the coefficients are finite). Asserts that position keeps its intercept and the others still update.

Before / after on an H100:

```bash
# Pre-fix kernel (base 191e5d5df2).
git checkout 191e5d5df2 -- vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/acceptance_estimator.py
pytest -v tests/v1/spec_decode/test_acceptance_estimator.py -k non_finite
# Fixed kernel, full suite.
git checkout HEAD -- vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/acceptance_estimator.py
pytest -v tests/v1/spec_decode/test_acceptance_estimator.py
```

<details>
<summary>Output</summary>

Before:
```text
tests/v1/spec_decode/test_acceptance_estimator.py::test_refit_rejects_a_non_finite_slope_step FAILED                                                                                                                                  [ 25%]
tests/v1/spec_decode/test_acceptance_estimator.py::test_refit_rejects_only_non_finite_intercept_steps[inf] FAILED                                                                                                                     [ 50%]
tests/v1/spec_decode/test_acceptance_estimator.py::test_refit_rejects_only_non_finite_intercept_steps[-inf] FAILED                                                                                                                    [ 75%]
tests/v1/spec_decode/test_acceptance_estimator.py::test_refit_rejects_only_non_finite_intercept_steps[nan] PASSED                                                                                                                     [100%]
```

After:

```text
tests/v1/spec_decode/test_acceptance_estimator.py::test_refit_rejects_a_non_finite_slope_step PASSED                                                                                                                                  [ 25%]
tests/v1/spec_decode/test_acceptance_estimator.py::test_refit_rejects_only_non_finite_intercept_steps[inf] PASSED                                                                                                                     [ 50%]
tests/v1/spec_decode/test_acceptance_estimator.py::test_refit_rejects_only_non_finite_intercept_steps[-inf] PASSED                                                                                                                    [ 75%]
tests/v1/spec_decode/test_acceptance_estimator.py::test_refit_rejects_only_non_finite_intercept_steps[nan] PASSED                                                                                                                     [100%]
```

## Details

**Root cause.** The slope step is `(g0 - Σ bₖg1ₖ/cₖ) / (a - Σ bₖ²/cₖ)`. The denominator is at least `L2` in exact arithmetic, but it is a difference of large raw-moment sums, so fp32 can cancel it to zero when features barely vary within each position (e.g. saturated at the ±40 clamp). The guard `x == x` rejects NaN but not `+inf`, and `w + inf >= 0` also passes the non-negative-slope check. Once the slope is `inf`, the intercepts follow to `-inf`, `ω·f + β` is NaN in `_predict_kernel`, and the NaN predictions poison the IRLS statistics every round after. Every later step is then masked to 0, so the coefficients never recover.

**Fix.** `tl.abs(x) < float("inf")` is false for NaN and ±inf and true for every finite value.

**Relation to #66673.** That PR clips steps to `±MAX_STEP_SLOPE` / `±MAX_STEP_BIAS` but keeps the `x == x` guard and floors `a` and `cₖ`, not the Schur complement. On its own, a `+inf` slope step therefore becomes a `+10` jump (by inspection, the slope test above would end at 10.5). The two compose: with this predicate the clip never sees an infinity. Whichever lands second has a small conflict on the two guard lines.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Core] Fix Gemma-4 MTP prefix-cache hit loss when lookahead block hashes are off
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Follow-up to #64808, which reported that Gemma-4 MTP gets about half the prefix-cache hits of MTP0.

Gemma-4 MTP falls into the coordinator fallback that flags every KV group as EAGLE, because its KV-shared draft layers own no group. So it is treated as a drafter that needs the EAGLE trailing-block drop, even though it writes no draft KV of its own.

`needs_eagle_block_drop()` now returns False for Gemma-4 MTP. As a result:
- **`"disable_lookahead_block_hashes": true`:** Gemma-4 MTP no longer drops the last block of a prefix-cache hit.
- **Default setup:** `num_hash_lookahead_tokens` for Gemma-4 MTP goes from 1 to 0, so its block hashes match MTP0's.
  - This fixes a hit loss when two requests share a prefix that ends exactly on a block boundary and differ at the next token (table below).
  - It also changes the block hashes Gemma-4 MTP produces, which matters for hash-keyed external KV stores.

Since #64096/#65448, KV connectors use lookahead hashes too, so the connector case from #64808 no longer reproduces on main.

## Results

Setup:
- B200, TP2
- `nvidia/Gemma-4-31B-IT-NVFP4` with `google/gemma-4-31B-it-assistant` as MTP3 drafter
- `TRITON_ATTN` backend, FP8 KV
- `--prefix-cache-retention-interval 8192`
- main `153dc04646`

**Probe from #64808:** 4 sequential requests sharing a 16384-token prefix, cached tokens per request. The connector rows show local GPU hit + CPU hit.

| Config | main | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| MTP0 | 0 / 16384 / 16384 / 16384 | – |
| MTP3 (default) | 0 / 16384 / 16384 / 16384 | 0 / 16384 / 16384 / 16384 |
| MTP3 + `disable_lookahead_block_hashes` | 0 / 8192 / 16256 / 16256 | 0 / 16384 / 16384 / 16384 |
| MTP3 + OffloadingConnector | 0 / 16384+0 ×3 | 0 / 16384+0 ×3 |
| MTP3 + SimpleCPUOffloadConnector | 0 / 16384+0 ×3 | 0 / 16384+0 ×3 |

**Exact boundary, default config:** two requests share exactly N tokens and differ at token N+1. Cached tokens on the second request:

| N | main | This PR | MTP0 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2048 | 0 | 2048 | 2048 |
| 8192 | 0 | 8192 | 8192 |
| 16384 | 8192 | 16384 | 16384 |

- **Outputs:** greedy outputs and acceptance (AL 3.53) are identical on main, this PR, and main with `disable_eagle_block_drop`. The check used 14 requests: 8 GSM8K + 6 long-prefix.
- **Unit test:** `tests/test_config.py::test_gemma4_assistant_needs_no_eagle_block_drop` is parametrized over the `gemma4_assistant` and `gemma4_unified_assistant` checkpoint types and goes through `SpeculativeConfig.hf_config_override`.
  - It fails on main (2/2) and passes with this PR (2/2).
  - It also fails if the rename in `hf_config_override` breaks.
- **Lint:** `pre-commit run --files` on the changed files passes.

## Scope and related PRs

- **Out of scope:** the second bug in #64808 (periodic SWA retention tail under EAGLE) stays open for drafters that write their own KV. Gemma-4 MTP no longer reaches that path with this change. Related: #64843, #64875.
- **Related PRs, measured on the same setup** (each applied on main `153dc04646`):

  | | main | This PR | #64875 | #66542 | #64875 + #66542 |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | Boundary N=2048 / 8192 / 16384, default | 0 / 0 / 8192 | 2048 / 8192 / 16384 | 0 / 0 / 8192 | 0 / 0 / 8192 | 0 / 0 / 8192 |
  | Probe, `disable_lookahead_block_hashes` | 0 / 8192 / 16256 / 16256 | 0 / 16384 ×3 | 0 / 16384 ×3 | 0 / 8192 / 16256 / 16256 | 0 / 16384 ×3 |

  #64875 fixes the `disable_lookahead_block_hashes` path generically (for any KV-shared drafter). The default exact-boundary case is fixed by this PR's lookahead 1 → 0 change. This PR touches only `vllm/config/speculative.py`, so it doesn't conflict with either.
- **Overlap:** #66234 removes the EAGLE block drop entirely and also excludes Gemma-4 MTP in the same function. If it lands first, it covers this fix, and this PR reduces to the test.
- **Design choice:** I excluded Gemma-4 MTP in `needs_eagle_block_drop()` rather than changing the coordinator fallback. Changing the fallback is the more general fix (that is what #64875 does, and the two are compatible), but it does not change the hash lookahead, so it does not fix the default exact-boundary case. This change touches only the one drafter known to write no KV.

commits.pr_title: [CI][Test] Ignore the key file path when checking that the watermark key is not quoted
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`tests/test_config.py::test_invalid_watermark_key_file_is_rejected_without_quoting_it[-5]` (added in #64550) fails on CI whenever the Buildkite job id starts with `5`. Seen in the daily Full CI [build 104023](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/104023) on `(MI355 DPX) Engine Core`, but it is platform independent.

## Claims

- The test checks that the invalid key file content is not quoted in the error, ignoring the key file path that the error message does quote.
- Test-only change; no behavior change.

## Validation

Same command on `main` (5a803779c3) and this PR, with a pytest base temp dir named like the failing CI job's (`vllm-56911fa022e1`):

```
pytest -q --basetemp=<dir>/vllm-56911fa022e1/pt \
  "tests/test_config.py::test_invalid_watermark_key_file_is_rejected_without_quoting_it"
```

| | Result |
|---|---|
| main | `1 failed, 4 passed`: `AssertionError: assert '-5' not in '... Watermark key file '.../vllm-56911fa022e1/pt/.../watermark_key' must contain a decimal integer ...'` |
| PR | `5 passed` |

`pytest tests/test_config.py -k watermark` with the default temp dir: `18 passed`.

## Details

The error message includes the key file path (`{path!r}`). CI sets the temp dir to `/tmp/vllm-<job id suffix>`, so the path contains `-5` whenever that suffix starts with `5` (about 1 job in 16), and the `content not in message` assertion trips on the path, not on a leaked key. Stripping the path before the check keeps the test's intent: a message that quotes the file content still fails.

No duplicate: no open PR touches this test.

commits.pr_title: [Model Loader] Remove the torchao reload decorator
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Implements the removal proposed in #65913: the torchao reload decorator (`support_quantized_model_reload_from_hp_weights`, added in #26327) is removed. It was a third reload lifecycle that ran only when user code called `model.load_weights` directly on an already loaded torchao model.

- `reload_weights` and the weight-transfer engines already reload torchao models through the shared reload lifecycle, which switched the decorator off (`tests/quantization/test_torchao.py::test_reload_weights`).
- The decorator assumed every weight arrives in one `load_weights` call, so it could not serve bucketed RL updates, and it skipped the model-level post-load hooks every other load path runs.
- The only caller in the repository was the reload step at the end of `test_online_quant_config_dict_json`.

Part of #54477 (one finish for every load and update path; F7, removing layerwise reload, needs torchao off its own layerwise path).

## Change

- Delete `model_loader/reload/torchao_decorator.py` and its exports.
- `AutoWeightsLoader.load_weights` is no longer decorated; `process_weights_after_loading` no longer sets `_do_torchao_reload`.
- Drop the `_do_torchao_reload` / `_original_do_torchao_reload` save and restore in layerwise reload and the sharded RDT engine.
- `test_online_quant_config_dict_json` no longer reloads through `model.load_weights`; `test_reload_weights` keeps covering torchao reload.

torchao quantization itself is unchanged: loading and `reload_weights` keep working.

Migration: replace `llm.apply_model(lambda model: model.load_weights(weights))` with `llm.collective_rpc("reload_weights")` (optionally with `weights_path`), or a weight-transfer engine for RL updates.

## Validation

`tests/quantization/test_torchao.py` on GB200 (nightly image, torch 2.14.0+cu130, torchao 0.18.0): 4 passed, 5 skipped. The 4 that run are `test_pre_quantized_model`, `test_online_quant_config_dict_json`, `test_online_quant_config_file` and `test_reload_weights`; the 5 skipped are unconditionally marked `skip` on main (torchao nightly).
