commits.pr_title: [Perf][Frontend] Seed the fast detokenizer with a prompt tail, not the full prompt
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Purpose

`FastIncrementalDetokenizer` seeds `DecodeStream` with the whole prompt, so each request's first output token decodes the entire prompt on the output-processing loop, stalling every other stream (17 ms at 100k tokens, ~40 ms with byte-fallback tokenizers). After its first emitted chunk `DecodeStream` keeps only the new ids, so the seed only shapes the first delta. This PR seeds it with a short prompt tail that reproduces that delta exactly:

- the tail holds 5 tokens (`INITIAL_INCREMENTAL_DETOKENIZATION_OFFSET`) that decode to text on their own, since Metaspace, WordPiece and leading-`Strip` decoders treat the start of the text specially;
- if the tail's text ends in U+FFFD (it starts inside the prompt's last character), it is extended by up to 3 tokens; if the prompt itself ends in U+FFFD, or the walk exceeds 256 tokens, the full prompt is used.

No new config or env var.

## Results

First output token (`FastIncrementalDetokenizer` construction + first `decode_next`), 100k-token prompt, median of 21, one core of an EPYC 9575F:

| tokenizer | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` (byte-level BPE) | 17.2-17.5 ms | 0.005 ms |
| `codellama/CodeLlama-7b-hf` (byte fallback) | 39.4-41.6 ms | 0.007 ms |
| `amd/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-Quark-MXFP4` (served below) | 18.6-18.7 ms | 0.005 ms |

Run from the repo root on each branch:

```bash
python - Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B codellama/CodeLlama-7b-hf amd/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-Quark-MXFP4 <<'EOF'
import glob, statistics, sys, time
from transformers import AutoTokenizer
from vllm.sampling_params import SamplingParams
from vllm.tokenizers.hf import get_cached_tokenizer
from vllm.v1.engine import EngineCoreRequest
from vllm.v1.engine.detokenizer import FastIncrementalDetokenizer

text = "".join(open(f).read() for f in sorted(glob.glob("vllm/v1/core/**/*.py", recursive=True)))
for name in sys.argv[1:]:
    tok = get_cached_tokenizer(AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(name))
    request = EngineCoreRequest(
        request_id="", prompt_token_ids=tok.encode(text, add_special_tokens=False)[:100_000],
        mm_features=None, sampling_params=SamplingParams(), pooling_params=None,
        arrival_time=0.0, lora_request=None, cache_salt=None, data_parallel_rank=None)
    next_id = tok.encode(" Hello", add_special_tokens=False)[0]
    times = []
    for _ in range(21):
        t0 = time.perf_counter()
        FastIncrementalDetokenizer(tok, request).decode_next(next_id)
        times.append(time.perf_counter() - t0)
    print(f"{name}: {statistics.median(times) * 1e3:.3f} ms")
EOF
```

**Serving.** Muse Spark Open (TEP4, FP8 KV, DSpark k=7) on 4x MI355X, server `--max-num-batched-tokens 16384`. Both arms ran at the same time on the two halves of one node, then swapped (two pairs per row):

```bash
vllm bench serve --dataset-name prefix_repetition \
  --prefix-repetition-prefix-len 100000 --prefix-repetition-suffix-len 128 \
  --prefix-repetition-num-prefixes 4 --prefix-repetition-output-len 32 \
  --num-prompts 64 --max-concurrency 8 --ignore-eos
```

| prefixes | output tok/s (main -> PR) | ITL p50, ms | ITL p99, ms |
|---|---|---|---|
| 100k, uncached | 38.0 / 37.9 -> 39.2 / 39.4 | 18.2 / 18.6 -> 21.9 / 22.4 | 1129 / 1093 -> 988 / 993 |
| 32k, uncached (`--prefix-repetition-prefix-len 32000`) | 123.2 / 124.6 -> 125.7 / 126.2 | 45.5 / 55.0 -> 55.0 / 54.3 | 812 / 803 -> 786 / 790 |
| 100k, cached (after a warm-up pass) | 170.4 / 147.8 -> 167.4 / 185.1 | 17.5 / 18.2 -> 20.0 / 21.5 | 148 / 138 -> 63 / 62 |

Output throughput does not regress. ITL p99 is lower in every pair: about 11% at 100k uncached, 2-3% at 32k, and 138-148 -> 62-63 ms with cached prefixes (at concurrency 8, several first-token stalls can land in one output-loop pass). ITL p50 is 2.5-4 ms higher in both 100k rows and within noise at 32k. This is accounting, not slower decoding: on main the first token waits for the full-prompt detokenization and the decode steps finished meanwhile arrive right behind it, so that time lands in TTFT; with this PR the first token arrives earlier and the same time falls between later chunks. Time to the last token is unchanged (streamed single requests: 150k-token prompt, TTFT 153 -> 90 ms, ITL 1.97 -> 2.09 ms, last token 1159 -> 1157 ms). Pairs of the same arm differ by up to 15% (cached row, main), so the throughput differences are within run-to-run noise.

## Test plan

```bash
pytest tests/detokenizer/test_decode_stream_seed.py   # 121 passed (CPU; downloads 11 ungated tokenizers)
pytest tests/tokenizers_/test_detokenize.py           # 581 passed, 251 skipped
```

The new file streams a continuation twice, seeded by `get_decode_stream_seed` and by the full prompt (the seed function monkeypatched to identity), through `FastIncrementalDetokenizer.decode_next`, and requires identical deltas: every cut of a prompt with multi-byte characters, combining marks, emoji and whitespace runs, followed by 0-40 special tokens, both `skip_special_tokens` settings, plus random token ids. When the prompt's text does not end in U+FFFD, it also requires the seed to hold at most 8 tokens with text. Tokenizers: one in-process tokenizer per context-dependent decoder (ByteLevel, ByteFallback + Fuse + Strip, Metaspace, WordPiece, BPEDecoder suffix, CTC) and 11 ungated hub tokenizers (byte-level BPE, Llama byte fallback, BERT, T5, XLM-R). If `get_decode_stream_seed` returns `prompt_token_ids[-5:]` instead, 35 of the 121 tests fail. The file runs in the "Async Engine, Inputs, Utils, Worker" step.

## Notes

- **Prompts ending in U+FFFD (#48853, pre-existing).** If the prompt's text ends in U+FFFD (a token-id prompt cut inside a multi-byte character, or ending in invalid byte tokens), `DecodeStream` streams its whole seed text in the first delta, so main returns the entire prompt text there. Seeding with a tail would only shorten the leaked text, so this PR keeps full-prompt seeding in that case: output is unchanged and the cost stays O(prompt). #48854 routes these requests to the slow detokenizer.
- **Limits.** A decoder that rewrites text across tokens after `Fuse` (e.g. a multi-character `Replace`) could in principle differ; no tokenizer we checked has one. For a token-id prompt whose byte-fallback run is invalid only before the tail, the tail streams the correct text where full-prompt seeding streams the whole prompt.
- **Supersedes #51281 and #57330** (stalled), which truncate to a fixed 32 / 128-token tail. Per @njhill's review, a fixed tail is not always safe: prompts ending in 32+ skipped special tokens lose the first output token's leading space with Metaspace / WordPiece / `Strip` decoders, which this PR avoids by counting only tokens that decode to text. Thanks to @elad-inferize and @cqulilujia for the bounded-tail idea.
- With the fastokens patch applied (`VLLM_USE_FASTOKENS=1`, fastokens 0.3.6), the test file passes for `gpt2` and `Qwen3-0.6B`; fastokens does not load the other hub tokenizers.

commits.pr_title: [Model][LoRA] Enable LoRA for GTE (bert_with_rope) embedding and reranker models
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Enables LoRA for the GTE `bert_with_rope` models: `GteNewModel` (`Alibaba-NLP/gte-multilingual-base`), `GteModel` (`Snowflake/snowflake-arctic-embed-m-v2.0`) and `GteNewForSequenceClassification` (`Alibaba-NLP/gte-multilingual-reranker-base`). Supersedes #40581 (co-authored with its author).

## Claims

- These checkpoints fuse the GeGLU MLP as `up_gate_proj` = `[up; gate]`. vLLM split it at load and reordered it into `gate_up_proj` = `[gate; up]` for `GeluAndMul`. LoRA only renames adapter tensors, so an adapter on that projection would land on the wrong halves (the mapping in #40581 expects separate `gate_proj`/`up_proj` adapters, which these checkpoints do not have). The MLP now keeps the checkpoint's `up_gate_proj` layout and computes `gelu(gate) * up`, so a single-slice mapping applies as trained, as for ModernBERT's `Wi`. The GTE models opt into this layout with `fused_up_gate = True`; other `geglu` `bert_with_rope` models keep the gated MLP and its loading.
- `GteNewForSequenceClassification` gets a LoRA name mapper that keeps the `new.` prefix, and `self.config` for the LoRA manager.
- Base-model outputs are unchanged.

## Validation

New `tests/lora/test_gte_lora.py`: serving a random PEFT adapter on `qkv_proj`, `o_proj`, `up_gate_proj` and `down_proj` (all 12 layers) must match serving the checkpoint with the LoRA delta merged into its weights, to within 5% of the merged-vs-base difference. The reranker adapter also replaces the `classifier` head through `modules_to_save`. Runs on CPU (fp32) were done locally, with this branch's Python sources on the vLLM CPU wheel.

| check | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `test_gte_lora_matches_merged[embed]`, `[classify]` | fails: `LoRA is not supported for GteNewModel` | 2 passed |
| same test with the merged reference's `up_gate_proj` halves swapped (sensitivity check) | n/a | fails: mismatch is 72% of the signal |
| same test with the adapter's `classifier` head dropped (sensitivity check) | n/a | fails: mismatch is 70% of the signal |
| same test on `snowflake-arctic-embed-m-v2.0` (local only) | n/a | passed |
| base outputs without LoRA, 3 prompts, fp32 | reference | gte-multilingual-base, reranker, arctic-embed and nomic-embed-text-v1 bit-identical |

GPU, one RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell (SM120), fp16, before the review follow-up (which leaves the GTE MLP unchanged), on the vLLM post-merge image for this branch's base with this branch's `bert_with_rope.py` copied in:

| check | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/lora/test_gte_lora.py` | n/a | 2 passed |
| `pooling_mteb_test/test_gte.py`, `test_snowflake_arctic_embed.py` | n/a | 6 passed, 5 passed (rest skipped as in CI) |
| 4096 prompts (946k tokens), median of 5: gte-multilingual-base | 3.277 s | 3.255 s |
| same, gte-multilingual-reranker-base | 3.165 s | 2.971 s |
| base outputs, 64 prompts: embedding max abs diff / min cosine | reference | 1.3e-4 / 1.000000 |
| base outputs, 64 prompts: reranker logit max abs diff | reference | 1.1e-3 |

`pre-commit run` passes.

## Details

- The MLP activation is now `gelu` followed by a multiply instead of the fused `GeluAndMul`. Throughput is unchanged within run-to-run noise (table above); the GEMMs dominate in these 0.3B encoders.
- Out of scope: Nomic BERT (its `fc11`/`fc12` already map to `gate_up_proj` correctly) and Jina v3 (merges its own task LoRA at load); RoBERTa embedding LoRA from #40581 already landed in #61033.
- Duplicate check: #40581 is the only open PR for this; its author is a co-author here.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KV Cache] Don't size KV cache groups from draft-only sliding-window buckets
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

`_get_kv_cache_groups_uniform_page_size` sets the KV cache group size from the smallest layer bucket. Since #64109, a DFlash/DSpark drafter's sliding-window layers get their own tail-only manager, and therefore their own small bucket. That bucket then sets the group size and forces padding onto the target's full-attention layers. This PR leaves draft-only **sliding-window** buckets (SWA, SWA-MLA, DFlash/DSpark) out of the group-size choice, so the small windowed draft bucket is padded instead. Draft-only buckets with an unbounded manager, such as MQA drafters, still size the groups as on main.

## Claims

- On a model with a small draft-only bucket, the target's full-attention layers no longer get padding layers. For Muse Spark Open (46 sliding-window + 16 full-attention layers, 5-layer DSpark drafter), the full-attention layers go from 4 groups of 5 (16 padded to 20) back to 1 group of 16 with no padding. That removes 20% of full-attention KV memory per token.
- Grouping is unchanged for models without a draft-only sliding-window bucket. That includes drafters that share a bucket with the target (EAGLE full attention, gpt-oss + eagle) and draft-only full-attention/MQA buckets, which would otherwise be padded on every token.

## Validation

Two new unit tests, both using a Muse-shaped target (46 SWA + 16 full):
- `test_draft_only_bucket_does_not_set_the_group_size`: adds a 5-layer DSpark draft. It fails on main and passes with this PR.
- `test_full_attention_draft_only_bucket_still_sets_the_group_size`: adds a 1-layer full-attention draft in its own bucket. It passes on main and with this PR, and fails on this PR's first commit, which skipped every draft-only bucket.

Run on PR head `0a60b31` (base `2aa3f0e`), CPU-only:

```
$ pytest -q tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_planning.py::test_draft_only_bucket_does_not_set_the_group_size \
            tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_planning.py::test_full_attention_draft_only_bucket_still_sets_the_group_size
# main (2aa3f0e)
FAILED test_draft_only_bucket_does_not_set_the_group_size     # assert [4, 4, 4, 4] == [16]
1 failed, 1 passed in 0.78s
# first commit (c1883ec, skipped all draft-only buckets)
FAILED test_full_attention_draft_only_bucket_still_sets_the_group_size
1 failed, 1 passed in 0.45s
# this PR (0a60b31)
2 passed in 0.43s
```

Full `tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_planning.py` and `tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py` on the same CPU-only host:
- main: `91 failed, 110 passed in 64.39s`
- PR: `90 failed, 111 passed in 44.85s`

The only differences are the new tests. `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` pass. The 90 shared failures are all the environment (`RuntimeError: Failed to infer device type`, no GPU); none are new.

<details>
<summary>Production observation that motivated this (Muse Spark Open NVFP4, TP4/EP4 on GB200, DSpark k=3, fp8 KV)</summary>

Same model, flags and default `gpu_memory_utilization` on both builds; numbers from startup logs and `/metrics` (`vllm:cache_config_info`, `vllm:kv_offload_config_info`):

| | before #64109 (`a2bcb5657`) | after (`536f3caa2` base) |
|---|---|---|
| padding warning | `Add 13 padding layers, may waste at most 25.49%` (sliding-window bucket 46+5=51 → 64) | `Add 4 padding layers ... 8.70%` (SW 46 → 50) and `Add 4 padding layers ... 25.00%` (full 16 → 20) |
| groups | `kv cache group sizes (16, 16, 16, 16, 16)` | `kv cache group sizes (64 × 15)` |
| available KV memory / GPU | 44.1 GiB | 43.0 GiB |
| GPU KV cache size | 3,386,630 tokens | 2,484,461 tokens |
| CPU offload tier, same 644,245,094,400 bytes | 19,508,390 tokens (524,288 B/chunk) | 15,644,611 tokens (655,360 B/chunk = ×1.25) |

The CPU tier ratio is exactly 20/16, the full-attention padding. The GPU pool also drops with the 64-token blocks, which is outside this PR.
</details>

**Not yet validated end to end:** I'll serve Muse Spark Open with this patch on GB200 and add the startup log (`kv cache group sizes`, `GPU KV cache size`) here. Expected: 5 groups and the full-attention padding warning gone. Keeping this as a draft until then.

## Details

- **Root cause:** #64109 gives DFlash/DSpark drafter sliding-window layers `DFlashSlidingWindowManager`. `can_share_block_table` requires the same manager config, so they no longer join the target's sliding-window bucket. `_get_kv_cache_groups_uniform_page_size` then uses the smallest bucket (the drafter's 5 layers) as the group size, and every other bucket is padded to a multiple of it.
- **Why padding moved somewhere expensive:** padding sliding-window or tail-only draft layers costs memory only for the window or tail. Padding full-attention layers costs memory for every token of context.
- **Fix:** compute `min_num_layers`/`max_num_layers` without buckets that are draft-only (`KVCacheLayerConfig.is_draft`) **and** use a `SlidingWindowManager` subclass (SWA, SWA-MLA, `DFlashSlidingWindowManager`). It falls back to all buckets if nothing else is left. Draft-only buckets with other managers (full attention/MQA) are unbounded: padding them costs memory on every token, so they keep counting as on main. The draft bucket is then padded up to the target's group size, e.g. 5 → 16 (11 padding layers). That's cheap because `DFlashSlidingWindowManager` backs only the tail blocks.
- **Limitation:** this keeps the existing min/max heuristic (see the `FIXME` above it). A draft-only bucket is the case where that heuristic reliably picks badly, so it's the only one handled here.

commits.pr_title: [EC Connector] Add ECTieringConnector filesystem tiering for encoder cache
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Add filesystem tiering for native encoder-cache offloading. CPU memory serves as the primary tier, with encoder outputs persisted to filesystem storage for reuse when the working set exceeds CPU-cache capacity.

## Claims

- Support asynchronous CPU-to-filesystem write-through and filesystem-to-CPU promotion.
- Prefetch encoder outputs during request queuing and retry preparation during scheduling admission.
- Support persistent cache reuse across service restarts .
- Reduce replay mean TTFT by **34.41%** and increase request throughput by **25.84%** in the workload below.

## Validation

### Benchmark configuration

- **Model:** Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct, BF16, TP=1.
- **Hardware:** NVIDIA H800.
- **Cache:** 8 GiB CPU, 128 GiB filesystem; encoder-cache working set of 22.416 GiB.
- **Serving:**  max-model-len=8192, GPU memory utilization=0.8.
- **Clients:** eight processes, total concurrency 48.
- **Workload:** 32 independent warmup images, 1,024 fill requests, followed by three replays of the same images; 100 output tokens per request.
- **Settings:** prefix caching disabled, filesystem backpressure disabled, fsync disabled.

Three configurations were compared: no EC offloading, CPU-only ECCPU, and filesystem tiering.

### Combined replay results

Each configuration completed 3,072 replay requests. Percentiles are calculated from pooled request samples; throughput uses the combined request-window duration.

| Metric | No offloading | CPU-only | Tiering | Tiering vs. no offloading |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Mean TTFT (ms) | 1102.80 | 1080.68 | 723.30 | −34.41% |
| p50 TTFT (ms) | 1102.94 | 1082.92 | 712.34 | −35.41% |
| p95 TTFT (ms) | 1657.96 | 1624.19 | 1133.85 | −31.61% |
| Mean TPOT (ms/token) | 14.13 | 13.86 | 12.74 | −9.83% |
| Mean end-to-end latency (ms) | 2501.31 | 2453.23 | 1984.40 | −20.67% |
| Request throughput (req/s) | 18.84 | 19.21 | 23.71 | +25.84% |

### Cache-path verification

All **12,384 requests** across the three configurations, including warmup, completed successfully.

Each tiering replay recorded:
- 1,024 successful filesystem reads.
- 1,024 CPU-load selections.
- Zero recomputation selections.
- Zero filesystem read/write failures.

## Details

### Usage

Enable Model Runner V2 and configure `ECTieringConnector` through `--ec-transfer-config`:

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 \
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct \
  --dtype bfloat16 \
  --ec-transfer-config '{
    "ec_connector": "ECTieringConnector",
    "ec_role": "ec_both",
    "ec_connector_extra_config": {
      "ec_cpu_bytes": 8589934592,
      "secondary_tiers": [{
        "type": "fs",
        "root_dir": "/data/ec-cache",
        "capacity_bytes": 137438953472,
        "n_read_threads": 4,
        "n_write_threads": 2,
        "fsync": false,
        "backpressure": {
          "enabled": false
        }
      }]
    }
  }'
```

This configures an **8 GiB CPU cache** and a **128 GiB filesystem tier**. Keep `root_dir` on persistent storage to reuse compatible files after restarting the service.

Filesystem options:

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `type` | Secondary-tier type; currently `"fs"` | Required |
| `root_dir` | Absolute cache-directory path | Required |
| `capacity_bytes` | Filesystem-cache capacity used for LRU eviction | Required |
| `n_read_threads` | Read-priority worker count | `4` |
| `n_write_threads` | Write-priority worker count | `2` |
| `fsync` | Synchronize file contents before publication | `false` |
| `backpressure.enabled` | Enable adaptive write admission | `true` |
| `backpressure.high_water_s` | Upper threshold for smoothed write latency, in seconds/MiB | `0.010` |
| `backpressure.low_water_s` | Lower recovery threshold, in seconds/MiB | `0.002` |

Backpressure reuses the native KV offloading `EMABackpressureDetector` to adapt cache-write admission to filesystem pressure. 


### Write-through and loading

Encoder outputs first follow the existing ECCPU GPU-to-CPU path. Once a CPU entry is ready, it is pinned while its complete allocated blocks are written asynchronously to a `.ec` file. The write pin is released after completion.

Request arrival initiates CPU-cache checks and filesystem prefetch. Shared prefetch pins protect CPU entries while interested requests remain.

During scheduling admission:
- GPU-cache hits proceed without waiting for lower tiers.
- Ready CPU entries use the ECCPU CPU-to-GPU load path.
- Preparation is retried if arrival-time prefetch could not start.
- CPU allocation failure before read submission permits a cache miss and encoder recomputation.

### Lookup and persistence
A stable namespace identifies compatible files using model identity, revision, dtype, encoder-output dimensions, and file-format version. Startup recovery rebuilds the index and capacity accounting; LRU eviction manages filesystem-cache capacity.

Compatible instances can discover and reuse files in the same directory. Capacity accounting and active-read protection are local to each instance.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] Fix MultiConnector handshake metadata routing
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fix handshake metadata routing in `MultiConnector` by collecting metadata from every sub-connector and returning each one only its own entries. This fixes startup failures when combining NIXL with a KV store on a pipeline-parallel prefill instance, and when multiple sub-connectors produce handshake metadata.

## Claims

- `MultiConnector(NIXL, MooncakeStoreConnector)` starts with a PP2 prefill instance at TP1 and TP2 in both push and pull mode. PP pull transfer also requires #65336.
- Each sub-connector receives its own handshake metadata, or an empty dict if it reports none.
- Across 36 prompts in both modes, PP2 produces exactly the same output token IDs and top-5 logprobs as PP1 at the same TP, including the second pass that loads prompts from MooncakeStore.

## Validation

**Unit tests**

The regression test places a real `ExampleConnector`, which reports no handshake metadata, between two test connectors that report distinct metadata:

```bash
pytest -v tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_multi_connector.py::test_handshake_metadata_reaches_only_its_connector
```

On main with only the test added:

```text
E   ValueError: ExampleConnector received pp_rank > 0 handshake metadata but does not support PP-disaggregated KV transfer.
1 failed
```

With this PR: **1 passed**.

- `test_handshake_metadata_of_subclass_reaches_every_connector` passes on main and with this PR. It verifies the existing behavior for subclasses such as Dynamo's `PdConnector`, which report a single sub-connector's metadata.
- Nearby MultiConnector tests (`-k "handshake or worker_metadata or overrides_all_base_methods or lookahead or role_follows"`): **20 passed**.
- pre-commit passes.

**End-to-end tests**

Single-node B300 GPUs; Qwen3-0.6B; eager execution; greedy decoding; one request at a time; prefix caching disabled on P and D.

- **P:** TP1 or TP2, PP1 or PP2; `MultiConnector(NixlConnector or NixlPushConnector, MooncakeStoreConnector)`; Mooncake standalone store over RDMA.
- **D:** PP1, matching P's TP; `NixlConnector` or `NixlPushConnector` as `kv_consumer`.
- **Workload:** 36 prompts of 127–8192 tokens, 32 output tokens with top-5 logprobs, sent twice. In pass 2, P loads the prompts from MooncakeStore.

The runs used these revisions and NIXL roles on P:

| TP | Push | Pull | NIXL role on P |
|---|---|---|---|
| TP1 | main + #65336 + this PR | main + #65336 + this PR | `kv_producer` |
| TP2 | main + this PR | main + an earlier revision of #65336 + this PR | `kv_both` |

TP2 was tested before #65336 required `kv_producer` for NIXL with PP > 1. Push works on main with this PR; pull additionally requires #65336.

Without this PR, PP2 P fails at startup in both modes on main (`kv_both`) and main + #65336 (`kv_producer`):

```text
ValueError: MooncakeStoreConnector received pp_rank > 0 handshake metadata but does not support PP-disaggregated KV transfer.
```

With this PR, push and pull produce the same counts:

| P | Pass | D prompt tokens from NIXL | NIXL transfers | P tokens loaded from MooncakeStore | P tokens computed |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TP1, PP1 | 1 | 82,652 | 36 | 35,840 | 46,812 |
| TP1, PP1 | 2 | 82,652 | 36 | 79,744 | 2,908 |
| TP1, PP2 | 1 | 82,652 | 72 | 35,840 | 46,812 |
| TP1, PP2 | 2 | 82,652 | 72 | 79,744 | 2,908 |
| TP2, PP1 | 1 | 82,652 | 72 | 35,840 | 46,812 |
| TP2, PP1 | 2 | 82,652 | 72 | 79,744 | 2,908 |
| TP2, PP2 | 1 | 82,652 | 144 | 35,840 | 46,812 |
| TP2, PP2 | 2 | 82,652 | 144 | 79,744 | 2,908 |

There are **0 failed transfers or notifications**, with one NIXL transfer per request, TP rank and PP stage of P.

At each TP, the output token IDs and top-5 logprobs from PP1 pass 2, PP2 pass 1 and PP2 pass 2 exactly match PP1 pass 1 on **36/36 prompts**, in both modes.

## Details

Previously, `MultiConnector.get_handshake_metadata()` returned the first non-`None` sub-connector metadata. The engine core merged worker reports into a `{(pp_rank, tp_rank): metadata}` dict, which `MultiConnector` forwarded to every sub-connector.

This caused two failures:

- **PP startup:** a sub-connector such as `MooncakeStoreConnector` received NIXL's metadata and hit the base-class rejection of `pp_rank > 0`, despite reporting no metadata of its own.
- **Multiple metadata producers:** later sub-connectors received the first one's metadata instead of their own. For example, `UMBPStoreConnector` after NIXL failed even without PP with `ValueError: UMBP workers must report exactly one namespace, got []`. This was checked with UMBP's in-memory test runtime; with this PR, UMBP receives its own metadata.

The worker now returns `MultiKVConnectorHandshakeMetadata`, a tuple with one entry per sub-connector, following the existing `MultiKVConnectorWorkerMetadata` pattern. Both handshake setters split the merged reports by sub-connector and omit that child's `None` entries. Every sub-connector is still called, including those receiving an empty dict.

Subclasses that return a single sub-connector's metadata, such as Dynamo's `PdConnector`, retain the existing behavior: every child receives that metadata unchanged. Connectors that report handshake metadata without supporting PP still encounter the base-class PP check.

Related: #56185 (closed) proposed a MooncakeStore-only no-op setter. This PR fixes routing in `MultiConnector` for all sub-connectors.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Responses] Keep empty reasoning blocks in Responses output
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

When a model emits an empty reasoning block, vLLM drops it from the Responses API output. Clients that send earlier output back as input, like Codex, then replay that turn with no reasoning. This PR keeps the empty reasoning instead.

## Claims

- Non-streaming `/v1/responses` returns an empty reasoning item for an empty reasoning block instead of leaving it out.
- Streaming no longer drops `""` reasoning when it ends in the same delta that starts a tool call.
- `None` still means "no reasoning", so models without reasoning are unaffected.

## Validation

Three new regression tests. Each fails on `main` and passes with this PR:

```bash
python -m pytest \
  "tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_responses_utils.py::TestResponsesUtils::test_build_output_items_keeps_empty_reasoning" \
  "tests/parser/test_streaming.py::test_parse_delta_empty_reasoning_kept_on_boundary" \
  "tests/reasoning/test_k2_horizon_reasoning_parser.py::test_composed_streaming_empty_reasoning_before_tool_call"
```

| Test | Checks | `main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_build_output_items_keeps_empty_reasoning` | Non-streaming: `""` gives a reasoning item, `None` gives none | `assert isinstance(items[0], ResponseReasoningItem)` fails (first item is the message) | Pass |
| `test_parse_delta_empty_reasoning_kept_on_boundary` | Streaming, generic `<think>` and Hermes parsers, empty block and tool call in one delta | No delta has `reasoning == ""` | Pass |
| `test_composed_streaming_empty_reasoning_before_tool_call` | Streaming, K2 Horizon parsers, one token at a time | `assert [] == ['']` | Pass |

Wider check: `tests/parser`, `tests/reasoning` and `test_responses_utils.py`, run with and without the fix (CPU, macOS):

| | Passed | Failed |
|---|---|---|
| `main` | 8,202 | 96 |
| This PR | 8,205 | 93 |

The only difference is the 3 new tests. The other 93 failures are identical on both sides and unrelated to this change: Cohere tests need the optional `cohere-melody` package, and the Mistral tool-call tests fail on `main` too in this environment.

The same change has also run on a K2 Horizon 375B Codex endpoint for about 100 Codex sessions (multi-turn, sub-agents, streaming) with no broken turns on replayed reasoning.

`ruff check` and `ruff format --check` pass with the pinned ruff 0.17.2.

## Details

**Root cause.** The reasoning parser returns `reasoning=""` for an empty block such as `<think></think>`. Two truthiness checks then treat `""` like `None`:

- `build_response_output_items` (`responses/utils.py`): `if reasoning:` skips the reasoning item.
- `DelegatingParser.parse_delta` (`parser/abstract_parser.py`): `if reasoning_from_this_batch:` drops `""` when reasoning ends in the same delta that starts the tool-call phase.

Both now check `is not None`.

**Why it matters.** Codex sends previous output items back as input on every turn. Without the reasoning item, the replayed assistant turn has no reasoning. For K2 Horizon, whose chat template requires a reasoning field on every earlier assistant turn, the next request fails or is rendered wrongly. K2 Horizon emits an empty block before many tool calls.

**Side effect.** `parse_delta` is shared with Chat Completions, so Chat Completions streams now also send `reasoning: ""` in this case. Non-streaming Chat Completions already returned `reasoning: ""`, so streaming now matches it.

**Not a duplicate.** I searched open PRs for empty reasoning in Responses output and in `parse_delta` and found none. #49130 and #56285 touch `responses/utils.py` but not this check.

AI assistance was used. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

---

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Bound multi-module MTP re-prefill to valid request history
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Prevent short requests from re-prefilling the previous occupant's token IDs, hidden states and embeddings when multi-module MTP reuses a request-state slot. Fixes #66886.

Technical validation is complete. The human submitter has confirmed reviewing the newly added tests and final refinements and running the relevant tests.

## Claims

- Record the valid, right-aligned history length per request-state slot, reset it on admission with a device-side `zero_()`, and bound both re-prefill readers by that length.
- A real-request regression reproduces foreign tokens and negative positions with the original production file and passes with the fix, using the same test and real Qwen weights.
- This existing PR predates overlapping draft #67132. Refreshed searches confirm the overlap, and this update extends #66951 with end-to-end coverage and GPU evidence.

## Validation

Rebased onto upstream `main` at `2be71b1831385115258a3158103ae0a711e3e037`; current head is `eb5425f223565ca51401dd285fc229501cda3695`. The six PR patches are unchanged according to `git range-diff`. The GPU results below were collected before the rebase on the stated source; GPU validation has not been repeated on this rebased head.

<details>
<summary>Post-rebase local checks</summary>

macOS ARM64, Python 3.12.12, on `eb5425f223565ca51401dd285fc229501cda3695`. All applicable pre-commit hooks passed, including Ruff, mypy and CI selection. `git diff --check` passed.

```sh
.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --files \
  vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/multi_module_mtp/speculator.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_target_dependent_ar_speculator.py \
  tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/mtp/qwen3_5/test_mtp.py
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_target_dependent_ar_speculator.py -q --tb=short
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/mtp/qwen3_5/test_mtp.py \
  --collect-only -q -k 'reused_slot or test_mtp_correctness'
```

```text
32 passed, 3 skipped, 14 warnings in 4.09s
2/7 tests collected (5 deselected) in 0.74s
```

The two kernel regression cases and existing CUDA Graph case were skipped locally because no GPU is available. The request test was collected, not executed.

</details>

The trimmed tests were run on NVIDIA RTX PRO 4000 Blackwell 24GB, driver 595.112.07, Python 3.12.3, Torch 2.14.0+cu132, CUDA 13.2 and Triton 3.8.0. All runs unset `TRITON_INTERPRET` and enabled `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`.

The tested source was `787153659adca05046be1c03ac298a8385067396` plus the two-file test reduction committed as `a0ed1c53b`. The baseline used the same source and tests, replacing only `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/multi_module_mtp/speculator.py` with its version from merged-main base `ba5477f3df9f3fe058db69b3f2ef4954d0a31e89`. Both used that base's `cu132` precompiled artifacts. Separate import paths and SHA256 hashes were verified.

| Trimmed GPU validation before rebase | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Complete worker test file, including both embedding-mode regression cases and the existing CUDA Graph case | 33 passed, 0 skipped in 13.66s |
| Real-request slot-reuse regression, fixed production file | 1 passed in 204.07s |
| Same request regression, original production file | 1 failed in 68.34s on the expected stale token and negative position |
| Applicable pre-commit hooks, including Ruff, mypy and CI selection | Passed |
| `git diff --check` | Passed |

The kernel regression covers a two-token request rejecting all four drafts, with and without input embeddings, and persistent slot 1 distinct from batch index 0. It exactly checks token IDs, positions, the last valid index, hidden states and embeddings.

The real-request regression runs a long request followed by a two-token prompt, with `max_num_seqs=1`, four speculative tokens, prefix caching disabled and the existing synthetic zero-acceptance sampler. It checks the first two observed drafter input windows and the deterministic final output. A read-only forward hook uses a scoped `gpu_sync_allowed()` region and checks positions before model forward.

Raw baseline evidence shows token 9007 from the preceding request in the new request's context.

```text
AssertionError: Invalid MTP replay inputs: ids=[9007, 5001, 42, 42], positions=[-1, 0, 1, 2]
================== 1 failed, 49 warnings in 68.34s (0:01:08) ===================
```

With the fix, the exact input assertions pass for `([5001,42],[0,1])` and `([5001,42,42],[0,1,2])`, followed by output `[42] * 8`.

```text
Running 33 items in this shard
.................................                                        [100%]
33 passed in 13.66s

================== 1 passed, 49 warnings in 204.07s (0:03:24) ==================
```

Run from the corresponding isolated checkout, with `PYTHONPATH` selecting that checkout.

```sh
export PYTHONPATH="$PWD"
unset TRITON_INTERPRET
export VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error
uv run --no-sync .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_target_dependent_ar_speculator.py -q --tb=short
uv run --no-sync .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/mtp/qwen3_5/test_mtp.py::test_multi_module_mtp_reused_slot_has_only_current_request_inputs \
  -v -s --tb=short
```

The baseline runs the request command above. Its first attempt failed during initialization because the isolated checkout lacked the precompiled package's generated FlashMLA Python files. After completing the same package dependencies, the unchanged test reached the request and produced the stale-token assertion above. The initialization failure is retained in the logs and excluded from the reproduction evidence.

<details>
<summary>Earlier validation retained as historical evidence</summary>

The earlier, larger tests ran on RTX PRO 4000 Blackwell 24GB, driver 595.91.07, Torch 2.14.0+cu132 and Triton 3.8.0, with source `ba08a8c` plus the then-current tests and base `54b29e254` precompiled artifacts.

| Earlier check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Native 24-case kernel regression, original kernels | 4 failed, 20 passed |
| Same kernel regression, fixed kernels | 24 passed |
| Entire worker test file at that revision | 55 passed |
| Original real-request regression covering one- and two-token prompts | Fixed version passed in 74.05s |
| Real-model per-module selection and acceptance with default CUDA graphs and strict sync checking | Passed |
| Reference GSM8K, 1319 questions, 5-shot, greedy, max 256 output tokens | Accuracy 0.346 |
| Two-module MTP GSM8K, same evaluation | Accuracy 0.344 |
| Reference vs two-module MTP exact text comparison | 96/100 matches, required 81 |
| Combined multi-module correctness test | Passed in 239.40s |

The earlier accuracy evaluation used real Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B-Base target weights with a second random-weight MTP module, two speculative tokens and default CUDA graphs. Reference and speculative runs used the same local model configuration and target weights. The original 0.20 GSM8K threshold and 81/100 output-match requirement were retained. The extra multi-module correctness parametrization has been removed following review, restoring the existing correctness test. These earlier evaluation results remain historical evidence.

</details>

Validation covers this synthetic two-module Qwen configuration on one NVIDIA GPU. The exact slot-reuse request runs eagerly. No throughput benchmark was run.

## Details

The cache writer updates only the tail of its fixed-capacity history row. Short requests can leave entries from an earlier occupant in the prefix. Previously readers derived their history length solely from the rejection count, allowing those entries into the new request's draft context. The new per-slot int32 device counter records the available tail length in the existing writer launch and limits token and hidden-state/embedding reads consistently.

The request-admission reset uses a one-element view and `zero_()`. Earlier strict-sync validation caught a host synchronization from scalar assignment, and the final implementation passes that validation.

The existing worker and Qwen3.5 MTP Buildkite suites select the regression files and list the changed production area in their source dependencies. The change adds no public configuration. AI assistance was used for implementation, tests, investigation, GPU execution and this description. The human submitter remains responsible for reviewing and defending the final change and running relevant tests.

commits.pr_title: [CI] Enroll 8 CPU steps in automatic sharding
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Enrolls eight CPU steps in automatic runtime sharding, and the AMD mirror of one of them. They are the first CPU steps to be enrolled. Main has recorded per-test timings for them since vllm-project/ci-infra#908, so the generator can plan them.

No other open PR enrolls these steps.

| Step | Was | Planned shards |
|---|---|---:|
| CPU V1 Others | one job | 3 |
| CPU Multimodal + Config | one job | 2 |
| CPU Reasoning + Renderers | one job | 2 |
| CPU Tool Parsers | one job | 1 |
| CPU Qwen4 Exp | one job | 1 |
| CPU Basic Models Other | one job | 1 |
| CPU Docker Build Metadata (+ MI250 mirror) | one job | 1 (+1) |
| CPU Multimodal Processor | 4 fixed pytest-shard jobs | 8 |

## Claims

- Every test each step runs today still runs, exactly once across its shards.
- The one-shard steps still run as one job; they are enrolled so they split on their own when their tests grow.
- Multimodal Processor drops its `--num-shards/--shard-id` flags and `parallelism: 4` for planned shards: 8 jobs of about 16 minutes instead of 4 of over 30.
- No test is added, removed or changed.

## Validation

- [`/ci run` 104003](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/104003) on head `ab193d526a` (rebased onto main `2be71b1831`, built merged with main `536f3caa28`) passed with no retries. Against main [103990](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/103990) (V1 Others, Multimodal + Config, Reasoning + Renderers) and [103981](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/103981) (the rest), every step ran the same node IDs: 0 missing, added, changed or duplicated. Multimodal Processor: 2011 tests in 8 jobs, slowest 22.0 min instead of 37.1, machine time +4%.
- Machine time against main: V1 Others +17%, Multimodal + Config +10% (+6% to +19% over earlier PR builds), Reasoning + Renderers +9%, the one-job steps within noise (+1% to +7%). Earlier builds: [103644](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/103644), [103655](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/103655), [103719](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/103719).
- Sharding harness (the real generator renders each step, and every shard's commands run against a stand-in test tree) for the four multi-shard steps, as a PR build and as a main build: each test runs in exactly one shard.
- Per-job details in the build note comment.

## Details

- **V1 Others costs more machine time, on purpose.** In build 103644 its 3 shards matched main's 3317 node IDs, slowest 12.5 min against main's 31-minute single job, for 18% more machine time (about 2 minutes of setup repeated per shard). We take that trade for time to signal.
- **Decision for a maintainer: cut the repeated setup instead of the shards.** Each CPU job spends about 2 minutes before its first test (measured in V1 Others shard 1, build 103644): about 30 s of git checkout, then about 80 s pulling the `<commit>-cpu` test image, because each CPU test job runs on a fresh instance with an empty Docker cache. Two commits' CPU images share 91% of their 2.4 GB of layers, so a warm cache would leave about 0.2 GB to pull. Option: pre-pull a recent main `-cpu` image into the AMI of the two queues these steps run on (`small_cpu_queue_premerge` for `cpu-small`, `medium_cpu_queue_premerge` for `cpu-medium`), the way the daily CPU AMI build already warms the image-build queues. The image-build and release queues don't run these tests and need no change. This would cut every CPU test job's start, sharded or not; it is not part of this PR and the saving is not measured.
- **Multimodal Processor** measured +4% machine time against today's 4 fixed jobs in build 104003 (-2% in 103719), with the slowest job going from 37.1 to 22.0 minutes (19.5 in 103719). #68030 makes the same change to this step; whichever merges second drops it.
- **Timeouts are unchanged.** Per-job `timeout_in_minutes` stays as it is. If a build gets no plan (no timings, or `VLLM_CI_RUNTIME_SHARD` off), each step runs as one job; for Multimodal Processor that is the whole suite, which can outrun its 125-minute limit where today it is 4 fixed jobs. Fallback-aware timeouts are planned as a central timeout setting rather than per-step increases.

---

commits.pr_title: [CI] Enroll Entrypoints Integration (API Server) and Rust Frontend Serve/Admin in automatic sharding
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

**Trunk change: needs line-by-line review** (it changes how CI steps' tests are split across jobs).

Enrolls every remaining step whose pytest commands set `PYTHONPATH`, with their AMD mirrors, in automatic sharding: Entrypoints Integration (API Server) and Rust Frontend Serve/Admin Coverage. LM Eval Spec Decode, the third such step, is left as on main; see Details. These waited on ci-infra#825 (merged), which installs the sharding plugin where a command's own `PYTHONPATH` can't hide it; before it, every shard of these steps failed with `No module named 'runtime_shard_plugin'` (#62513, build 97706).

## Claims

| Step | Was | Planned shards |
|---|---|---:|
| `entrypoints-integration-api-server` | 4 fixed shards | 7 |
| `amd-entrypoints-integration-api-server` | 4 fixed shards | 4 |
| `rust-frontend-serve-admin-coverage` | one job | 2 |
| `amd-rust-frontend-serve-admin-coverage` | one job | 1 |

- Every test runs exactly once across the shards, with the same environment and filters as before.
- API Server's shard-1-only `dev/rpc` command and its `--num-shards/--shard-id` flags give way to the planner, so new test files no longer need placing by hand.
- API Server and its mirror use about 40% less machine time than main; Rust Frontend and its mirror stay within main's own run-to-run spread. Every shard finishes under the 20-minute target.

## Validation

- [`/ci run` 104096](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/104096) on head `1d054463d4` (rebased onto main `5d4a24ea33`, built merged with main `6f687a0836`): every job passed, no retries. Earlier builds with Spec Decode still in: [104005](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/104005), [104019](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/104019).
- Against main [104023](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/104023), every step and mirror ran the same tests (API Server 875, Rust Frontend 100), with 0 missing, added, changed or duplicated. The only ID differences are a version-derived parameter in `test_metrics.py` that the PR image renders differently; same tests, same outcomes.
- Machine time against main 104023 / 104059: API Server -46% / -38% and its AMD mirror -40% / -42%; Rust Frontend -13% / +9% and its AMD mirror -8% / +8%, within main's own run-to-run spread for that step. Slowest shard 19.2 min.
- The `PYTHONPATH` commands' tests are among those node IDs, so the plugin loaded under them; its guard fails a job whose pytest runs without the shard plan.

## Details

- **LM Eval Spec Decode is left out.** Sharded, its slowest shard ran 26.7 min (build 104005), over the 22-minute bar, because one configuration alone takes about 26 minutes; and it used 15% more machine time than main, since each shard repeats compilation, autotuning, model loading and CUDA graph capture that one job does once. A nightly step gains little from a shorter wall time at that cost, so it stays one job as on main, with its AMD mirror.
- **API Server** goes from 4 fixed shards to 7 planned ones on NVIDIA (4 on AMD). `entrypoints/serve/dev/rpc` now runs in whichever shard the plan gives it rather than always in shard 1.
- **Timeouts unchanged.** `timeout_in_minutes` stays per job. If a build gets no plan (no timings, or `VLLM_CI_RUNTIME_SHARD` off), API Server runs as one job instead of its old 4 fixed shards and can outrun that timeout; fallback-aware timeouts belong in a central timeout setting.
- **Overlap:** no other open PR enrolls these keys.
- AI assistance (Claude Code) was used.

commits.pr_title: [CI] Upload command spans first and give big job-end flushes more time
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Trunk change: needs line-by-line review (`.buildkite/scripts/ci-otel/`, which every traced CI job loads).

On a shard with thousands of tests, the job-end span flush in `ci_otel.py` sends every spooled span within one 3-second budget, in spool-file name order. The command span sits in its own file, which can sort after the pytest process's file; when the budget runs out, the test spans already uploaded are left without the command span they point to, and the timings endpoint can't use that build. Since 2026-11-15 this hit nearly every build of `(L4) Quantization Kernels` and `(L4) MoE Kernels`, and on 2026-11-17 both fell back to one unsharded job and timed out (unblocked on the dashboard side by vllm-project/vllm-dashboard#307, which skips such builds; this PR stops the loss).

This sends non-test spans first and gives the flush more time when it has more to send.

## Claims

- The job-end flush uploads command spans before test spans, so a timeout can drop some test spans but never their parent.
- Its budget is 3 s for one batch plus 3 s per additional batch (a batch ends at 2,000 spans or 1 MiB, whichever comes first), capped at 20 s. Jobs with one batch, almost all of them, keep today's 3 s.
- The shell's guard around the flush goes from `timeout 4s` to `timeout 25s`, above the cap. The Python budget limits each network wait to the time left, so a slow or hung endpoint normally ends the flush at the budget; the shell guard is the hard wall-clock limit, for an endpoint that trickles its response. That limit is now 25 s for every traced job, one-batch jobs included (was 4 s).
- A failed or slow upload still can't change a job's exit status.

## Validation

- `pytest .buildkite/scripts/ci-otel/tests/test_ci_otel.py`: 71 passed (7 new cases): command spans first, budget per batch count and cap, three slow uploads all landing inside the flush budget, a batch that exactly fills the byte limit, and the shell guard above the cap.
- Mutation testing (mutmut) on the changed lines: 30 killed, 0 survived.
- The real `ci_otel.py flush` process against a local upload server that takes 1.2 s per request, with the command span's spool file sorting last:

  | test spans | main | this PR |
  |---|---|---|
  | 3,126 | all land | all land, command span in the first batch |
  | 8,412 | 6,000 land, command span lost, "timed out" | all land in 6.4 s |
  | 40,000 (hypothetical: about 3.5 times the largest job today) | (not run) | stops at the 20 s cap with 32,000 test spans and the command span landed |
  | 8,412, endpoint hangs | gives up at 3.1 s, command span lost | gives up at its 15 s budget with the command span landed, before the shell's 25 s guard |

- The largest test step today (11,540 tests when it runs as one job: 6 batches, an 18 s budget) against the same server at 2.5 s and 2.9 s per request: every span lands (15.5 s, 17.9 s).
- `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` (the pinned v0.17.2) clean.
- Not shown yet on CI: a PR build doesn't trace, and the span ingest only accepts uploads from `main` (and one treatment branch), so the end-to-end check is the first main builds after merge: every shard of the two steps above should have its command span again.
- No open PR touches `ci_otel.py`'s flush (searched open PRs for `ci_otel` and flush/upload terms).

## Details

- **Sort in the flush, not in the spool.** Ordering by span name at flush time covers every writer (pytest, commands, GPU samples, BuildKit) without changing how files are named. Turned down: renaming command spool files so they sort first, which leaves the order to a naming convention.
- **Budget per batch instead of one larger flat timeout.** A flat 20 s would let a hung endpoint add 20 s to every traced job; scaling keeps small jobs at 3 s.
- **3 s per extra batch** gives each request more than twice the about 1.2 s seen in the failing jobs' timing, since the endpoint's real latency isn't measured here. Up to six batches (12,000 spans, more than any job sends today) get their full allowance; past that the 20 s cap applies, and whatever doesn't fit in 20 s is test spans, never the command span.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Core] Drop streaming updates that would overflow max_model_len
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Streaming-input sessions merged the next input chunk into their prompt without checking the accumulated length against `max_model_len`, wedging or crashing the engine. This PR rejects such an update at merge time, parks the session so a shorter update can continue it, and adds scheduler-level and e2e regression tests.

Fixes #62707 (V2 evidence). Same defect family as #42489, whose fix PR #42502 has been stalled with merge conflicts since Sep 30.

## Claims

- A streaming update whose merged session would leave no room for a sampling step within `max_model_len` is now dropped (with a server-side warning) instead of being merged.
- The session stays **resumable** (`WAITING_FOR_STREAMING_REQ`): a subsequent, shorter update continues it normally. This is the softer outcome requested in the [#42502 review](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/42502#issuecomment-3624351968) ("rather than FINISHED_LENGTH_CAPPED, end the reply and leave the session resumable").
- No regression for sessions whose updates fit: the merge path is unchanged apart from the pre-check, which only trips in the previously-fatal region.

## Validation

Ran on an aarch64 dev box (Jetson Thor) against this checkout with `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`, `pytest 7.4.4` via `uv`/`.venv` per the contributing guide.

**1. New tests fail on base (`main` @ b3b0bc3059) for the reported reason:**

```
$ VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py -q -k "overflow"
4 failed, 15 deselected
```

The regression test diverges exactly at the unguarded merge (`assert <RequestStatus.WAITING: 1> == <RequestStatus.WAITING_FOR_STREAMING_REQ: 4>`), i.e. main merges an update that pushes the session to 19 tokens with `max_model_len=16`.

A standalone scheduler-level drive of the same scenario on base shows the downstream failure — the session is merged beyond the limit and then wedges with empty schedules forever:

```text
after stop: status=WAITING num_tokens=19        # > max_model_len=16, merged anyway
turn 3 (poisoned):
  scheduled={'session': 5} num_tokens=19 computed=16   # prefill clamped mid-way
  scheduled={} num_tokens=19 computed=16               # wedged: zero-token clamp (skip), never progresses
```

On the V2 runner this zero-clamp path is the one that produced the negative `num_scheduled_tokens` (-14 / -36) and the `assert num_tokens > 0` EngineCore crash reported in #62707; on current main the clamp is floored at zero, so the session wedges in `RUNNING` and the client hangs with no further outputs and no error.

**2. With this fix, everything passes:**

```
$ VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/streaming_input/ -q
28 passed, 2 errors   # the 2 errors are pre-existing GPU-only tests that cannot
                      # set up on the cpu platform (get_accelerator_view_from_cpu_tensor);
                      # verified identical on base via git stash
$ VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/test_request.py tests/v1/engine/test_output_processor.py tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py -q
48 passed, 34 errors  # error set byte-identical between base and fix (environment-only)
```

**3. No regression in the core scheduler suite.** `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py` run on base vs. with the fix (237 tests): `54 failed, 183 passed` on both, with **byte-identical failure lists** — all 54 are environment failures on this box (model-architecture inspection subprocess / GPU-only fixtures), unaffected by this change.

**4. CI coverage / disclosure.** The new scheduler-level tests run in the `V1 Executor + Worker` step (`pytest -v -s v1/streaming_input`, H200 MIG 18GB). The new e2e test in `tests/v1/e2e/general/test_streaming_input.py` runs in the `E2E` step (`pytest -v -s v1/e2e/general ...`). **I could not run the GPU e2e test locally** (the dev box is aarch64 Jetson Thor without a CUDA build of this checkout); it mirrors the existing patterns in that file (`finish_reason` turn-boundary counting, event-based input pacing, `asyncio.wait_for` timeout instead of sleeps) and needs CI/human confirmation. The e2e test asserts: the overflowing chunk produces no turn, the session continues with a fitting chunk (2 turn boundaries), and the stream finishes with `has_unfinished_requests() == False`.

No model evaluation is included: the change does not alter generation for sessions that stay within `max_model_len` (the guard only trips in the previously-fatal region, where no valid output exists to preserve).

## Details

**Root cause.** `_update_request_as_session` extends the session prompt with (all outputs but the last sampled token) + the update's tokens, with no length check. `check_stop` only fires when output tokens are appended, so nothing bounds the session at a turn boundary. Once the merged `num_tokens` exceeds `max_model_len`:

1. The waiting-branch prefill schedules the full remaining chunk (it has no `max_model_len` clamp), computing positions past the limit, and drives `num_computed_tokens` past it.
2. The running-branch clamp `max_model_len - num_computed_tokens - num_sampled_tokens_per_step` then goes negative. On current main `_reserve_prefill_lookahead` floors it to zero, so the request is skipped every step and **wedges permanently in `RUNNING`** while occupying a sequence slot; on the V2 build in #62707 the negative value reached `num_scheduled_tokens` and killed EngineCore (`assert num_tokens > 0` → `EngineDeadError` for the client).

**Fix.** Reject the update **before** mutating the session when the merged token count `(num_tokens - 1) + len(update.prompt_token_ids)` plus one sampling step would exceed `max_model_len`. On rejection:

- `_handle_stopped_request` (queued-update path) parks the session in `WAITING_FOR_STREAMING_REQ` and returns `False`, reusing the exact bookkeeping of the existing queue-empty path (the caller's `continuing_reqs` machinery then re-enqueues it into the KV-holding waiting queue).
- `add_request` (parked-session path) needs no change: the rejected update simply leaves the session parked.

The boundary matches the one reviewed in #42502: a merged session of `max_model_len` tokens is rejected (`>=`), one token less is accepted; the accepted edge case yields at most a single-sampled, length-capped turn, which mirrors how an ordinary request with a `max_model_len`-boundary prompt behaves.

**Relationship to #42502.** Not a duplicate: #42502 predates the V2 scheduler split, has been unmergeable (conflicts) since Sep 30, and its outcome (`FINISHED_LENGTH_CAPPED` for the whole session) is the one the maintainer asked to soften. This PR implements the softer outcome on current main; #42502 can be closed in favor of it.

**Limitations / follow-ups.**

- The dropped chunk is reported only via a server-side `logger.warning`; there is no per-chunk error surfaced to the client stream (the collector has no channel for it today). Surfacing a turn-level `model_context_window_exceeded` — as the `/v1/messages` path does (#59616) — is a natural follow-up, as is the bounded-session design discussed in #51948/#53876.
- Sessions already parked at the boundary reject every further update until closed; they hold KV blocks exactly like any other parked streaming session and are cleaned up when the client closes the input generator.

---

commits.pr_title: [Multimodal] Allow disabling embed inputs per modality in `--limit-mm-per-prompt`
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Add `embeds` option to `--limit-mm-per-prompt` so that precomputed embedding inputs can be opted out for a single modality while `enable_mm_embeds` stays on for the others.

## Claims

- `--limit-mm-per-prompt '{"video": {"count": 0, "embeds": false}}'` disables the video modality completely: `video_embeds` inputs are rejected and the modality no longer sizes the encoder cache.
- With 0-limits for all modalities and `enable_mm_embeds=True`, the encoder cache budget of Qwen2.5-VL-3B drops from 114688 to 16384 tokens once video embeddings are opted out.
- Pixtral-family models keep their image encoder CUDA graph when `enable_mm_embeds` is on but image embeddings are opted out. (This is unreachable in upstream main, a bugfix on its own)
- Default behavior is unchanged (`embeds` defaults to `true`).

## Validation

```shell
python -m pytest \
  tests/config/test_multimodal_config.py tests/multimodal/test_registry.py \
  tests/renderers/chat_utils/test_video.py -v
# 101 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (115.86 s, rc=0)
```

The three new tests fail on the base commit because the option does not exist there:

<details>
<summary>New tests on main</summary>

```text
$ python -m pytest \
    tests/config/test_multimodal_config.py::test_mm_embeds_disabled_per_modality \
    tests/multimodal/test_registry.py::test_encoder_budget_excludes_modality_with_embeds_disabled \
    tests/renderers/chat_utils/test_video.py::test_parse_chat_messages_video_embeds_disabled_modality -q
E       pydantic_core._pydantic_core.ValidationError: 1 validation error for MultiModalConfig
E       limit_per_prompt.embeds
E         Unexpected keyword argument [type=unexpected_keyword_argument, input_value=False, input_type=bool]
FAILED tests/config/test_multimodal_config.py::test_mm_embeds_disabled_per_modality
FAILED tests/multimodal/test_registry.py::test_encoder_budget_excludes_modality_with_embeds_disabled
FAILED tests/renderers/chat_utils/test_video.py::test_parse_chat_messages_video_embeds_disabled_modality
3 failed in 2.82s
```
</details>

### E2E test

GLM-5.3-Flash served with `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` KV offloading.

**Before:** With the video limit set to 0, the video modality still sizes the encoder cache:

```shell
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash -tp8 -ep \
  --kv-transfer-config.kv_connector SimpleCPUOffloadConnector \
  --kv-transfer-config.kv_role kv_both \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt.video 0
```

```log
(EngineCore pid=765) INFO 11-16 22:24:26 [utils.py:428] Using BLHNC KV cache layout.
(Worker_TP7_EP7 pid=1173) INFO 11-16 22:24:31 [encoder_cache_manager.py:378] Raising encoder_cache_size from 16384 to 32242 tokens so one video item fits.
...
```

**After:** With video embeddings opted out, the "Raising encoder_cache_size ... so one video item fits" line no longer appears:

```shell
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash -tp8 -ep \
  --kv-transfer-config.kv_connector SimpleCPUOffloadConnector \
  --kv-transfer-config.kv_role kv_both \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt.video.count 0 \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt.video.embeds false
```

## Details

### Motivation

`enable_mm_embeds` is a single global switch, and a modality with 0-limit is treated as embedding-only when it is on: it still accepts `*_embeds` and is included in the encoder cache budget. Since #56379, EC/KV consumers turn `enable_mm_embeds` on automatically, and KV offloader counts as a KV consumer. A deployment that only enables KV offloading therefore has no way to fully disable a modality: `--limit-mm-per-prompt.video 0` still reserves encoder cache space for the largest video item.

### Design

- New attribute: `BaseDummyOptions.embeds: bool`, and `MultiModalConfig.is_mm_embeds_enabled(modality)` combines it with `enable_mm_embeds`.
- Per-modality embedding decision uses the new method: the embedding-only set in `MultiModalBudget`, the embeddings check in `parse_mm_data`, the count-validation bypass in the chat item tracker, and Pixtral's `pixels_only` check for the encoder CUDA graph.
- It is opt-out rather than opt-in because the automatic enablement on consumers overrides any opt-in list.

### Diuplicate check

Searched open PRs and issues for `enable-mm-embeds modality`, `limit-mm-per-prompt embeds`, and `enable_mm_embeds encoder cache limit 0`; none address this.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][Ray] Kill RayExecutorV2 actors before joining the monitor thread
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`RayExecutorV2.shutdown()` joins its monitor thread before killing the Ray actors, so it waits up to the monitor's 5 s `ray.wait()` poll. Kill the actors first: the monitor's `ray.wait` returns at once, `_should_stop()` is true, and the loop exits. Split out of #68288 at review; **land after #68288**, which fixes the EngineCore reaping race that this faster teardown makes frequent.

## Claims

- Ray-backend engine teardown drops from a median of 4.06 s (range 2.07-6.87) to about 1 s.

## Validation

MI300X/MI355X, local, `LLM(..., distributed_executor_backend="ray", tensor_parallel_size=2)` create/generate/delete at a random 0-5 s phase.

| Run | Teardown | False "force killing remaining process EngineCore" |
|---|---|---|
| `main` | median 4.06 s (2.07-6.87) | |
| This change alone (without #68288) | median 0.96 s (0.82-1.10) | 7/10 test runs (`test_basic_correctness.py -m 'distributed(num_gpus=2)' -k ray`) |
| This change on top of #68288, 20 runs | about 1.2 s | 0/20 |

## Details

After `ray.kill`, the monitor thread's `ray.wait` returns and `_should_stop()` is true, so `_join_monitor_thread()` returns quickly instead of waiting out the poll. The faster teardown lets EngineCore exit inside the liveness monitor's 1 s wake window, which exposed the double-reap race fixed in #68288; that is why this must land after it.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Peek at the EngineCore exit status instead of reaping it in the liveness monitor
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`CoreEngineProcManager` reaps each EngineCore from two threads: the liveness monitor reads `proc.exitcode` (a `waitpid(WNOHANG)`) while `shutdown()` joins the process. When the monitor reaps first, the main thread's `waitpid` gets ECHILD, `Popen.poll()` turns that into "still running", and `shutdown()` logs `force killing remaining process EngineCore` and calls `kill_process_tree()` on a pid that was already reaped. The monitor now reads the exit status with `os.waitid(..., WNOWAIT)`, which does not reap, so `shutdown()` is the only reaper.

## Claims

- An EngineCore is reaped by exactly one thread: no false "force killing remaining process EngineCore" after a clean exit, and no SIGKILL sent to an already-reaped (possibly reused) pid.
- A clean exit is no longer misread as a failure when the sentinel fires a moment before the child becomes reapable (`exitcode` was still `None` there).
- No locking: the monitor only observes, and the weakref finalizer is unchanged from `main`.

## Validation

MI355X, local.

| Check | `main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Model of the pattern: monitor checks the exit status on sentinel wake while the main thread runs `vllm.v1.utils.shutdown()`, 400 teardowns | 122 false force-kills | 0 |
| Same model, children exiting with 0 or 1 and no shutdown: failures reported correctly | 400/400 | 400/400 |
| `LLM(Qwen3-0.6B, tensor_parallel_size=2)` create/generate/delete at a random 0-5 s phase, mp backend, 20 runs | | 0 force-kills |
| Same, Ray backend with the kill-before-join reorder from #68526 applied (the fast teardown that made the race common), 20 runs | | 0 force-kills, teardown ~1.2 s |
| `v1/engine/test_startup_watch_processes.py`, 20 runs | | 23 passed every run |
| `v1/engine/test_engine_core_client.py` + `v1/shutdown` | 24 passed, 29 failed | identical: same 24 passed, same 29 failed |

The 29 failures in the last row fail identically without this change: on this snapshot of `main`, `CacheConfig` rejects `enable_extensible_kv_cache=None` while building the engine config (a pydantic `bool_parsing` error), before any EngineCore starts.

## Details

The second reaper came with #35862 (b5e608258e), which moved the monitor into `CoreEngineProcManager.monitor_engine_liveness()` and added `proc.exitcode` there; before it, the monitor only waited on sentinels.

`_exited_cleanly()` relies on the EngineCore being a direct child, which holds for both start methods `get_mp_context()` uses (fork and spawn). Without `WNOHANG` the call blocks through the short gap between the sentinel firing and the child becoming reapable; it never reaps, so it cannot race `shutdown()`. If `shutdown()` has already reaped the child, `waitid` raises `ChildProcessError` and the exit is treated as clean, since shutdown is under way. macOS before Python 3.13 has no `os.waitid`, so there it falls back to `proc.exitcode`.

Per review, the Ray kill-before-join reorder that was in this PR moved to #68526, to land after this fix: it makes EngineCore exit within the monitor's wake window, which made the race frequent.

No open PR fixes this (searched `waitpid race engine monitor`, `monitor_engine_liveness`, `force killing remaining process`).

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to draft this change. Every line was reviewed by the submitter.

commits.pr_title: [Feature][KV Connector] Notify connectors after startup KV cache preparation
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Add `KVConnectorBase_V1.on_kv_cache_ready()` after final KV sizing, before the first request. Connectors can finish deferred registration at this boundary.

## Claims

- Every worker completes preceding device work before calling the hook. Eager mode uses the same boundary.
- The default is a no-op. MultiConnector forwards the call to each child.
- Initialization waits for the hook and propagates exceptions. The callback must return in bounded time: no hook timeout or cancellation is provided, and an unbounded wait blocks startup indefinitely. Background tasks are not awaited.

## Validation

Runtime/test revision `424a2e5747e2a769fd349ee68fd167ce0dbde03e`; branch based on main `68a62a2940a90ccea0d61c1159651c98fbe8e6bf`. Source-level checks on macOS arm64, Python 3.12.13, PyTorch 2.13.0: **48 passed, 4 deselected**. Run from the checkout root in a [vLLM development environment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/68a62a2940a90ccea0d61c1159651c98fbe8e6bf/docs/contributing/README.md#developing), with pytest/tblib and the `facebook/opt-125m` configuration cached:

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 PYTHONPATH="$PWD" \
  uv run --no-project .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_kv_cache_ready.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_multi_connector.py \
  -k 'not before_first_request and not multi_example_connector_consistency and not multi_connector_mixed_hma_disables_hybrid_kv_cache' -q
```

The CPU cases use real workers and connectors to check child notification and exception propagation. Copying the new test file to the base revision and running its `-m cpu_test` cases produces **2 failures**, both `AttributeError: 'WorkerBase' object has no attribute 'notify_kv_cache_ready'`; both pass on this head. Changed-file pre-commit passed, including mypy and CI test tethering.

The LLM-entrypoint test checks notification before constructor return, final KV capacity, and generation of one new token, in eager and graph modes. With extensible KV cache disabled so the connector exists during capture, it also requires capture reset before notification and rejects reset after notification. It runs in the existing `v1-kv-connectors` job; CPU cases run in `v1-others-cpu`. No Buildkite configuration change is needed.

CUDA serving remains unvalidated. A local CPU LLM attempt was blocked before the hook by an older native extension missing `gumbel_sample_cpu`. No E2E or performance pass is claimed. With matching native artifacts, CUDA hardware and public OPT-125m weights/tokenizer, run:

```bash
VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error \
  uv run --no-project .venv/bin/python -m pytest -v -s \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_kv_cache_ready.py -k before_first_request
```

## Details

`register_kv_caches()` runs earlier and does not signal completion of warmup. The new call follows final KV sizing, including `extend_kv_cache()`. With `VLLM_ELASTIC_EP_SCALE_UP_LAUNCH`, warmup and capture are deferred to `warm_and_capture()`, so this notification precedes them and is not repeated afterward. The method docstring documents this exception. It runs only during startup; existing sleep/wake hooks remain unchanged.

This initial API deliberately leaves deadlines to the connector. A multiprocess RPC timeout only ends the caller's wait, and UniProcExecutor calls the worker inline. Startup watchdog and worker cancellation/teardown are outside this change. The tests cover exceptions and ordering, not recovery from a callback that never returns.

Duplicate checks found no existing startup notification. [#54578](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54578) adds asynchronous readiness reporting and request gating; [#59976](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59976) adds optional decode-shape warmup. Neither supplies this lifecycle hook. LMCache resource activation remains downstream work.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex assisted with implementation and validation. CUDA serving validation remains pending.
