commits.pr_title: [Perf][Qwen4Exp] Fuse HyperConnection up projection and gate mix on SM90
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Qwen4Exp's SM90 HyperConnection path materializes a 10,240-column BF16 gate between the up projection and four-stream mixing. Fuse the projection, sigmoid and mixing in Triton to consume gate tiles directly.

The specialization covers BF16, four streams, hidden size 2560, low-rank dimension 320 and at least 512 local rows. It preserves BF16 gate rounding and FP32 mixing order and uses the existing dispatch and weights. No new parallelism or communication is introduced.

Duplicate searches found no other open PR implementing this SM90 fusion. This adds a Hopper path alongside the SM100 implementation from #64898; existing ROCm, padding and sequence-parallel changes address different work.

## End-to-end results

<!-- hc-tep8-20261118:start -->
### H20 TP8/EP8 on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8

Rebased on `81a8cb063e62` in `1e5d6b3e7208`. The HC runtime file is byte-identical to the original PR. The test matrix retains the upstream 1,599/1,600-row SM100 boundary from #68154 alongside the 512-row serving threshold.

We ran four independent starts in upstream/PR/PR/upstream order with two measured rounds per start and 160 completed serving requests. Both arms used the same integration image (`796dc4b9aa05`, PyTorch 2.15.0+cu132, Triton 3.9.0, FlashInfer 0.7.4), identical native extensions and upstream QSA. Only `nvidia/ops/hc.py` changed. The upstream HC blob in this image matches the rebase target. Settings were 8×H20, TP8/DP1/EP8, MP, AUTO selecting FlashInfer CUTLASS MoE, autotuning on, 48 GiB KV per GPU, 262,144 context, 8,192 batched tokens, 64 sequences, chunked prefill and one CPU thread per worker. MTP, LMCache and prefix caching were off. Both arms replayed the same fixed token IDs and generated 128 tokens.

| Input / concurrency | TTFT P50, upstream → PR | TTFT change | Boot-pair TTFT changes | E2E P50 change | Input tok/s change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1,024 / 1 | 121.85 → 125.45 ms | +2.95% | +5.71% / -5.68% | ≈0.00% | +0.57% |
| 32,768 / 4 | 2.950 → 2.868 s | -2.76% | -2.68% / -3.23% | -2.51% | +2.49% |
| 131,072 / 1 | 6.263 → 6.090 s | -2.77% | -2.50% / -2.95% | -2.34% | +2.42% |
| 261,888 / 1 | 13.263 → 12.945 s | -2.40% | -2.36% / -2.40% | -2.31% | +2.37% |

Both boot pairs improved at 32K, 128K and 261,888 tokens. At 1K the two pairs moved in opposite directions and both arms had about 893 ms full-request P50. These measurements support the long-prefill claim.

The updated repository HC suite passed all 20 cases on H20. Three additional serving-dispatch checks passed at 511/512/513 rows. Each of the eight fixed 32K/128K retrieval and arithmetic cases returned the same output token IDs on all four starts (32/32 correct). An untimed 8,192-token probe on rank 0 recorded 97 original gate-mix kernels on each upstream start and 97 fused SM90 kernels on each PR start. All eight ranks agreed on eligibility. Timed groups had zero monitored JIT events, preemptions and prefix hits.

<details><summary>Reproduce the TP8 measurements</summary>

HC numerical tests on a CUDA vLLM checkout:

```bash
uv run --offline --no-project --python .venv/bin/python .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_hc_ops.py -q
```

For the first 128K/C1 round, create a timed trace of four independent prompts and use the same tokenizer, weights and trace in both arms. The second round uses seed 922200 in both the trace generator and serving client.

```bash
export PYTHONHASHSEED=0
uv run --offline --no-project --python .venv/bin/python .venv/bin/python - <<'PY'
import json
from pathlib import Path

with Path('hc-128k.jsonl').open('w') as output:
    for i in range(4):
        print(json.dumps(dict(timestamp=0, input_length=131072, output_length=128,
                              hash_ids=[f"921200-{i}-{k}" for k in range(256)])), file=output)
PY
vllm bench serve --backend openai --base-url "$HC_BASE_URL" --model "$HC_MODEL_DIR" \
  --served-model-name Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 --dataset-name timed_trace --dataset-path hc-128k.jsonl \
  --timed-trace-chunk-hash-size 512 --timed-trace-label-input-length input_length \
  --timed-trace-label-output-length output_length --timed-trace-label-hash-ids hash_ids \
  --num-prompts 4 --max-concurrency 1 --ready-check-timeout-sec 0 --ignore-eos \
  --seed 921200 --temperature 0 --extra-body '{"seed":42}' --save-result --save-detailed
```

A separate single-H20 cold-L2 CUDA Graph/CUPTI benchmark of the strided BF16 input reduced median kernel time from 68.71 to 61.46 µs at 1,024 rows and from 498.85 to 390.47 µs at 8,192 rows. Those timings exclude the rest of the model.

</details>
<!-- hc-tep8-20261118:end -->

### Earlier H20 TP4/EP4 measurements

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 on 4×H20, TP4/DP1/EP4, default FlashInfer CUTLASS MoE with autotuning enabled, OMP_NUM_THREADS=4, token budget 8192, maximum context 262144, fixed **48 GiB KV per GPU**, MTP/LMCache off. Baseline **U** restores all 3,982 tracked vLLM package files to upstream `8db73f26c`; **H** adds only this PR's HC production file. Generated metadata, bundled FlashAttention and native extensions are shared from one immutable image.

| Input / output / concurrency | TTFT P50, U → H (ms) | TTFT change | Input throughput change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 32,768 / 32 / 4 | 4,825.28 → 4,715.70 | −2.27% | +2.30% |
| 131,072 / 32 / 1 | 8,196.60 → 8,017.83 | −2.18% | +1.95% |
| 261,888 / 32 / 1 | 17,159.53 → 16,793.36 | −2.13% | +2.13% |
| 131,072 / 32 / 4 | 17,503.75 → 17,101.62 | −2.30% | +2.15% |

Two fresh starts per arm, two measured rounds per workload. The full four-arm experiment ran **480 timed requests** in U/Q/H/QH/QH/H/Q/U order, where Q is the separate QSA PR #65606. All completed at the requested lengths, with zero timed prefix hits or preemptions. U-to-U TTFT P50 drift was 0.01%–0.26%. These are bounded repeats, not a statistical-significance claim.

Earlier same-runtime A/B/B/A controls covered short prompts and 256-token outputs: 1,176 timed requests passed; 1K/256/C1 decode TPOT was 7.259 → 7.263 ms/token.

<details>
<summary>Optional composition with QSA #65606 — not a dependency of this PR</summary>

All reductions below are relative to the same U baseline.

| Input / output / concurrency | HC TTFT reduction | QSA reduction | Both |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 131,072 / 32 / 1 | 2.18% | 1.92% | 4.71% |
| 261,888 / 32 / 1 | 2.13% | 5.76% | 8.34% |
| 131,072 / 32 / 4 | 2.30% | 3.91% | 6.25% |

At 261,888 tokens, combined input throughput increased 9.14%. The two independent TTFT savings predict 7.90%; the measured combined reduction is 8.34%. This supports approximate additivity in the measured configuration, not universal linear scaling. The combined gain is not attributed to HC alone.

</details>

### Official nightly on H20, TP4 and TP8 (2026-11-18)

Tested the official linux/amd64 vLLM nightly at `7c3a9302`, platform digest `sha256:2ec7538c60759a14cab5bd3161c024aba0e74155a2643dc3e7d19d2ede1d2bf1`. The image contained Torch 2.14.0 (CUDA 13.0 as reported by Torch), Triton 3.8.0 and FlashInfer 0.7.4. Its stock HC source matches this PR's parent. The candidate mounted the reviewed `ops/hc.py` from `1e5d6b3e7208` in the same image. [Upstream source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/7c3a9302f5ac2441ad199134129e973d22a46797)

Each topology used DP1 with EP, FP8 FlashInfer CUTLASS experts, an 8,192-token scheduler budget, 48 GiB KV per GPU and chunked prefill. Speculation, prefix caching and external KV were disabled. Each topology ran A/B/B/A across four independent server starts with the same prompt token IDs, fixed output lengths and vLLM's streaming completions benchmark client. The 2,496 timed requests exclude compilation, warmup, profiling and quality checks.

| Topology | Input / output / concurrency | Requests per implementation | Stock → PR median TTFT (ms) | TTFT change on each boot pair | Median end-to-end change |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| TP4 | 4,096 / 32 / 4 (closed loop) | 192 | 482.9 → 471.8 | -2.44% / -2.40% | -1.84% |
| TP4 | 32,768 / 128 / 4 | 32 | 3,224.9 → 3,148.9 | -2.28% / -2.39% | -1.96% |
| TP4 | 131,072 / 128 / 1 | 16 | 7,708.1 → 7,542.6 | -1.94% / -2.20% | -2.03% |
| TP8 | 4,096 / 32 / 4 (closed loop) | 192 | 538.6 → 365.8 | -32.19% / -21.03% | -1.36% |
| TP8 | 32,768 / 128 / 4 | 32 | 2,575.6 → 2,502.6 | -2.99% / -2.92% | -2.54% |
| TP8 | 131,072 / 128 / 1 | 16 | 6,236.4 → 6,066.8 | -2.79% / -2.75% | -2.48% |

The 4K median is sensitive to arrival cadence. Replaying both historical clocks on each implementation gave these pooled median TTFT and end-to-end changes.

| Arrival trace | TP4 TTFT / end-to-end | TP8 TTFT / end-to-end |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Historical stock arrivals | +38.63% / -1.48% | -13.49% / -2.54% |
| Historical candidate arrivals | -25.00% / -1.60% | -2.29% / -2.23% |

On TP4 with the historical stock arrivals, the pooled TTFT median increased from 487.7 to 676.1 ms. The two boot pairs moved -1.43% and +39.10%. Of 192 requests per arm, 98 stock and 86 candidate requests received a first token within 550 ms. The fraction crossed the median boundary, while mean TTFT moved 622.7 → 618.7 ms and P95 moved 927.6 → 910.5 ms. This workload remains a short-request TTFT caveat.

The six H20 HC up/gate numerical cases passed. Fixed 32K/128K retrieval and arithmetic checks scored 64/64. All four starts within each topology produced identical token IDs on each case. All accepted timing groups recorded zero monitored JIT events, KV preemptions and prefix hits. Rank-local source checks and untimed kernel probes confirmed the original and fused paths. FlashInfer's cold H20 compilation was excluded. Across relinked MoE modules we compared the named device code, constants, resource metadata and shared-memory sections of all 242 embedded cubins. The two long-input settings are the basis for the performance claim. The 128K tail has 16 requests per implementation per topology.

## Validation

- **18/18 HC tests passed**, including strided low-rank inputs, odd row counts and BF16 reference comparisons. The combined source also passed 23 QSA configuration tests and the real TP4 collective test; these tests belong to the separate QSA change.
- Five-shot greedy GSM8K on the same 64-example slice, **C1 with the prefix cache reset before every question**, scored **60/64 in all four arms**, with all 64 parsed answers matching and zero prefix hits. Four 128K/near-256K retrieval checks passed in every arm. Short GSM8K prompts do not exercise the QSA sharding gate.
- Long random greedy output is not bitwise equivalent. Repeating the same four requests on unmodified U within one boot also changed 3/4 outputs; U's concurrent cached-prefix GSM8K repeated at 59/64 and 58/64. This bounds the quality evidence; the source of upstream repeat variation remains unresolved.
- Four-rank traces collected outside timings confirmed 97 fused HC calls per measured H/QH step. Source/native-library/GPU audits passed; all starts had identical KV capacity. Maximum sampled temperature was 60°C, with no thermal slowdown observed.

Runtime: image `5b2f9872e599`, PyTorch `2.15.0+cu132.upstream199418`, Triton `3.9.0+upstream12049.12153`, FlashInfer `0.7.3`. TP4 measurements used `b07c6bb5ccf7`. The November 18 rebase retains that HC runtime file.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction commands</summary>

HC test invocation used the repository's distributed fixture in the validation container:

```bash
PY=/opt/glm53-image-gn/.venv/bin/python
PYTHONPATH=/qa uv run --offline --no-project --python "$PY" "$PY" -B \
  -m pytest --noconftest -p tests.conftest \
  /qa/tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_hc_ops.py -q
# 18 passed
```

Representative long-prefill benchmark command (reset prefix cache before each group):

```bash
MODEL=/models/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8
vllm bench serve --backend openai --base-url http://127.0.0.1:28947 \
  --model "$MODEL" --served-model-name Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 261888 --random-output-len 32 \
  --random-range-ratio 0 --ignore-eos --num-prompts 4 --max-concurrency 1 \
  --seed 900200 --ready-check-timeout-sec 0 --save-result --save-detailed
```

The serving benchmark uses the CLI's model-default sampling; quality checks explicitly use temperature=0. Startup, warmup, quality evaluation and profiling are excluded from performance timings.

</details>

## Scope

Performance is qualified on this H20 runtime. An older Torch 2.14/CUDA 13.0 closed-loop 4K run regressed median TTFT from 487 to 658 ms despite higher throughput; the newer-runtime 4K repeat improved 820.09 → 803.06 ms. H100/H200, DP greater than one and larger deployment windows remain outside these measurements. All new starts used the same FlashInfer FABRIC-to-POSIX fallback.

commits.pr_title: [Multimodal] Pass placement with Omni embeddings to drop the audio-in-video host read
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Follow-up to #68099 (merged; this branch now contains only its own changes). The Omni models (Qwen3-Omni, Qwen2.5-Omni, LFM3-Omni) still copy `input_ids` to the host on steps that gather both audio and video embeddings, to find the video and audio positions for the interleaved audio-in-video merge. The encoder runners already know those positions on the CPU, so they now pass them with each embedding and the models build the masks without any device read.

## Claims

- The encoder runners (GPU and CPU) attach each gathered embedding's batch placement `(start, end, is_embed)` next to its existing modality tag. `copy_mm_embedding_modality` carries it through re-wrapped embeddings (EVS pruning, Qwen3-Omni deepstack split).
- New `get_mm_embedding_modality_masks` rebuilds the per-modality masks from the placements. Qwen3-Omni, Qwen2.5-Omni and LFM3-Omni use it instead of `input_ids.cpu()`.
- With #68099, Qwen3-Omni needs no host sync at all for image, video, audio or audio-in-video requests. Audio-in-video goes from 1 sync to 0, down from 66 on main.
- If an embedding has no placement, the models fall back to the token-id read, which is **no longer allow-listed**, so `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK` reports any path that loses the placement instead of hiding it.
- Outputs are unchanged.

## Validation

MI355X (gfx950), `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`, compared against #68099 (sync check off for the baseline):

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B offline: audio-in-video (`use_audio_in_video=True`), image + audio-in-video, image + audio + video, image only; `max_num_batched_tokens=1024` so prefill is chunked across the interleaved span; cold batch, warm batch (prefix hits), each prompt alone, and a prefix hit that ends inside the span | 0 sync errors; all 14 outputs identical in token ids, top-5 logprobs and cached-token counts |
| Qwen2.5-Omni-3B, same prompts and passes, engine in-process | 0 sync errors; all 14 outputs identical |
| Fuzz: 2,814 random batches through the real GPU `EncoderRunner.gather_mm_embeddings` (1–4 requests, images, audio-in-video spans, plain audio and video, repeated items, chunk windows starting and ending inside spans, draft look-ahead 0/1) | placement masks equal `is_mm_embed & (input_ids == token_id)` for video, audio and image in every batch |
| `pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_qwen2_5_omni_embed.py tests/v1/worker/test_encoder_runner.py tests/model_executor/test_qwen3_omni.py` | 61 passed |

New tests cover placement propagation through `copy_mm_embedding_modality`, mask construction with `is_embed` slices, the missing-placement fallback, and the runners attaching placements.

## Details

- **Coordinates:** `start` and `end` are the same batch-token coordinates the runner uses to fill `is_mm_embed` (including the drafter look-ahead shift), and `is_embed` is the CPU slice it ORs in. So the masks are exactly `is_mm_embed` split by modality. Each gather slices a new view of the encoder output, so a placement can't carry over from an earlier step.
- **Why tensor attributes:** this is the mechanism the modality tag already uses (`set_mm_embedding_modality`), introduced to avoid threading per-embedding metadata through `embed_input_ids`. No model or runner signature changes.
- **Fallback:** if any embedding lacks a placement (a future path that re-wraps embeddings without `copy_mm_embedding_modality`), the models fall back to the previous `input_ids` read. That read is no longer inside `gpu_sync_allowed()`, so the sync check flags it instead of hiding a regression.
- **Not run end to end:** the CPU worker (its suite skips on GPU hosts) and LFM3-Omni (no checkpoint available). Both were checked by code reading and unit tests.
- **Size:** about 150 non-test lines across the two runners (11 lines each), `vllm/multimodal/utils.py` and the three models.
- Not a duplicate: no open PR touches this path.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Kernel] Apply beta after the K loop in chunk_scaled_dot_kkt
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes #65385. `chunk_scaled_dot_kkt_fwd_kernel` now applies `beta` after the K loop, as upstream FLA does, instead of scaling `k` inside it.

## Claims

- On Hopper, the autotune configs with `BK < K` and `num_warps >= 4` gave different results from run to run. With this change, all 27 configs give the same result on every run at K=128 and K=256.
- Every config is now within 2.8e-7 of a float32 reference, where main’s deterministic configs were 1.7e-3 off.
- The autotuned kernel is 4–6% faster on an H100.

## Validation

H100 80GB HBM3, torch 2.14.0+cu132, Triton 3.8.0, main `919d45fc3`.

- New test `pytest -q tests/kernels/fla/test_chunk_scaled_dot_kkt.py`: it runs each config 5 times and compares the runs bitwise and against a float32 reference at 1e-5.
  - On main it fails: 25 configs differ between runs (8 of 12 at K=128, 17 of 18 at K=256, all with `BK < K` and `num_warps >= 4`), and the other 29 are 1.7e-3 off the reference.
  - With this PR: 2 passed, in 3 runs.
- Existing tests: `pytest -q tests/kernels/fla tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_forward_core_split.py tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_fused_mtp.py tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_output_projection.py` gives 1752 passed and 1 skipped, on both main and this PR.
- GSM8K (5-shot, greedy, 1319 questions) with `Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B`, `--gdn-prefill-backend triton` and `max_num_seqs=1`, so that runs are deterministic (a 200-question rerun matched 200/200): main 31.5%, this PR 32.2%. 19 and 29 questions respectively are answered correctly only by that version, p = 0.19. Batch-invariant mode doesn’t support GDN, and batched runs of the same build differed on 106–121 answers.
- Kernel time (`triton.testing.do_bench`, T=4096, H=32, Hg=16): autotuned 26.6 → 25.0 µs at K=128 and 34.5 → 33.1 µs at K=256. Across all 27 configs, the geometric-mean ratio is 0.94 and 0.95.

<details>
<summary>New test output</summary>

main:
```
AssertionError: BK: 32, num_warps: 2, num_ctas: 1, num_stages: 2, maxnreg: None: relative error 1.66e-03
BK: 32, num_warps: 2, num_ctas: 1, num_stages: 3, maxnreg: None: relative error 1.66e-03
BK: 32, num_warps: 2, num_ctas: 1, num_stages: 4, maxnreg: None: relative error 1.66e-03
BK: 32, num_warps: 4, num_ctas: 1, num_stages: 2, maxnreg: None: differs between runs
BK: 32, num_warps: 4, num_ctas: 1, num_stages: 3, maxnreg: None: differs between runs
...
FAILED tests/kernels/fla/test_chunk_scaled_dot_kkt.py::test_every_config_is_deterministic[128]
FAILED tests/kernels/fla/test_chunk_scaled_dot_kkt.py::test_every_config_is_deterministic[256]
2 failed in 2.55s
```

This PR (3 runs):
```
2 passed in 2.35s
2 passed in 2.31s
2 passed in 2.27s
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>GSM8K output</summary>

```
Using Triton/FLA GDN prefill kernel (requested=triton, head_k_dim=128)
GSM8K_OWN main_b1 acc=0.3146 n=1319
GSM8K_OWN fix_b1 acc=0.3222 n=1319
GSM8K_OWN main_b1rep200 acc=0.2700 n=200   (200/200 predictions identical to the first main run)
```
</details>

## Details

- Root cause: `k` feeds the wgmma through shared memory and also has a register user (`k * beta`). In that case Triton’s pipeliner gives its buffer one slot too few, so the next iteration’s load overwrites it while the async wgmma still reads it (triton-lang/triton#12738 fixes this in Triton). Scaling after the loop leaves `k` with no other user.
- RDNA: the dot now always takes `k`’s dtype, so the RDNA cast branch is no longer needed and is removed.
- Not a duplicate: #65927 prunes configs with `BK < 128`. At K=256 that leaves the six `BK=128`, `num_warps >= 4` configs, which all race here. pkusp suggested this approach in #65385.
- Who is affected: on Hopper, Qwen3-Next and Qwen3.5 use FlashInfer GDN prefill by default. This kernel runs with `--gdn-prefill-backend triton`, and for OLMo Hybrid, which calls the vendored `chunk_gated_delta_rule` directly.
- CI: `tests/kernels/fla` runs on B200 and MI355, where this race doesn’t occur. The new test still checks every config against the reference there. The Hopper results above come from an H100.

## Overview GLM-5.3-Flash on ROCm: the kpool sparse indexer (`vllm/models/glm5next/amd/sparse_indexer.py`) launches int32↔int64 casts, a `+1`, a `-1` fill and a buffer copy around `expand_pools_and_append_tail` in every sparse-attention layer. This PR lets the expand kernel read int32 pool ids and int64 positions as they are (the `+1` moves into the kernel) and write straight into `topk_indices_buffer`, removing 6 launches per sparse-attention layer, 66 per decode step. ## Claims - 1.7–4.4% lower median TPOT at 1–32 concurrent requests on 1k/1k, 8k/1k, 64k/1k and 128k/1k (MI355X, TP4, `amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4`) against the same ROCm nightly without this PR, and 0.9–1.8% at 64; flat at 64k c16 (−0.2%), where each step carries other requests' long prefill. commits.pr_title: [Perf][GLM-5.3-Flash] KDA decode and prefill through FlashInfer
commits.pr_body:
## Overview This PR moves GLM-5.3-Flash's KDA (Kimi Delta Attention) layers onto FlashInfer kernels: - the fused single-token decode (`fused_kda_decode`); - the packed multi-token decode for draft-verify rows (`packed_fused_kda_decode`); - optionally, the CuTe DSL chunked prefill (`recurrent_kda(backend="cute-dsl")`). Kimi K3 already uses these kernels through the same `vllm.utils.flashinfer` wrappers and the same `kda_decode_backend` / `kda_spec_decode_backend` / `kda_prefill_backend` options. The model has 34 KDA layers (64 heads of 128). Today each decode step runs three Triton kernels per layer, and mixed steps send their decode rows through the chunked prefill kernel. - **Decode:** default `auto`; activates where FlashInfer supports the layer. - **Prefill:** opt-in `--kda-prefill-backend flashinfer`. > [!IMPORTANT] > **Requires FlashInfer 0.7.3.** This PR assumes the FlashInfer pin bump to 0.7.3 (a separate PR) has landed. > 0.7.3 contains flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#7132 (16/64 heads in `fused_kda_decode` / `packed_fused_kda_decode`, and > the DS conv-state layout) and #6201 (SM107 prefill). GLM-5.3-Flash's 64-head (TP1 / DP attention) and 16-head > (TP4) ranks, and the DS layout that NIXL P/D needs, rely on #7132. With the current pin (0.7.2.post1) the static > support checks accept configurations that 0.7.2 rejects at its first call, so this PR should merge after the bump. ## Claims - **Decode kernels** (VR200, 34 layers per step, CUDA graph, L2 flushed): - 1.9–2.1x faster at 1–8 rows per GPU; - 1.3–1.8x faster at 32–512 rows (H64 fp32 at 512 rows: 19.5 → 12.4 ms per step; H64 bf16: 16.2 → 9.2 ms); - pure decode steps run in a FULL CUDA graph (`FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, KDA captured), so the GPU times above are what serving pays; in eager (PIECEWISE, mixed/prefill) steps the host enqueue also drops, 3.0 → 0.95 ms per 34 layers. - **Mixed prefill + decode steps** (one layer, H64): 46–61% faster (32K prefill tokens + 512 decode rows: 6.96 → 2.72 ms). Most of it is the decode-row peel. - **FlashInfer prefill (opt-in):** 8–12% per layer at 4+ long sequences; 3–8% slower in eager steps with 1 sequence at H64 or a few at H16, mostly from the call's host time (about 95 µs vs FlashKDA's 18 µs on VR200, where FlashInfer's kernel is faster). This is why it stays opt-in. - **Serving on GB300 and GB200**, native srt-slurm sa-bench 8K/1K, Dynamo, base vs this PR (+ the FlashInfer change): - agg DEP2 (64 KDA heads per rank): +13.7% / +24.9% TPS/GPU on GB300 at C512 / C1024 (2847 → 3237, 2402 → 2999); +13.5% / +14.8% on GB200, which is KV-capacity bound; - disagg with the DS conv layout via NIXL, C512: +5.1% (GB300) and +6.0% (GB200) TPS/GPU; - agg TP4 (16 heads per rank): +1.4–3.0% at C1–C32. - **Where it comes from:** decode steps run one fused FlashInfer kernel per layer instead of three Triton kernels, and mixed steps send their decode rows to that kernel instead of the chunked prefill kernel (the decode-row peel). - **FlashInfer prefill (opt-in):** faster for several long sequences per step; slower for one or a few sequences at low concurrency, mostly from the call's host time (Follow-ups). This is why it stays opt-in. - **Also validated on VR200 (SM107):** unit tests, GSM8K accuracy (with and without MTP) and end-to-end serving, including disaggregated P/D; performance numbers for VR200 are not included here. - **Accuracy:** 40-shot GSM8K (7–8K-token prompts), agg DEP2 on VR200, 6 runs each: base 91.85 ± 0.59%, PR (decode + prefill on FlashInfer) 91.88 ± 0.76%. - **Numerics vs an fp32 reference:** - FlashInfer decode error ≤ the Triton path's; - conv states bit-identical to the Triton path's; - in mixed steps, the decode rows equal a decode-only step bit for bit, and the prefill rows (outputs and states) are bit-identical to the Triton path. ## Validation ### Unit tests `tests/models/glm5next/test_kda_flashinfer_decode.py` (new): - backend resolution and fallback; - decode steps for 8/16/32/64 heads × fp32/bf16 state × SD/DS layout, against the Triton path and an fp32 reference, with null and padding slots; - mixed steps (peeled decode rows; prefill rows with the Triton or FlashKDA prefill); - spec-verify rows, pure and mixed with prefills, at 16/32/64 heads; - CUDA-graph capture and replay of a decode step. `tests/models/glm5next/test_kda_flashinfer_prefill.py` (new): - FlashInfer prefill vs the Triton chunk path and an fp32 reference, with fresh and continued sequences, 1-token and >16-token sequences; - untouched slots; one-token steps; - FlashInfer decode + prefill in one step; - prefill rows alongside spec-verify rows; - a step without draft rows in an MTP deployment, whose slot indices are a strided block-table column. Existing: `tests/models/glm5next/` (one test updated for the `_forward` signature) and `tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda.py`. | Where | FlashInfer | Result | |---|---|---| | VR200 (SM107), nightly c50aca14 + this branch | 0.7.2 + final #7132 files + #6201 prefill | 180 passed, 18 skipped (ROCm-only and Kimi K3-gated), 0 failed; all 50 FlashInfer KDA tests ran | | GB300 (SM103), nightly c50aca14 + this branch | 0.7.2 + final #7132 files | 183 passed, 15 skipped, 0 failed; all 50 FlashInfer KDA tests ran | ```bash pytest -v tests/models/glm5next tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda.py ``` The strided-slot-index test fails without the prefill fix (VR200, the same test file run against the prefill commit without `.contiguous()`) and passes with it: ```text $ pytest tests/models/glm5next/test_kda_flashinfer_prefill.py -k block_table_column test_block_table_column_state_indices[prefill] FAILED test_block_table_column_state_indices[mixed] FAILED E ValueError: backend='cute-dsl' does not support this recurrent_kda prefill contract # with this branch test_block_table_column_state_indices[prefill] PASSED test_block_table_column_state_indices[mixed] PASSED ``` ### Accuracy (GSM8K 40-shot, 1319 questions, greedy, 6 runs per arm, agg DEP2, mnbt 32768) | Arm | Runs | Mean ± sd | |---|---|---| | base (nightly 8e2beaa3) | 92.42, 91.51, 91.51, 92.04, 91.05, 92.57 | 91.85 ± 0.59 | | this PR, decode + prefill on FlashInfer | 90.67, 91.36, 92.49, 92.72, 92.12, 91.89 | 91.88 ± 0.76 | Greedy runs differ by about ±1 point from batch-dependent numerics, so 6 runs per arm were taken; the difference is +0.03 points (t = 0.06). Reference from earlier VR200 work: 91.40%. ### MTP (speculative decoding, 2 draft tokens) GSM8K 40-shot as above with `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":2}'`, agg DEP2, VR200, nightly c50aca14. Covers the draft-verify path (`packed_fused_kda_decode`) and prefill/decode with spec-decoding metadata. | Arm | Runs | Mean | Draft acceptance (accepted / drafted tokens, both runs) | |---|---|---|---| | base (nightly c50aca14) | 92.27, 91.89 | 92.08 | 88.6% (162475 / 183370) | | this PR, decode + prefill on FlashInfer | 91.21, 91.89 | 91.55 | 88.7% (160379 / 180818) | Accuracy is within the ±1-point spread of greedy runs seen above, and draft acceptance is unchanged. The PR arm's logs show the FlashInfer prefill and the packed decode (3 tokens per row) in use. Serving with MTP (sa-bench 8K/1K random, agg DEP2, C128 and C256, VR200) also completed every request in both arms, with the same draft acceptance. This check found a bug in an earlier revision: under speculative decoding the builder's non-spec slot indices are a strided column of the [N, 1 + num_spec] block table, which FlashInfer's prefill rejects. Warmup failed with `ValueError: backend='cute-dsl' does not support this recurrent_kda prefill contract`. The prefill now passes contiguous indices, and a unit test covers it. ### Serving (GB300 and GB200) Native srt-slurm sa-bench, ISL 8192 / OSL 1024, random data, Dynamo frontend, on Lyris (GB300 and GB200, 4 GPUs per node). Settings: - `max-num-batched-tokens` 32768; - fp8 KV; - FlashInfer TRT-LLM NVFP4 MoE; - SD conv layout for agg, DS for disagg. Base: nightly 8e2beaa3. PR: the same image + this branch's `kda.py` + the final flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#7132 files, with `--kda-prefill-backend flashinfer`. Single runs; all points completed every request. The same recipes were also run on VR200. | GPU | Config | C | Base TPS/GPU | PR TPS/GPU | Δ | Base tok/s/user | PR tok/s/user | Base TPOT ms | PR TPOT ms | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | GB300 | agg DEP2 (2 GPU) | 512 | 2847 | 3237 | +13.7% | 11.13 | 12.66 | 82.75 | 71.48 | | GB300 | agg DEP2 (2 GPU) | 1024 | 2402 | 2999 | +24.9% | 4.76 | 5.93 | 158.91 | 133.83 | | GB300 | agg TP4 (4 GPU) | 1 | 54.7 | 55.4 | +1.4% | 218.66 | 221.66 | 4.44 | 4.36 | | GB300 | agg TP4 (4 GPU) | 8 | 299.4 | 307.3 | +2.6% | 149.73 | 153.68 | 6.10 | 5.88 | | GB300 | agg TP4 (4 GPU) | 32 | 678.4 | 692.0 | +2.0% | 84.84 | 86.53 | 10.36 | 10.10 | | GB300 | 4P(TP1)+1D(DEP4) (8 GPU), DS layout | 512 | 2657 | 2793 | +5.1% | 43.02 | 45.27 | 20.74 | 19.18 | | GB200 | agg DEP2 (2 GPU) | 512 | 2090 | 2372 | +13.5% | 8.41 | 9.52 | 61.91 | 64.22 | | GB200 | agg DEP2 (2 GPU) | 1024 | 2100 | 2410 | +14.8% | 4.26 | 4.87 | 62.30 | 64.05 | | GB200 | agg TP4 (4 GPU) | 1 | 53.1 | 54.7 | +3.0% | 212.47 | 218.90 | 4.57 | 4.41 | | GB200 | agg TP4 (4 GPU) | 8 | 294.7 | 302.8 | +2.8% | 147.38 | 151.45 | 6.16 | 5.94 | | GB200 | agg TP4 (4 GPU) | 32 | 671.6 | 683.3 | +1.7% | 83.98 | 85.44 | 10.45 | 10.24 | | GB200 | 2P(DEP2)+1D(DEP4) (8 GPU), DS layout | 512 | 2199 | 2330 | +6.0% | 35.73 | 38.03 | 18.58 | 17.63 | - **DEP2 at C1024 with fp32 KDA state** is capacity-bound: the state takes about 142 MB per sequence, so requests queue and every step is a mixed step. That is where the decode-row peel pays most. - **TP4 at low concurrency** is decode-bound; KDA is only part of each step, so the per-step gain is a few percent. - **GB200 agg DEP2** is KV-capacity bound (about 186 GB per GPU): TPOT stays at 62–64 ms from C512 to C1024 and requests queue (mean TTFT 58 s for base at C512). The PR's gain there is admission: faster mixed steps cut mean TTFT 58 → 42 s (C512) and 176 → 145 s (C1024), while per-token decode time is slightly higher with the larger running batch. Hence +14.8% at C1024 rather than about +25%. - **GB200 disagg shape:** one GB200 cannot hold the 191 GB checkpoint at TP1, so each prefill worker is DEP2 (TP1 per rank, experts over 2 GPUs). A TP2 prefill does not work with a TP1-per-rank decode for this model: the hybrid KDA block size follows the per-rank KDA state, and NIXL rejects the mismatched blocks (8576 vs 4352). - **TTFT at TP4, C1–C8** is 20–47 ms higher in the PR arm (GB300 C1 143 → 163 ms, C8 603 → 650 ms; GB200 C1 147 → 169 ms, C8 652 → 681 ms). These steps prefill one or a few sequences at 16 heads. On GB300 the FlashInfer prefill call costs about 190 µs of host time vs FlashKDA's 50–56 µs (34 layers per step), and at 1–4 sequences its kernel is also 7–13% slower; this is why the FlashInfer prefill stays opt-in. Decode alone was not run on GB300/GB200. ## Details **Decode.** - **Plain decode steps** call `flashinfer_fused_kda_decode` once per layer: conv + SiLU with the conv-state update, the recurrence, and the gated RMSNorm, writing the layer output buffer. Slot ≤ 0 rows are null rows. - **Draft-verify steps** (MTP) call `flashinfer_packed_fused_kda_decode` with the existing `spec_state_indices_tensor` / `num_accepted_tokens`. Mixed steps with verify rows keep the Triton spec path. - **Mixed steps without spec rows** run the leading decode rows (vLLM orders decodes first) through the fused kernel. The conv then skips those rows as null slots, so the builder's existing causal-conv metadata stays valid. The prefill kernel uses the builder's prefill tail (`prefill_query_start_loc` / `prefill_state_indices` / `prefill_has_initial_state`), as the GDN layer already does. FlashKDA's prepare kernel thus no longer scans hundreds of one-token sequences, and gather / scatter no longer move their states. With prefix-cache checkpoints the step keeps today's path. - **Selection:** `--kda-decode-backend` (`additional_config.kda_decode_backend`) and `additional_config.kda_spec_decode_backend` take `auto` / `flashinfer` / `triton`. - As for Kimi K3, a static check decides (`_is_flashinfer_kda_decode_supported`): CUDA SM10x, D=128, conv width 4, bf16 activations and conv state, fp32 or bf16 recurrent state, a bounded gate, and the head counts and layouts of FlashInfer with #7132 (single-token rows: 8/12/16/24/32/48/64/96 heads, SD or DS; draft-verify rows: 12–96 heads, SD only, at most 7 draft tokens). - `auto` falls back to Triton when the check fails; `flashinfer` raises. - The prefill opt-in uses the same pattern (`_is_flashinfer_kda_prefill_supported`: SM100 / SM103 / SM107, D=128, bf16 activations, fp32 or bf16 state, bounded gate) and raises at startup when it fails. - **Norm placement:** the fused kernel applies `o_norm`, so with the FlashInfer backend `_forward` returns normed output for every step type. In PIECEWISE (mixed/prefill) steps, breakable CUDA graphs run `_forward` eagerly but the code after it is replayed as captured, so whether to norm must not depend on the step type. **Prefill (opt-in).** - **Call:** `--kda-prefill-backend flashinfer` (already a CLI choice, previously rejected for GLM-5.3) calls `recurrent_kda(backend="cute-dsl")` with the raw gate and beta logits. - **In place:** it reads and writes the recurrent state pool through `ssm_state_indices`, so there is no gather, scatter or final-state buffer. - **Fresh sequences:** FlashInfer has no has-initial-state flag, so their slots are zeroed first with one `index_fill_`; rows with state zero the unused null slot. - **Edge cases:** - a step whose prefill rows total one token uses the recurrent kernel; - steps with verify rows write their own output buffer and need no FlashKDA workspace. - **Opt-in** (as for Kimi K3), and it produces no prefix-cache checkpoints (`kda_prefill_checkpoint_alignment` is None). **Numerics.** FlashInfer's kernels are not bit-identical to Triton/FlashKDA (different summation orders). Against an fp32/fp64 reference they are as close or closer: - decode error equals the Triton path's; - FlashInfer prefill: 4.2e-3 vs FlashKDA 5.1e-3 (max abs error, H64, 8 x 8192 tokens). GSM8K above is the end-to-end check. **Limitations / follow-ups.** - Requires flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#7132 (and #6201 for SM107 prefill); bump the FlashInfer pin to the first release that has it before this PR leaves draft. - Host cost (eager PIECEWISE steps only; FULL-graph decode steps do not pay it): FlashInfer's validating decode wrapper costs more per call than its cached kernel launch; a cheaper FlashInfer launch path would help low concurrency. - Not in this PR: a faster prefill conv (planar / TMA output; overlaps vllm-project/vllm#61614), 64-row norm tiles, and a pipelined bf16-state decode kernel. - CI: `tests/models/glm5next` runs on H200 (SM90), where these tests skip or exercise FlashInfer's kernels only where FlashInfer supports them. SM10x coverage needs a Blackwell lane. - Follow-up: few-sequence prefill steps. With `--kda-prefill-backend flashinfer`, TTFT at low concurrency is higher (GB300 TP4: C1 143 → 163 ms, C8 603 → 650 ms). Most of the cost is the prefill call's host time, paid 34 times per eager prefill step: on GB300 about 190 µs on FlashInfer's two-kernel route (2 x sequences x heads <= SMs) and 110 µs on its one-kernel route, vs FlashKDA's 50–56 µs; at 1–4 sequences the kernel is also 7–13% slower than FlashKDA's. A prototype that routes such steps to FlashKDA brings C1 TTFT back to base, with unchanged throughput, but reserves FlashKDA's workspace (less KV cache) and ties the cutover to FlashInfer's routing rule. It is left out of this PR; the host overhead is reported to FlashInfer, whose fix would make it unnecessary. ---

commits.pr_title: [Quantization] Support ModelOpt INT8_PB_WO routed experts
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Extends ModelOpt `INT8_PB_WO` (#65272) from linear layers to routed MoE experts, in both `modelopt_int8` (whole-model) and `modelopt_mixed` (per-layer `quantized_layers`). Until now an `INT8_PB_WO` entry on routed experts raised `NotImplementedError`.

Most of a MoE model's weights are in its routed experts, so an `INT8_PB_WO` checkpoint of a MoE model needs its experts served too. Until now, INT8 group-quantized experts could be served only from a compressed-tensors checkpoint, which cannot keep ModelOpt's other layers (FP8 attention, NVFP4) as they are. With this PR, the checkpoint stays a ModelOpt checkpoint end to end.

## Claims

- Routed experts whose `quantized_layers` entries (or whole-model `quant_algo`) are `INT8_PB_WO` load and run on the existing WNA16 MoE kernels. No new kernels.
  - `ModelOptInt8PbWoMoEMethod` is self-contained ModelOpt code on the shared WNA16 MoE oracle (`fused_moe/oracle/int_wna16.py`): `select_wna16_moe_backend`, `convert_to_wna16_moe_kernel_format`, `make_wna16_moe_quant_config` and `make_wna16_moe_kernel`, so `--moe-backend` works as for the other WNA16 frontends. It imports nothing from compressed-tensors.
  - Its steps mirror a per-QuantKey MoE scheme (setup, `create_weights`, process, quant config; see #55997), so it maps onto one for `kInt8Static`.
  - The oracle gains `WNA16WeightFormat(num_bits, group_size)`, a format-neutral description of symmetric group weights in its canonical layout, for frontends without a quantization config of their own there. Marlin selection and conversion and Humming conversion accept it; existing frontends are unchanged.
  - On an RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (sm_120), group 32 runs on Marlin, group 16 on Triton (Marlin MoE has no group 16), and `--moe-backend humming` on Humming.
  - It registers ModelOpt's per-expert `weight` (int8 `[out, in]`, packed on load to uint8b128 in int32 with the same helper as the linear path) and `weight_scale` (`[out, in // group_size]`, cast to the activation dtype).
- Usage is unchanged: `vllm serve <ModelOpt INT8_PB_WO checkpoint>` (routed to `modelopt_int8` or `modelopt_mixed` from its config), optionally with `--moe-backend humming`.
- The same expert weights served as `INT8_PB_WO` and as compressed-tensors `pack-quantized` give bit-identical prompt logprobs.
- In `MIXED_PRECISION`, if any expert or projection of a MoE layer is `INT8_PB_WO`, all must be, with one `group_size`: one kernel serves the whole layer. Otherwise loading raises `ValueError` instead of serving every expert with the first entry's format (e.g. `INT8_PB_WO` gate/up beside NVFP4 down).

## Validation

Environment: this branch on `main` @ cfd86e432, editable install whose compiled ops come from the precompiled wheel the venv was installed with (`vllm 0.33.0rc1.dev774+gb1b0f16ce`, older than this branch's Python sources; no compiled sources are changed here). The OLMoE runs below were first made on `main` @ 05caae03c. Python 3.12, torch 2.14.0+cu130, transformers 5.22.1, humming-kernels 0.1.18, 1-2x NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q (sm_120).

**Tests in `tests/quantization/test_modelopt.py`:**
- `test_modelopt_int8_pb_wo_checkpoint` now also builds a tiny random Qwen3-MoE (8 experts, top-2) and compares its prompt logprobs with the same checkpoint holding the dequantized weights (atol 0.02). New cases:
  - whole-model `INT8_PB_WO` group 32, bf16 (experts and attention; router excluded);
  - `MIXED_PRECISION` in bf16: group-16 experts beside group-32 q/k/v, an FP8 `o_proj`, and an unquantized router and `lm_head`.
  - The expert weights get uneven magnitudes per 16 inputs, as trained experts have, so a scale applied to the wrong group or expert shows.
- `test_modelopt_int8_pb_wo_experts_share_algo_and_group_size` replaces `test_modelopt_int8_pb_wo_rejects_moe`: `INT8_PB_WO` experts beside NVFP4 ones, or beside another group size, raise `ValueError`.

```
VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn pytest tests/quantization/test_modelopt.py -k int8_pb_wo   # 12 passed (4 e2e: 47-69 s each)
VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn pytest tests/quantization/test_modelopt.py                # 129 passed, 1 failed (pre-existing, see below)
pre-commit run --files <changed files>                                                         # all hooks pass
```

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| New MoE e2e cases, max \|Δ prompt logprob\| vs dequantized reference | 0.002 (whole-model g32, Marlin); 0.004 (mixed g16, Triton) |
| New tests on `main`'s `modelopt.py` | all 4 fail: both MoE e2e cases with `NotImplementedError: ModelOpt INT8_PB_WO supports linear layers only`, both validation cases with that instead of `ValueError` |
| Injected scale bug (expert scales rolled by one group) | Δ 0.106 (g32 Marlin), vs 0.002 without |
| This method vs the previous one (a `CompressedTensorsWNA16MoEMethod` subclass), same base, scratch matrix below | bit-identical prompt logprobs in all 11 setups, same backends selected |
| Feature parity with the previous method, same base: forced `--moe-backend` triton / marlin / humming, fp16 activations, DP=2 + EP, `reload_weights`, `VLLM_HUMMING_INPUT_QUANT_CONFIG` | bit-identical where both run; the same backends and configurations refused in both |

**Tiny-MoE scratch matrix** (same model as the test; max \|Δ\| of `INT8_PB_WO` vs dequantized reference): TP=1 Marlin g32 0.0020, Triton mixed g16 0.0039, Humming g32 0.0020 / mixed g16 0.0020, CUDA graphs on (Marlin g32 0.0019, Triton mixed g16 0.0020), TP=2 Triton g16 0.0019, TP=2 + expert parallel (mixed g16) 0.0020, TP=2 Humming g32 0.0000, TP=2 Marlin g32 with `moe_intermediate_size` 256: 0.0020.

**Real model** (scratch script, not committed): OLMoE-1B-7B-0924-Instruct (64 experts, top-8, 16 layers) with every routed-expert projection RTN-quantized to `INT8_PB_WO` (3072 layers) as `MIXED_PRECISION`; everything else BF16. The reference is the same checkpoint with the experts dequantized to BF16. Mean prompt logprob over a 158-token passage, and greedy output (identical 48-token continuations in every run):

| Setup | INT8_PB_WO | dequantized reference | original BF16 |
|---|---|---|---|
| g16, TP=1, Triton | -2.2224 | -2.2243 | -2.2211 |
| g16, TP=1, Humming | -2.2204 | -2.2243 | -2.2211 |
| g32, TP=1, Marlin | -2.2213 | -2.2190 | -2.2211 |
| g16, TP=2, Triton | -2.2173 | -2.2129 | -2.2113 |
| g16, TP=2 + EP, Triton | -2.2064 | -2.2026 | -2.2147 |

Rerun with this method on `main` @ cfd86e432 (g16, TP=1, Triton): prompt logprobs bit-identical to the first run for the `INT8_PB_WO`, reference and BF16 checkpoints alike. Per token, `INT8_PB_WO` vs reference differs by a mean \|Δ\| of 0.033-0.047 (max 0.22-0.49). That is OLMoE's routing noise, not quantization: the original BF16 checkpoint run on two setups (Triton MoE at TP=1 vs default at TP=2) differs by a mean of 0.040 (max 0.22), and the reference by 0.056 (max 0.51).

**Not run:** other GPU generations (Hopper, Ampere, L4; SM75 is claimed from the kernels' capability), ROCm/XPU, a checkpoint written by ModelOpt itself (NVIDIA/Model-Optimizer#3176), large MoE models (e.g. GLM-5.3-Flash), lm-eval accuracy, layerwise weight reload, EPLB, experts with biases.

Notes:
- CI: main's re-enabled `:nvidia: (H200 MIG 35GB) Quantization` step runs `tests/quantization/`, including these tests, on Hopper; this PR changes no CI file. These tests have not run on Hopper yet, so that step will be their first Hopper run.
- Pre-existing, not changed here: at TP=2 with a 32-wide intermediate partition (tiny model, `moe_intermediate_size` 64), Marlin MoE output deviates (max \|Δ\| 0.023-0.117 vs its TP=1 result), for compressed-tensors checkpoints exactly as for `INT8_PB_WO` (bit-identical logprobs between the two). Humming and Triton do not, and Marlin does not with a 128-wide partition. The tests run at TP=1.
- Pre-existing on `main` on this machine: `test_modelopt_fp8_pb_wo_checkpoint_setup` fails on sm_120 (UE8M0-packed scale dtype assertion).

## Details

- `ModelOptInt8Config.get_quant_method` returns `ModelOptInt8PbWoMoEMethod(group_size, moe_config)` for routed experts that are not excluded; `ModelOptMixedPrecisionConfig` does so when `_int8_pb_wo_experts_group_size` finds `INT8_PB_WO` entries under the experts' prefix. The latter scans every `quantized_layers` key under `<experts>.`, so a mixed layer is caught regardless of which entry comes first.
- `ModelOptInt8PbWoMoEMethod` selects the backend in `__init__` with the uint8b128 group `QuantKey` and `WNA16WeightFormat(8, group_size)`. `create_weights` registers `w13_weight` / `w2_weight` (int32, packed on load) and `w13_weight_scale` / `w2_weight_scale` under the names ModelOpt's per-expert tensors map to. The scales are tagged as block scales, like ModelOpt MXFP8's, so the ModelOpt branch of `RoutedExperts.weight_loader` loads them per group rather than as per-tensor scales. `process_weights_after_loading` converts through the oracle and builds the kernel; `get_fused_moe_quant_config` uses Humming's quant config on Humming and `make_wna16_moe_quant_config` otherwise.
- `WNA16WeightFormat` is handled where the oracle reads bit width and group size: Marlin's group-size check and conversion, and a Humming adapter (`_WNA16FormatHummingWeightSchema`) that passes the packed weights and scales to Humming's native weight schema, as the existing `moe_wna16` adapter does.
- `_pack_int8_pb_wo` is now shared by the linear `KInt8Static` loader and the MoE loader.
- Docs: `docs/features/quantization/modelopt.md` describes `INT8_PB_WO` MoE support and the one-format-per-MoE-layer rule.

**Limitations**:
- Experts with biases (gpt-oss style) raise `NotImplementedError`, and so does EPLB (`enable_eplb`): its rebalancing is not validated for these experts.
- MoE experts are supported on NVIDIA GPUs (Marlin, Triton, Humming). On other platforms they raise `NotImplementedError`, including ROCm, where #67302 serves `INT8_PB_WO` linear layers with Triton but these experts are not validated.
- With fp16 activations, `INT8_PB_WO` linear layers at group 16 still hit the Exllama bug (#60608, fixed by #60921); MoE experts do not use Exllama.
- `modelopt_int8` is still not added to ROCm's or XPU's supported-quantization lists.

**Duplicate check**: I searched open PRs (`modelopt int8 moe`, `INT8_PB_WO`, `modelopt W8A16 moe`, `modelopt int8 experts`, `modelopt weight-only moe`, `ModelOptInt8`, `int8 weight-only fused moe modelopt`). None adds INT8 weight-only MoE for ModelOpt checkpoints.

commits.pr_title: [CI] Say when /ci rocm cache comes before the base image is pushed
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`/ci rocm cache` now says when this PR's CI is still building the ROCm base image, instead of claiming that no build built it.

## Claims

- If a build of the PR is still running and hasn't recorded `rocm-rocm-stack-built` yet, the reply links that build and asks the author to comment `/ci rocm cache` again once its ROCm base image step finishes. It also says the rest of the build doesn't need to pass.
- The reply when no build exists and the other refusals are unchanged.

## Validation

```bash
cd .github/workflows/scripts && python -m pytest -q test_run_ci_command.py
# 75 passed, 117 subtests passed
```

- New test `test_cache_waits_for_a_running_build_to_push_the_base_image`: fails without the change, passes with it.
- `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `pre-commit run` on both files are clean.

## Details

`build.sh` sets `rocm-rocm-stack-built` only after it pushes the base image. A PR that changes `docker/Dockerfile.rocm_base` therefore has no source build for the first hour or more of its first CI run.

During that window, `/ci rocm cache` used to reply: "no CI build of this PR built the ROCm base image itself. Run `/ci run`, then `/ci rocm cache` once it passes". That points authors at a second `/ci run` they don't need, and at waiting for the whole build to pass, which isn't required either.

The handler already lists every build of the PR to find the source. It now keeps that list and, when no source is found, checks it for an active build using the existing `is_active_build`.

commits.pr_title: [Frontend] Port the Muse Spark parsers to the streaming parser engine
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Port the Muse Spark parsers (`muse`, `musespark`) to the streaming parser engine instead of patching the legacy reasoning parser. Since `muse_glimmer` is unchanged, #54453 stays open for #54585.

## Claims

- `muse` and `musespark` resolve to a `ParserEngine` parser. The only engine change is a `_streaming_engine_cls` hook.
- Parser CPU time for one 7,608-token reply: 3.79 s to 0.027 s for `parse_delta`, 4.68 s to 0.002 s for the structured-output reasoning-end check.
- ATEM quoted in a `to=user` answer is no longer parsed as a tool call, and output without a message header is no longer dropped in streaming.

## Validation

macOS arm64 (CPU). Tokenizers from `amd/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-Quark-MXFP4` (tokenizer files hash-identical to the gated repo) and `meta-models/Muse-Glimmer-30B`.

- `pytest tests/parser/engine/test_muse.py`: 26 passed. On main, 4 fail.
- `MUSE_CKPT=... MUSE_GLIMMER_CKPT=... pytest tests/tool_use/test_muse*.py tests/parser/engine/test_replay.py tests/parser/engine/test_delegating_replay.py`: all passed.
- A parity harness over 62 outputs (streaming at 1, 2, 5 tokens and one delta, non-streaming, reasoning tokens, reasoning end) matched the old parser except for the changes below.

## Details

Each message is routed by the recipient before `<|message|>`, matched by token id. A `to=NAME` written after a body without `<|eom|>` is held back until the next token. Reasoning end is found with `rfind_tokens`, so steps without `<|message|>` decode nothing. Differences from the old parser:
- Reasoning ends at the tool header, 5 tokens before `<atem:function_calls>`.
- With `tool_choice="none"` or no tools, a tool message is dropped instead of returned as raw framing.
- A tool call cut off by `max_tokens` no longer leaks framing in non-streaming.
- Non-streaming drops content after a tool call in the same reply, as for other engine parsers (#55199).

Engine tests are allowlisted out of CI like the rest of `tests/parser/engine`. No model was served.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Fix GPU sync check failures in NemotronLabsDiffusion
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`test_greedy_generation` and `test_stochastic_rollouts` in `tests/models/language/generation/test_nemotron_dllm.py` fail with `RuntimeError: GPU<->CPU sync detected` since https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58387. This change removes the blocking syncs in the NemotronLabsDiffusion request state and in its logprobs path. Only top-k logprobs wider than the fixed stash (more than `MAX_LOGPROB_TOKEN_IDS`, or `logprobs=-1`) keep an explicit `gpu_sync_allowed()` read, as in `diffusion_gemma.py`.

## Claims

- `test_nemotron_dllm.py` passes in full under `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` (24 passed, 0 failed).
- Per-request state setup and teardown (`add_request`, `remove_request`, `init_canvas`) and the logprobs path for `logprobs` from 0 to `MAX_LOGPROB_TOKEN_IDS` no longer sync with the host.
- Requests with `logprobs=0` in a batch with top-k requests now report each token's logprob at the step it was revealed. Before, they reported the converging step's logprob of tokens revealed earlier (for example rank 67747 for a greedy token).
- Batches where every request asks for the same `logprobs` return the same tokens, logprobs, and ranks as before.
- New tests in `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_nemotron_dllm_sampler.py` cover mixed-width and full-vocab logprobs under the sync check. They run in `V1 Executor + Worker`; existing tests are unchanged.

## Validation

Failing jobs in the 2026-11-18 nightly (ci #103780, `main` @ `e975177`):

- `(MI355 DPX) Language Models (Extended Generation)` Shard 4/5, both attempts on different nodes: https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/103780#01a1ed78-adb7-4c81-8729-a1c59971ff65 and https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/103780#01a1ed88-cc6e-47f8-befc-ccbcaba50745
- `(H200 MIG 35GB) [Nightly] Language Models (Extended Generation)` Shard 7/7, same two tests and the same traceback: https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/103780#01a1ed78-ae2f-4e2f-8224-bd705445e26a

Validation ran on MI355 in that build's CI image `rocm/vllm-ci:build-01a1ed74-99d9-46e2-a7fb-13fa0bdee43d`, which sets `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`. The patched runs copy only the changed `nemotron_dllm.py` (and the new test file) over the image.

```bash
cd /vllm-workspace/tests
pytest -v -s models/language/generation/test_nemotron_dllm.py
pytest -v v1/worker/test_gpu_nemotron_dllm_sampler.py
```

| Run | `test_nemotron_dllm.py` | `test_gpu_nemotron_dllm_sampler.py` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Stock image | 2 failed, 22 passed (`test_greedy_generation`, `test_stochastic_rollouts`) | n/a |
| Previous PR commit `72d63a2` (syncs under `gpu_sync_allowed()`) | 24 passed | 2 failed (wrong `logprobs=0` rank in a mixed batch; narrow requests get full-vocab rows next to `logprobs=-1`) |
| This change | 24 passed | 2 passed |

Output comparison with `nvidia/Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion-3B` (4 chat prompts, `max_tokens=64`, seed 0), stock code with the sync check off against this change with it on:

| Batch | Tokens | Logprobs and ranks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `logprobs=5`, greedy | identical | identical |
| `logprobs=3`, temperatures 0 / 0.7 / 1.0 / 1.5, `top_p=0.9` | identical | identical |
| `logprobs=0`, greedy | identical | max difference 9.5e-7 |
| `logprobs` None / 0 / 2 / 5 in one batch | identical | identical for 2 and 5. For 0, stock gave ranks up to 67747 with logprobs near -22.9; this change gives rank 1 and matches the `logprobs=0`-only batch exactly |

<details>
<summary>Raw output</summary>

Stock image:

```text
/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/model_executor/models/nemotron_dllm.py:452: in add_request
E               RuntimeError: GPU<->CPU sync detected - avoid it or wrap with gpu_sync_allowed()
FAILED models/language/generation/test_nemotron_dllm.py::test_greedy_generation
FAILED models/language/generation/test_nemotron_dllm.py::test_stochastic_rollouts
============= 2 failed, 22 passed, 21 warnings in 92.56s (0:01:32) =============
```

With this change:

```text
================= 24 passed, 23 warnings in 107.90s (0:01:47) ==================
v1/worker/test_gpu_nemotron_dllm_sampler.py::test_mixed_logprobs_reach_the_commit_step_without_a_host_sync PASSED [ 50%]
v1/worker/test_gpu_nemotron_dllm_sampler.py::test_full_vocab_logprobs_come_on_the_commit_step PASSED [100%]
======================== 2 passed, 17 warnings in 3.75s ========================
```

New tests against the previous PR commit `72d63a2`, in a copy without the `max_logprobs` constructor argument that commit lacks:

```text
            if k == 0:
                # Greedy reveals the argmax, so its rank is 1.
>               assert (lp.sampled_token_ranks == 1).all()
E               assert np.False_
FAILED v1/worker/test_unit_oldpr.py::test_mixed_logprobs_reach_the_commit_step_without_a_host_sync
FAILED v1/worker/test_unit_oldpr.py::test_full_vocab_logprobs_come_on_the_commit_step
```

</details>

## Details

Root cause: assigning a Python scalar to a single element of a 1-D GPU tensor (`t[i] = v`) gives a 0-dim destination, so PyTorch performs a blocking host-to-device `copy_` of the scalar. Assigning to a row of a 2-D tensor goes through `fill_` and does not sync. The same holds for `t[gpu_index] = v`. After warmup the sync check rejects these in `execute_model` and `sample_tokens`:

- `add_request`: `is_encoder_phase[slot_idx] = True` and `step[slot_idx] = 0`. `remove_request` has the same pattern.
- `init_canvas`: `canvas[slot_indices] = mask_token_id` with a GPU index tensor.
- `MaskedDiffusionSampler.__call__` with logprobs: `just_converged.any()`, per-index `.item()`, and `is_committing.cpu()`.

The change:

- Uses `.fill_()` for the per-slot scalars and `index_fill_()` for the canvas reset, matching `diffusion_gemma.py`.
- Replaces the host reads in the logprobs path with the design `diffusion_gemma.py` uses:
  - Top-k of the converging step goes into a fixed `[max_num_reqs, canvas_length, 1 + max_logprobs]` GPU stash (capped at `MAX_LOGPROB_TOKEN_IDS`) through a masked write, so the host never learns which slots converged. It is allocated before memory profiling.
  - Every logprobs request in decode gets a canvas of rows each step: the at-reveal logprob for `logprobs=0`, the stash for top-k. The scheduler slices only `num_sampled` rows per request, so the host never learns which slots commit.
  - Top-k wider than the stash reads back which of those slots converged and which emit, inside `gpu_sync_allowed()`, only on steps with such a request. A `[canvas_length, vocab]` stash per slot would not fit.
- Top-k requests now compute their top-k on every denoising step instead of only on the converging step. One sampler step on MI355 (64 requests, canvas 32, vocab 131072, eager sampler outside the model) measures:

  | Batch | Before (`72d63a2`) | This change | Peak memory |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | all `logprobs=5` | 1.86 ms | 4.57 ms | +2.00 GiB in both |
  | half `logprobs=5`, half none | 1.85 ms | 3.46 ms | +2.00 GiB in both |
  | all `logprobs=0` | 1.82 ms | 1.66 ms | +2.00 GiB in both |

  Peak memory is set by the masked step's own fp32 copies of the logits, so the top-k does not raise it. When every decode request asks for top-k, the top-k runs on those logits without a copy. Skipping unconverged rows on the device would need a fused kernel like `stash_converged_logprobs` in `diffusion_gemma.py`, which puts the argmax rather than the sampled token in column 0.

No open PR touches `vllm/model_executor/models/nemotron_dllm.py` (checked all PRs opened since 2026-11-17).

commits.pr_title: [Feature] Add optional GPU timing to iteration metrics
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Add optional GPU duration to the existing iteration logs (`--enable-logging-iteration-details`). The output worker times each iteration with CUDA events and attaches each finished record to a step output or dummy-batch reply it sends anyway; nothing waits for a timing. **In the configurations the worker does not time (listed under Limits), the Iteration line is still logged but no longer carries an elapsed time:** the wall-clock measurement EngineCore makes on main (logged since #31193, reported through `SchedulerStats.iteration_details` since #46647) is removed, as requested in review. Builds on the scheduling snapshots of #61424; adds no workload statistics, heartbeat or publisher.

**Latest change (three commits, head `f792dcaabb`): the remaining three review comments, with one change to the log output and one to the stat-logger interface (see Limits).**

- `936fbc97d0` removes the wall-clock fallback. `EngineCore.capture_iteration_details` was a context manager only to take two timestamps; it is replaced by a plain method, `EngineCore._untimed_iteration_details`, that builds the record once the step's output is in. `SchedulerIterationDetails.elapsed_ms` is `float | None`, and the logger leaves `, iteration elapsed time: … ms` out when it is unset. Compared with main, the configurations listed under Limits lose that number and keep every Iteration line; the commit itself adds or removes no Iteration line in any configuration.
- `aaa3b945fd` puts EngineCore's record into `SchedulerStats.iteration_records`, the field the worker's records already use, and removes `SchedulerStats.iteration_details` (which main has) and the logger's second branch.
- `f792dcaabb` names the three conditions of `VllmConfig.gpu_iteration_timing` (`frontend_logs`, `worker_returns_records`, `worker_times`); its value is unchanged.

**Before that (`8a70ac285f`), no behavior change:** the timer module is now `vllm/v1/worker/iteration_timing.py` and its test `tests/v1/worker/test_iteration_timing.py`; the timer is created in `Worker.__init__` instead of through a class attribute assigned in `init_device`; the two paragraphs this PR had added to `docs/design/metrics.md` are dropped.

**Earlier (`d9b0077803`): the idle flush is gone.** Until then the PR sent an RPC when the engine ran out of work and waited for it in the idle loop. Removing it deleted 154 lines from `vllm/` (and added 17). It also withdrew the previous claim that every timed iteration is logged before the engine idles: the last records (0 to 2 on one engine, 1 to 12 per DP rank in the runs below) are now logged when the engine next steps, however much later, and never if it shuts down first.

Dependency navigation: **#61690 (timing)** → #61691 (workload) → #52061 (FPM exporter). Only #61690 is updated here; the follow-ups are not restacked. [Review this layer](https://github.com/tedzhouhk/vllm/compare/adadaad8b185568d1e91cf6ed92ee687469ee819...f792dcaabbaae03b0e5b5eb221dc672a623ee220). Not a duplicate: #61424 (merged) collects the per-iteration request and token counts this PR reuses and measures no GPU time; #61842, which explored ending the interval at output readiness, is closed. Related RFCs: #61423, #39979, #38760.

## Claims

- **Same flag, GPU time where supported.** `--enable-logging-iteration-details` stays default-off. For generative models on a `cuda` device (multimodal encoder-only serving excluded) with the `uni` or `mp` executor, one API server process and `VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING` at its default, the logged elapsed time is measured on the GPU, from the start of `execute_model` to the end of sampling and drafting (with the built-in worker class; see Limits for custom ones).
- **Elsewhere the line has no elapsed time.** Other configurations log the same iterations as on main, in the same order and with the same index and counts, without the `iteration elapsed time` clause. On main that clause holds EngineCore's wall-clock time around its wait for the step's output. With more than one API server there are no iteration lines at all, as on main.
- **A record is logged at most once, with the request and token counts of its iteration,** DP dummy batches included, and in order (one exception, which was not run: DP with pipeline parallelism, see Limits). Records not yet handed to a reply when the engine stops stepping stay in the worker and leave with the first reply after it resumes, or a later one if the GPU has not finished them by then (never later than the second in the runs below). Apart from a record dropped for a CUDA error or carried by an output that fault-tolerance recovery discards, only those pending at shutdown are never logged.
- **The engine waits for nothing new.** There is no flush, polling, thread, timeout or new channel. `vllm/v1/engine/core.py` changes by +26 / −26: the wall-clock context manager around the wait for a step's output becomes a method called after that wait, which builds an untimed record only where the worker does not time; that record goes into `iteration_records`; and `EngineCoreProc.execute_dummy_batch` publishes the records a dummy batch returns.
- **The bookkeeping is in the worker.** `IterationTimer` is touched only by the worker's main thread. The engine sends the worker no iteration id and matches nothing on return: a record carries its own index and counts. There is no engine-side collector, no event pool and no lock. `gpu_worker.py` changes by +12 / −0: an import, one line in `Worker.__init__` that creates the timer, and three function-level decorators. The bodies of `execute_model`, `sample_tokens` and `execute_dummy_batch` are unchanged.
- **The timer never waits for the GPU.** It records two events per iteration and reads a duration only once `query()` reports the end event complete. Its calls take about 35 µs of host time per iteration.
- **A CUDA error in the timer does not fail the step.** PyTorch raises CUDA errors as `RuntimeError`; one raised while creating, recording or reading an event drops that record, and the iteration keeps its index. The warning is logged once per process for each distinct message.

## Validation

Head `f792dcaabbaae03b0e5b5eb221dc672a623ee220` is `26d21f5a0a` plus two merges of main by a maintainer (up to main `adadaad8b185568d1e91cf6ed92ee687469ee819`) and the four review follow-up commits above. `26d21f5a0a` is this PR's change (`d9b0077803`), a merge of main `4b88a438fb3efd4e11186ab06571d43d8eb514de` (two conflicting import lines; the PR's diff against main was unchanged) and a one-line fix that moved the timer's creation out of `_init_workspace_and_model_runner`, which `test_cumem.py::test_runtime_state_survives_sleep` calls on a stand-in worker. On a GPU that test failed before the fix; it passes on this head, where the timer is created in `Worker.__init__`.

Everything below except the unit tests and the comparison of lines before and after the last three commits was measured before that merge, on `d9b0077803` and its base `75be5c3919b6a82fa1885c0d0a2250adba477413` ("the base"), with the test-only logging described below, on two H100 PCIe GPUs with PyTorch 2.14.0+cu130 and the precompiled binaries of the base. After those runs one docstring, two comments and one paragraph of `docs/design/metrics.md` (since removed) were reworded to give `d9b0077803`; no code changed. After the merge the record checks were repeated and passed: 11 server runs on the merged tree (8,579 iterations timed, 8,527 logged, 52 pending at shutdown), 2 runs where timing must stay off, and 5 runs on `26d21f5a0a` (3,016 / 2,990 / 26). Latency was not measured again. No server was run on a GPU after `26d21f5a0a`: the two later merges of main and the review follow-ups are covered only by the unit tests and the simulated comparison below. In particular, no server run has produced an Iteration line without an elapsed time, and the GPU-timed server runs were not repeated after the engine-side changes of the last three commits. No upstream CI result is part of this evidence; when this was written Buildkite had last run on `fad5e56392` (build 103510), not on this head.

**Records.** Test-only instrumentation, not part of this PR, wrote three views of every iteration, from the engine, the worker and the frontend (three processes; two with UniProc, where the worker runs in the engine process): the engine logged each iteration it launched that the worker should time, the timer logged each iteration it timed and how many finished records left with each reply, and the frontend logged each record on arrival. A checker required for every engine that:

- the logged indices are exactly 0 to n−1 in log order;
- the timer timed exactly the iterations the engine launched, in the same order;
- each logged record carries the request and token counts and the dummy flag of the iteration with its index;
- each logged duration is at least 0.2 ms and fits between the worker's `start()` call and the record's arrival at the frontend, singly and summed over 8 consecutive iterations;
- every record handed to a reply was logged, and the records not logged are the ones in the timer's queue at shutdown.

All checks passed in the 25 server runs before the merge: 48,054 iterations timed, 47,890 logged, 164 pending at shutdown. Independently written scripts recomputed these and the items below from the raw logs.

<details>
<summary>Per-run counts and server commands</summary>

| Configuration | Model | Timed / logged / pending at shutdown |
| --- | --- | --- |
| UniProc; with `--no-async-scheduling` | Qwen3-0.6B | 389 / 387 / 2, 229 / 228 / 1 |
| Multiproc; with `--no-async-scheduling` | Qwen3-0.6B | 390 / 388 / 2, 229 / 228 / 1 |
| TP = 2; PP = 2 | Qwen3-0.6B | 230 / 228 / 2, 1,168 / 1,168 / 0 |
| EAGLE-3; MTP speculative decoding | Qwen3-0.6B; Qwen3.5-0.8B | 278 / 277 / 1, 185 / 183 / 2 |
| DP = 2 with expert parallel, one API server; with `--no-async-scheduling` | PowerMoE-3b | 832 / 812 / 20, 512 / 494 / 18 |
| Multiproc; Multiproc with `--no-async-scheduling`; TP = 2; UniProc; DP = 2, each with 2,000 to 3,000 one-token requests at random times | Qwen3-0.6B; PowerMoE-3b | 3,015 / 3,013 / 2, 3,119 / 3,118 / 1, 2,713 / 2,711 / 2, 3,119 / 3,117 / 2, 10,208 / 10,190 / 18 |
| Multiproc; UniProc; DP = 2; DP = 2 with `--dp-sync-interval 1`, requests that end at a stop token | Qwen3-0.6B; PowerMoE-3b | 311 / 309 / 2, 307 / 305 / 2, 3,520 / 3,500 / 20, 1,228 / 1,226 / 2 |
| DP = 2 with expert parallel, probes 0 to 70 ms after a request | PowerMoE-3b | 12,960 / 12,940 / 20 |
| Multiproc; DP = 2, with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` | Qwen3-0.6B; PowerMoE-3b | 669 / 669 / 0, 832 / 812 / 20 |
| Reruns of UniProc, Multiproc and DP = 2 with the timer's host time logged | Qwen3-0.6B; PowerMoE-3b | 389 / 387 / 2, 390 / 388 / 2, 832 / 812 / 20 |

## Details

**What is measured.** One pair of CUDA events per iteration on the output worker's stream, from the start of `execute_model` to the end of sampling and speculative drafting. It is the time the iteration occupied that stream, including host submission gaps, not kernel-busy time. With pipeline parallelism it is measured on the last stage and includes waiting for the earlier stages.

**How a record reaches the log.** The worker attaches each record to the first step output or dummy-batch reply built after the record's end event has completed: the iteration's own output when the GPU has already finished (most one-step requests in the runs above), otherwise a later reply.

**Where the worker does not time,** EngineCore builds the record itself once the step's output is in, with the index and counts it has on main and no elapsed time, and reports it in the same `iteration_records` field. With the built-in worker and scheduler classes an engine has one producer of records: the worker where `gpu_iteration_timing` holds, EngineCore elsewhere. Such a line reads `Engine 000: Iteration(6): 1 context requests, 8 context tokens, 2 generation requests, 2 generation tokens, CPU KV cache usage: 25.0%`; a timed one has `, iteration elapsed time: 1.50 ms` after the generation tokens.

**When the engine goes idle** nothing is sent. Records not yet handed to a reply stay in the worker's `IterationTimer`. A log line has no timestamp of its iteration, only the logger's, so a held line appears among the lines of the next busy period, however long the engine was idle. Its KV cache usage is the usage when it is logged.

**Limits.**

- Iterations still pending at shutdown are not logged: 0 to 2 on one engine and 1 to 10 on each DP rank in the runs above.
- A consumer that pairs DP ranks by `iteration_index` has to keep records across idle periods. The index counts a worker's timed iterations since it started; nothing renumbers it when a rank is added or restarted, which was not tested.
- **Configurations that lose the elapsed time they log on main.** The worker does not time them, so their Iteration lines keep the counts and drop the time: devices other than `cuda` (CPU and XPU in-tree, and out-of-tree platforms such as TPU; ROCm's device type is `cuda`, so the timer is enabled there, which was not run); pooling models (only the `generate` runner reaches `sample_tokens`, where the worker ends a timed iteration; speculative decoding is not affected, its draft model runs inside a `generate` engine); multimodal encoder-only serving; the `ray` and `external_launcher` executors and any executor given as a class or qualified name, which includes the in-tree `CUDACheckpointExecutor`; and `VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0`, where the offline `LLM` runs the engine in-process and only `EngineCoreProc` publishes the records a dummy batch returns (the server keeps its engine process with that setting, and the timer is off there too). The DP dummy lines of those configurations, which are logged only without a DP coordinator, lose it as well. `--no-async-scheduling` alone is not in this list: on a timed configuration the worker times synchronous steps too.
- What is given up there: main's number is the wall-clock time of EngineCore's wait for a step's output. Without a batch queue (async scheduling off, PP = 1) and with a multi-process executor that wait covers the worker's `execute_model` and `sample_tokens` (it starts after the step is dispatched and its grammar bitmask computed, so a structured-output step is under-reported by the bitmask time), so the number was a usable step duration; the CPU platform runs that way by default. This follows from the code and from `EngineCore.step()` run over a fake executor, not from a server run.
- The predicate does not look at `--worker-cls` or the scheduler class. On a configuration it treats as timed, an out-of-tree worker that does not go through `Worker.execute_model`, `sample_tokens` and `execute_dummy_batch` returns no records and EngineCore builds none, so no Iteration line is logged, where main logs it with the wall-clock time; a custom scheduler that does not hand on the worker output's `iteration_records` has the same effect. This was already so before the last three commits; it follows from the code and was not run.
- For stat loggers and other consumers: `SchedulerStats.iteration_details`, which main has since #46647, is removed. A stat logger reads the list `SchedulerStats.iteration_records` instead, and `SchedulerIterationDetails.elapsed_ms` can be `None`, so a record no longer implies a GPU time. `rust/` is not touched: the Rust client's mirror of `SchedulerStats` keeps an optional `iteration_details` field that nothing reads, and ignores the new key.
- With DP, pipeline parallelism and async scheduling (the default) together, the batch queue holds PP + 1 steps, three or more. A dummy batch can then run while a sampled step is still in flight. Its records are published at once, ahead of the records on that step's output, so neighbouring records can be logged out of order. This follows from the code and was not run.
- Fault-tolerance recovery drains the batch queue and keeps only the KV connector outputs, so records on the drained outputs are lost. This follows from the code and was not run.
- The unit tests use fake CUDA events, a stand-in worker and `SimpleNamespace` stand-ins for the engine, the config and the stat logger. This PR adds no test that runs a server with GPU timing; that path is covered only by the serving runs above, outside CI.
- Latency was not measured for DP with load on both ranks (the record checks include iterations that were real on both). Not run: AMD GPUs (ROCm's device type is also `cuda`, so the timer is enabled there), more than two DP ranks, DP without expert parallel, larger models, several nodes, streaming, aborted or preempted requests, structured output, and a shutdown under load.

Add optional GPU duration to the existing iteration logs. The output worker times each iteration with CUDA events and emits complete records, which ride on later step outputs. ## Claims

- **Same flag, GPU time where supported.** `--enable-logging-iteration-details` stays default-off. For generative models on CUDA with the `uni` or `mp` executor, one API server process and an out-of-process EngineCore, the logged elapsed time is measured on the GPU, from the start of `execute_model` to the end of sampling and drafting. Other configurations keep the wall-clock time they log today.

- **The bookkeeping is in the worker.** `IterationTimer` is touched only by the worker's main thread and emits self-describing records. - **The idle flush is one RPC on the existing reply path:** no polling, thread, timer or new channel. The engine waits for it the way it waits for a step's output, and new work ends the wait, so a request that arrives while the flush is outstanding is not held up by it (measured below).
- **Timing cannot fail a step.** A CUDA error while recording or reading an event drops that record with one warning.

**Review feedback.** There is no polling: the flush is the signal sent when the engine switches from active to inactive, and its reply is an ordinary model-runner output. The worker methods carry decorators only. `vllm/v1/engine/core.py` changes by +87 / −3 lines and `gpu_worker.py` by +19 / −0.

- With a worker that never answers the flush: a request that arrives in the first second makes the engine fail at the step's timeout instead of the flush's, and a control call that was deferred during the last step, or is queued behind new work, runs while the flush is pending, so its own RPC can wait without a timeout, as on main.

The `model_step_cuda` interval includes host submission gaps and stream dependencies; PP measures the last-stage output worker, not whole-pipeline latency, summed GPU time or kernel-only busy time.

Multiple DP dummy records can be discarded at one idle transition; the integration stress observed up to nine per rank/eighteen across two ranks, not a general bound. ## Overview

Add nonblocking GPU duration to existing per-iteration logging. This is the timing layer split from #52061; it does not change scheduler counters or add a workload/export API.

Dependency order: **#61690 (timing)** → #61691 (workload) → #52061 (FPM exporter). This stack is independent of, and complementary to, #61424; that PR is not a prerequisite.
