This main-merge update applies to #61690 only; #61691 and #52061 are intentionally not restacked or updated.

## Claims

- `--enable-logging-iteration-details` enables timing when log statistics and runtime support permit it. Timing remains default-off; `iteration_timing_enabled` is derived before worker initialization, not exposed as another CLI or constructor option. Unsupported logging configurations keep counts-only logs with a warning.
- Existing `compute_iteration_details` supplies the logging snapshot before worker execution. This PR does not change `scheduler.py`, `vllm/v1/utils.py`, or the profiler's counter algorithm. Workload counts and phase snapshots belong to #61691.
- Only the output worker of each DP replica owns pooled `torch.Event` pairs. Completed durations join their own snapshots by iteration ID in `SchedulerStats.iteration_records`. Records are delivered only after both timing and model-output processing complete; internal durations stay in milliseconds.
- Timing covers execute, sampling and speculative drafting, including the complete DP dummy call. Function-level decorators in `iteration_timing.py` keep execution, sampling and dummy control flow out of the worker method bodies while preserving their timing boundaries and cancelling failed iterations. Timing is attached to MRV2 and its encoder-only override, following main's removal of MRV1.
- Existing scheduler statistics stay on their original frontend, preserving request-local LoRA enrichment; completed records are attached once. Frontend zero is only the fallback when no stats owner exists. The producer only appends to the timing deque; one nonblocking drain lock serializes removal, without a second pending-deque lock.
- Normal outputs carry ready samples. Tail collection allows one outstanding RPC and checks readiness/FIFO before consuming it through the existing `result()` path. Unavailable and completed-empty responses remain distinct. Delayed associations survive until the complete record can be joined; no timing-specific CUDA synchronization or blocking flush is added.
- Historical iteration records no longer include current KV-cache usage; periodic KV reporting remains. This layer adds no workload/context statistics, idle heartbeats, Prometheus instruments or publisher.

## Overview

Clean up bitmask allocation in `allocate_token_bitmask`, following up https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/67335.

## Claims

`allocate_token_bitmask` attempted to allocate bitmask with `pin_memory=PIN_MEMORY` and fell back to allocation without `pin_memory`. This copied `llguidance` library's`allocate_token_bitmask` implementation where it first tries with `pin_memory=torch.cuda.is_available()` then falls backs `pin_memory=None`.

In vLLM, `PIN_MEMORY` is true if and only if platform actually supports pinned memory. Fallback is uncessary and an antipattern. This removes it.

commits.pr_title: [MoE][NVIDIA] Support MXFP4 experts on SM107 in flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Stacked on #65974; review only the last commit.

This PR lets flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl run MXFP4 expert layers on SM107 (compute capability 10.7, NVIDIA Rubin) GPUs through FlashInfer's Sm107_Mxfp8_Mxfp4_Bf16_Cutedsl_MegaMoeConfig (FlashInfer >= 0.7.3, detected at runtime). MXFP4 weights and their E8M0 per-32 scales are used as stored; the kernel quantizes activations and the FC1 output to MXFP8.





## Claims

- MXFP4 experts on SM107. Validated end to end on one node with 4x SM107 GPUs (DP4 + EP), one run per arm, 1319 questions each:

  - The original MXFP4 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, with every target expert layer MXFP4 on this backend: GSM8K 0.9022 vs 0.9007 with the default backend.

  - DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-NVFP4 with DSpark (num_speculative_tokens=5), target NVFP4 and draft MXFP4 experts both on this backend: acceptance length 3.553 vs 3.557 with the default backend. The eval is greedy, so GSM8K reflects the target, not the draft: 0.8840 vs 0.8946, within the noise of one run.

- Older FlashInfer is refused per weight format: the probe checks the 0.7.3 field on the MXFP4 config itself, which the pinned 0.7.2.post1 lacks. This is from the FlashInfer source and a CPU case with a fake module; it was not run on a real 0.7.2.post1 install.

- Still refused on SM107: flashinfer_moe_ep_mega_deep_gemm and EPLB at selection; weight reload at load (now for MXFP4 layers too).

- No behavior change on SM100/SM103, including the bf16 requantization of MXFP4 checkpoints. That path's current load failure is addressed by #64563 (open); this PR does not touch it.

  - The SM100/SM103 GPU tests were not re-run: all 16 test_init_warmup_forward_is_exact_on_grid_inputs ids skipped on every runner used here.

  - The claim rests on the new branches being keyed on compute capability 10.7 (the DeepGEMM clause: on any capability outside SM100/SM103), the (10, 0) cases of the CPU selection tests, and the [cutedsl]/[deep_gemm] kwargs ids.

- No performance claim.

## Validation
### Unit tests

| Hardware | FlashInfer | Result (CPU file; kernel file) |
|---|---|---|
| GH200 (SM90) | 0.7.2.post1 (pinned) | `40 passed`; `6 passed, 26 skipped` |
| GH200 (SM90) | 0.7.3 | `40 passed`; `6 passed, 26 skipped, 5 warnings` |
| 4x SM107 | 0.7.3 | `40 passed`; `16 passed, 16 skipped, 5 warnings` |

- Each file was run on its own with `python -m pytest -v -rA <file>`, this commit's `vllm/` files overlaid on a build of 520cae222. On SM107, `flashinfer.__version__` is 0.7.3 and all 4 GPUs report compute capability 10.7; of the documented variables only `CUTE_DSL_ARCH=sm_107a` was set, with no NVSHMEM variable.
- The SM107 exactness tests (6 MXFP4 ids, 4 NVFP4 ids) need 2-4 SM107 GPUs and do not run in CI. They were run on one 4x SM107 node (last row), once each, and all 10 passed. The kwargs test, including its 2 SM107 MXFP4 ids, and the CPU file run in CI against the pinned FlashInfer.
- The MXFP4 exactness test feeds checkpoint-format experts whose every quantization step is exact, and compares bit for bit. It covers the E8M0 scale hand-off, gate/up order, per-expert and EP-local scale indexing, the MXFP8 scale exchange between epilogue warps, and the SwiGLU gate clamp at DeepSeek-V4.1's limit (on the draft-layer geometry).
- `test_sm107_admits_cutedsl_and_refuses_deep_gemm` runs `select_deepseek_v4_mxfp4_moe_backend`, the selector of every CUDA `Mxfp4MoEMethod` layer, at compute capability 10.7.
- What passed and skipped:
  - SM107: the 16 passes are the 6 MXFP4 exactness ids (`[2-dsv4.1-flash]`, `[2-dsv4-flash]`, `[2-dsv4.1-flash-mtp]` and the same at EP 4), the 4 NVFP4 exactness ids and the 6 kwargs ids. The 16 skips are the SM100/SM103 test, "The bf16 MXFP4 path and the DeepGEMM megakernel require SM100/SM103".
  - GH200: the 6 passes are the kwargs ids. The 26 skips are those 16, plus 4 x "The SM107 NVFP4 MoE-EP megakernel requires SM107" and 6 x "The SM107 MXFP4 MoE-EP megakernel requires SM107".
- The 5 warnings on 0.7.3 are FlashInfer's `DeprecationWarning: apply_topk_in_fc1 is deprecated; use apply_routing_weights_before_fc2.` One comes from the unchanged SM100 call (`[cutedsl]`), four from the SM107 config call (`[cutedsl-sm107]`, `[cutedsl-sm107-default]`, `[cutedsl-sm107-mxfp4]`, `[cutedsl-sm107-mxfp4-default]`), as in #<base PR>.
- CuTe DSL's `TYPE_INT_LITERAL_OUT_OF_RANGE` warning from FlashInfer's `software_sync.py` (see #<base PR>) prints once per rank in all 10 SM107 exactness cases, which passed bit-exact, and once per worker at server startup in the arms on this backend; the default-backend arms do not print it.
- On #<base PR> without this commit, the same files give `10 failed, 30 passed` and `6 failed, 26 skipped` (FlashInfer 0.7.3, GH200): 15 failures come from the renamed probe and the new `weight_format` keyword; `test_mxfp4_kernel_format_passes_megakernel_weights_through_on_sm107` fails on behavior (the base still dequantizes MXFP4 experts to bf16 at compute capability 10.7).
- `pre-commit` (ruff, ruff-format, mypy, typos, markdownlint and the repo hooks) passes on the changed files.

### FlashInfer version check

`flashinfer_sm107_gap("nvfp4")` is #<base PR>'s probe, renamed; its table there still applies. For `("mxfp4")`:

| FlashInfer | `flashinfer_sm107_gap("mxfp4")` | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| 0.7.2.post1 (pinned) | ``SM107 with FlashInfer 0.7.2.post1 (requires flashinfer-python>=0.7.3, then `vllm download-kernels`)`` (expected) | Its `Sm107_Mxfp8_Mxfp4_Bf16_Cutedsl_MegaMoeConfig` has `apply_topk_in_fc1` but not `apply_routing_weights_before_fc2` (FlashInfer v0.7.2.post1 source); the CPU case `[mxfp4-old-field]` covers this with a fake module. Not run on a real 0.7.2.post1 install. |
| 0.7.3 | `None` | On the SM107 node the class has the field (the same `inspect.signature` check), and arms SB and MB selected the backend. |

### End to end on SM107

No CI runner has SM107 GPUs, so there is no `LLM`/`RemoteOpenAIServer` regression test in CI for this path. The end-to-end regression is the on-node GSM8K run of DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-NVFP4 with DSpark below (the upstream `gsm8k_eval.py`, plus acceptance length).

Setup:
- One node with 4x SM107 GPUs (compute capability 10.7 on all 4), FlashInfer 0.7.3.
- DP4, TP1, expert parallel, `--max-num-batched-tokens 4096`, `--max-num-seqs 128`; default CUDA-graph mode, FlashInfer autotune at its default (on).
- Runtime environment: of the documented variables only `CUTE_DSL_ARCH=sm_107a` was set. No NVSHMEM variable was set in any step, so this backend ran with NVSHMEM's default heap, and `FLASHINFER_SM107_MEGA_CHECK_ROUTES` was not set. No fallback was used. As in #<base PR>, the server arms also exported harness settings only: home, temp and cache directories, `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1`, a longer engine-ready timeout, Python fault-handler and unbuffered output, and the site's NCCL settings (IB service level, socket interface, NVLink scheduling).
- Arms, one server at a time in this order on the same node:
  - **CP** (fail-before): SB's command on #<base PR> without this commit;
  - **SB** / **SA**: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-NVFP4 with DSpark, with this backend / the default backend;
  - **MB** / **MA**: the original MXFP4 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, no speculative decoding, with this backend / the default backend;
  - **RD**: MB's command with `--moe-backend flashinfer_moe_ep_mega_deep_gemm`.
- Each server arm ran GSM8K and scraped `/metrics` after startup and after GSM8K. Acceptance length (AL) is `1 + accepted / drafts` from the difference of those two scrapes, summed over the 4 DP engines.

Environment: as in #<base PR> (the same image and packages). Differences:
- This PR's four changed files under `vllm/` (#<base PR>'s three plus `oracle/mxfp4.py`) were overlaid on the installed package; arm CP overlaid #<base PR>'s three files instead. The PR changes no compiled code.
- SB, SA and CP run DSpark speculative decoding; #<base PR> ran without it. MB, MA and RD serve the original MXFP4 checkpoint.

Server, NVFP4 + DSpark. One command for SB, SA and CP; only SB and CP pass `--moe-backend`:

```bash
export CUTE_DSL_ARCH=sm_107a
vllm serve nvidia/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-NVFP4 \
  --revision 3431dde3247c13b5957f682b1e3c6fcae2566079 \
  --served-model-name dsv41 --port 8000 --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --language-model-only --trust-remote-code \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 --data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla --max-model-len 8192 --max-num-seqs 128 --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 \
  --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true,"embedding_across_dp":true,"dp_shared_memory":false,"use_thp":true}' \
  --attention-config '{"backend":"FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41","indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5}' \
  --moe-backend flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl   # SB and CP; SA leaves this out
```

Fail-before (CP). With this command on #<base PR> alone, the target's NVFP4 experts load on this backend (#<base PR>'s `Sm107_Nvfp4_Nvfp4_Bf16_Cutedsl_MegaMoeConfig` INFO line on all 4 workers). Loading the DSpark draft then fails at startup with the same error on each of the 4 workers:

```text
(Worker_DP3_EP3) ERROR 11-05 16:29:11 [multiproc_executor.py:1073] ValueError: Mxfp4 MoE backend 'FLASHINFER_MOE_EP_CUTEDSL' does not support the deployment configuration since kernel does not support MXFP4 weights on this GPU.
```

Server, original MXFP4. One command for MB, MA and RD:

```bash
export CUTE_DSL_ARCH=sm_107a
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --revision dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277 \
  --served-model-name dsv41 --port 8000 --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --language-model-only --trust-remote-code \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 --data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla --max-model-len 8192 --max-num-seqs 128 --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 \
  --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true,"embedding_across_dp":true,"dp_shared_memory":false,"use_thp":true}' \
  --attention-config '{"backend":"FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41","indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}' \
  --moe-backend flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl   # MB; MA leaves this out; RD passes flashinfer_moe_ep_mega_deep_gemm
```

RD is still refused at startup, with the same error on each of the 4 workers:

```text
(Worker_DP3_EP3) ERROR 11-05 17:15:30 [multiproc_executor.py:1073] ValueError: Mxfp4 MoE backend 'FLASHINFER_MOE_EP_DEEP_GEMM' does not support the deployment configuration since kernel does not support MXFP4 weights on this GPU.
```

Notes on the server commands:
- The NVFP4 revision is pinned as in #<base PR> (later revisions store the Engram tables as MXFP4); `tests/evals/gsm8k/configs/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-NVFP4-DSpark-TP4.yaml` uses the same pin.
- The MXFP4 revision is the one that ran. On the Hub, the later revisions up to main as of 2026-11-05 (`314113f8`) change no `.safetensors` file and not `config.json`. They add `chat_template.jinja`, which `/v1/completions` does not use, and a `.gitignore`, and change the reference inference code and the encoding scripts.
- Both checkpoints were served from local copies of those revisions. Before the run, a check confirmed each copy's revision marker and FP8 Engram tables, and that the NVFP4 checkpoint's bundled draft experts (`mtp.*`) are MXFP4. The run passed the local directories in place of the Hub ids and `--revision`; the other arguments are as above.

GSM8K, the same command in every server arm:

```bash
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --num-questions 1319 --num-shots 5 \
  --max-tokens 256 --max-concurrency 64 --seed 42
```

NVFP4 + DSpark:

| Arm | `--moe-backend` | MoE backend selected (from the log): target NvFp4 / draft Mxfp4 | GSM8K accuracy | Invalid rate | n | AL |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SA (baseline) | not set | `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM` / `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MXFP4_MXFP8` | 0.8946 | 0.0008 | 1319 | 3.557 |
| SB (this PR) | `flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl` | `FLASHINFER_MOE_EP_CUTEDSL` / `FLASHINFER_MOE_EP_CUTEDSL` | 0.8840 | 0.0008 | 1319 | 3.553 |

Original MXFP4 (no speculative decoding):

| Arm | `--moe-backend` | MoE backend selected (from the log): Mxfp4 | GSM8K accuracy | Invalid rate | n |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| MA (baseline) | not set | `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MXFP4_MXFP8` | 0.9007 | 0.0015 | 1319 |
| MB (this PR) | `flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl` | `FLASHINFER_MOE_EP_CUTEDSL` | 0.9022 | 0.0000 | 1319 |

Why the draft is judged by AL:
- The eval sends temperature 0 to `/v1/completions` (its default), and vLLM's greedy verification accepts a draft token only if it equals the target's argmax. So the GSM8K answers are the target's greedy output, up to numerical differences between batch shapes, and SB - SA compares the target's NVFP4 backends. The draft's experts change how many tokens a step accepts.
- The upstream DSpark GSM8K config notes that loading this draft as NVFP4 "keeps accuracy but drops acceptance length to 1.0 (3.57 when correct)". AL and per-position acceptance are the check on the draft's MXFP4 experts.
- Both drafts compute MXFP4 weights x MXFP8 activations, with different kernels: FlashInfer's SM107 MegaMoE in SB, `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MXFP4_MXFP8` in SA.
- Acceptance per draft position (accepted at position k / drafts, over the 4 engines): SB 0.806, 0.660, 0.486, 0.358, 0.244; SA 0.807, 0.659, 0.488, 0.357, 0.245. Per-engine AL: SB 3.530-3.568, SA 3.552-3.561. Counts: SB 33,966 drafts, SA 34,204.
- AL is not a draft-only measure: acceptance is against the target's argmax, and the DSpark draft reads the target's hidden states, so AL(SB) vs AL(SA) compares the (target, draft) pairs, which differ in both kernels. What AL does detect is a broken draft, which collapses AL toward 1.0. Here the per-position rates agree within 0.002, and AL(SB) - AL(SA) = -0.004 is smaller than the spread across SB's 4 engines (0.038).

How to read the tables:
- One greedy run per arm; within each pair only `--moe-backend` differs.
- The binomial stderr, sqrt(p(1-p)/1319), is 0.0088 (SB), 0.0085 (SA), 0.0082 (MB) and 0.0082 (MA). The stderr of a difference is about 0.012, so one run per arm cannot resolve differences smaller than about 2-3 points.
- SB - SA = -0.0106, about 0.9 of that stderr. MB - MA = +0.0015.
- For reference, #<base PR>'s runs without speculative decoding, on another node with the same image, scored 0.9067 (default) and 0.9007 (this backend). Both DSpark arms here are 1.2-1.7 points lower, within about 1.4 stderr. SA, which runs none of this PR's kernels, shows the same drop, so it is not attributable to this change.
- The main check is the A/B difference on the same node, fixed before the run: |SB - SA| <= 0.03 and |MB - MA| <= 0.03. For the draft, AL >= 2.5 in both SB and SA (the upstream config's `min_acceptance_length`) and AL(SB) >= AL(SA) - 0.10. AL(SB) - AL(SA) = -0.004. All checks pass.
- All four arms are above the 0.85 floor (0.88 - 0.03) of the upstream DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-NVFP4 DSpark config, which runs TP4. There is no upstream GSM8K config for the original MXFP4 checkpoint; the same floor was applied to MB and MA.

## Details

### Design

- Gate: `_FORMAT_CAPABILITIES["mxfp4"]` adds (10, 7); a kernel clause keeps the DeepGEMM megakernel on SM100/SM103 with the existing "MXFP4 weights on this GPU" reason (same shape as #64289's SM90 clause). After this PR the `nvfp4` and `mxfp4` rows are equal; the table is kept for #62603/#64289's `fp8_block` row, and on SM107 only that check's DeepGEMM clause can fire.
- FlashInfer probe per weight format (`flashinfer_sm107_gap`), same field marker and message as #<base PR>.
- Native weight hand-off: `mxfp4_moe_ep_weights` keeps the checkpoint tensors on SM107, as for DeepGEMM; the adapter reinterprets the uint8 E8M0 scale bytes as `torch.float8_e8m0fnu`, which FlashInfer requires. No bf16 copy at load, no `None` scales.
- `FlashInferMoeEp(..., weight_format=)` is optional. The experts set it on SM107 only, from the quant config's weight dtype (the shape of #64289's `sm90_format`). The SM107 config is chosen per format and built with the same keywords as for NVFP4 (`apply_topk_in_fc1=`, `knobs=None`, `combine_dtype="bf16"`); MXFP4 takes no `input_norm_const` and no epilogue.
- Labels: the backend's activation key and quant config keep their existing values; nothing reads them for this backend. Checkpoints that declare MXFP4 activations (compressed-tensors W4A4 MXFP4, online MXFP4) run with MXFP8 activations on SM107 (by code reading; not run), as they run with NVFP4 activations on SM100/SM103; the docs say so.
- The reload refusal on SM107 now covers every format: the existing mark moves out of the NVFP4-only branch. Verified by inspection, as in #<base PR>.
- NVSHMEM: the documented bound becomes `(2 * top_k + 2) * hidden_size * max_num_batched_tokens` per distinct MoE layer shape and format, summed (MXFP4 staging holds activations at 1 byte per element, so the old `+1` bound is too small for it). For DeepSeek-V4.1 at 4096 batched tokens the bound is 280 MiB for the target (top_k 6, hidden 5120) plus 160 MiB for the DSpark draft (top_k 3), 440 MiB in total for SB; MB's MXFP4 target alone is 280 MiB. FlashInfer 0.7.3's symmetric allocation, computed from its sizing code at EP4 and not measured, is about 252.5 + 141.3 = 393.8 MiB for SB. MXFP4 at 1 byte per activation exceeds the old bound: 261.9 vs 260 MiB for an MXFP4 target, 141.3 vs 140 MiB for the draft.
- Size: `vllm/` +63/-29, docs +5/-4, tests +369/-57. Most test lines are the SM107 MXFP4 bit-exact GPU test (weight builder, worker, constants) and the tail it shares with the NVFP4 test; short of end to end, it is the only check of the MXFP4 kernel's numerics. The CPU file gains 3 test ids.

### Limitations

- Validated: DeepSeek-V4.1 only (layouts as in #<base PR>), on FlashInfer 0.7.3. DSpark is the only speculative method run, and only on the NVFP4 checkpoint; the original MXFP4 checkpoint was run without speculative decoding, so an MXFP4 target with an MXFP4 draft on this backend was not run. DeepSeek-V4 MXFP4 is covered by the exactness test's `dsv4-flash` expert shape only. Other MXFP4 producers take the same path but are untested.
- The SwiGLU up clamp on the MXFP4 kernel is not exercised by the exactness test, which covers the gate clamp; it is reached only if the end-to-end runs produce up values beyond the limit.
- MXFP4 on SM107 needs hidden and intermediate sizes divisible by 128 (FlashInfer errors at load otherwise).
- Online MXFP4 still logs a BF16-activation fallback warning for this backend. The kernel quantizes activations itself (MXFP8 on SM107, NVFP4 on SM100/SM103); the same warning already appears on SM100/SM103.
- DSpark (and XPress, which loads its draft through DSpark's loader) still ignores `speculative_config.moe_backend` (#63875 is the prerequisite for overrides); so do the V2 model runner's DFlash and Gemma4 MTP drafters.
- `get_acceptance_length` in `tests/evals/gsm8k/test_gsm8k_correctness.py` keeps only the last `engine=` series of each counter under DP (for example, 3.568 instead of 3.553 for SB here). This PR sums the counters over engines between two scrapes. Fixing the helper is a follow-up.

### Related PRs

- #65974  adds SM107 support for NVFP4 experts; this PR is stacked on it.
- #62603 and #64289 (SM90 MegaMoE) change the same capability gate; this PR keeps their names, and `weight_format` could subsume #64289's `sm90_format`.
- #64563 (open) addresses the SM100/SM103 MXFP4 load failure; this PR does not touch that path.
- #63875 is the prerequisite for a draft `moe_backend` override with this backend; see Limitations.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to write this change and its tests.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Core] Reject batch-sharded sampling with LoRA at startup
commits.pr_body:
﻿## Purpose
Fixes #56068. Models implementing `compute_logits_local` (llama, qwen3_5, deepseek_v4-nvidia, minimax_m3-nvidia) skip the TP logits gather, and the `lm_head` LoRA delta can only be applied after that gather, so `--enable-lora` + `--enable-batch-sharded-sampling` crashed at the first sampling step with `NotImplementedError`. This blocks the combination in `_validate_batch_sharded_sampling` so it fails at startup with a clear reason, matching the existing blockers (return_sampling_mask, adaptive verification).

The rejection is scoped to LoRA configs that target `lm_head` (default targets or an explicit `lm_head` entry), per review feedback; restricted targets such as `["o_proj"]` remain allowed and are covered by a test.

## Test Plan
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_config.py -k batch_sharded -v

## Test Result
Without fix: the new test fails (no ValueError raised). With fix: 3 passed. The 13 other failures in tests/test_config.py are pre-existing on clean main (network/download tests), verified by stash-compare. Crash link reproduced on CPU: NotImplementedError with the wrapped LogitsProcessor and skip_gather=True.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Test] Skip the AITER MoE alignment test where AITER isn't supported
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Gate `test_aiter_moe_alignment_rule_holds_across_block_m` on `is_aiter_found_and_supported()` instead of `on_cdna()`, so it skips instead of failing on gfx90a (MI250) and on ROCm installs without AITER, as raised in review.

This PR originally also made `AiterUnquantizedExperts` reject hidden sizes not divisible by 128. Per review, that gate and its tests were dropped in favor of fixing the kernel limitation in CK (ROCm/rocm-libraries#14587, ROCm/rocm-libraries#14588), so this PR no longer addresses the `tiny-random/qwen3-next-moe` failure in the AITER-ON build.

## Claims

- On gfx90a and on ROCm without AITER, the test is skipped. Before, it ran and failed in `_assert_aiter_supported()` with `AssertionError: aiter is required on supported ROCm hardware for this test`.
- With AITER available, the test still runs and passes on MI300X.
- Test-only change; no runtime code is touched.

## Validation

MI300X (gfx942), AITER 0.1.25, torch 2.12.0+rocm10.0.0:

| Command | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_rocm_aiter_moe.py -k alignment_rule_holds_across_block_m` | 9 passed |
| Same test with gfx90a simulated (below) | main: 9 failed with `aiter is required on supported ROCm hardware for this test`; this PR: 9 skipped |
| Same test with AITER reported missing (below) | main: 9 failed with the same assertion; this PR: 9 skipped |
| `pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_rocm_aiter_moe.py` | 90 passed, 5 skipped |
| `pre-commit run --files tests/kernels/moe/test_rocm_aiter_moe.py` | passed |

No model eval: test-only change.

<details>
<summary>Simulating gfx90a and a missing AITER on MI300X</summary>

Both patch module-level flags before pytest collects the test:

```bash
# gfx90a (MI250)
python -c "
import vllm.platforms.rocm as r; r._ON_GFX90A, r._ON_GFX942 = True, False
import sys, pytest
sys.exit(pytest.main(['tests/kernels/moe/test_rocm_aiter_moe.py', '-k', 'alignment_rule_holds_across_block_m', '-rs']))
"

# AITER not installed
python -c "
import vllm._aiter_ops as a; a.IS_AITER_FOUND = False
import sys, pytest
sys.exit(pytest.main(['tests/kernels/moe/test_rocm_aiter_moe.py', '-k', 'alignment_rule_holds_across_block_m', '-rs']))
"
```

</details>

## Details

- Root cause: `on_cdna()` is also true on gfx90a (CDNA2), but `is_aiter_found_and_supported()` requires CDNA3+ and an installed AITER, so the old gate let the test run where its own `_assert_aiter_supported()` check fails.
- CI coverage: AMD CI only runs this file on GPUs with AITER support, so it doesn't exercise the new skip path; the simulation above covers it.
- Not a duplicate: `main` still gates this test on `on_cdna()`, and no open PR mentions it.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] ParserEngine: scan for the tool name incrementally while streaming
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

While a `ParserEngine` tool call has no name yet, `_handle_arg_chunk` calls `_try_extract_name` for every argument chunk. That joins all argument text received so far (`ToolCallSlot.args`) and searches it again with `_NAME_RE`, so streaming costs O(N^2) until a `"name"` member appears. This PR makes the search incremental: each call scans only the newly appended text plus the tail where a partial match can still complete, using the `regex` module's `partial=True` search. The result is the same leftmost match as before.

## Claims

- Streaming becomes linear for JSON-envelope parsers whose output has no `"name"` member yet. Measured cases through `ChatStreamProcessor.step` (one token per delta):
  - `llama3_json`: a plain JSON answer from Llama 3 when the request has tools (`llama_json` routes any output starting with `{` into the tool path). 16011 tokens: 36.0 s on main, 0.96 s with this PR.
  - `llama3_json`: a call with `"parameters"` before `"name"`. 16022 tokens: 38.5 s on main, 1.00 s with this PR.
  - `ripple`: a call with `"arguments"` before `"name"`. 16026 tokens: 37.5 s on main, 1.07 s with this PR.
- The extracted names, streamed arguments and content are unchanged.

## Validation

Benchmark script: one request, Llama 3 8B Instruct tokenizer (Qwen3 tokenizer for Ripple), the output text tokenized and fed one token per `ChatStreamProcessor.step`, with `tools` on the request and `--enable-auto-tool-choice` behaviour.

| case | tokens | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| llama3_json, JSON answer without `"name"` | 2011 | 0.882 s | 0.186 s |
| | 4011 | 3.457 s | 0.337 s |
| | 8011 | 12.116 s | 0.693 s |
| | 16011 | 36.031 s | 0.957 s |
| llama3_json, `"parameters"` before `"name"` | 2022 | 0.643 s | 0.123 s |
| | 4022 | 2.128 s | 0.211 s |
| | 8022 | 8.084 s | 0.468 s |
| | 16022 | 38.543 s | 1.001 s |
| ripple, `"arguments"` before `"name"` | 2026 | 0.730 s | 0.181 s |
| | 4026 | 2.804 s | 0.343 s |
| | 8026 | 9.389 s | 0.642 s |
| | 16026 | 37.506 s | 1.070 s |

The machine was shared and heavily loaded (load average about 60 on 32 cores) during both columns. A cProfile of the main run at 4011 tokens (llama3_json JSON answer) puts 1.92 s of 2.61 s in `str.join` from `ToolCallSlot.args` and 0.26 s in `_NAME_RE.search`, each called once per argument chunk (21635 calls).

Exactness of the incremental search: a standalone differential over 200000 random strings built from `"`, `name`, `:`, whitespace and backslash fragments, fed in random pieces, compares the new search with `_NAME_RE.search("".join(parts))` after every piece. 0 differences.

New tests, on main:

```
$ pytest -q tests/parser/engine/test_llama_json.py
E           AttributeError: 'ToolCallSlot' object has no attribute 'search_name'
5 failed, 40 passed in 3.43s
```

With this PR:

```
$ pytest -q tests/parser/engine/test_llama_json.py
45 passed in 5.20s
$ pytest -q tests/parser --ignore=tests/parser/cohere --ignore=tests/parser/mistral
7419 passed, 74 errors, 384 subtests passed in 523.29s
```

All 74 errors are fixture setup errors in `test_parse.py`, `test_streaming.py` and `test_include_reasoning.py`, which load tokenizers that are not cached on this offline machine (`LocalEntryNotFoundError`). There are no test failures. `tests/parser/cohere` needs the `cohere_melody` package and `tests/parser/mistral` fails at collection with the `mistral_common` version installed here (`ResponseFormats` has no `json_object`), so both were left out locally. The interpreter segfaults at exit after printing the summary. I saw the same exit crash in this environment from a script that only calls xgrammar, so I did not look into it further. `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` (v0.17.2) and `mypy --python-version 3.11` pass on the changed files. The CPU step that runs `pytest -v -s parser` is commented out on main in `.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml` ("Disabled until the cmake installation is locked"), so CI does not run `tests/parser` today. I could not run `vllm serve` on GPU on this machine (its driver is older than the CUDA build of the installed torch), so the server path was exercised through `ChatStreamProcessor` with real tokenizers.

## Details

`ToolCallSlot.search_name(pattern)` keeps the text where a partial match is still alive and the number of argument parts already scanned. On each call it searches the kept text plus the new parts. If there is no complete match, a `partial=True` search gives the leftmost position where a match could still complete, and only text from there is kept. A match that completes later must start at or after that position, so the leftmost complete match is the same one a full search finds. Once a match is found it is cached, because appending text never changes the leftmost match. This also covers the existing behaviour for an empty name and for a name that `_accept_tool_name` rejects (both kept returning the same first match on main).

`_try_extract_name` keeps its signature, so the Mistral override is untouched. The one-time call in `_handle_tool_end` uses the same cached search.

Limit. A partial match that stays open for a long time (for example `"name": "` followed by a very long unterminated name) is kept as one growing window, which scans the same as main.

Follow-up commit 8529212354 (review). The slot method was called `search_args(pattern)`, which reads as a generic search, but it keeps the first match as the slot's name for the slot's lifetime. It is now `search_name`, and its docstring says every call must pass the same name pattern. Only the method and test names changed. `tests/parser/engine` passes on the new head (6982 passed), and the renamed tests give the same 5 failed, 40 passed on main as before.

Related. #58824 / #58829 address the content that `llama3_json` streaming drops for a JSON answer that is not a tool call. This PR only changes the cost of the name search and leaves that behaviour as it is on main.

commits.pr_title: [Quantization] Give linear kernels a common LinearKernel base class
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Give every quantized linear kernel a common `LinearKernel` base class. This is the first, deliberately small step toward a linear kernel oracle that mirrors the MoE one (#65978, and the linear half of #54959); it changes no kernel selection.

## Claims

- All seven linear kernel families (scaled-mm, block-scaled, mixed-precision, NVFP4, MXFP4, MXFP6, MXFP8) now derive from one `LinearKernel` root in `kernels/linear/base.py`. It owns the constructor and the interface the families declared separately: `is_supported`, `can_implement`, `executed_activation_key`, `input_quant_key`, `process_weights_after_loading`, `apply_weights`. A few families gain methods they lacked: `input_quant_key` on MXFP4/MXFP6 (returns None), and `is_supported` and `executed_activation_key` on mixed-precision. None has a caller today.
- No concrete kernel file changes and no `init_*_linear_kernel` signature changes, so quantization methods are untouched.
- The MXFP8, MXFP4, MXFP6 and NVFP4 selectors share one selection loop (`_first_usable_kernel`) instead of four near-copies, with the same checks, order and failure-reason strings. MXFP4's extra quant-scheme gate is passed in as a callback.
- Net -347 lines in `vllm/` (157 added, 504 removed).

## Validation

Kernel selection is unchanged, so validation is the existing selection suites plus end-to-end loads.

On the commit before rebasing onto current `main` (B300, SM103, `chg run -g=1`):

```bash
python -m pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_scaled_mm_kernel_selection.py \
  tests/kernels/quantization/test_mxfp4_kernel_selection.py \
  tests/kernels/quantization/test_mxfp6_kernel_selection.py \
  tests/kernels/quantization/test_mxfp8_kernel_selection.py \
  tests/kernels/quantization/test_nvfp4_kernel_selection.py \
  tests/kernels/quantization/test_w4a16_kernel_selection.py \
  tests/kernels/quantization/test_rdna3_w4a16_selection.py \
  tests/model_executor/kernels tests/fusion/test_quant_activation_contract.py \
  tests/quantization/test_humming_mxfp4_block_fp8.py
# 166 passed, 16 skipped

python -m pytest tests/quantization/test_modelopt.py tests/quantization/test_quark.py \
  tests/quantization/test_online_mxfp4.py tests/quantization/test_compressed_tensors.py \
  tests/quantization/test_online.py
# 499 passed, 28 skipped, 12 failed
```

The 12 failures are the same test names that fail on a clean `main` checkout on this machine (8 in `test_compressed_tensors.py`, 3 in `test_quark.py`, `test_modelopt_fp8_pb_wo_checkpoint_setup`); that baseline was taken on 2026-11-11, not on the same base commit.

End to end on that commit, `LLM(...)` load plus one greedy completion, same linear kernel selected as on `main` in each case:

| Checkpoint | Linear kernel |
|---|---|
| `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8` | `DeepGemmFp8BlockScaledMMKernel` |
| `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8`, `linear_backend="marlin"` | `MarlinFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel` |
| `nvidia/Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4` | `FlashInferCuteDslNvFp4LinearKernel` |
| `mgoin/Qwen3-0.6B-MXFP8` | `FlashInferCutedslMxfp8LinearKernel` |

After rebasing onto current `main` (three conflicts, all additive: `LinearKernelOracle` import, `MxFp4LinearKernel.fuse_input_hadamard`, `Mxfp8LinearKernel.supports_batch_invariance`): pre-commit including mypy passes, and the six selection suites pass CPU-only (110 passed, 3 skipped; 4 ROCm MXFP8 tests need a visible GPU and failed with "No CUDA GPUs are available"). On the rebased first commit, three of the four end-to-end loads were repeated on GPU with the same kernels and completions (FP8 auto, FP8 forced Marlin, NVFP4); the MXFP8 load failed before model construction with a `CacheConfig` validation error unrelated to kernel code, not yet compared against `main`. The end-to-end loads have not been repeated on the second commit.

The follow-up commit (docstring trim, shared constructor) was checked the same way: pre-commit including mypy passes, and eight selection and fusion-contract suites pass CPU-only (135 passed, 3 skipped, the same 4 GPU-requiring ROCm MXFP8 tests failing). GPU comparison on B300 (`chg run -g=1`), the ten suites listed above, base commit 78aa0f15f7 versus branch tip 867a3e3b49: identical results, 170 passed, 16 skipped, 2 failed on both. The two failures (`test_checkpoint_mxfp8_runs_as_block_fp8_on_hopper[90-None-128]` and `test_humming_nvfp4_linear_declares_executed_activation[capability4-False-True]` in `tests/quantization/test_humming_mxfp4_block_fp8.py`) are a test-order interaction already on `main`: the file passes on its own (22 passed) on the branch.

Not exercised: ROCm, XPU and CPU kernels beyond what the selection suites mock.

## Details

**Why.** The linear families had no shared type: `MMLinearKernel`, `ScaledMMLinearKernel`, `MPLinearKernel` and the NVFP4/MXFP4/MXFP6/MXFP8 bases were unrelated ABCs that each redeclared the same methods. #59460 had to add the same `executed_activation_key` default to six of them, selection code typed kernels as `type[Any]`, and each selector carried its own loop. A common root is the prerequisite for selecting linear kernels by quant key the way the MoE oracles do.

**What changed.**

- `LinearKernel(ABC, Generic[ConfigT])` holds the shared constructor and interface, with short docstrings in the style of `FusedMoEExperts`. Each family base now derives from it and keeps only what is specific to the family: its config and helpers such as `NvFp4LinearKernel.prepare_input` or `MxFp4LinearKernel._supports_quant_scheme`. `MMLinearKernel`, `ScaledMMLinearKernel` and `MPLinearKernel` keep their own constructors because their signatures differ.
- `MPLinearKernel` gains `is_supported`, derived from its existing `get_min_capability` (checking the current device when no capability is passed). `choose_mp_linear_kernel` uses it; the failure message is unchanged.
- `_first_usable_kernel` replaces the four identical loops. MXFP4 passes its `_supports_quant_scheme` gate as a callback so the check order is preserved.
- No new test: the registries are typed per family base, so mypy already requires every registered kernel to be a `LinearKernel`.

**Not in this PR (follow-ups).**

- Constructors still differ for scaled-mm (`layer_param_names`) and mixed-precision (weight/scale/zero-point names).
- `ScaledMMLinearKernel`, `Int8ScaledMMLinearKernel` and `MMLinearKernel` are near-empty shells and int8 shares nothing with FP8 through them; removing them and separating int8 is the next refactor. The two FP8 template bases stay, since most of their kernels use the template unchanged.
- `choose_scaled_mm_linear_kernel` and `choose_mp_linear_kernel` keep their own loops (forced kernels, explicit compute capability, different message formats).
- Family configs do not yet all carry `weight_quant_key` / `activation_quant_key` (NVFP4's is empty and uses `use_a16`; INT8 uses booleans). That is the next step, followed by one key-based `select_linear_kernel` behind the `init_*` wrappers.
- `_first_usable_kernel` is a module function; it can move onto the `LinearKernelOracle` placeholder from #66803 when that class grows.

**Related.** #65394 (MXFP8 activation gate) and #66077 (MXFP6 activation gate) touch the selection loops this PR replaces and will need a small rebase whichever lands second. No other open PR adds a shared linear kernel base.

No user-visible change, so no docs update.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][NIXL] Decline remote prefill reads after the producer's KV lease expired
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

In P/D disaggregation with `NixlConnector`, the decode (consumer) could issue the NIXL read of a request whose KV blocks the prefill (producer) had already released and recycled because its lease ran out. The read succeeds and silently loads other requests' KV cache and SSM state. This reuses the deadline gate that already protects the bidirectional turn-2 readback and applies it to every remote-prefill read, with an exact model of the lease renewals the consumer's own heartbeats cause.

Fixes #66009.

## Claims

- A consumer never reads KV blocks past the producer's lease deadline (minus a safety margin of `min(5 s, kv_lease_duration / 6)`). The read is declined, counted in the new consumer-side counter `vllm:nixl_num_declined_expired_reads`, reported as `failed_recving`, and the request follows `kv_load_failure_policy`: with the default `fail` it finishes with an error, with `recompute` it is prefilled locally. Before this change such a read loaded recycled memory with no error at all.
- Requests that waited inside the consumer's scheduler keep working: the consumer keeps an exact model of the producer's lease as renewed by the heartbeats it sent (the scheduler ships the exported deadline and `remote_lease_extension` with each heartbeat batch, and the worker applies the producer's own renewal rule to it), so reads after long but heartbeated waits are not declined. A request is heartbeated at the first scheduler step after D starts tracking it rather than at the next periodic round, since a router may already have held it for most of its lease. The model can only lag the real lease (the send time plus the margin stands in for the arrival time; a round that missed any remote rank is not counted; without the producer's exported fields heartbeats are not modelled at all; request ids containing `,` are never credited because the comma-separated heartbeat payload cannot carry them).
- Peers that do not export `remote_blocks_expiry_time` / `remote_lease_extension`, or whose clock offset is unknown, are read exactly as before. `NIXL_CONNECTOR_VERSION` is bumped to 17 because the semantics of `kv_transfer_params` change (see Version compatibility).

## Validation

Root cause and fix were established on a 2xB200 1P1D lab (vLLM 0.32.0, NIXL 1.5.0, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next NVFP4 with MTP k=3, prefix caching) driven by NVIDIA Dynamo 1.7.0.dev20261025, whose frontend holds prefilled requests outside the decode engine while it is at capacity:

- Instrumented runs (block ids logged on both sides, NaN detector per request): **100% of the requests that produced NaN logits (48/48, 25/25, 14/14, 42/42, 46/46 across five runs) had their producer lease expire before the consumer read them**; prefill->read delay p50 32-51s (lease 30s) vs 12-14s for healthy requests. The producer logged `Releasing expired KV blocks ... retrieved by 0 remote worker(s)` for every one of them.
- `kv_lease_duration=600` on both sides: 0 expiries, 0 NaN in the same 11-minute test (control).
- This commit's gate and lease model backported to 0.32.0 with the default `kv_load_failure_policy=fail`, 10 minutes at 9 req/s with 2k-token prompts and outputs: 1,817 producer leases expired, 121 requests reached the consumer's read path, 59 were declined and finished with an error, the other 62 were read (prefill->read delays p50 25 s / max 59 s, i.e. beyond the 30 s initial lease and kept alive by heartbeats), 0 NaN, no crash. **All 59 declines were requests without any heartbeat model** (held by the router before reaching the decoder); the exported deadline at decision time ranged from 29.5 s past to 4.9 s ahead (inside the margin). Without the gate the engine died in 2-3 minutes (`cooperative_topk` illegal memory access on fully-NaN rows, see #63118).
- Same, with `kv_load_failure_policy=recompute`: 1,812 producer leases expired, 119 requests reached the read path, 59 declined and handed to the recompute path, again all without a heartbeat model, 0 NaN, no crash.
- With an orchestrator that hands requests to the decode engine immediately (Dynamo dev20261103), the same load showed prefill->read delays of p50 90s / max 339s with 0 NaN before the change, and with the gate: 264 reads, delays p50 61s / p90 231s / max 343s, **0 declined**, 0 NaN. Heartbeats kept the leases alive and the model accepted every one of them; the 5 producer-side expiries in that run were requests the frontend never forwarded to the decoder.
- The lab backport ran in pull mode with a single PCP rank and predates the heartbeats-first ordering in `start_load_kv` and the later hardening on this branch (newly tracked requests heartbeated at the next step, margin capped at `kv_lease_duration / 6`, deadline-based pruning). Those parts (replicated-PCP ranks keeping a model, same-step rounds, short leases, first heartbeat of a new request) are covered by the unit tests below.
- Unit tests (29 new, 415 passing in the NIXL connector unit suite): `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_remote_read_expiry.py` (gate parametrised over expired / inside margin / live / absent deadline; full local hit; unknown and non-zero clock offset; the lease model both injected and driven end-to-end through `_send_heartbeats` on a fake clock, including a pause inside the initial lease that must not count as a lapse, a lapse that later heartbeats cannot revive and the exact deadline after each heartbeat; no model without the exported fields or a clock offset; request ids with commas; per-engine keying; failed and partially failed sends; pruning of lapsed models; a short lease kept alive by heartbeats; producer export for two lease durations; the decode scheduler shipping the lease with heartbeats; replicated-PCP ranks keeping a model; a round shipped in the read's own step credited first) and `test_nixl_heartbeat.py` (a newly tracked request heartbeated without waiting for the round). `test_bidirectional_kv_transfer.py`, `test_nixl_heartbeat.py`, `test_nixl_connector.py`, `test_multi_connector.py` and `test_nixl_push_connector.py` pass with the counter changes.

## Details

**Root cause.** `kv_transfer_params` carried `remote_block_ids` but, for prefill blocks, no validity deadline (`remote_blocks_expiry_time` was exported for D blocks only). The design doc assumes heartbeats start as soon as the request enters D's scheduler; a request parked earlier (router/proxy queue) renews nothing, the producer reaps the lease (`_reap_expired_send_leases`) and reuses the blocks, and the consumer's later NIXL read is a plain memory pull of whatever is there now.

Failing flow (before):
1. P scheduler finishes the prefill: `request_finished` returns `kv_transfer_params` with `remote_block_ids` and arms a 30 s lease (`_reqs_need_send`), exported to the P worker as `reqs_to_send`.
2. The router receives the response but holds the request (D is at capacity). No heartbeat: D's scheduler does not know the request yet.
3. At 30 s the P worker's `_reap_expired_send_leases` reports the request as sent; the P scheduler frees the blocks, which new prefills reuse.
4. The router hands the request to D. D's scheduler allocates local blocks and builds `reqs_to_recv` with the stale `remote_block_ids`.
5. D's worker posts the NIXL read; it completes successfully with the new occupants' KV and SSM state. The request decodes on corrupted state: NaN logits, then `cooperative_topk` illegal memory access.

With this PR, step 1 also exports the lease deadline (and the renewal amount), and step 5 becomes: the worker compares the rebased deadline (renewed by its own heartbeats, if any) with now; the read above is declined and the request follows `kv_load_failure_policy`. A request that instead waited inside D's scheduler is heartbeated from admission on, the model renews its deadline like P does, and its read proceeds.

**Fix.**
1. `pull_scheduler.request_finished` exports the lease deadline for P blocks as well, plus `remote_lease_extension` (how many seconds a heartbeat renews the lease by, from the new shared helper `nixl.utils.kv_lease_extension`, also used by `_handle_heartbeat`'s initialisation). D blocks (fixed TTL) export no extension.
2. `pull_worker._is_remote_read_expired` replaces `_is_turn2_read_expired` and runs for every read, not only bidirectional: the exported deadline is rebased with the handshake clock offset. D's scheduler ships the exported deadline and renewal amount with each heartbeat batch (`HeartbeatInfo.leases`); `base_worker._send_heartbeats` applies every heartbeat it sends to a modelled deadline per (remote engine, remote request), exactly as the producer's `_handle_heartbeat` would (a heartbeat that goes out while the modelled lease is alive renews it to `send time + extension`; one that goes out after it ran out renews nothing, nor does anything after it), only for rounds that reached every remote rank. The read uses the modelled deadline. Without the exported fields no model is built and the initial deadline stands. The scheduler sends a newly tracked request at the next step instead of waiting for the periodic round (up to `kv_lease_duration / 6`), and the safety margin is `min(5 s, kv_lease_duration / 6)` so that heartbeats can keep a short lease alive. Heartbeats are now sent at the top of `start_load_kv`, so replicated-PCP ranks > 0 (which return early) keep a model for the reads they gate, and a round shipped in the same step as a read is credited before the gate.
3. A declined read is counted in `num_declined_expired_reads` (new counter, Prometheus `vllm:nixl_num_declined_expired_reads`, tracked on the reading instance, documented in the usage guide) instead of the producer-side `num_kv_expired_reqs`; the existing bidirectional turn-2 decline moves to the new counter too, which matches that metric's documentation ("tracked on the P instance"). One `warning_once` per remote engine explains the condition; each occurrence is logged at debug level and shows up in the periodic KV transfer metrics line.
4. Modelled deadlines are pruned once they have passed (the read is declined either way), so the bookkeeping stays bounded without hooks on read or transfer completion. The handshake callback now logs the measured clock offset per engine so the clock assumption below can be checked in production.

**Behaviour change.** Under the default `kv_load_failure_policy="fail"`, a read that would previously have loaded recycled blocks now fails that request with an error finish reason. Deployments whose router may hold requests longer than `kv_lease_duration` should raise the lease, fix the router, or set `"kv_load_failure_policy": "recompute"` (local prefill, correct output, higher TTFT for those requests). The design doc (`docs/design/nixl_kv_cache_lease.md`) documents this and what the check does not cover.

**Version compatibility.** `NIXL_CONNECTOR_VERSION` 16 -> 17. One mixed pair would regress without it: a new producer with an old consumer running `bidirectional_kv_xfer=True`, because the old consumer gated every read on `remote_blocks_expiry_time` without heartbeat modelling and the old producer never exported it for P blocks; it would now decline heartbeated waits longer than the lease. The other pairs degrade to today's behaviour (old producer exports no P-block deadline -> no gate; new producer + old non-bidirectional consumer -> fields ignored). `enforce_handshake_compat=false` remains the escape hatch for rolling upgrades.

**Trade-offs.** Clock-offset error and heartbeat propagation are absorbed by the safety margin (the producer processes heartbeats before reaping and renews from its processing time, so its own lag only lengthens the real lease); the offset is estimated once per handshake and assumes rate-disciplined monotonic clocks on both hosts (documented). The heartbeat model can only lag the producer's state: a round that did not reach every remote rank is not counted, and a heartbeat that goes out within the margin of the modelled deadline is not credited even though the producer may still have renewed. What it cannot see is a heartbeat notification that takes longer than the margin to reach the producer; that is the assumption the heartbeat protocol itself rests on, and a confirmation round-trip before the read would be the follow-up that removes it. The design doc lists what the check does not cover (no exported deadline or offset, clock drift beyond the margin, in-flight expiry, blocks released early by replayed `kv_transfer_params`, a producer restarted behind the same engine id).

commits.pr_title: [Frontend][DeepSeek-V4.1] Render tool search like deepseek-recipe
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

DeepSeek V4.1 tool search now renders like [deepseek-recipe](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-recipe), DeepSeek's production prompt library, and like vLLM's Rust renderer:
- Deferred tools stay out of the system prompt.
- A user turn whose tool results contain `tool_reference` is followed by a `### Updated Tool Schemas` system turn listing the referenced tools.

Before, the Python renderer listed every tool, deferred ones included, and rendered references as names only.

Not a duplicate: no open PR changes this. #62196 touches the same files for thinking and tool-result turns.

## Claims

- The V4.1 prompt is byte-identical to deepseek-recipe 0.2.0 (`935817c`) and to the Rust renderer's `tool_search_references.txt` fixture.
- The prompt prefix is stable across a search. On replayed Claude Code requests, the request after a search keeps 11,273/11,273 cached tokens; `main` keeps 8,668/11,324.
- If all tools are deferred, or a reference names an unknown tool, the request returns HTTP 400, matching deepseek-recipe and the Rust renderer.

## Validation

Each Anthropic `/v1/messages` request was rendered by deepseek-recipe (`MessagesRequest.convert` + `DeepseekV41Encoding`) and by vLLM (Anthropic converter + V4.1 tokenizer). These cases now give identical prompts; all differ on `main`:
- thinking on and off
- search result as the last turn
- the loaded tool called afterwards
- two searches
- deferred tools with no search
- no deferred tools

Both error cases are rejected by both.

```bash
pytest tests/tokenizers_/test_deepseek_v41.py tests/tokenizers_/test_deepseek_v4.py tests/tokenizers_/test_registry.py \
  tests/test_request_input_bounds.py tests/entrypoints/scale_out/render/test_render.py tests/renderers/test_tokenizer_pool.py \
  tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v41.py tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py
# 513 passed, 3 skipped
```

New tests, which fail on `main`:
- `test_tool_references_list_deferred_tools_like_deepseek_recipe`, which uses the Rust fixture copied unchanged
- `test_tool_search_request_errors`

`test_messages_render_tool_search_result_for_deepseek_v41` now expects the updated-schemas turn.

No model evals were run: prompts with deferred tools now match DeepSeek's encoder, and other prompts only drop the `defer_loading` and `null` fields from tool schemas.

## Details

- Out of scope:
  - DeepSeek Harness `tool_addition` blocks (the Rust renderer doesn't handle them either).
  - deepseek-recipe printing `"description": ""` for tools without a description, which both vLLM frontends omit.

commits.pr_title: [Core] Log the backends each kind of layer selected after model load
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

After a model loads, log one compact table of the backends its layers selected: the attention backend and the linear and MoE kernels, with the layers that run each. On by default, logged once per model. Part of the "Unified dispatch and inspectability" item in the Q4 roadmap (#61024).

## Claims

- A short preamble naming the resolved model class and the model, a header row, then one row per (layer kind, backend): layer count, the selected kernel or attention backend, and the layer names with index ranges and sibling names collapsed.
- Covers decoder, linear-attention and vision-encoder attention layers, quantized and unquantized linear layers, and MoE layers. MoE rows also show the weight and activation precision the kernel runs.
- Logged once per model at INFO, from the first rank only, after weights are processed (MoE kernels do not exist before that). A failure while building the table is logged as a warning and never fails the load.
- The individual selection logs the table covers move from INFO to DEBUG (55 calls in 25 files): the attention backend lines, the MoE oracle `Using X MoE backend` lines, and the linear `Selected <kernel> for ...` / `Using <kernel> for ... GEMM` lines. Logs that explain a fallback or an override stay as they are, as do selections the table does not show (MoE prepare/finalize, FlashInfer's prefill/decode sub-backends, KV cache dtype and block size).
- The model runner logs it for each model it loads, the target and then the draft model, so it appears for every load format and for out-of-tree loaders. Loaders do not log it, except that `BaseModelLoader.load_model` logs it when loading fails (next point), since the runner never receives that model.
- If loading the weights fails, the table is logged before the error with the selections made so far, and the original exception propagates unchanged.
- The existing `VLLM_LOG_MODEL_INSPECTION` tree view is unchanged.

## Validation

```bash
python -m pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_model_inspection.py tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_kernel_oracle.py   # 80 passed (CPU)
```

Output on B300 (SM103), `LLM(...)` startup with the INFO preamble removed:

`Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8` with `moe_backend="marlin", linear_backend="marlin"`:

```text
Backends selected for Qwen3MoeForCausalLM (Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8):
  layer     | count | backend                                 | modules
  attention |    48 | FLASHINFER                              | model.layers.[0-47].self_attn.attn
  linear    |    50 | unquantized [w=bfloat16]                | model.embed_tokens, model.layers.[0-47].mlp.gate, lm_head
  linear    |    96 | MarlinFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel           | model.layers.[0-47].self_attn.{qkv_proj,o_proj}
  moe       |    48 | MarlinExperts [w=float8_e4m3fn, a=none] | model.layers.[0-47].mlp.experts.routed_experts
```

`Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B` with `quantization="fp8"` (multimodal, hybrid attention, shared experts):

```text
Backends selected for Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration (Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B):
  layer     | count | backend                                          | modules
  attention |    27 | FLASH_ATTN                                       | visual.blocks.[0-26].attn.attn
  attention |    30 | GDN_ATTN                                         | language_model.model.layers.[0-38 (30)].linear_attn
  attention |    10 | FLASHINFER                                       | language_model.model.layers.[3-39 (10)].self_attn.attn
  linear    |   300 | CutlassFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel                   | visual.merger.{linear_fc1,linear_fc2}, visual.blocks.[0-26].attn.{qkv,proj}, visual.blocks.[0-26].mlp.{linear_fc1,linear_fc2}, language_model.model.layers.[0-38 (30)].linear_attn.{in_proj_qkvz,in_proj_ba,out_proj}, language_model.model.layers.[0-39].mlp.shared_expert.{gate_up_proj,down_proj}, language_model.model.layers.[3-39 (10)].self_attn.{qkv_proj,o_proj}
  linear    |   112 | unquantized [w=bfloat16]                         | language_model.model.embed_tokens, language_model.model.layers.[0-38 (30)].linear_attn.conv1d, language_model.model.layers.[0-39].mlp.{gate,shared_expert_gate}, language_model.lm_head
  moe       |    40 | TritonExperts [w=float8_e4m3fn, a=float8_e4m3fn] | language_model.model.layers.[0-39].mlp.experts.routed_experts
```

`deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017` (custom model definition):

```text
Backends selected for DeepseekV41ForCausalLM (deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017):

  attention |    32 | FLASH_ATTN                                        | vision.blocks.[0-31].attn.attn
  attention |    40 | FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41 [kv_cache=nvfp4_ds_mla]  | language_model.model.layers.[0-39].attn
  attention |    40 | DEEPSEEK_SPARSE_SWA                               | language_model.model.layers.[0-39].attn.swa_cache_layer
  attention |     4 | DEEPSEEK_V41_SPARSE_INDEXER                       | language_model.model.layers.[2-20 (4)].attn.indexer.k_cache
  attention |     3 | CompressorBackend                                 | language_model.model.layers.[2, 8, 14].attn.compressor.state_cache
  linear    |   189 | unquantized [w=bfloat16]                          | vision.patch_embed.proj, vision.blocks.[0-31].attn.{wqkv,wo}, vision.blocks.[0-31].mlp.{w1,w2}, aligner.{w1,w2}, language_model.model.embed_tokens, language_model.model.layers.[0-39].ffn.gate, language_model.model.layers.[2-36 (8)].attn.indexer.weights_proj, language_model.model.layers.[2-20 (4)].attn.indexer.wk, language_model.model.layers.[2-20 (4)].attn.compressor.fused_wkv_wgate, language_model.lm_head
  linear    |   210 | FlashInferCutedslMxfp8LinearKernel                | language_model.model.layers.[0-39].attn.{fused_wqa_wkv,wq_b,wo_b}, language_model.model.layers.[0-39].ffn.shared_experts.{gate_up_proj,down_proj}, language_model.model.layers.[1, 14].engram.wkv, language_model.model.layers.[2-36 (8)].attn.indexer.wq_b
  linear    |    40 | DeepGemmMxfp8BmmLinearKernel                      | language_model.model.layers.[0-39].attn.wo_a
  moe       |    40 | TrtLlmMxfp4Mxfp8ExpertsModular [w=mxfp4, a=mxfp8] | language_model.model.layers.[0-39].ffn.experts.routed_experts
```

Also run: `nvidia/Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4` (ModelOpt, FP8 KV cache), `openai/gpt-oss-20b` (MXFP4 MoE), `RedHatAI/Qwen3-0.6B-FP8-BLOCK` (compressed-tensors), and unquantized `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` at TP=1 and TP=2 (logged once, from rank 0).

The model runs above predate the log demotion, the model name in the preamble, the `w=` detail on unquantized rows, the failure path and the move to the model runner. The tables are edited by hand to the current format (model name, `w=`); the later changes were only run on CPU (unit tests, and a toy model driven through the real `load_model` with a failing weight load), because the GPU box was fully reserved. Speculative-decoding draft models load through the same loader and get their own table, which is why the preamble names the model; that was checked by reading the code, not by a run.

Not run: a checkpoint with quantized routed experts and unquantized shared experts (none cached locally); ROCm, XPU and CPU. No end-to-end test asserts on the log; the unit tests cover name collapsing, grouping, and that a layer the summary cannot describe does not fail the load.

## Details

- `collect_layer_backends` in `vllm/model_inspection.py`, next to the tree view, returns structured `LayerBackend` entries (kind, backend, details, module names); `format_layer_backends` renders the table. Collection and formatting are separate so the entries can be returned over an RPC or asserted on in tests, and so further attributes of the execution plan can be added without changing how it is emitted. Runtime attributes that are only known after loading (CUDA graph and compile modes, KV cache layout) would be added by the same owner, the model runner.
- Quant methods keep their kernel under different attribute names (`kernel`, `fp8_linear`, `ocp_mx_linear`, `moe_kernel`, ...), so the kernel is found by type: a `FusedMoEKernel`, or an instance of a class under `vllm.model_executor.kernels.linear`. A shared linear kernel base class would replace this.
- Shared experts that are not fused into the routed experts are linear layers and show up in the `linear` rows. Fused shared experts are part of the MoE kernel and are not reported separately.

What the demotion gives up at INFO, by design:

- The candidates that were not chosen, the MoE backend enum name (the table shows the experts class), and whether a backend was forced or auto-selected. All three are still in the DEBUG lines.
- A record of the selections when the process is killed during weight loading (OOM killer, segfault, CUDA abort). Python-level load errors are covered by the failure path.

Limitations, left for follow-ups:

- Linear rows have no weight/activation precision tag; linear kernels do not expose it uniformly yet.
- Kernel class names are long and could be shortened. The quantization method class is not shown, only the kernel.
- Embeddings and `lm_head` are listed as `linear`, since they carry a quant method.
- Cache-style layers that register through the attention layer base class (e.g. the DeepSeek V4.1 sliding-window, indexer and compressor caches above) are listed as `attention`.
- Every module pattern is printed, so rows for models with many distinct layer names are long and wrap.
- There is no dedicated switch to turn the table off, other than the log level.
- The table comes from the first rank, which under pipeline parallelism holds only its own layers.
- Encoder and decoder attention are both listed as `attention` and are told apart by module path.

**Why not duplicate:** #62005 adds the selected kernel to each layer of the opt-in `VLLM_LOG_MODEL_INSPECTION` tree. This PR is a separate default-on summary and leaves the tree alone; both touch `model_inspection.py` and the loader hook, so the second to merge needs a small rebase.

Docs: new "Check which backends a model runs on" section in `docs/usage/troubleshooting.md`.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Report the final SWA tail in first_live_chunk_idx
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`OnComputeStoreHandler.first_live_chunk_idx` reported a chunk above the final SWA tail that the handler stores at finish. So the stale-block scan of the scheduler did not clean that tail. The store could then copy KV that another request owns. This PR lowers the reported chunk to the start of the final tail segment.

Follows #64286 (store trigger handlers) and #65197.

## Claims

- A finish-time store of the final SWA tail no longer copies a GPU block that the core gave to another request. This applies to aborts, to normal finishes after decode, to DCP, and to blocks that leave the window one step before the finish.
- `OnHandoffStoreHandler.first_live_chunk_idx` stays `None`. A new comment and a new test explain why this is correct.
- No store job changes when no block is reused. All existing scheduler tests pass without changes.

## Validation

The new test fails on `upstream/main` (b5b9f7982c) and passes on this PR. To run it on main, I used the three handler files of `upstream/main` with the test file of this PR:

```
$ pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py -p no:randomly -k final_swa_tail_store_skips --tb=line
tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py:1012: assert not ({1001, 1002, ...} & {1247, 1248})
tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py:1012: assert not ({1001, 1002, ...} & {1124})
tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py:1012: assert not ({1001, 1002, ...} & {1310, 1311, 1312, 1313, 1314, 1315})
tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py:1012: assert not ({1001, 1002, ...} & {1310, 1311, 1312, 1313, 1314, 1315})
FAILED ...::test_final_swa_tail_store_skips_reused_blocks[aborted-prefill]
FAILED ...::test_final_swa_tail_store_skips_reused_blocks[aborted-prefill-dcp2]
FAILED ...::test_final_swa_tail_store_skips_reused_blocks[stopped-decode-bpc3]
FAILED ...::test_final_swa_tail_store_skips_reused_blocks[stopped-decode-bpc3-reuse-while-running]
4 failed, 541 deselected

# this PR
4 passed, 541 deselected
```

The right-hand set is the SWA blocks that the finished request stores. The left-hand set is the blocks that another request got in the same step.

The full scheduler suite on this PR, on macOS:

```
$ pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py -p no:randomly -k 'not cache_reset and not lookahead_partial'
531 passed, 14 deselected
```

The 14 deselected cases need Linux and fail on macOS without this change. `pre-commit` passes on the changed files.

### End-to-end run on an H100 (pokprod001 cluster)

Setup: `google/gemma-2-2b-it` (sliding window 4096 plus full attention, so two KV groups), `OffloadingConnector` with `CPUOffloadingSpec` (20 GB), `--num-gpu-blocks-override 1024`, one GPU. Three Python trees on the same nightly image `0.34.0rc1.dev776` (compiled `.so` from the image): this PR (`05feacbec6`), `upstream/main` (`b5b9f7982c`), and this PR without the connector.

Workload: 12 greedy prompts of about 5k tokens, longer than the SWA window; 24 filler prompts to evict the GPU tier; the same 12 prompts again; then 30 requests cancelled mid-flight. A monitor inside the scheduler checked every store job: a job fails if one of its GPU source blocks belongs to another request in the same step.

| | this PR | `upstream/main` | this PR, no connector |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| store bytes | 19.34 GB | 19.34 GB | 0 |
| load bytes | 7.42 GB | 7.42 GB | 0 |
| external cache hits | 90,240 | 90,240 | 0 |
| store jobs | 45 | 44 | 0 |
| scheduler steps | 250 | 250 | n/a |
| store jobs with a foreign block | 0 | 0 | n/a |
| server tracebacks | 0 | 0 | 0 |

Greedy text is identical between this PR and `upstream/main` (12 of 12 prompts), and identical to this PR without the connector (12 of 12). The repeated round differs in 1 of 12 prompts on this PR and 2 of 12 on `upstream/main`; the run without the connector also differs in 2 of 12, so this is batching nondeterminism, not a store defect. The one store-job difference comes from the same nondeterminism; the stored and loaded byte counts match exactly.

The changed line did not fire in this run: `first_live_chunk_idx` returned the stored progress on all 209 calls. Two server-side gates keep it out of the branch, neither related to the patch:
- `reconsider_final_swa_tail` requires `prefix_cache_retention_interval is None`, and the default is `0`.
- `alignment_blocks` is 1 for this model, because its sliding-window group and its full-attention group both use 64-token blocks, so the tail start equals the progress.

So that run shows that the patch does not change serving when the branch is not taken. A second run opens both gates.

### Reaching the changed branch live (2 GPUs)

Both gates are constructible:
- `prefix_cache_retention_interval=None` (an offline `LLM` argument; there is no CLI spelling).
- A sliding-window group with a smaller block size than the full-attention chunk: `tensor_parallel_size=2` with `decode_context_parallel_size=2` doubles the full-attention block (`resolve_dcp_kv_block_size`), and a harness patch marks the SWA group `dcp_sharded=False`, which is what `vllm/models/glm5next/common/attention.py` does for a real model. `alignment_blocks` then becomes 2.

`google/gemma-2-2b-it` cannot run at DCP=2 (4 KV heads, and GQA DCP needs more TP ranks than KV heads), so this run uses `google/gemma-3-1b-it` (1 KV head, sliding window 512). Same workload shape, offline, one monitor:

| | this PR | `upstream/main` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `first_live_chunk_idx` below the stored progress | 132 of 876 calls | not reported (no such code) |
| store jobs | 17 | 17 |
| store jobs that read a foreign block | 0 | 0 |
| server tracebacks | 0 | 0 |
| repeated round differs | 2 of 12 | 2 of 12 |

So the changed line runs in a live engine, lowers the stale-scan start on 15% of the calls, and no store job read a block owned by another request. The harness patch is test-only and stays outside the repository.

A model evaluation was not run: the fix changes stored KV only when the old code read a block that another request owns.

## Details

**Root cause.** In `_update_req_states`, the scheduler sets stale SWA block ids to 0 from the lowest `first_live_chunk_idx` of all handlers. `OnComputeStoreHandler` returned its stored progress. When a request ends inside an aligned SWA segment, `select_store_candidates` (`reconsider_final_swa_tail`) stores the last window of that short segment. It starts from the segment start, which can be below the progress. An example with 1 block per chunk, 9-chunk segments and a 4-chunk window:
1. A prefill computes 250 of 300 prompt chunks. Segment 243–251 is aligned to the prompt end, so only chunks 248 and 249 are stored. The progress is 250.
2. The request is aborted. Its last segment is now 243–249, so chunks 246 and 247 need a store.
3. In the same step, another request gets the blocks of chunks 246 and 247. The scan starts at chunk 250 and does not clean them.
4. The tail store copies the KV of the other request under the keys of the aborted prompt.

With more than one block per chunk, a block of a tail chunk can leave the window before the finish. Then it can go stale while the request still runs (the `reuse-while-running` case). Thus the bound must be correct in every step, not only at finish.

**Fix.** `final_swa_tail_start_chunk` (`candidates.py`) gives the start of the final tail segment, and `first_live_chunk_idx` returns `min(progress, start)`. It uses the finish-time commit point `min(num_computed_tokens, max(num_prompt_tokens, num_tokens - 1))`. That value is exact at a normal finish. It is a lower bound for a running request, because the value only goes up, and for an abort, which stores up to `num_computed_tokens`. The bound and `select_store_candidates` share `_committed_num_tokens` and `_segment_start_chunk`.

**Cost.** The scan of each SWA group now starts up to one alignment segment lower.

**Hand-off handler.** Its partial tail reads request block ids only for groups that are not CoW sources. `supports_partial_tail` is false when a sliding-window group is not a CoW source. So those groups are full attention. The scheduler never cleans them, and `None` is correct. `test_handoff_partial_tail_excludes_sliding_window_groups` guards that rule.

**Tests.** `test_final_swa_tail_store_skips_reused_blocks` uses a real scheduler and real requests. The cases vary:
- the blocks per chunk (1 and 3)
- the horizon path (abort in prefill, stop after decode)
- DCP
- the step of the reuse (finish, or the last decode step)

A clean run first makes sure that the tail reads blocks that the core can give away. `test_dcp_abort_reconsiders_final_swa_tail` now uses the same scheduler helper.

commits.pr_title: [CI] Make the Nemotron GSM8K offload entries exercise the CPU reload
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`(H200 MIG 35GB) LM Eval KV-Offload` fails intermittently on main (builds 102994, 103085):

```
evals/gsm8k/test_gsm8k_offloading.py::test_gsm8k_offloading_correctness
AssertionError: GSM8K run 2/2 accuracy 0.390 below 0.4
```

This is score noise, not KV corruption. Over all 28 runs of this step in the last two days, `simple-nemotron-h-8b` (SimpleCPUOffloadConnector) scored a mean of 0.422 (run 1) and 0.425 (run 2), with a standard deviation of about 0.013 and a range of 0.39–0.455. The OffloadingConnector entry for the same model scores the same (0.427 / 0.423).

The OffloadingConnector entry already uses `accuracy_threshold=0.39` (floor 0.34). The SimpleCPUOffloadConnector entry kept 0.45 (floor 0.40), which sits less than 2 standard deviations below the H200 mean. The file's 0.49 baseline was measured on GB200. Both failures were run 2 at exactly 0.390, while run 1 and every other config in the same job scored normally. Corrupted KV would score far lower.

The fix sets the simple-nemotron threshold to 0.39, the same as the other entry for this model, with a comment. This loosens the assertion, which is justified because the old floor didn't match this model's score distribution on H200.

## Not a duplicate

#56632 is stale and only relaxes run 1, so it wouldn't have caught these run-2 failures.

## Test Plan

- Scores taken from the logs of all 28 jobs of this step between 11-14 and 11-16.
- CI: `kv-offload-small`.

## Test Result

- With the new 0.34 floor, all 56 observed runs (28 jobs × 2) pass; the lowest observed score is 0.39.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used; I reviewed the change.
