commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Recipe] Qwen3.8-Flash-Next: verify BF16 on MI325X with AITER
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Add MI325X to the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next recipe:

- `meta.hardware.mi325x: verified`
- `meta.default_variant.mi325x: bf16`
- `variants.bf16.hardware_overrides.mi325x.docker_image: vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly`
- `variants.bf16.hardware_overrides.mi325x.extra_env`:
  - `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`: Gated DeltaNet prefill moves to the AITER FlyDSL kernel (the default `auto` backend picks it on MI3xx, and every AITER-on serve log shows `Using AITER FlyDSL GDN prefill kernel (requested=auto, ...)`, so no `--gdn-prefill-backend` flag is needed), the MoE to `AiterUnquantizedExperts`, and RMSNorm and all-reduce to AITER kernels. The serve log shows no fallback warnings.
  - `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1`: AITER runs the shared expert inside the routed-expert MoE kernel (513 experts, top-11) instead of as a separate MLP, as the MI355X MXFP4 variant already does.

## Claims

4x MI325X, TP4, MTP3:

- **AITER:** +1.9% to +7.3% output throughput at every point from 1K to 252K input; mean TPOT and end-to-end latency lower at every point. Rechecked at three cells on the newer build used for the fusion runs: +5.5% to +8.2%, every run.
- **Shared-expert fusion:** another +1.3% to +3.7% output throughput at 1K and 8K input and +0.9% to +1.4% at 128K. Each value is the median of 4 runs per arm, and at every point the slowest fusion-on run is faster than the fastest fusion-off run.
- **Accuracy:** GSM8K unchanged within one standard error by either setting; RULER NIAH 1.00 on all three tasks at 32K and 128K with AITER on, and at 128K with fusion on.

## Test plan

4x MI325X, TP4. Benchmarks use synthetic MTP acceptance (0.92 / 0.83 / 0.70, measured with real MTP on GSM8K), so both arms decode the same tokens per step; accuracy uses standard MTP3.

- **AITER off vs on:** vLLM `0.34.0rc1.dev142+g96710245e`, one server start per arm, a fresh seed per point (prefix cache hit rate 0%).
- **Fusion off vs on, and the AITER spot check:** vLLM `0.34.0rc1.dev206+gf5d93296c`, AITER `0.1.29`, `AITER_CUSTOM_AR_DISABLE_LAMPORT=1` in both arms. Two server starts per arm, alternating, order reversed in round 2; two seeds per start, the same in both arms; each value is the median of the 4 runs.
- **Lamport all-reduce default:** same nightly build (vLLM `0.34.0rc1.dev206+gf5d93296c`, AITER `0.1.29`), `AITER_CUSTOM_AR_DISABLE_LAMPORT` unset (AITER default) vs `=1`, same protocol. At 128K (131,072 tokens) c1, the best runs are equal (90.4 vs 90.5 output tok/s) and median TTFT is 8.8 s in both arms; at 32K c8 and 8K c32 the runs of the two arms overlap and the medians differ by less than 1%. 1K c8 is −3.8% on the median, from two slow runs on the first Lamport server; the second matched off (1574 / 1587 vs 1570–1586 tok/s). So the recipe keeps the AITER default. TEP8 with the default: GSM8K 0.9666, RULER 128K 1.00.

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

Serve (recipe flags). The off arm of each comparison drops that comparison's variable. All runs set `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1`.

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1 \
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --max-num-seqs 256 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 --enable-prefix-caching \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3,"rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","synthetic_acceptance_rates":[0.92,0.83,0.70]}'
```

Accuracy runs use `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'`.

Benchmark, common part (`$ISL` input length, `$C` concurrency):

```bash
vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len $ISL --random-output-len 1024 --random-range-ratio 0 --ignore-eos \
  --max-concurrency $C --num-prompts $N --num-warmups $W --seed $SEED \
  --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el
```

| Runs | `$N` prompts | `$W` warm-ups |
| ---- | ------------ | ------------- |
| AITER, 1K–32K | 8 x C, at least 16 (512 at C = 128) | min(C, 32) |
| AITER, 128K and 252K | 8 | 1 |
| Fusion and spot check | 8 x C, at least 16 | C |

Every run has its own `$SEED`, so prefix caching never replays a prompt; paired runs use the same seed in both arms.

GSM8K:

```bash

  --model_args model=Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=32,max_retries=3,max_gen_toks=2048,tokenized_requests=False \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --apply_chat_template --fewshot_as_multiturn \

```


</details>

## Not covered

Throughput was measured only on plain TP4 with MTP3. The FP8 checkpoint was not tested. MI300X (also gfx942, 304 CUs; BF16 fits at TP4) should take the same override but was not tested, so this PR only adds MI325X. `AITER_USE_FLYDSL_MOE_SORTING=1`, which the MI355X variant sets, runs on MI325X but was left out: +0.8% to +1.0% output throughput at concurrency 1, −0.2% to −0.6% at 8 and 32 (1K / 8K input, 4 runs per arm). `default_strategy` stays `single_node_tep`, because the schema has no per-GPU default strategy. The recipes schema validator was not run locally.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][ROCm][MiniMax-M3.1] Fix the decode glue crash with preshuffled MXFP8 weights
commits.pr_body:
## Overview
#67072 broke MiniMax-M3.1 on MI355X at TP4. The server crashes at startup. This PR fixes it.

## Cause
#65479 added `AiterFlyDSLMxfp8LinearKernel`. This kernel shuffles each MXFP8 linear weight in place (16x16 layout) and views its scales as E8M0. The M3.1 decode glue from #67072 still reads these weights as row-major:

1. `fp8_rows()` builds the glue's shared-expert copies from the shuffled weight.
2. Above 72 rows, `shared_decode()` gives the shuffled weight and the E8M0 scales to vLLM's Triton `dot_scaled` GEMM. Triton fails at the 192-row warmup:

```
File ".../minimax_m3/amd/glue/shared.py", line 196, in shared_decode
    return _mxfp8_dot_scaled_gemm(a_q, a_s, dn.weight, dn.weight_scale, OUT_DTYPE)
KeyError: 'float8_e8m0fnu'
```

## Fix
1. `fp8_rows()` reads the weight through `row_major_weight()`, as the DSpark drafter already does.
2. The glue uses the Triton down GEMM only when the layer's weight is row-major with uint8 scales. Otherwise it uses the AITER GEMM on its own copy.

## Validation
MI355X, TP4, `amd/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Quark-MXFP4`, DSpark 7, AITER v0.1.29, GSM8K through `lm_eval --model local-chat-completions --tasks gsm8k --apply_chat_template`:

| Code | Server start | GSM8K (flexible / strict) |
| -- | -- | -- |
| main 748f1ab35 | crash (`KeyError: 'float8_e8m0fnu'`) | - |
| main 748f1ab35 + this PR | OK, decode glue on at 24-192 rows | 0.8332 / 0.8180 |

`glue/shared.py` is the same on the current main. Runs on the current nightly (7c3a9302f) are in progress for these cases: DSpark 7, DSpark 3, no speculative decoding, AITER off and the mono decode cell. I will add the results in a comment.

CI cannot run this path: it needs MI355X (gfx950), TP4 and the M3.1 checkpoint.

No open PR changes `glue/shared.py` or fixes this crash.

---

commits.pr_title: [Quantization][GLM-5.3] Let online quantization reach the BF16 attention projections
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

GLM-5.3-Flash builds its attention projections (KDA, MLA, DSA indexer) with `quant_config=None`, so online quantization requested with `--quantization-config '{"targets": ...}'` silently skips them. This PR passes the model's quant config to these modules, so they follow the checkpoint's own skip list and the online targets, as other models do. The one special case is the MLA projections of FP8 / Quark checkpoints, which the model already dequantizes to BF16 at load. Related: #59833, #55741 (see Details).

## Claims

- **Online quantization now reaches the BF16 attention projections** when `--quantization-config` names them. On `nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4`, the targets under Recommended configuration now quantize 196 layers (attention + shared experts) instead of 84 (shared experts only).
- **No change without `--quantization-config`:** on GB300, the default greedy outputs of the NVFP4 checkpoint (with and without MTP) and of the Z.ai FP8 checkpoint match `main` token for token.
- **No GLM-specific quant config:** the KDA and MLA modules get the model's `quant_config`. The Z.ai FP8 checkpoint names its BF16 layers `model.layers.N.self_attn.*` in `modules_to_not_convert`, so the model's `hf_to_vllm_mapper` maps that prefix, and `packed_modules_mapping` lists the shards of the fused KDA `in_proj_qkvbfg_a`. Shared quantization code is unchanged, and there is no new flag.
- **Recommended, behavior-preserving configurations** (MXFP8 on the 128 non-KDA projections for aggregated serving; MXFP8 on all 196 on prefill instances only for disaggregated serving) keep accuracy and output length unchanged on 7 benchmarks, and give +2% output throughput (aggregated) and up to +12% (disaggregated, prefill-bound) on GB300.
- MXFP8 on all 196 projections in aggregated serving is faster still (+8% on GB300), but measurably shortens reasoning; this PR describes it as an opt-in with that disclosure.

## Validation

### Unit tests

```bash
pytest tests/models/glm5next
```

GB300, upstream nightly `96710245` with this branch's Python sources copied over the installed package: 113 passed, 9 skipped (ROCm-only `test_sparse_indexer_topk_dispatch` cases). `pre-commit` passes. CI selects these tests in the `glm5next-unit-tests` step (`pytest -v -s models/glm5next`, H200; the MI355 mirror step runs them on ROCm).

The new tests (`tests/models/glm5next/test_online_quantization.py`, 5 cases) use real configs and real `ColumnParallelLinear` layers:

- a block-FP8 `Fp8Config` whose `modules_to_not_convert` names KDA projections as in the Z.ai config (`model.layers.0.self_attn.*`): the KDA `o_proj` and the fused `in_proj_qkvbfg_a` stay unquantized; with an online `mxfp8` target, `o_proj` gets the online method starting from BF16 (no FP8 requantization); a shared expert keeps the checkpoint's FP8 method;
- an NVFP4 `ModelOptNvFp4Config` that excludes `model.layers.45*`, configured for the target model and then the MTP draft (they share the quant config): the MTP layer stays unquantized.

On `main` @ `bec08b701`, the three KDA cases fail, because the checkpoint's names do not match vLLM's; the shared-expert and MTP cases pass:

```text
FAILED test_fp8_checkpoint_keeps_kda_projections_bf16[o_proj]
FAILED test_fp8_checkpoint_keeps_kda_projections_bf16[fused-in_proj]
FAILED test_fp8_checkpoint_keeps_kda_projections_bf16[o_proj+online]
E   AssertionError: assert <class '...fp8.Fp8LinearMethod'> is <class '...linear.UnquantizedLinearMethod'>
```

### Default behavior (GB300)

Tensor parallel 4, `enforce_eager`, 4 prompts x 64 greedy tokens, upstream nightly `96710245` with `main` @ `bec08b701` or this branch's Python sources:

| checkpoint | `main` vs this branch |
|---|---|
| `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash-FP8` (`46a050b`) | 4/4 identical |
| `nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4` | 4/4 identical in a paired run; MLA KV-cache dtype and effective q/k/v/prob scales identical (see below) |
| `nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4`, MTP (`num_speculative_tokens=1`) | 4/4 identical |

The NVFP4 eager greedy outputs vary between runs of the same tree (`main` vs `main`: 1/4 identical), so a single pair can differ; no difference was specific to this branch.

With the online targets, the startup log shows the expected counts: `Quantizing 196 layers` and `Quantizing 128 layers` on the NVFP4 checkpoint (the two configurations under Recommended configuration), and `Quantizing 68 layers` (`self_attn.in_proj_qkvbfg_a: 34, self_attn.o_proj: 34`) on the FP8 checkpoint with KDA targets.

### End to end and performance (GB300)

`nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4` (`da920bb`), upstream nightly `edad8b03` with this branch's `vllm/models/glm5next` mounted over the installed package (the stock nightly for the BF16 rows), Dynamo frontend, sa-bench random prompts (8K in / 1K out, all requests at once, concurrency-capped), `--max-num-batched-tokens 32768` (prefill / aggregated), `--kernel-config '{"linear_backend_per_quant": {"mxfp8": "torch"}}'` for the MXFP8 rows. These runs predate the rebase onto `cdd2750cd`; the commits in between change no compiled code, and the only one touching GLM-5.3 (#61457) affects AITER fused shared experts on ROCm. Every run completed all requests (0 failed), and the startup log showed the expected `Quantizing N layers` count (none on the BF16 rows and on the disaggregated decode instance).

Aggregated, 1 node, DP2 + expert parallel (2 GPUs), 5,120 / 10,240 requests:

| config | layers quantized | C512 output tok/s/GPU | C1024 output tok/s/GPU | C512 / C1024 mean TTFT |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BF16 projections (today) | 0 | 2,839 | 2,441 | 7.8 s / 52.2 s |
| MXFP8, non-KDA 128 | 128 | 2,896 (+2.0%) | 2,488 (+1.9%) | 7.3 s / 49.5 s |
| MXFP8, all 196 (opt-in) | 196 | 3,075 (+8.3%) | 2,641 (+8.2%) | 6.0 s / 42.2 s |

Disaggregated, 2 prefill instances (TP1, 1 GPU each) + 1 decode instance (DP2 + expert parallel), 4 GPUs on 2 nodes, NIXL KV transfer:

| config | C128 output tok/s/GPU | C256 | C512 | C128 / C256 / C512 mean TTFT |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BF16 projections (today) | 1,438 | 2,234 | 2,695 | 1.04 s / 1.97 s / 17.5 s |
| MXFP8 all 196 on prefill only | 1,446 (+0.6%) | 2,254 (+0.9%) | 3,025 (+12.2%) | 0.97 s / 1.69 s / 8.7 s |

Single runs per point, so the sub-1% C128 / C256 disaggregated differences are not significant. At C512 the 2 prefill GPUs are the bottleneck (17.5 s TTFT), and faster prefill roughly halves TTFT and raises output throughput by 12%; decode step time is unchanged at C128 / C256 (TPOT 20.6 / 25.8 ms in both).

### Accuracy

**Setup:**

- Checkpoint: [`nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4`](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4) (revision `da920bb`), served with `--quantization modelopt_fp4`.
- NeMo-Skills 0.7.0 against an OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
- Model-card sampling: temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, max_new_tokens 327,680, default chat template (reasoning effort Max); reasoning stripped before scoring.
- Run on NVIDIA VR200, on a `main` nightly with this branch's `glm5next` package. The reference is the same nightly without the branch, so its projections are BF16. Only the `--quantization-config` targets differ between the arms.
- Deltas are paired by problem; 95% CIs are a bootstrap over problems. Pass rule: no significant regression, and the pooled CI must exclude a loss of more than 1 point.

| benchmark | samples | BF16 | all 196: Δ [95% CI] | non-KDA 128: Δ [95% CI] |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AIME25 | 30 x 8 | 97.08 | -1.25 [-4.58, +1.67] | +0.83 [-1.67, +3.75] |
| GPQA-Diamond | 198 x 4 | 90.15 | +1.26 [-0.76, +3.41] | +1.14 [-0.38, +2.78] |
| MATH-500 | 500 x 1 | 97.60 | -0.40 [-1.80, +1.00] | +0.60 [-0.60, +2.00] |
| GSM8K | 1319 x 1 | 96.89 | +0.76 [+0.15, +1.44] | +0.30 [-0.45, +1.06] |
| BeyondAIME | 100 x 8 | 87.75 | -0.50 [-2.62, +1.50] | +0.38 [-1.50, +2.25] |
| HMMT Feb 2025 | 30 x 16 | 97.29 | -1.04 [-3.75, +1.46] | -0.21 [-2.29, +1.88] |
| APEX shortlist | 47 x 8 | 86.17 | -3.19 [-8.78, +1.60] | -2.66 [-7.18, +1.60] |
| pooled, 3 hard long-output sets | | | -1.58 [-3.69, +0.44] | -0.83 [-2.61, +0.84] |
| **pooled macro, 7 benchmarks** | | | **-0.62 [-1.69, +0.42]** | **+0.05 [-0.85, +0.94]** |

- **The hard, long-output sets** (BeyondAIME, HMMT, APEX shortlist) were added because 8-bit numerics on a linear-attention model's recurrent path have been reported to shorten reasoning with flat accuracy on easier sets but a loss on HLE. HLE itself needs an external LLM judge, so we used these judge-free, symbolically graded sets instead.
- **Non-KDA** passes the rule on all 7 benchmarks. Its APEX dip is within the noise of a 47-problem set and is not mirrored on the other two hard sets.
- **All 196** has no significant loss on any benchmark, but it is lower on all three hard sets, and neither pooled CI excludes a loss above 1 point. We disclose it as a possible cost, not a proven one.

Output length, paired by (problem, seed), both finished, ties excluded. Under BF16-vs-BF16 replicates, "shorter" stays near 50% (z within about ±1.5):

| set | all 196: shorter, z | non-KDA 128: shorter, z | median tokens, BF16 / all 196 / non-KDA |
|---|---|---|---|
| AIME25, GPQA, MATH-500, GSM8K | 58.5% of 2,567, **+8.6** | 48.4% of 2,542, -1.6 | AIME25 6,642 / 4,546 / 6,833; GPQA 4,237 / 3,378 / 3,965 |
| BeyondAIME, HMMT, APEX | 63.6% of 1,649, **+11.1** | 51.2% of 1,648, +1.0 | BeyondAIME 20.3K / 15.9K / 20.4K; APEX 69.7K / 59.1K / 71.3K |

<details>
<summary>Broader coverage: all 196 on an earlier build (8 benchmarks + RULER 64K)</summary>

Same quantization path (`mxfp8_e4m3_quantize` plus `TorchMxFp8LinearKernel` on the same 196 layers, at every M, decode included) on a downstream build of the same model code. The reference is the same build with BF16 projections.

| benchmark | samples | BF16 | MXFP8 (all 196) | Δ [95% CI] |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AIME24 | 30 x 16 | 95.83 | 96.46 | +0.62 [-1.25, +2.92] |
| AIME25 | 30 x 16 | 94.17 | 94.38 | +0.21 [-2.71, +3.12] |
| GPQA-Diamond | 198 x 8 | 91.16 | 91.04 | -0.13 [-1.07, +0.82] |
| MATH-500 | 500 x 4 | 97.70 | 97.65 | -0.05 [-0.80, +0.70] |
| GSM8K | 1319 x 2 | 97.08 | 97.31 | +0.23 [-0.27, +0.72] |
| MMLU-Pro | 12032 x 1 | 87.48 | 87.65 | +0.17 [-0.21, +0.53] |
| IFEval (prompt strict) | 541 x 4 | 90.25 | 89.97 | -0.28 [-1.39, +0.83] |
| LiveCodeBench v6 (2408-2505) | 454 x 4 | 50.50 | 51.65 | +1.16 [+0.11, +2.26] |
| RULER 64K (13 tasks) | 1300 | see note | see note | no regression |
| **macro average, 8 benchmarks** | | | | **+0.24 [-0.28, +0.77]** |

- **RULER 64K:** NIAH x8 and VT are 100% for both. QA_1 is 92 vs 95 and QA_2 is 74 vs 78. CWE/FWE are noisy in both arms (frequent repetition loops at max effort).
- **Output length:** the MXFP8 output is shorter in 59-66% of pairs on AIME/GPQA/LiveCodeBench. Fewer generations end in runaway repetition loops at the token cap (LiveCodeBench 9.7% vs 17.1%), which is where the LiveCodeBench gain comes from.
- **Where the shift comes from:** a teacher-forced logprob comparison on identical token sequences, quantizing one projection group at a time, located the shift on the KDA in/out projections. On the hesitation-token measure, each other group's effect was at most about 1/5 of either KDA group's. That localization is what defines the non-KDA config.

</details>

## Details

### Why the projections were unreachable

GLM-5.3-Flash loads its attention projections as BF16 in every checkpoint:

- KDA `in_proj_qkvbfg_a`, `f_b_proj`, `g_b_proj`, `o_proj`;
- MLA `fused_qkv_a_proj`, `q_b_proj`, `o_proj`;
- DSA indexer `wq_b`.

The KDA and indexer projections are BF16 in every official checkpoint. The MLA projections are BF16 in the NVFP4 checkpoint and block-FP8 in the Z.ai FP8 checkpoint, which the model dequantizes to BF16 at load (`_try_load_fp8_attn_proj`). The model therefore built all of them with no quant config: MLA passed `quant_config=None`, and KDA cleared `vllm_config.quant_config` around its constructor. Passing the quant config through was not enough by itself: the Z.ai FP8 config lists the BF16 layers in `modules_to_not_convert` as `model.layers.N.*`, while the weights are `model.language_model.layers.N.*`, so none of the 1,509 entries matched vLLM's module names. With `--quantization modelopt_fp4 --quantization-config '{"targets": {...}}'`, composition with the checkpoint method worked for the shared-expert linears (84 layers) but silently skipped the 112 attention projections. No warning was printed.

### What changes

- **KDA and MLA get the model's `quant_config`**, so each projection follows the checkpoint's skip list (`exclude_modules`, `modules_to_not_convert`), and online targets compose with it through the existing `resolve_quant_method` path. Layers that match no online target keep the checkpoint's decision.
- **One special case:** with an FP8-serialized `Fp8Config` or a `QuarkConfig`, MLA keeps `quant_config=None`, because those checkpoints store the MLA projections in FP8 and the model dequantizes them to BF16 at load. As a result, online quantization does not reach the MLA projections of these checkpoints; it still reaches their KDA projections.
- **Name mapping:** the model's `hf_to_vllm_mapper` adds `model.layers.N.self_attn.` → `language_model.model.layers.N.self_attn.` to the GLM-4V prefixes, so the FP8 skip list matches. Only `self_attn` names are mapped: the NVFP4 checkpoint excludes the MTP layer as `model.layers.45*`, and the MTP draft shares the target's quant config, so that entry must keep its name. `packed_modules_mapping` lists the six shards of `in_proj_qkvbfg_a`.
- **The GB300 specialized decode** (#63102, `decode_backend=latency_specialized`) reads the KDA `f_b_proj` (and, with its skinny GEMMs, `in_proj_qkvbfg_a` and `o_proj`) directly as BF16. Its `KdaStage` now checks these weights and fails at startup, naming the projections to exclude from `--quantization-config`, instead of running on quantized weights.

Other effects:

- `kv_b_proj` gets the same config as the other MLA projections. It is excluded in the NVFP4 checkpoint and BF16 under the FP8 special case, and the recommended regexes do not match it. Online quantization of `kv_b_proj` (absorbed into the W_UK / W_UV bmm weights after loading) was not tested.
- The MLA attention module (`self_attn.attn`) now receives the checkpoint config. With the NVFP4 checkpoint it gets `ModelOptKVCacheMethod`; the checkpoint has no attention scale tensors, so the effective scales stay 1.0 with an `fp8_e4m3` KV cache, as on `main` (checked on GB300).
- `--quantization mxfp8` (or another online shorthand) with a BF16 checkpoint now quantizes the attention projections too, like every other linear layer. Use `targets` to choose layers.
- A third-party checkpoint whose skip list omits a BF16 attention projection would now try to load it with the checkpoint method. The official NVFP4 and FP8 checkpoints were checked layer by layer against their real configs.

| file | change |
|---|---|
| `vllm/models/glm5next/common/model.py` | MLA gets `quant_config` (except the FP8 / Quark case); `hf_to_vllm_mapper` and `packed_modules_mapping` for the checkpoint's skip-list names |
| `vllm/models/glm5next/common/kda.py` | KDA projections get `quant_config`; no more clearing of `vllm_config.quant_config` |
| `vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/specialized_decode/kda.py` | the specialized decode rejects quantized KDA projections |
| `tests/models/glm5next/test_online_quantization.py` | new, 2 tests (5 cases) |

No docs change: the projections now follow the existing contract in `docs/features/quantization/online.md` ("Online quantization on unquantized layers from partially-quantized checkpoints"). The GLM-5.3-Flash-specific recommendation stays in this description.

### Recommended configuration

All measurements use NVIDIA's NVFP4 checkpoint, [`nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4`](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4) (revision `da920bb`). Its routed experts and dense MLPs are NVFP4. The 196 projections studied are BF16:

| group | projections | layers |
|---|---|---|
| KDA (34 linear-attention layers) | `in_proj_qkvbfg_a`, `o_proj` | 68 |
| MLA / DSA (11 layers: 3, 7, ..., 43) | `fused_qkv_a_proj`, `q_b_proj`, `o_proj`, `indexer.wq_b` | 44 |
| shared expert (42 MoE layers) | `gate_up_proj`, `down_proj` | 84 |

We tested MXFP8 (E4M3 values, one E8M0 scale per 32 elements, for weights and dynamic activations). Accuracy holds in every configuration. However, MXFP8 on the **68 KDA in/out projections at decode** measurably changes reasoning behavior: traces get 20-30% shorter on AIME/GPQA, with fewer hesitation and self-correction tokens, and accuracy on hard long-output problems trends lower (not significant). The other 128 projections leave behavior unchanged.

| deployment | recommended config | behavior vs BF16 |
|---|---|---|
| **aggregated (or any decode-serving instance)** | **MXFP8 on the 128 non-KDA projections** (MLA, indexer `wq_b`, shared expert); KDA in/out stay BF16 | unchanged: accuracy and output length match BF16 on 7 benchmarks |
| **disaggregated** | **MXFP8 on all 196 projections on the prefill instances only**; decode instances unchanged | decode, which produces nearly all of the output tokens, runs exactly as today |
| opt-in, aggregated | MXFP8 on all 196 projections | **changed**: shorter reasoning, and a possible 1-2 point cost on hard long-output problems |

- **Where the throughput comes from:** the prefill-heavy, large-M GEMMs. The largest projection is KDA `in_proj_qkvbfg_a` (4096 → 24,896), so excluding the KDA projections keeps only part of the gain in aggregated serving (+2% instead of +8% on GB300).
- **Why prefill-only is behavior-preserving:** the behavior change comes from MXFP8 numerics at decode, which pick each next token. With MXFP8 only on prefill instances, prefill computes the KV cache and KDA state in MXFP8, while every generated token after the first comes from BF16 decode. An aggregated variant with exactly that split (MXFP8 for GEMMs of ≥ 2048 tokens, BF16 weights kept for decode; not part of this PR, it needs a second weight copy) showed no length change and no accuracy change: macro +0.09 pt [-0.43, +0.61] over 8 benchmarks. The disaggregated deployment itself was not accuracy-tested.
- **Use the cuBLASLt MXFP8 kernel** (`--kernel-config '{"linear_backend_per_quant": {"mxfp8": "torch"}}'`). On SM10x, the automatic choice (FlashInfer CuTe-DSL) was markedly slower for these shapes at large M. The kernel priority is a separate follow-up.

Commands for the NVFP4 checkpoint. Each regex covers layers 0-44, so the MTP layer (45) is excluded; the K=128 KDA gate projections, `kv_b_proj`, the indexer `wk_weights_proj` and the dense MLPs never match.

Non-KDA, 128 layers (aggregated; behavior-preserving). The MLA layer indices are those of the released 45-layer config:

```bash
vllm serve nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4 --quantization modelopt_fp4 \
  --quantization-config '{"targets": {"re:.*[.]layers[.]((3|7|11|15|19|23|27|31|35|39|43)[.]self_attn[.](o_proj|fused_qkv_a_proj|q_b_proj|indexer[.]wq_b)|([0-9]|[1-3][0-9]|4[0-4])[.]mlp[.]shared_experts[.](gate_proj|up_proj|gate_up_proj|down_proj))": "mxfp8"}}' \
  --kernel-config '{"linear_backend_per_quant": {"mxfp8": "torch"}}'
```

All 196 (prefill instances of a disaggregated deployment; or the disclosed aggregated opt-in):

```bash
vllm serve nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4 --quantization modelopt_fp4 \
  --quantization-config '{"targets": {"re:.*[.]layers[.]([0-9]|[1-3][0-9]|4[0-4])[.](self_attn[.](in_proj_qkvbfg_a|o_proj|fused_qkv_a_proj|q_b_proj|indexer[.]wq_b)|mlp[.]shared_experts[.](gate_proj|up_proj|gate_up_proj|down_proj))": "mxfp8"}}' \
  --kernel-config '{"linear_backend_per_quant": {"mxfp8": "torch"}}'
```

The startup log confirms the coverage, e.g. `Quantizing 196 layers of types: ... self_attn.in_proj_qkvbfg_a: 34, self_attn.o_proj: 45, ...` (128 layers for the non-KDA regex).

<details>
<summary>Other checkpoints and other FP8 schemes</summary>

Other checkpoints (static analysis; only the NVFP4 checkpoint was run):

| checkpoint | how to use it |
|---|---|
| shared experts BF16 (NVIDIA NVFP4, RedHat / LibertAI NVFP4, W4A16 quants) | the regexes above |
| shared experts already quantized (RadixArk NVFP4) | drop the `mlp.shared_experts` alternative (112 attention layers). With it, the checkpoint method cannot re-quantize (no `dequantize_weight`) and loading fails, as on `main`. |
| Z.ai FP8, AMD Quark | KDA `in_proj_qkvbfg_a` / `o_proj` only (68 layers on the FP8 checkpoint, run on GB300). The MLA projections stay BF16 (dequantized at load), and the shared experts are already quantized. |
| BF16 (`zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash-BF16`) | add `--quantization online`; `--quantization-config` alone is ignored (existing behavior) |

The regexes above cover layers 0-44, so the MTP layer (45) keeps the checkpoint's decision.

- **Do not use a per-tensor activation scale on these layers at decode.** One scale shared by every row of a decode batch couples all requests. FP8 per-tensor W+A at every batch size was broken in our runs: AIME 94-97% → 53-60%, MATH-500 98% → 65%, with 20-25% runaway repetition loops. Upstream's online `fp8_per_tensor` uses per-token activation scales on CUTLASS-capable GPUs and does not have this coupling; we did not evaluate it.
- **Per-channel FP8 (`fp8_per_channel`) on all 196** mostly avoids the behavior change but also keeps only a small part of the throughput gain, so it offers nothing over the non-KDA MXFP8 config.

</details>

### Not a duplicate

Searched open PRs: "glm5next quantization", "glm online quantization", "online quantization attention", "GLM-5.3 mxfp8", "quant_config=None MLA", "glm5next mxfp8", "GLM-5.3 quantization config", "kda online quantization", "glm5next quant_config", "modules_to_not_convert glm".

- **#59833** (GLM-5.x: load ModelOpt NVFP4 MLA projections into BF16 `fused_qkv_a_proj`) changes how *checkpoint-quantized* MLA weights are loaded into BF16 targets. It does not touch the `quant_config=None` wiring, and it is complementary: such weights could then be online-quantized.
- **#55741** (MLA bmm abstraction and `kv_b_proj` online quantization) makes a generic MLA `kv_b_proj` quantizable through the bmm path. This PR does not change how GLM's `kv_b_proj` is absorbed, so it does not conflict, and GLM could adopt #55741 later.
- **#61457** (per-layer fused shared expert selection, merged; this branch is rebased on it) and **#61662** / **#64121** / **#64245** (ROCm GLM-5.3-Flash MonoKernel decode) edit `glm5next/common/model.py` in unrelated places; the open ones merge cleanly with this branch.
- **#49313** (Quark: online requant of unquantized layers through a `quantization_config` overlay) is a Quark-specific generic mechanism and does not reach GLM's `quant_config=None` projections.

### Limitations

- Hardware-neutral, but validated on NVIDIA only; ROCm uses the same code path (MXFP8 via `RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel`) and is untested.
- CI covers the config wiring (unit tests); no CI job serves GLM-5.3-Flash (191 GB checkpoint). End-to-end validation was done outside CI as listed above.
- The throughput and accuracy runs used an earlier revision of this PR (a GLM-specific online-only config for these projections). On the NVFP4 checkpoint it quantized the same layers with the same method, which the `Quantizing N layers` counts above confirm for this revision.
- The disaggregated prefill-only configuration was measured for throughput, not for accuracy (see the aggregated equivalent above).

### AI assistance

This change was prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code). The submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Metrics] Count preemptions in the scheduler, not on resume
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

`vllm:num_preemptions` is counted from the request's `PREEMPTED` event, which only reaches the frontend with that request's next output. So a request that is preempted and then aborted before it resumes is never counted, and the rest are counted late. This counts preemptions in the scheduler and reports them in `SchedulerStats`, like the prefix cache stats.

## Claims

- Requests aborted while preempted are counted.
- The counter moves when the preemption happens, not when the request resumes.
- `IterationStats.num_preempted_reqs` is removed (no longer used); `vllm:request_num_preemptions` is unchanged.

## Validation

New test: a request is preempted by KV pressure and aborted; the next step's `SchedulerStats` counts it once.

```
pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -k aborted_request_is_counted
main:     failed (SchedulerStats has no num_preempted_reqs)
this PR:  passed
```

`tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py` (297) and `tests/v1/metrics/test_logging_stat_logger.py` + `test_stats.py` (28) pass; pre-commit passes.

End to end on CPU (SmolLM2-135M, 8 KV blocks, 8 concurrent requests, clients killed while some were preempted; true count from a temporary log line):

Each run had 2 real preemptions:

| Counted | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 1 API server | 0, 1, 2, 2 | 2, 2, 2, 2 |
| 2 API servers | 0, 1, 1, 2 | 2, 2, 2 |
| no aborts (7 real) | 7 | 7 |

## Details

The `PREEMPTED` event stays as it is for the interval metrics (#13169); only the counter moves. An aborted request's events can't be applied on the frontend, which has already dropped it, so counting in the scheduler is the simpler fix.

No existing PR or issue covers this. Related: #38452 and #61492 fix the `Preemptions:` log field (small overlap in `loggers.py`), and #58037 adds a by-reason counter from the same event.

Not tested on GPU or with data parallelism. AI assistance (Claude Code) was used; I reviewed the change and ran the tests.

commits.pr_title: [Frontend][Multimodal] Return mm_hashes from /inference/v1/generate
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`/inference/v1/generate` now returns `mm_hashes` next to `mm_placeholders`, so multi-turn callers can pass earlier media back as `features` without building cache keys themselves. Follows up on #57796 and #67564.

## Claims

- New `mm_hashes` field on the generate response, streaming and non-streaming. It's set under the same conditions as `mm_placeholders`: `return_token_ids`, a multimodal prompt and not encoder-decoder. Streaming sends it on the first chunk only.
- The keys come from the engine input, so they're correct with `--mm-processor-kwargs` / `--media-io-kwargs` and for items sent without a `uuid`.
- The Rust frontend returns the same field.
- The docs example uses `turn1["mm_hashes"]` instead of the `"uuid:<uuid>"` workaround.

## Validation

- `pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_serving_multimodal_tokens.py -v`
  - `test_content_parts_generates_tokens`: `mm_hashes` matches `/render`'s `features.mm_hashes`.
  - `test_features_with_content_parts[cached=True]`: turn 1 is sent without a `uuid` and turn 2 reuses the hashes turn 1 returned. This covers the `content:` path.
  - `test_content_parts_streaming`: only the first chunk carries `mm_hashes`.
- `cargo test -p vllm-server --lib -- generate:: routes::tests::generate_expands_content_parts_after_features`
- `cargo fmt --check`, clippy, ruff and mypy are clean on the changed files.

No model eval: this only adds a response field and doesn't change outputs.

## Details

Today the docs tell callers to send a `uuid` on turn 1 and pass back `"uuid:<uuid>"`. That broke when #66473 added the `uuid:` / `content:` tags (#67564). It's also an issue when the server sets processor or media IO kwargs  because those get hashed into the key. Items sent without a `uuid` get a `content:` key the client never sees. Returning the keys the server actually used fixes all three.

I didn't return a full `features` object because it would duplicate `mm_placeholders` and suggest `/generate` returns tensors which is `/render`'s job. Having the server add `uuid:` to bare keys was already rejected in #67564.

This doesn't expose anything new. `/render` already returns the same tagged keys and callers only get keys for media they sent.

Limitations:
- Rust `/generate` still requires `kwargs_data` in `features`, so on the Rust frontend the returned keys can't be sent back yet. The field is there to match Python and `/render`. Both limitations are in the docs.
- With `--mm-processor-cache-gb 0` the keys can't be reused.

Not a duplicate: I searched open PRs for `mm_hashes`. #64721, #60526 and #65018 touch nearby code, but none add this field to the generate response.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][CI] Force the ASM path in test_online_mxfp4_hadamard[aiter-asm]
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`test_online_mxfp4_hadamard[*-aiter-asm]`, added in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63272, fails on the MI355 DPX nodes of AMD CI because AITER has no tuned a4w4 config for its shape at 128 CUs, so the layer never takes the ASM path it checks. The test now forces the ASM path, so it covers the fused Hadamard rotation independently of AITER's tuned configs.

Failing jobs on the 2026-11-17 AMD nightly (amd-ci #15843, `main` @ `f91a777`):
- https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/15843#01a1e8f5-12b3-4e77-a796-49ab0d2eb4c2
- https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/15843#01a1e8f5-12b3-48d7-9137-2963c4cda026

## Claims

- `test_online_mxfp4_hadamard[16-aiter-asm]` and `[256-aiter-asm]` pass on a gfx950 device with 128 CUs (an MI355 in DPX mode), where they fail on `main` with `assert False == True` on `layer.input_hadamard_fused`.
- The test still checks the fused path on 256-CU MI355: same assertions, same shapes.
- No change outside the test.

## Validation

Both runs use the CI image of the failing build, `rocm/vllm-ci:build-01a1e8f2-fb2c-4d4f-926c-6f691496c43c`, on one MI355X in SPX mode (256 CUs). The test file and every file it exercises are the same in that image's commit and in this PR's base, apart from this change. To reproduce the 128-CU lookup, a pytest plugin makes AITER's a4w4 config lookup see 128 CUs:

```python
# /tmp/i510/dpx_cu.py
import os
if os.environ.get("FAKE_CU_NUM"):
    import aiter.ops.gemm_op_a4w4 as m
    m.get_cu_num = lambda: int(os.environ["FAKE_CU_NUM"])
    print(f"patched aiter gemm_op_a4w4.get_cu_num -> {os.environ['FAKE_CU_NUM']}")
```

```bash
docker run --rm --device /dev/kfd --device /dev/dri --group-add video --ipc host \
  --security-opt seccomp=unconfined -e HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=6 -e FAKE_CU_NUM=<unset|128> \
  -e PYTHONPATH=/i510 -v /tmp/i510:/i510 \
  [-v $PWD/tests/quantization/test_input_hadamard.py:/vllm-workspace/tests/quantization/test_input_hadamard.py:ro] \
  -w /vllm-workspace/tests --entrypoint bash rocm/vllm-ci:build-01a1e8f2-fb2c-4d4f-926c-6f691496c43c \
  -c 'pytest -q -p dpx_cu quantization/test_input_hadamard.py[::test_online_mxfp4_hadamard]'
```

| Test file | CUs seen by the a4w4 lookup | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `main` | 256 | 6 passed (`test_online_mxfp4_hadamard`) |
| `main` | 128 | 2 failed, 4 passed: both `aiter-asm` cases, same assertion and log line as CI |
| this PR (2 runs) | 256 | 16 passed, both runs (whole file) |
| this PR (2 runs) | 128 | 16 passed, both runs (whole file) |

<details>
<summary>Raw output</summary>

`main`, 128 CUs:

```
patched aiter gemm_op_a4w4.get_cu_num -> 128
=================================== FAILURES ===================================
>       assert layer.input_hadamard_fused == fused
E       assert False == True
[aiter] shape is M:1024, N:3072, K:1536, not found tuned config in /tmp/aiter_configs/a4w4_blockscale_tuned_gemm.csv, will use default config!
INFO     aiter:gemm_op_a4w4.py:155 shape is M:1024, N:3072, K:1536, not found tuned config in /tmp/aiter_configs/a4w4_blockscale_tuned_gemm.csv, will use default config!
>       assert layer.input_hadamard_fused == fused
E       assert False == True
FAILED quantization/test_input_hadamard.py::test_online_mxfp4_hadamard[16-aiter-asm]
FAILED quantization/test_input_hadamard.py::test_online_mxfp4_hadamard[256-aiter-asm]
2 failed, 4 passed, 16 warnings in 35.02s
```

`main`, 256 CUs:

```
6 passed, 16 warnings in 35.28s
```

This PR:

```
===== FAKE_CU_NUM=unset
16 passed, 16 warnings in 47.06s
===== FAKE_CU_NUM=unset
16 passed, 16 warnings in 39.62s
===== FAKE_CU_NUM=128
patched aiter gemm_op_a4w4.get_cu_num -> 128
16 passed, 16 warnings in 38.30s
===== FAKE_CU_NUM=128
patched aiter gemm_op_a4w4.get_cu_num -> 128
16 passed, 16 warnings in 38.13s
```

CI, `(MI355 DPX) Quantization Shard 3`, build 15843:

```
quantization/test_input_hadamard.py::test_online_mxfp4_hadamard[256-aiter-asm]
[aiter] shape is M:1024, N:3072, K:1536, not found tuned config in /tmp/vllm-2963c4cda026/tmp/aiter_configs/a4w4_blockscale_tuned_gemm.csv, will use default config!
FAILED
...
>       assert layer.input_hadamard_fused == fused
E       assert False == True
E        +  where False = Module().input_hadamard_fused

quantization/test_input_hadamard.py:311: AssertionError
```

</details>

`ruff check` and `ruff format --check` (0.17.2, the pinned version) pass on the changed file.

## Details

**Root cause.** `AiterMxfp4LinearKernel` takes the ASM path only when `rocm_aiter_ops.is_asm_fp4_gemm_tuned(n, k)` and `is_triton_gemm_afp4wfp4_presh_ws_tuned(n, k)` are true, and only the ASM path fuses the rotation. The first check calls AITER's `get_GEMM_config`, which keys rows by `(gfx, cu_num, M, N, K)` with the device's CU count. In AITER 0.1.29, the rows for N=3072, K=1536 all have `cu_num=256`. The MI355 DPX nodes expose 128 CUs per GPU (`NPS2, DPX` in the job log), so the lookup misses and the layer stays on the Triton path. The PR that added the test was validated on 256-CU MI355X.

**Change.** In the fused case the test sets both checks to return `True`. With 128 CUs, the ASM GEMM then runs AITER's default config for the shape, which the 128-CU runs above exercise. The second check reads AITER's Triton configs, which have no 128-CU tree on gfx950 today. It is forced too, so the test does not break if one is added without this shape. `tests/kernels/quantization/test_rocm_mxfp4.py` patches the same two checks to select the layout.

Patching the checks is a narrow exception to the guidance against patching methods in tests: whether AITER has tuned rows for a shape depends on the device's CU count, and which rows exist is outside this test's scope. The two alternatives are worse. A skip on DPX leaves the fused path with no MI355 coverage, since `(MI355 DPX) Quantization` is the MI355 job that runs `tests/quantization/`. A 128-CU tuned CSV generated by the test would test AITER's config merging instead of the rotation.

**Limitations.** The 128-CU runs above change only the CU count used by AITER's a4w4 config lookup, on a 256-CU device. The `(MI355 DPX) Quantization` job on this PR is the check on DPX hardware.

**Not a duplicate.** No open PR changes `tests/quantization/test_input_hadamard.py` (checked against all open PRs created since https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63272 merged on 2026-11-16), and searches for `test_online_mxfp4_hadamard`, `input_hadamard_fused`, and "DPX cu_num" find no PR.

AI assistance was used to investigate the failure and prepare this change. The submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

commits.pr_title: [Model] Add Inkling 2 Small
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Adds Thinking Machines' [Inkling 2 Small](https://huggingface.co/thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Small): a 594B-total / 17B-active MoE (text + image in, text out, up to 1M context) with a DSpark speculator bundled in the checkpoint. Both released checkpoints are supported: [`Inkling-2-Small`](https://huggingface.co/thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Small) (NVFP4 experts in layers 0–39, MXFP8 in 40–47) and [`Inkling-2-Small-MXFP8`](https://huggingface.co/thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Small-MXFP8) (MXFP8 experts in all layers). Blog: https://vllm.ai/blog/2026-11-12-inkling2-small. Recipe: #67319, #67322.

Follow-ups: Hopper (SM90) support in #67880 and AMD support, which add their kernels next to `vllm/models/inkling2/nvidia/`.

No open PR adds this model (searched open PRs for "Inkling2" / "Inkling 2").

## Claims

- New model `Inkling2ForConditionalGeneration` (`vllm/models/inkling2/nvidia/`): block attention residuals, gated attention with per-token sink, relative-bias GQA (no RoPE) with short convolutions, 384-expert top-8 MoE with NVFP4 (layers 0–39) / MXFP8 (layers 40–47) experts, 23-layer ViT image encoder.
- DSpark speculative decoding (`Inkling2DSparkModel`, 7 tokens per step), including probabilistic drafting.
- Inkling 2 rendering and output parsing (reasoning, tool calls) in both the Python and Rust frontends, matching the reference renderer.
- Kernels: all-reduce + short conv + residual + attention-residual mix + RMSNorm fused into one NVLink-multicast kernel; sequence-parallel prefill (−22% / −26% on an 8K prefill step at TP4 / TP8); a Gluon relative-bias decode/verify attention kernel (batch-1 decode step at 100K context: 15.1 → 4.8 ms); MoE activation quantization fused into routing and SwiGLU.
- Loads both released checkpoints as published: their `config.json` declares a ModelOpt (NVFP4) or FP8 (MXFP8) `quantization_config`, and the per-tensor precisions come from `hf_quant_config.json`.
- LoRA on attention projections. The NVFP4 / MXFP8 experts are not LoRA targets, so `--enable-lora` serves attention-only adapters on the released checkpoints; experts that support LoRA (e.g. SkyRL's BF16 experts) keep expert adapters.
- After a target weight update (reload, RL weight transfer), the DSpark draft re-derives its folded LM head in place via the runner's `on_target_weights_replaced` hook.

## Validation

GB200, TP4 (one tray) unless noted, DSpark k=7 with probabilistic drafting.

**Accuracy** (measured on the Nov 12 revision of this PR, same model code; [inkling-verify](https://github.com/thinking-machines-lab/inkling-verify), T=1.0 except NIAH):

| Eval | Result |
|---|---|
| MMMU-Pro vision (first 150) | 84.7% |
| MMMU-Pro standard-10 (first 150) | 86.0% |
| HLE (first 50) | 50.0% |
| NIAH 4K–1M, 11 depths × 10 samples (TP8, T=0) | 550/550 |

Repeated runs on earlier revisions were within sampling noise (MMMU-Pro std-10 86.0–86.7%, HLE 46–52%), and scores match runs without speculative decoding.

**Performance:** single user at TP4 ≈ 630 tok/s with acceptance length 3.5. Agentic multi-turn at TP8 with prefix caching, 100 tok/s/user: ~1,070 output tok/s/GPU at 32K session context, ~700 at 128K.

**Tests** (latest revision on current main: torch 2.14.0, FlashInfer 0.7.4; official checkpoints from the HF Hub, no HF token):

```bash
pytest tests/models/inkling2 tests/models/inkling/test_fa4_rel_attention.py \
       tests/renderers/test_inkling.py tests/parser/engine/test_inkling.py                         # 458 passed
cargo test --release -p vllm-chat inkling                                                          # 35 passed
```

`compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck` with `PYTORCH_NO_CUDA_MEMORY_CACHING=1` reports 0 errors on the expert GEMM / MoE layer tests and a tiny-config engine.

Serving smoke test, TP4 with DSpark (greedy and probabilistic drafting) (`--reasoning-parser inkling --tool-call-parser inkling --enable-auto-tool-choice`), Python and Rust frontends: text, image and tool-call requests return correct answers.

| Checkpoint | Result |
|---|---|
| `thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Small`, `--max-model-len 262144` | passed (117 tokens accepted over 35 drafts) |
| `thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Small-MXFP8`, `--max-model-len 65536 --max-num-batched-tokens 4096` | passed (111 tokens accepted over 33 drafts) |

**CI:** `tests/models/inkling2/` needs Blackwell GPUs (and the 393 GB checkpoint for `test_model.py`), so the files are in `tools/pre_commit/test_tethering_allowlist.txt`; validation above was run outside CI.

## Details

- Layout: the implementation (model, kernels, DSpark draft, LoRA) lives in `vllm/models/inkling2/nvidia/`; configs, processing, quantization metadata and the speculator are shared at the package root, and `vllm/models/inkling2/__init__.py` resolves the model and draft classes for the registry, so platform implementations can be added alongside.
- Self-contained under `vllm/models/inkling2/`, `csrc/inkling2/` and the Inkling renderer/parser. Shared-code changes are small: registry and config entries, the `inkling2` quant method (only the routed experts are quantized), a `replicate_hidden` option for Inkling's conv state, and DSpark draft config resolution.
- Numerics follow the reference implementation: same dtypes at every step, FP32 attention output and router, same NVFP4/MXFP8 activation quantization (NVFP4 uses per-token scales and Four Over Six block-scale selection by MAE); only reduction order and the BF16 all-reduce partials differ.
- The attention prefill path uses `tml-fa4`, bumped to vllm-project/tml-fa4#6 (no vLLM-side patch): it takes the bias already sheared by Inkling 2's attention prologue, writes FP32 output for the gate/sink epilogue, and runs the reference softmax's `exp2` emulation on biased blocks (`bias_ex2_emu`). All three are opt-in; Inkling's `rel_bias` path is unchanged.
- MXFP8 at TP4: its weights take 146 GiB per GPU (93 GiB for the original checkpoint). The short-conv state sits in 4-token sliding-window KV groups whose blocks share the attention page size, and a request's conv blocks cover its in-flight prefill chunk, so with the default `--max-num-batched-tokens` (= `max_model_len`) a single 16K request needs ~25 GiB of KV cache. A smaller prefill chunk (`--max-num-batched-tokens 4096`) leaves room for 64K contexts at TP4; use TP8 for longer ones.
- Limitations: Blackwell (SM100) only; expert LoRA requires BF16 experts; a 1M-token request needs TP8 (TP4 caps at 262K).

---

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Fix AITER shared-expert fusion routing for gate-less MoE (DeepSeek-V2-Lite)
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fix silently wrong MoE routing on ROCm when `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1` is used with softmax-routed models whose fused shared experts have no gate, such as DeepSeek-V2-Lite (any model built on `DeepseekV2MoE` with softmax routing and one expert group). `AiterSharedRoutedFusedMoERouter` (added in #39280 for Qwen3-Next) treated the last router-logit columns as a shared-expert gate for every such model.

## Claims

- Fixes wrong outputs with AITER shared-expert fusion on gate-less models, matching fusion off:
  - DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat (on `main`) GSM8K (strict) goes from 0.095 to 0.661 (fusion off 0.656).
  - Mistral-Large-4-1T-A52B, with a local model implementation that builds its MoE layers with `main`'s `DeepseekV2MoE` (see Validation; not the `MistralMoE` of #64534): GSM8K (strict) goes from 0.718 to 0.959 at 5-shot (fusion off 0.957) and from 0.770 to 0.965 at 20-shot (fusion off 0.962), mean of 3 runs each.
- Qwen3-Next (gated shared expert) routing is unchanged: Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct with fusion on scores the same before and after this PR (GSM8K flexible-extract 0.952 vs 0.953, fusion off 0.953, 3 runs each), and the gated cases of the router test pass on `main`.
- With the fix, shared-expert fusion becomes usable for such models. On that Mistral Large 4 implementation, median TPOT is 21% lower than fusion off at concurrency 1, 7.5% lower at 8 and 5% lower at 32 (MI325X, TP8). No throughput regression on DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat.

## Validation

All runs on MI325X (gfx942), AITER 0.1.26, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, on a local ROCm build (vLLM 0.32.1rc1.dev361, 83c078d955). "Before" and "after" differ only in the three changed Python files, taken from before and after this change. The evals and benchmarks below were run before the review round; the review changes only remove a `fill_` that no in-tree model reached (every caller has `shared_expert_weight == 1.0`, see Details) and change how the factory derives the gate flag, so they don't change routing for any of these models.

Mistral Large 4 is not in `main` yet, so we used a local Mistral Large 4 implementation that is not in `main` or in another PR. It builds every MoE layer (softmax top-4 over 128 routed experts plus one shared expert, no shared-expert gate, no score bias) with `main`'s `DeepseekV2MoE`, the class DeepSeek-V2-Lite uses, which passes `n_shared_experts` and `fuse_shared_experts` to `FusedMoEFactory`. With the flag set, it fuses the shared expert and takes this router. Mistral's working branch #64534 (at `bd4fa26`) instead passes the shared expert to `MistralMoE` as a separate MLP, so `num_fused_shared_experts` is 0, the factory picks `FusedTopKRouter`, and the flag has no effect: as published, #64534 neither hits this bug nor gets the TPOT gain from this PR alone. Fusing its shared expert would be a separate change, and it would need this fix.

**GSM8K, 5-shot (strict-match / flexible-extract)**

| Model | Fusion off | Fusion on, before | Fusion on, this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mistral-Large-4-1T-A52B (FP8), TP8, 1319 questions, run 1 | 0.960 / 0.970 | 0.717 / 0.889 | 0.958 / 0.967 |
| run 2 | 0.958 / 0.967 | 0.723 / 0.910 | 0.960 / 0.971 |

Run 2 leans towards this PR (p = 0.04, not corrected for the six comparisons); with flexible-extract the three runs are 8 vs 11, 10 vs 6, 14 vs 8 (p = 0.65, 0.45, 0.29).

Qwen3-Next ends its answers in a Markdown form such as "Final Answer: **160 minutes**", which strict-match mostly misses, so flexible-extract is the meaningful score here.

| | Run 1 | Run 2 | Run 3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fusion off | 0.652 / 0.951 | 0.659 / 0.954 | 0.663 / 0.954 |

Fusion is active in both fusion-on servers: their compiled graph has no `moe_forward_shared` op (fusion off: one per MoE layer, 48 layers), and both load the same compiled graph, so they differ only in the router code inside the MoE op.

```bash

  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --apply_chat_template --fewshot_as_multiturn --seed 0,0,0,0

# DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat: same model_args as
# .buildkite/lm-eval-harness/run-lm-eval-gsm-vllm-baseline.sh, with -t 1
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS={0,1} \

  --model_args "pretrained=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat,tensor_parallel_size=1,add_bos_token=true,trust_remote_code=true,max_model_len=4096" \
```

The FP8 `mistralai/Mistral-Large-3-675B-Instruct-2512` checkpoint (TP8) is not affected: with the flag set, every layer logs `shared-expert FSE quantization compatibility is not implemented for CompressedTensorsConfig` and runs unfused, so `main` and this PR take the same path.

**Tests.** Two existing files are extended; no new test file.

- `tests/kernels/moe/test_rocm_aiter_topk.py::test_rocm_aiter_shared_routed_router`, next to `test_rocm_aiter_topk_gating_shared_expert_suffix`. It builds the router with `create_fused_moe_router` with fusion enabled through the environment, and routes through `select_experts` with the real pre-filled AITER buffer. The last routed experts get the top logits for the first token and must be selected. The selection is checked against the softmax top-k cutoff over the routed columns, the routed weights against the scores of the selected experts (BF16 logits can tie at the boundary), and the shared slots must keep their ids, with weight 1.0 without a gate and the sigmoid of the gate logit with one. Cases, each with BF16 and FP32 logits: Mistral Large 4 (128 experts, top-4, 1 shared, renormalized), DeepSeek-V2-Lite-like (64 experts, top-6, 2 shared, not renormalized as with `norm_topk_prob=False`), and Qwen3-Next with its gate (512 experts, top-10, 1 shared; the fused-sigmoid kernel path with AITER 0.1.26).
- `tests/model_executor/layers/test_fused_shared_expert.py::test_models_fse_init` now also asserts that every fused layer using this router has `has_shared_expert_gate` set for its model: `True` for Qwen3-Next, Qwen3.5 and Qwen4-exp, `False` for DeepSeek-V2 and DeepSeek-V3.2.

On `main` (3fe0d44) with this PR's test files (the router test without the `has_shared_expert_gate` argument, which `main` doesn't have), the gate-less cases fail on the routing itself and the gated cases pass:

```
$ pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_rocm_aiter_topk.py -k shared_routed_router
main:     4 failed, 2 passed
          [bf16/fp32-mistral_large_4]:  assert {127} <= {11, 26, 112, 120}         (last routed expert never selected)
          [bf16/fp32-deepseek_v2_lite]: assert {62, 63} <= {11, 18, 26, 30, 39, 42}
$ pytest tests/model_executor/layers/test_fused_shared_expert.py -k test_models_fse_init
main:     10 failed, 65 passed, 3 skipped
          AttributeError: 'AiterSharedRoutedFusedMoERouter' object has no attribute 'has_shared_expert_gate'

$ pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_rocm_aiter_topk.py tests/model_executor/layers/test_fused_shared_expert.py
this PR (on main b2094ac): 283 passed, 3 skipped
```

Behavioral reproducer on `main` (router built by `create_fused_moe_router` exactly as `FusedMoEFactory` does for a gate-less model; 128 experts, top-4, 1 shared, as in Mistral Large 4; 4096 tokens):

```
                         main            this PR
top-4 matches reference  96.6% of rows   100%
expert 127 selected      0 (ref 139)     139 (ref 139)
shared-expert weight     0.0012..0.9984  1.0 (constant)
```

**Related tests** on the local build, before and after: `tests/model_executor/layers/test_fused_shared_expert.py`, `tests/kernels/moe/test_routing.py`, `test_rocm_aiter_topk.py`, `test_fused_topk.py`, `test_rocm_aiter_num_expert_group.py`, `tests/quantization/test_online_shared_expert_fusion.py`: 1538 passed on both. 16 online-quantization FSE tests fail identically before and after on this local build; they don't touch the router.

**Performance**, `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 1024 --ignore-eos --num-prompts 8×C --max-concurrency C`, seeds 0, 1 and 2, after a warm-up. Mistral Large 4 with the server above, fusion on (this PR) vs fusion off, mean over the 3 seeds (the seed ranges of the two arms don't overlap in any cell; no failed requests):

| Concurrency | TPOT p50 (ms) | ITL p50 (ms) | Output tok/s | TTFT p50 (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 13.50 → 10.69 | 13.46 → 10.66 | 73.4 → 92.6 | 139 → 116 |
| 8 | 17.73 → 16.40 | 17.75 → 16.43 | 437 → 476 | 623 → 464 |
| 32 | 28.00 → 26.67 | 27.40 → 26.29 | 1092 → 1154 | 1193 → 949 |

Both arms use the same AITER GEMM and fused-MoE tuning tables for this model; with the default tables the absolute numbers will differ. Before this PR, fusion on is not a usable baseline on this model because its outputs are wrong.

DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat TP1, random 1024 in / 256 out, 3 runs each: output throughput with fusion on (this PR) vs fusion off is 268 vs 262 tok/s at concurrency 1, 2175 vs 2170 at 16, 5371 vs 5357 at 64. No regression; no speedup is claimed there.

**CI.** The router test runs in the AMD "MoE Kernels Shard" steps (`pytest kernels/moe`, MI300 and MI355) and `test_models_fse_init` in the AMD "(MI300) Model Executor" step (`pytest model_executor`). All three are `optional: true` in `.buildkite/test-amd.yaml`, so they don't run on a PR by default. They ran in [build #101076](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/101076) (this PR at c6d8a2b merged with `main`): [(MI300) MoE Kernels shard 1/3](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/101076#01a1bfca-4d70-43e3-b9fd-a49ca6ed545e) passes all six `test_rocm_aiter_shared_routed_router` cases, and [(MI300) Model Executor shard 3/4](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/101076#01a1bfca-4d7a-4fb2-97e1-949eb7a595bc) passes all 73 `test_models_fse_init` cases. 

## Details

**Root cause.** `create_fused_moe_router` selects `AiterSharedRoutedFusedMoERouter` when `num_fused_shared_experts > 0`, scoring is softmax, there is no `e_score_correction_bias` or custom routing function, grouping is degenerate, and `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, AITER MoE and `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1` are set. The router assumes every such model has a sigmoid shared-expert gate whose logits are appended as the last `num_fused_shared_experts` columns of `router_logits` (true for Qwen3-Next, where `MoERunner` concatenates `gate` and `shared_expert_gate`). For gate-less models, `router_logits` only has routed experts, so the last routed experts are treated as gate logits: they can never be selected, and their sigmoid becomes the shared-expert weight. Shapes stay valid, so nothing crashes.

Affected:

- Mistral Large 4 (128 experts, top-4, 1 shared) when its MoE layers fuse the shared expert, as in the local implementation measured above. Not #64534 as published, which keeps the shared expert unfused.
- DeepSeek-V2-Lite / -Lite-Chat and DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite-Instruct (64 experts, top-6, 2 shared, 1 group), measured above.
- The BF16 Mistral-Large-3 checkpoint has the same gate-less softmax routing (128 experts, 1 shared) and takes the same path by code inspection; not measured here.

Not affected: gated shared experts (Qwen3-Next, Qwen3.5), sigmoid routing with a score bias (DeepSeek-V3/R1, Kimi-K2, GLM), and real expert grouping (DeepSeek-V2, V2.5).

**Fix.** `FusedMoEFactory` passes `has_shared_expert_gate=gate is not None and shared_expert_gate is not None` through `create_fused_moe_router` (default `False`). That is the condition under which `MoERunner` concatenates the two gate weights, so the flag matches the `router_logits` layout by construction on every backend. The only other `create_fused_moe_router` caller (Step5 on NVIDIA) doesn't use fused shared experts. Without a gate, the router runs the softmax top-k over all routed logits directly into the routed columns of `aiter_topK_meta_data`, picked by `dispatch_topk_softmax_func` like the fusion-off `FusedTopKRouter` (`topk_gating` on gfx942/gfx950 up to 4096 tokens, legacy `topk_softmax` otherwise). Both kernels honor the row stride, and `init_aiter_topK_meta_data` pre-fills the shared slots (ids after the routed experts, weight 1.0; per-rank sentinel ids with EP). It stays one kernel launch, in the same in-place branch as the gated fused-sigmoid launch, which only adds the shared-expert arguments. The gated kernel calls are unchanged.

**Shared-expert weight.** `aiter_topK_meta_data` is one buffer shared by all MoE layers, so a per-layer constant can't be honored by writing it once. The factory therefore asserts `shared_expert_weight == 1.0` when it picks this router, matching the other AITER buffer paths (grouped top-k, `inject_shared_expert_weights`), which also rely on the pre-filled 1.0. No in-tree model trips it: the gate-less callers use grouped top-k, which reaches this router only with `routed_scaling_factor == 1.0` (otherwise the factory keeps `GroupedTopKRouter`), and the non-grouped callers (Qwen3-Next, AliceAI) are gated with weight 1.0.

**Duplicate check.** No open or merged PR or issue mentions `has_shared_expert_gate` or fixes this; the related hits (#42964, #44651, #53248, #61457) address imports and quantization compatibility, not the routing. #60217 (MoE balanced routing) only touches `base_router.py`.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Metrics] Restart the logging interval clock on empty intervals
commits.pr_body:
`SpecDecodingLogging.log()` and `PerfMetricsLogging.log()` return early when nothing was observed during the interval, without advancing `last_log_time`. The clock is only moved by `reset()`, at the end of the non-empty path. `LoggingStatLogger.log()` calls both unconditionally on a fixed `VLLM_LOG_STATS_INTERVAL` timer, so the first busy interval after any quiet stretch divides its counters by the whole idle gap.

The under-report factor is `1 + idle_intervals`. After 100s idle at a 10s cadence, 300 accepted tokens in a 1s busy interval report 2.970 tok/s instead of 300.0, and MFU reports 0.0198 TF/s/GPU instead of 2.0. Not a crash and not a NaN, just a wrong throughput printed next to correct totals.

The fix calls `reset()` on the empty branch in both. `reset()` rather than assigning `last_log_time`, because `PerfMetricsDebugLogging` divides `total_calc_duration` by the same `delta_time`, so its accumulators have to restart with the clock or `mfu_calc_overhead` goes above 100%.

Two tests in `tests/v1/metrics/test_perf_metrics.py`, both failing on main.

I do not have a GPU. The tests were run against the genuine upstream modules with only their heavy transitive imports stubbed; the classes under test are pure Python and touch none of the stubs on the exercised paths. Worth someone running them in a real environment.

Developed with AI assistance per the policy in `docs/contributing/README.md`; the commit carries a `Co-authored-by` trailer.

commits.pr_title: [vLLM IR][RoPE] Port base RotaryEmbedding to a vLLM IR op (CUDA + ROCm/AITER)
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Migrate the base `RotaryEmbedding` from a plain `CustomOp` to a vLLM **IR op** (`vllm.ir.ops.rotary_embedding`), so the QK-norm + RoPE(+KVCache) fusion patterns match a stable IR node **without** having to force `custom_ops=["+rotary_embedding"]`.

This resolves the long-standing `# TODO: support rope native forward match` blocks in `vllm/config/compilation.py` and the underlying pattern-match failure tracked in **#28042** (RoPE only matched the fusion when registered as a custom op). It follows the direction of **#38756** ("Port RoPE ops to IR").

RoPE now emits the same IR node on every forward path (native/CUDA/HIP), so:
- fusion patterns match regardless of `custom_ops`, and
- the actual kernel (native vs. `_C` vs. AITER Triton) is chosen by **IR op priority** during lowering instead of a global custom-op flag.

## Why this is not duplicating an existing PR

The prior effort — **#43199** (`[vLLM IR][Rope] Port RotaryEmbedding to IR Ops`, @wxsIcey) and its predecessors #39488/#41773/#42264 — is **closed and unmerged** (last state: merge conflicts, `mergeable_state: dirty`), and RoPE is **not** an IR op on current `main`. This PR differs materially:

- **Rebased on current `main`** and conflict-free.
- **Keeps `MatcherRotaryEmbedding`** (making it emit the IR node) instead of deleting it. Current `main` gained `QkNormRopeKvCacheFusionPass` (the AITER QK-norm+RoPE+KVCache fusion, #42749) *after* #43199 was written, and that pass depends on the matcher — deleting it (as #43199 did) would break the AITER fusion.
- **Completes the ROCm/AITER path**: adds an `aiter` IR provider for `rotary_embedding`, decouples the AITER Triton dispatch from `RotaryEmbedding.enabled()`, and sets ROCm IR-op priority to prefer AITER when enabled. Removing the `+rotary_embedding` force otherwise silently disabled AITER RoPE on ROCm.
- Scope is intentionally limited to the **base `RotaryEmbedding`** (Neox + GPT-J, full/partial rope). `DeepseekScalingRotaryEmbedding`, mRoPE, flashinfer, and the `key=None` cross-layer-KV-sharing path are left on their existing paths and can be ported in follow-ups.

## What changed

| Area | File | Change |
|---|---|---|
| IR op | `vllm/ir/ops/rotary_embedding.py` (new), `vllm/ir/ops/__init__.py` | functional RoPE IR op (`activations=["query","key"]`, `allow_inplace=True`) |
| Providers | `vllm/kernels/vllm_c.py`, `vllm/kernels/aiter_ops.py` | `vllm_c` (`_C.rotary_embedding`) + `aiter` (`rocm_aiter_triton_rotary_embedding`) |
| Layer | `vllm/model_executor/layers/rotary_embedding/base.py` | `forward_native/cuda/hip` route through the IR op; AITER kernel now via IR priority, not a direct `enabled()`-gated dispatch |
| Priority | `vllm/platforms/cuda.py`, `vllm/platforms/rocm.py`, `vllm/config/kernel.py` | `rotary_embedding` IR-op priority (ROCm prefers `aiter` when AITER + a RoPE fusion / custom op is enabled) |
| Matcher | `vllm/compilation/passes/fusion/matcher_utils.py` | `MatcherRotaryEmbedding` emits the IR node (incl. ROCm/AITER) |
| Cleanup | `vllm/config/compilation.py` | remove the three `+rotary_embedding` force-appends |
| Test | `tests/kernels/ir/test_rotary_embedding.py` (new) | registration / native-vs-`forward_static` / provider dispatch / not-inplace / opcheck |

## Test plan

> **This is a draft.** It has been static-checked only; it is **not yet runtime-verified** — I do not currently have a GPU/ROCm box available for this branch. The following must pass before this leaves draft:

```bash
# IR op unit tests (CUDA/ROCm)
pytest tests/kernels/ir/test_rotary_embedding.py -v

# Fusion still matches WITHOUT +rotary_embedding (the point of #28042)
pytest tests/compile/passes/test_qk_norm_rope_fusion.py -v
# ROCm/AITER:
pytest tests/compile/passes/test_rocm_aiter_qk_norm_rope_kvcache_fusion.py -v
```

## Test result

- Static: `python -m py_compile` passes on all 11 changed files.
- Runtime: **pending** (draft) — unit/fusion tests above + a **gsm8k parity** run vs. the unfused baseline (this change alters the RoPE lowering path, so accuracy parity must be confirmed) will be added here before marking ready-for-review.

---

**AI assistance was used to prepare this change.** The submitter has reviewed the diff and will run and attach the test/eval results above before this PR is taken out of draft.

commits.pr_title: [CI][Test] Expect the decode-crossed Mamba hit in test_qwen_mtp_mamba_prefix_cache_hit_is_bounded
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Since #67053, `test_qwen_mtp_mamba_prefix_cache_hit_is_bounded` fails in the nightly on both MI355X and B200 ([build 103780](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/103780#01a1ed81-9c89-4efc-b830-5244ed405489)). This PR updates the test to expect the new, intended cache hit. Test only, no code change.

## Claims

Fixes `V1 E2E Hybrid Chunked Prefill` on AMD (MI355) and NVIDIA (B200).

## Validation

MI355X, `rocm/vllm-ci:test-deps-rocm-75228b7e47631bd9`, base df763962fc, `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` as in CI.

`pytest -v -s v1/e2e/test_hybrid_chunked_prefill.py`: 3 passed, 2 skipped (the Nemotron cases, skipped in CI too). On main the test fails with `assert 1088 == 544`, and it passes on main with only #67053 reverted.

With the 1088-token hit, all four access codes are found and every warm output matches the cold output exactly.

B200 was not run locally. Its nightly failure is `assert 1152 == 576`, and 1152 is `2 * block_size` there, which is what the test now expects.

## Details

Wave 1 decodes past `2 * block_size`. Before #67053, only prompt boundaries were cached under sparse retention, so wave 2 hit one block. #67053 also caches the Mamba state at the last boundary crossed in decode, so wave 2 now resumes at two blocks. The output check is unchanged, and the test still fails on any hit beyond that boundary.

The job runs only in the nightly, so the CI on #67053 did not run it.

commits.pr_title: [Feat] Support multiple structured-output backends on one server
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Support multiple grammar backends on one server (e.g. xgrammar + guidance) and route requests to the correct backend when `--structured-outputs-config.backend auto`.

This is useful for deployments that want to use strict-tool-calling (supported by xgrammar) and also user-provided constraints with features like JSON schema + multipleOf (not supported by xgrammar, but supported by guidance).

## Claims

- Previously, the server would pick a grammar backend based on the first request with structured outputs. Later requests will attempt to use that backend even when they are unsupported
- Now the server can lazily create multiple grammar backends depending on what each request needs
- Functionally the same as #62246 (draft and needs rebase). Major implementation difference is that, unlike `#62246`, this branch doesn't replicate a token mask buffer for each backend. Instead, all backends share the same token mask buffer (`StructuredOutputManager._grammar_bitmask`).
- Partially resolve #55152: it doesn't allow strict tool call tags to work with then guidance backend (by converting them into the guidance format), but it does allow strict tool call and guidance-only tags to both work on the same server.

## Validation

https://gist.github.com/yzong-rh/0f66a87dc2d2aa44b3386b079321af5a
`mixed_backends_client.py` sends a 4 chat completions requests with mixed structured output constraints:
1. yes or no choice: defaults to xgrammar
2. JSON with multipleOf: supported by guidance
3. JSON with patternProperties: supported by outline
4. lark grammar: defaults to xgrammar for non-mistral models and to guidance for mistral 

```
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-4B \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
  --port 8000 \
  --structured-outputs-config.backend auto \
  --speculative-config \
  '{"method":"dspark","model":"RedHatAI/Qwen3-4B-speculator.dspark","num_speculative_tokens":8}'

python mixed_backends_client.py --model Qwen/Qwen3-4B 

Main
[PASS] xgrammar-choice: 'yes'
[FAIL] guidance-multiple-of: Error code: 400 - {'error': {'message': "Structured output processing only supports one backend per engine. The engine is already using 'xgrammar', but this request resolved to 'guidance'. Configure `structured_outputs_config.backend` explicitly or use schemas supported by the initialized backend.", 'type': 'BadRequestError', 'param': None, 'code': 400}}
[FAIL] outlines-pattern-properties: Error code: 400 - {'error': {'message': "Structured output processing only supports one backend per engine. The engine is already using 'xgrammar', but this request resolved to 'outlines'. Configure `structured_outputs_config.backend` explicitly or use schemas supported by the initialized backend.", 'type': 'BadRequestError', 'param': None, 'code': 400}}
[PASS] lark-grammar: 'id=123456789012345678901234567890'

This
[PASS] xgrammar-choice: 'yes'
[PASS] guidance-multiple-of: '{\r\n  "value": 4\n}'
[PASS] outlines-pattern-properties: '{"name": "example"}'
[PASS] lark-grammar: 'id=123456789012345678901234567890'
```

```
vllm serve \
  RedHatAI/Mistral-Small-4-119B-2603-NVFP4 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 \

  --port 8000 \

  --speculative-config \

python mixed_backends_client.py --model RedHatAI/Mistral-Small-4-119B-2603-NVFP4

Main:
[PASS] xgrammar-choice: 'yes'
[FAIL] guidance-multiple-of: Error code: 400 - {'error': {'message': "Structured output processing only supports one backend per engine. The engine is already using 'xgrammar', but this request resolved to 'guidance'. Configure `structured_outputs_config.backend` explicitly or use schemas supported by the initialized backend.", 'type': 'BadRequestError', 'param': None, 'code': 400}}
[FAIL] outlines-pattern-properties: Error code: 400 - {'error': {'message': "Structured output processing only supports one backend per engine. The engine is already using 'xgrammar', but this request resolved to 'outlines'. Configure `structured_outputs_config.backend` explicitly or use schemas supported by the initialized backend.", 'type': 'BadRequestError', 'param': None, 'code': 400}}
[FAIL] lark-grammar: Error code: 400 - {'error': {'message': "Structured output processing only supports one backend per engine. The engine is already using 'xgrammar', but this request resolved to 'guidance'. Configure `structured_outputs_config.backend` explicitly or use schemas supported by the initialized backend.", 'type': 'BadRequestError', 'param': None, 'code': 400}}

This
[PASS] xgrammar-choice: 'yes'

```

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -v \
  tests/v1/structured_output/test_structured_output_manager.py \
  tests/v1/structured_output/test_grammar_backends.py \
  tests/v1/structured_output/test_backend_guidance.py \
  tests/v1/structured_output/test_backend_outlines.py \
  tests/v1/structured_output/test_backend_xgrammar.py

162 passed, 6 xfailed, 43 warnings
```

## Details

Previously, the `StructuredOutputManager` initialized one grammar backend and rejected later requests that resolved to a different backend. Since automatic backend selection depends on the request schema, mixed workloads failed with a 400 error.

The manager now caches backend instances by name, create grammar state using the correct backend, and make backends fill a shared token mask (`StructuredOutputManager._grammar_bitmask`) sized to model logits width.

Each grammar backend's individual `StructuredOutputBackend.allocate_token_bitmask()` is removed. `allocate_token_bitmask()` is now a common utility shared by all backends. Tests to ensure all backends respect the logits width (vocab size) used during sampling and work correctly with the shared utility.

- `vllm/v1/structured_output/__init__.py`: Core `StructuredOutputManager` changes
- `vllm/v1/structured_output/backend_*.py`: Remove per-backend `allocate_token_bitmask()`
- `vllm/v1/structured_output/utils.py`: new shared `allocate_token_bitmask` utility
- `tests/v1/structured_output/test_grammar_backends.py`: test backends work with the new `allocate_token_bitmask`
- `tests/v1/structured_output/test_structured_output_manager.py`: test `StructuredOutputManager`'s support for multiple backends
- Other files are mostly plumbing or comment updates

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Bugfix] W4A16 dense prefill cache: drop the load-time memory budget check
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Removes `_fits_in_memory_budget`, the load-time check that raised `Not enough room in the gpu_memory_utilization budget ...` for `kernel_config.rdna_hybrid_w4a16_prefill_dequant=enable` (#60710). It rejected configs that fit. The engine's KV-cache sizing already fails startup when the dense copies leave no room for one `max_model_len` request, so the check added no protection of its own.

## Claims

- Configs where the dense prefill cache fits now start; on main they fail at load with the `ValueError` above.
- A config that really does not fit still fails at startup, with the engine's KV-cache error instead of the kernel's.
- No runtime change: only weight loading is affected.

## Validation

gfx1151 (Strix Halo, 100 GiB reported), upstream main cfd86e4320 + this PR built from source.

Unit tests, `pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_rdna_hybrid_w4a16.py`: 344 passed. The three tests of the budget check are removed with it; `test_rdna_hybrid_w4a16_prefill_dequant_cached` still covers the cached copy.

End to end: `cyankiwi/gemma-4-31B-it-AWQ-4bit`, MTP draft `google/gemma-4-31B-it-assistant` (3 tokens), `max_model_len=4096`, `max_num_seqs=1`, `kernel_config={"rdna_hybrid_w4a16_prefill_dequant": "enable"}`; greedy chat prompt "What is the capital of France?".

| `gpu_memory_utilization` | main | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0.87 | `ValueError` at layer check 232/240 | starts, KV 10,326 tokens, "The capital of France is Paris." |
| 0.85 | `ValueError` at layer check 223/240 | starts, KV 7,985 tokens, "The capital of France is Paris." |
| 0.80 | `ValueError` (budget check) | `ValueError`: 3.49 GiB KV needed for one 4096-token request, 2.64 GiB available |

MMStar serving benchmark (same model and draft, 10 prompts, 512 output tokens, one run each, on the PR before merging main dc45a5f552):

| prefill dequant | result | model load | KV cache | TTFT | decode |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| off | pass | 21.23 GiB | 20.35 GiB | 1332.6 ms | 24.17 tok/s |
| on | pass | 76.36 GiB | 15.22 GiB | 992.8 ms | 24.61 tok/s |

## Details

The check reserved `total * (1 - util)`, a fixed 4 GiB of activation headroom and KV for one `max_model_len` request, then compared that against device free memory. It was stricter than the engine's sizing (`total * util` minus vLLM's own non-KV usage) in three ways, each of which rejects configs that fit:

- Blocks the torch caching allocator keeps after load-time temporaries counted as used. On Gemma-4-31B AWQ + MTP-3 that was 5.37 GiB of 81.46 GiB at the peak check, raising the lowest accepted `gpu_memory_utilization` from 0.840 to 0.891.
- The 4 GiB headroom is a fixed upper bound. Measured activation + CUDA graph peaks on gfx1151 range from 0.85 GiB (Qwen3-4B) to 3.27 GiB (Gemma-4-31B, MTP-3).
- Device free memory also subtracts memory held by other processes, which the engine does not take out of the KV budget.

The first version of this PR fixed only the allocator-cache case. Review pointed out that, without the old soft mode, the check decides nothing the engine's KV-cache check does not, so it is removed instead.

Trade-off: an over-budget config now fails after the profile run rather than mid-load, and the error no longer names the option. The load-time `Caching dense ... copies of W4A16 weights for prefill (kernel_config.rdna_hybrid_w4a16_prefill_dequant)` log still does.

AI assistance (Claude) was used. The submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the validation above.
